## 39. Ctrl+V on the customer's machine: the owner, not the data — 2026-09-21 (stage 3.5.1, closed)

**This closes §27.** Copy files on the console, press Ctrl+V on the customer's machine, and the
files appear. Proven on DESKTOP-OPHQIDH: `userpaste` 4 of 4, `clipcheck` 15 of 15 with the leak
test, `clipmirror` 18 of 18, `pastecheck` 17 of 17, `clipil` 15 of 15.

### What it was

**Explorer will not paste from a file list owned by a process above it.** The host runs as SYSTEM
so it can reach the Winlogon desktop (§4). It put a correct `CF_HDROP` on the correct window
station, pointing at files that existed and that the user could open — and the shell offered no
Paste at all, on a clipboard the user could read perfectly well.

Reading was never the problem, which is why six rounds of looking at the data found six real
faults and not this one. **The data was always fine. The owner was wrong.**

### How it was found, after §27 said not to guess again

By asking the question Explorer asks, from where Explorer stands. Every earlier probe read the
clipboard back from the host's own side of the fence: the host's `GetFiles`, or a PowerShell the
host spawned — which is SYSTEM too, because a script over there is a child of the host. Both said
the file list was there, and both were telling the truth about a question nobody needed answered.

`tools/userpaste` asks the other one. It pastes two files through the product's own transfer, then
has the host register a one-shot scheduled task **as the logged-on user, interactive, Limited**,
and that task asks the shell for the verbs on a folder. Before the fix, on Clint's own machine:

```
shell verbs on target folder: Open | Pin to Quick access | ... | Cut | Copy | Create shortcut | Delete | Rename | Properties
NO PASTE VERB OFFERED on the folder  <-- this is the greyed-out Paste, seen from inside
after the paste : 0 item(s)
```

and in the same run, with the *same paths* rewritten by that same user process:

```
Paste offered   : True
after the paste : 2 item(s)
```

Identical paths, identical files, opposite answers. The only difference was who owned the
clipboard. **That is the whole fault, and it took one measurement rather than a seventh theory.**

### The fix

`ClipboardAccess.SetFilesAsUser` — the host hands that one write to a short-lived copy of itself
running as the person at the machine. `UserProcess.RunAsInteractiveUser` gets the token from the
session the host is already in (`WTSQueryUserToken`), the same way the agent starts the customer's
tray app, so the helper is the user in every respect the shell checks: account, logon session,
integrity, window station. `RemoteSupport.Host.exe --put-files <list.txt>` is the helper; the paths
travel in a file because there can be thousands of them and they are long.

Three things worth keeping:

- **The clipboard data outlives the helper.** `SetClipboardData` hands the memory to the clipboard,
  so the paste works long after that process has exited. Confirmed on hardware — the owner window
  is gone and both files still paste.
- **No user, no helper.** At the lock screen or before anyone logs on there is no token, and there
  is also nobody to paste. It falls back to the direct write and **says in the trace that Explorer
  will not paste from it**, rather than reporting a success that is not one.
- **The watcher is held off across the whole thing**, helper included, so the host's own write
  never comes back as "the customer copied this".

When it works the trace says so in one line:

```
clipboard: the file list was written by a process running as DESKTOP-OPHQIDH\Lenovo, as Explorer requires
```

### What this does NOT change

**Text was never affected** and still crosses both ways. **The other direction was never affected**
either: the customer copies, the host reads their clipboard as SYSTEM (reading up is allowed), the
console fetches and puts it on the technician's own clipboard at Medium. **Drag and drop both ways
is untouched** — a drop onto their desktop is an ordinary file set with a target folder and never
goes near a clipboard, and a drag out lands on the technician's clipboard, on the technician's
machine, as the technician.

### The harnesses, and which question each one answers

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/userpaste <machine>` | **4 of 4 on DESKTOP-OPHQIDH.** The only one that asks the shell, as the user, on a real machine: does Explorer offer Paste for what the host wrote, and does invoking it land the files. **This is the one to run on any change to the paste path.** It ends a session already open, because a stale session keeps the host that was installed when it started. |
| `tools/clipil` | **15 of 15, this laptop, no server or machine needed.** The integrity boundary itself: a list written at Medium, read and pasted from a LOW child, and the reverse. Proves the relation rather than the product, and it is how to check the mechanism without a customer machine. |
| `tools/hostinfo/stationprobe.ps1` | Window station, desktop, sequence number, sessions, who owns explorer.exe, whether LogonUI is up. Run it through `runscript` when a clipboard question starts with "where is the host". |
| `tools/hostinfo/helperprobe.ps1` | What the `--put-files` helper did: trace lines, leftover list and result files, who owns and who holds the clipboard right now. |

### Two things that cost time here and will again

- **Every harness that opens a session needs a `Reason` now.** `ConnectDeviceMsg.Reason` became
  mandatory on the server when a session started writing its own ticket (§36), and every harness
  in `tools/` predating that silently got "no session" back. They all carry one now. A harness that
  stops working right after a server change is the first thing to check.
- **`pushfile --dir C:\Temp\hostupdate` loses its backslashes** through the shell and lands the file
  in a folder named `Temphostupdate` beside the host. `tools/hostinfo/hostupdatemove.ps1` finds it
  and moves it rather than making anyone push 72 MB twice.

### Still open

- ~~Nobody has performed the gesture by hand.~~ **DONE 2026-09-21** — Clint, after the ship and
  the platform restart: *"copy and paste is now working both ways, this is excellent."* Both
  directions, by hand, on real hardware. The specific cases are still worth doing: several files
  at once, a folder, a second paste of the same clipboard (checks 43, 44, 46, 47 in
  `docs/TEST-3.6.md`).
- **The 50 MB threshold has never been crossed**, in either direction. Unchanged from §26.
- **The helper starts a 72 MB single-file exe per paste**, which self-extracts. It is well inside
  the 15 s timeout on this hardware and invisible in use, but it is not free, and a slow or
  heavily-scanned machine is where that would first show.

## 40. Copy FROM the customer, and a clipboard leak found on the way — 2026-09-21

**CONFIRMED BY HAND ON HARDWARE** — Clint, after the ship and the platform restart: *"copy and
paste is now working both ways, this is excellent."* That closes the gesture no harness can
perform, in both directions, and with it stage 3.5.1.

**§39 made pasting INTO the customer's machine work. Clint then reported the mirror: copying FROM
it did nothing.** Two separate faults came out of that, and the second one is worse than the one
that was reported.

Proven on DESKTOP-OPHQIDH: `usercopy` 3 of 3, `clipcheck` **16 of 16** including both leak tests,
`codeccheck` 10 of 10. Locally `pullcheck` 8 of 8, `pastecheck` 17 of 17, `clipmirror` 18 of 18,
`clipil` 16 of 16, `dragoutcheck` 43 of 43, `filesetcheck` 35 of 35, `reconnectlocal` 20 of 20.

### Fault one: Explorer does not put the file list on the clipboard at all

**What a real Ctrl+C leaves behind is a promise, not data.** Measured by
`tools/hostinfo/oleprobe.ps1` while the logged-on user held a copy of two files, asked from the
SYSTEM host — which is where `SendClipboardToTechnician` asks it:

| route | answer |
|---|---|
| raw Win32 | the only format present is `DataObject`. **No CF_HDROP.** `GetClipboardData` returns NULL |
| OLE, `Clipboard.GetFileDropList` on an STA thread | **0 paths**, and the data object reports an **empty format list** |
| `Get-Clipboard -Format FileDropList` | "1 item" whose path is a **blank string** |

The file list is delay-rendered: it materialises only when somebody asks through OLE, in the
process that copied, and **that rendering does not cross to another account.** So it is the exact
mirror of §39 — there, Explorer would not read what SYSTEM wrote; here, SYSTEM cannot read what
Explorer wrote. Same boundary, opposite direction, and the same answer works:
`ClipboardAccess.GetFilesAsUser` asks a short-lived copy of the host running as that person
(`--get-files`, the mirror of `--put-files`).

**The helper is only started when it can possibly help** — the raw clipboard has no file list and
no text of its own, and yet something is on it. A plain text copy never pays for a process. And
the privacy gate is checked first (`OnCustomerClipboardChanged`), so nothing starts while nobody
is watching.

**That blank "1 item" is worth remembering.** An earlier probe counted it as a success and made
the OLE route look like the fix. A count is not a reading: print the paths.

**Text was never affected** and is still read the plain way — it lands as a real CF_UNICODETEXT.
A program that delay-renders its *text* would hit the same wall; nothing has tested that.

### Fault two: the clipboard kept crossing after the technician had gone — A LEAK

Found because `clipcheck`'s leak check, the one §26 says matters more than the rest put together,
**failed on a host a previous harness had subscribed to.** It is not caused by anything in §39 or
above; it has been there since the mirror was built on 2026-09-18.

`_subscribed` was added to on `SubscribeMsg` and **never cleared when a viewer went away.** A
viewer that simply disconnects — a dropped socket, a closed console, a technician going home —
never sends `On=false`. So the host went on believing somebody was watching, and the customer's
clipboard went on crossing into a session with nobody in it. A later viewer that had **never
subscribed** received the customer's copied text. That is precisely what Clint's decision of
2026-09-18 exists to prevent.

The server knew and did not say. Every branch of the viewer-disconnect path calls
`SendParticipants` **except the one where the last viewer leaves**, which calls `BeginGrace` and
tells the tray app and the technicians but not the host. `BeginGrace`'s own comment makes the
argument — the tray app must not claim somebody is watching a screen nobody is looking at — and
the host was the one party it was never applied to.

Two lines, one each side:

- `BeginGrace` now calls `SendParticipants(s)`. `Technicians` is already empty there, because a
  name is removed as that technician's last viewer goes.
- `HostEngine` handles `ParticipantsMsg` with an empty technician list by clearing `_subscribed`.
  A reconnecting viewer subscribes again, which is how the pointer and the first full frame
  already work, so nothing is lost by it — `reconnectlocal` 20 of 20 and `codeccheck` 10 of 10
  say the screen is unaffected.

**This needs the PLATFORM restarted as well as the host shipped.** It is the first change in this
stretch that touches the server.

### The harnesses this produced

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/usercopy <machine>` | **The only harness where the CUSTOMER copies as themselves.** Runs the copy from a task as the logged-on user, at Medium integrity, by `Set-Clipboard` and by the shell's own Copy verb, and asserts it reaches the technician. `clipcheck`'s copies are made by a script the host spawned, which is SYSTEM — that difference hid this fault completely. |
| `tools/pullcheck` | The console's RECEIVE half, no server or machine needed: the customer copies, and the fetched files must land on the technician's clipboard ready for Ctrl+V. §26 named this gap the day the mirror was built and it stayed open until now. It passed first time, which is how the fault was known to be upstream of the console. |
| `tools/hostinfo/oleprobe.ps1` | Every read strategy, from SYSTEM, while the user holds a copy, printing PATHS not counts. The threading is inside compiled C# because a PowerShell scriptblock cannot run on a raw .NET thread — trying killed the first version of this script outright. |
| `clipcheck`'s two leak checks | 3a was already there: nothing crosses before anybody subscribes. **3e is new: nothing crosses once the technician who WAS watching has gone**, done by dropping the socket rather than unsubscribing, because that is what closing a console actually does. It also now says WHAT leaked, which is the difference between an error reply and the customer's own text. |

### Still open

- **The specific cases have not been done by hand.** Checks 43, 44, 46, 47 and 48 in
  `docs/TEST-3.6.md`: several files at once, a folder, a second paste of the same clipboard, and
  the leak. The two that carry the claim, 42 and 45, are done.
- **Text that is delay-rendered** by the copying program has not been tested in either direction.
- **The helper costs a process per file-copy** while somebody is watching, the same as §39.

## 41. "The unattended switch does not allow unattended access" — 2026-09-21

Clint, 2026-09-21: *"the unattended switch is not working correctly. On a machine where i did the
normal install, then used the the unattended check in the tray, switches between attended and
unattended on the console, but does not allow for unattended access. the client still has to click
on allow."*

Every part of that is accurate, and nothing in the product was going to tell anybody why.

### Unattended access is two facts, and only one of them was ever displayed

§31 built it correctly: **the permission** (`Device.UnattendedEnabled`, stored on the server) AND
**the capability** (`DeviceInfo.AgentOnline`, an agent service actually connected). `StartSession`
still enforces exactly that, and it was not the fault:

```csharp
bool mayUseAgent = call != null || (_devices.TryGetValue(deviceId, out var di) && di.UnattendedEnabled);
hostConn = (mayUseAgent ? ...Agent... : null) ?? ...Client...;
```

With the permission granted and no agent connected, `mayUseAgent` is true, there is no agent to
find, and it falls through to the tray app — whose host is launched with `--consent ask`. So the
customer is asked. **The hub did the right thing.** What went wrong is that four separate things
reported success and not one of them was looking at the agent:

1. **The installer** printed `Agent service installed and running.` in green, unconditionally,
   with every `sc.exe` call piped to `Out-Null` — and sc.exe reports its failures on stdout. A
   create or a start that failed was swallowed and then contradicted.
2. **The tray app** enabled its tick box on `AgentServiceInstalled()`, a registry key that
   `sc create` writes and that stays there whether the service ever starts, ever reaches the
   server, or died months ago. Having ticked it, the customer was told *"Technicians at Anywhere IT
   can connect when nobody is at this computer."*
3. **The console** put the machine on the Unattended tab, correctly — `DeviceList.Belongs` goes by
   the permission on purpose, so the list holds still while agents come and go. But the dot is
   `Online`, which is `AgentOnline || ClientOnline`, so a dead agent behind a healthy tray app is
   as green as anything else. `AgentOnline` was carried to the console and never drawn.
4. **The hub** fell back to the tray app in total silence: no log line, and a technician watching a
   perfectly normal session start.

**The rule out of it: installed is not running, and running is not connected.** The only honest
answer to "will unattended access work" is the one the hub holds, because the hub is the only
thing that can see the agent's socket. Everything else is an inference, and all three of them
inferred the same wrong thing.

### What changed

Nothing about the enforcement — the security property from §31 is untouched. What changed is that
all four places now say what is true.

* **`UnattendedWording`** (new, in the client) — one pure function returning whether the switch is
  usable, the sentence under it and the tray item's text. There is now a fourth state: allowed,
  and the background service is not running, so *"technicians at Anywhere IT will still have to
  ask you first. Let them know."* The box stays operable — permission is the customer's to give or
  withdraw whatever the service is doing — it just stops promising something it cannot deliver.
* **`DeviceList.ClaimsUnattendedButCannot`** — permission granted, agent not connected, tray app
  connected. The console paints those rows' dots **amber**, gives them a tooltip in words, and the
  Unattended tab reads `Unattended  7  (1 not ready)`. A switched-off machine is deliberately not
  flagged: the red dot already says that, and a warning that means two things means neither.
* **The installer** verifies the service reached `Running` (with a short wait, because `sc start`
  returns as soon as the SCM accepts it) and says so plainly when it did not.
* **The hub** logs a warning naming the machine when it falls back for want of an agent.

### Why the wording had to leave the form

The state that matters — **service installed, not connected** — is not reachable on any machine
here, because no development machine has the agent service installed. `unattendedcheck` already
*skips* its no-service section on a machine that has one. So the single most important state the
switch can be in was the one state no test could visit. Asked as a function, every state is one
call. That is §30's lesson ("two of them invisible on this machine") arriving a third time, and
the same answer as `DeviceList`: put the decision where a harness can ask it directly.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/agentcheck` | **New.** Asks the live hub, as a technician, for the flags the console carries but has never drawn — tray app, agent service, permission — and then says, per machine, what would actually happen if somebody connected. Read-only: one technician socket, one state message, no session started and nothing written. This is what found that the fault is not in the hub. |
| `tools/agentstate.ps1` | **New.** The other end, run ON the customer's machine: is the service installed, running, connected, pointing at a binary that exists, branded at the right server, sharing one device id between SYSTEM and the person, and what its own event log says. Prints a verdict rather than a dump. Read-only — starts nothing, writes nothing. |
| `unattendedcheck` | **30 → 40.** Ten new checks on the fourth state, asked of `UnattendedWording` rather than the window, including that a machine whose agent IS connected still gets the plain promise and that the three states which were already right stay right. |
| `unattendedwire` | **7 → 13.** The hub's half, which every harness in this area has said in its own output was not covered. Against a real hub on a throwaway platform: permission on and no agent → **the session comes back ATTENDED**; then an agent connects, nothing else changes, and the same machine → **UNATTENDED**. That is the fault's mechanism, demonstrated. |
| `dashtabs` | **47 → 62.** The flag, the amber row, the tab warning and the fact it clears — plus that the tab grows wide enough for its own text, because `(1 not ready)` does not fit in the 150 px these buttons were born at. §30's rule, sideways. |

### Still open

- **Why the agent is not connected on Clint's machine is not yet known.** The measurement exists
  and has not been run there; `agentcheck` against the live hub shows DESKTOP-2N6FVGT with a tray
  app and no agent, which is the shape of it.
- **The portal's device list cannot show this.** Its "unattended allowed" pill comes from the
  database, and `AgentOnline` is in-memory on the hub. The console is the live view; the portal is
  the record.
- **The agent's own logging is thin and Information-level**, so an agent that is running and
  failing to connect says so only in a place nobody looks.

---

## 42. General, and the day display order stopped being the stored value — 2026-09-21

Clint, 2026-09-21:

> *"we need to add one more category to the ticketing system and that is general ticket which
> should also be the default"*

A fifth category, **General** — the job that is simply a job — and it is what a new ticket is
unless somebody says otherwise.

### The one decision worth recording

**General is numbered 4, and it is offered first.** Those two facts together are the whole of this
section, because they are the first time in this product that a category's position on screen is
not its number in the database.

`TicketCategory` is stored as an integer. `RemoteSupport = 0` is in every ticket row ever written,
and 0 is also what an unset column reads as. Putting General at 0 — the obvious way to make a
default — would have silently retyped every remote support ticket in every tenant as General, with
no migration to blame and nothing in the data to show it had happened. So the enum was appended to
and nothing was renumbered.

But a default that sits last in a row of five buttons reads as an afterthought. So display order
was separated from stored value:

| | |
|---|---|
| `TicketSummary.CategoryNames` | names **by value** — index 4 is General. Never reorder it. |
| `TicketSummary.CategoryOrder` | `{ 4, 0, 1, 2, 3 }` — the order a person is **offered** them. |

**Both pickers now walk `CategoryOrder` and carry the VALUE they find, never their own index.**
The portal's buttons emit `data-cat="@v"`, and the console's combo reads back through a single new
method, `NewTicketDialog.Chosen()`, instead of the six-times-repeated
`(TicketCategoryKind)_category.SelectedIndex` that was there before. That cast was correct for
three years' worth of code and became wrong the moment the two orders diverged; concentrating it
in one method is the only reason this change is small.

### The clamp that would have mis-filed jobs

`(TicketCategory)Math.Clamp(raw, 0, 3)` appeared three times — twice in the portal's page model,
once in `TenantHub`. Widening it to `0, 4` would have worked and would have been wrong: a clamp
sends an unrecognised number to the **neighbour of the nearest bound**, so a stray 7 was filed as
a Call out, with an appointment and a site address it never had. It is now
`TicketService.CategoryOf(int)`, which returns General for anything `Enum.IsDefined` does not
recognise. Unknown and default are the same answer, which is the only safe reading of either.

### What deliberately did NOT change

- **Automatic tickets are still Remote support.** A session (`AttachSessionToTicketAsync`) and a
  customer's call (`OpenTicketForCallAsync`) both pass `TicketCategory.RemoteSupport` explicitly
  and always did. That is a statement of fact about the job, not a default, and it must stay
  explicit — `TicketService.CreateAsync`'s default parameter is now General, so a path that says
  nothing gets General.
- **No migration.** The column is an `int` and gains a value; existing rows are untouched.
- **The photo gate.** Only Workshop is gated, and General joins the four categories that are not.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `photogate` | **36 → 37.** General joins the loop that proves a category needing no photographs is not asked for any. |
| `ticketformprobe` | **86 of 86, 20 of them new here.** (The 52 in §37 is that day's figure; the harness has grown since for reasons unrelated to this.) The new ones sit on top of the geometry: Every category is offered exactly once; the picker **opens on General**; General is **first**; and, per category, `Chosen()` agrees with the one that was selected. That last one is the fault this ordering could cause and that nothing else would see — the right fields on screen under the wrong heading, filed under the wrong category on OK. Its `perCategory` table is now keyed by `TicketCategoryKind` rather than by a position, and it selects through `Array.IndexOf(CategoryOrder, …)`. |

### Also fixed in passing

The console's right-hand hint read *"A walk in needs nothing else 2014 fill in the job…"* — a lost
`\u2014`, showing the four digits to the technician. Both strings were being rewritten to add
General's, so both were mended.

### Still open

- **Nothing here has been run on hardware.** It needs a platform restart and
  `ship-build.ps1 -OnlyTechnician`; no client reinstall, no migration.
  `docs/TEST-3.6.md` section K, checks 55–59, is the list.
- **The PORTAL half is compiled and nothing more.** `ticketformprobe` drives the real console
  dialog; no harness loads `/portal/tickets/new`, so the browser's five buttons have been proved
  by the Razor compiler and by reading. Check 58 is what settles it.
- **`docs/NEXT-SESSION-WORKFLOWS.md` now has five categories waiting, not four.** General's
  workflow is the one most likely to be "Open → In progress → Resolved → Closed and nothing else",
  which is worth saying out loud rather than leaving blank.

## 43. The console gets its own light-or-dark switch — 2026-09-23

Clint: *"Is it possible that a technician can set their console between light and dark mode, like
they can with the dashboard?"* It half was already: §38 put the setting on the PERSON, and the
console read it at sign-in. But the only switch was in the portal, and nobody would guess that the
portal is where the console's colours are chosen.

### What was built

- **A `Light mode` / `Dark mode` button in the console's header**, left of New ticket. Worded as
  what it DOES, like the portal's, for the reason §38's layout comment records. It offers whichever
  palette the person has NOT saved, so after a switch it offers the palette the window is still in
  — clicking it again takes the switch back.
- **`POST /api/appearance`**, bearer token only, writing the same `Technician.Appearance` column as
  the portal's switch through `AuthService.SaveAppearanceAsync`. Still one setting on the person,
  never one per surface.
- **It takes effect the next time the console STARTS.** Every window takes its `Theme` at
  construction, so repainting live would mean rebuilding every custom-drawn control, and restarting
  for them would drop any open session. The message says to Exit from the tray and open it again,
  because closing the window only hides it — "next time you open it" would have been a promise
  the next double-click did not keep.

### The fault it found on the way

**`/portal/enter` signed the browser in with the appearance the console had at SIGN-IN.** The
hand-off carries the `TechSession` the console's socket was opened with, and that record is frozen.
So flip the switch in the portal, then press Tickets in the console, and the portal came back in
the palette you had just left — the database right, the cookie wrong, and the switch looking broken.
That was true before today; a switch in the console would only have made it common. The hand-off
now reads the value fresh (`AuthService.AppearanceOfAsync`).

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `appearancecheck` (new) | **14 of 14**, against a platform of its own. No token and a bogus token refused and change nothing; what is saved is what the next sign-in is handed; junk is stored as "follow the company"; and the Tickets hand-off after a switch opens the portal in the NEW palette, both ways round. **With the old `/portal/enter` line put back it drops to 12** — exactly those two. |
| `dashtabs` | **62 → 72.** The real `DashboardForm` in each palette: the button offers the other one, is measured wide enough for either wording (§30), tall enough for its font, and does not touch New ticket. Pictures `mode-light.png` and `mode-dark.png` looked at. |
| `handoffcheck` | 42 of 42, unchanged. |

### Still open

- **Not on hardware.** Platform restart and `ship-build.ps1 -OnlyTechnician`; no migration, no
  client reinstall. `docs/TEST-3.6.md` section L, checks 60–63.
- The login dialog is still drawn in the company's palette (§38) — nobody has said who they are yet.

## 44. The Workshop workflow — 2026-09-24 (stage 3.7, the first category)

Clint wrote the Workshop route himself (verbatim in `docs/NEXT-SESSION-WORKFLOWS.md`), answered
two rounds of questions, and approved the map the same day. **Read that file first**: every
decision below is answered there in his words, and the build follows it. Workshop is the first
category and the pattern; General, Remote support, Walk in and Call out are still unwritten.

### Built in five steps, one commit each

1. **Owner and Supervisor, separated** (`967692a`). `TenantRole.Admin` is the SUPERVISOR now
   (label only — the number in the database did not move) and `Billing` is the OFFICE
   ADMINISTRATOR. Two new values: `Owner` (portal only, **no seat**) and `OwnerSupervisor` (takes
   the supervisor seat). Exactly one owner, kept true in `TenantService`: adding a second,
   promoting through the dropdown, demoting and removing the owner all refuse; only the owner may
   move their own row between the two forms; `set-owner` on the platform CLI hands a company over.
   Migration `OwnerRole` makes each company's first enabled administrator its Owner / Supervisor.
   **A company's owner is ASP.NET role "tenant", never "owner"** — "owner" is the PLATFORM's
   operator, and the two sharing a word is a trap `rolecheck` asserts against.
2. **Stages and their gates, in the service** (`5f05db3`). `Services/Workflow.cs` is the route,
   defined once: stages (key, label, lane, summary status) and actions (from, to, who, what must be
   typed, what must already exist). `TicketService.ActAsync` is the ONLY thing that moves a stage;
   `ActionsFor` is what both UIs draw. `UpdateAsync` refuses a raw status change on a workflow
   ticket, so the old status dropdown cannot walk past a gate.
3. **Items and quotes** (`04d0ef0`). `QuoteService`: one item list per company; `MatchKey` is the
   name's words sorted, so "memory DDR" is "DDR memory"; near-misses ask "did you mean". Quote
   lines, part photos (`PhotoKind.Part`), and the request email.
4. **@mentions** (`81704e5`). `TicketMention`, open until that person writes on THAT ticket.
5. **The screens** — the portal ticket page, the billing queue, the Items page (`5049c51`), and
   the console's badge. **The console's Tickets button shows the count** — `Tickets (2)`, red, a
   tooltip saying why — and opens the portal on "Waiting on my reply" when there is one.
   `TicketService.MentionsChanged` fires after the save; `HubRegistry` pushes a `MentionCountMsg`
   to that person's consoles, and every console is told its count when it signs in. The button is
   measured for "Tickets (99)" so the header does not shuffle (§30). `PortalHandoffService` gained
   ONE exact link with a query, `/portal/tickets?filter=asked` — whole-string, never a prefix.

**The console's own ticket window came the same day — §45.**

### The data model decision the brief warned about

**A ticket has a `Stage` (a string key) and a `Lane`; `Status` is derived from the stage.** Every
list that only knows Open / In progress / On hold / Closed keeps working unchanged, and a stage is
never renumbered by inserting one — the lesson of §42. `Lane` is copied onto the ticket so "the
billing queue" is one indexed query: Bench 0, Office 1, Supervisor 2, Done 3.

**"Billing" is not a sixth category and not a separate ticket** — Clint accepted this. A job
keeps its category and its one story; the billing queue is every ticket, of any category, whose
lane is Office or Supervisor, assigned to nobody (answer 16: every office administrator sees it).
Work returning to the bench goes to `WorkedBy`, the technician who made the decision — Parts
fitted, a rejected quote, a declined "do not invoice".

**Two stages from the brief became one step each.** "Client invoiced" then "Awaiting payment":
pressing Client invoiced records the invoice and the job IS awaiting payment. Same on the quote
route. A stage that exists only to be clicked past is a click nobody needs.

### Photos moved from the close to the collection

The three out-photos are required by **Machine collected**, not by closing — Clint: *"Ideally this
must be done in front of the customer before any machine leaves the workshop."* A close needs the
machine collected, or the job abandoned. So the finishing buttons (Payment received, Ticket
complete, Close for a do-not-invoice) close at once if it has been collected and otherwise land on
**Awaiting collection**. A machine may be collected before it is paid for (round two).

### Who presses what

`Workflow.MayAct`: bench buttons are the assigned technician's, or a supervisor's or the owner's;
billing buttons are the office administrator's, a supervisor's or the owner's (answer 15);
approving a Do not invoice is a supervisor's or the owner's (answer 14). **A technician never
closes anything.** New `Permissions` questions: `CanWorkBilling`, `CanApprove`,
`CanStepInAnywhere`, `CanAddWorkDone`, `CanEditItems`, `CanPassOn` (a technician may hand THEIR
OWN job to a colleague, answer 1), `CanAssignWhenOpening` (anyone booking in names the
technician), `CanManageCompany`, `CanChangeOwner`. A workshop booking with no technician is
refused (`TicketService.CheckBookIn`, on both booking paths).

### Visibility changed, deliberately

A technician sees: their own work; the unassigned **bench** pool (a billing job is assigned to
nobody too, and is not theirs to pick up); jobs they did the work on (`WorkedBy`); and any job
they were @mentioned on, so they can answer. `VisibleTo` is still the one place that says so.

### The quote request email — 3b, with the one-step check

Desktop mail gets a `.eml` draft marked `X-Unsent: 1`: addressed, written, part photos attached.
Gmail and Outlook on the web cannot open a draft file, so the person is asked ONCE which they use
(`Technician.MailClient`, migration `QuoteMail`) and web mail gets its compose window with the
address, subject and body filled in, and the photos offered to save and attach. Sending from the
server through the company's own SMTP (3a) is a later release.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `rolecheck` (new) | **37 of 37.** The migration against rows written the old way; seats; permissions; the one-owner rule through the service. |
| `workflowcheck` (new) | **85 of 85.** Every branch of the map end to end, every gate refused when not met, every wrong person refused, the old dropdown refused, other categories untouched, existing jobs placed by their status. **78 with the billing rule broken on purpose.** |
| `quotecheck` (new) | **50 of 50.** No duplicates, predictive text in any word order, merge and rename, line rules, the .eml read back as MIME byte for byte, the web mail links. **45 with word order made to matter again.** |
| `mentioncheck` (new) | **27 of 27.** Who is mentioned, the badge's source, and the flag clearing only on a reply on that ticket. **23 with replies made not to clear it.** |
| `mentionwire` (new) | **9 of 9**, against a platform of its own over real sockets: the count on sign-in, at the right console only the moment somebody is asked, surviving a reconnect, cleared by the reply; and the one hand-off link with a query. |
| `photogate` | 37 → **38**, rewritten where Clint changed the rule: out-photos at collection. |
| `ticketscope` | 26 → **27**: a technician CAN now pass on their own ticket, still cannot take a colleague's. |
| everything else | unchanged and passing. |

**The portal pages were looked at on a platform of their own.** `tools/workflowdemo <empty
folder>` seeds a company with one person per role and jobs parked at six stages, and
`tools/portallink` opens the portal as a console user with no password typed into a browser. The
decision toggle, "1:15" and "R 1 250,00" being read, the billing queue, "did you mean", the Gmail
compose link and the draft's headers and attachment were all checked in the real page. That found
two faults no harness could: "Take this ticket" offered on a billing-queue job, and the outcome
labels losing their capital letter.

### Traps

- **A harness that seeds "old" rows through today's model breaks the day a column is added.**
  `rolecheck` did, the moment `MailClient` arrived. Seed the past with SQL against the table as it
  stood; `workflowcheck` and `rolecheck` now both do.
- **Razor reads an at sign inside a `<script>` block, comments included.** Write it as
  `String.fromCharCode(64)`, and keep names with at signs out of JavaScript comments.
- **`TicketService.LastBlockedReason` is instance state on a singleton** (pre-existing). Two
  requests at once can read each other's reason. `ActAsync` returns its reason instead, which is
  the shape to copy.
- **The demo platform on 8095 and the harnesses share the Debug build**, and a running platform
  locks it. Stop the demo (only the process listening on 8095 — never 8090) before a harness run.

### Not on hardware — what to ship

**Full platform restart** (migrations `OwnerRole`, `WorkshopWorkflow`, `QuoteMail`, `Mentions` run
by themselves) and `ship-build.ps1 -OnlyTechnician` for the console badge. **No client
reinstall.** `docs/TEST-3.6.md` section M, checks 64–80. Still unwatched by eye: the red
`Tickets (n)` button — every harness passed, and §32 says that is not the same as looking.

## 45. The console's ticket window, rebuilt for the workflows — 2026-09-24

Clint: *"go ahead and build the console ticket window."* The brief had moved a technician's
tickets back into the console on 2026-09-20 and held the rebuild of `TicketsForm` until the
workflows existed — *"what a technician's ticket view needs is what the workflows decide."*

### The Tickets button opens it again

Since 3.6.3 the button had opened the portal. It now opens **this window** (one of it, brought to
the front if it is already open), on **My work** — or on **Waiting on my reply** while the badge
shows a count. The browser stays one click away, signed in: **Open in browser** in the window, on
the open ticket if there is one. `PortalHandoffService.SafePath` allows `/portal/tickets/<digits>`
and nothing else after that slash.

### It decides nothing

The right-hand side draws only what `TicketDetail` carries, and the server fills that from
`TicketService.FillWorkflowAsync` — the same `ActionsFor` the portal draws, the stage, whose desk,
the recorded facts, whether Work done and the quote belong on screen, what may be edited, who is
waiting on this person's reply. **The console holds no copy of the route.** Add a stage or a field
in `Workflow.cs` and both surfaces follow. A button that needs fields opens `StageActionDialog`,
built from the action's own field list; what is typed is sent AS TYPED and read on the server by
`TicketService.ParseMinutes` / `ParseMoney` (moved out of the portal page so both share them).

New messages: `TicketActMsg`, `TicketWorkDoneMsg`, `TicketNoticeMsg` (a refusal in words, shown at
the top of the ticket), `ItemSuggestMsg`/`ItemListMsg`, `QuoteLineAddMsg`/`QuoteLineRemoveMsg`,
`QuoteSimilarMsg` ("did you mean"). The hub scopes every one with `MayTouchTicketAsync`, and a
line removal must name the ticket the line is actually on — otherwise a line from a ticket the
technician may not see could be removed by naming one they may. Part photos go over HTTP
(`kind=part` on `/api/portal/photos`), never the socket.

### What stays in the browser

**Request quote** — the office's step, and it needs the mail-client choice; the console offers
"Request quote in the browser". **Looking at photographs** — the console counts them and uploads
the out-photos, but has no bearer-authenticated way to fetch an image, so "See them in the browser".

### Laid out the §37 way

Every size measured from its font; flow layout; the ticket side rebuilt from scratch on each
detail (and after a resize settles) rather than twenty controls updated in place. "Is it
repairable?" comes first and the outcomes appear under "Then, how does it end?"; other steps sit
under "Or:". A workflow job has no status box. The minimum window size is measured from what the
two columns need — `ticketwindowprobe` caught the fixed 900 px floor letting the ticket run 190 px
off the right-hand side. Dropdowns and the quantity box take the palette explicitly.

**`DrawToBitmap` lies about dark.** It draws dropdowns and scrollbars in their default light look
whatever the window has set, so the probe's ordinary pictures showed a white dropdown that was not
white on screen. The probe now also takes a REAL screen capture of the dark window
(`bench-dark-screen.png`), and that is what found the fault that was real: the ticket side's
scrollbar was light, because `NativeDark.Apply` runs when the window is shown and skips a control
with no handle yet — and the ticket side is hidden until a ticket is opened. It is themed when it
first appears now. **Any control created or first shown after `Shown` needs
`NativeDark.Scrollbars` itself.**

**Every console dropdown is now `ThemedCombo` (RemoteSupport.UI, same day, Clint: "fix the
dropdown in dark").** A flat ComboBox takes BackColor and ForeColor but paints its outer ring in
`SystemColors.Window` — white — and a focused one paints the chosen value in the system highlight
colour: a white outline on every dropdown in dark, and a white bar on whichever had focus.
`ThemedCombo` draws its own rows (the box never highlighted, the open list's hovered row in
`SurfaceAlt`), then paints its border (the field border, purple with focus) and a drawn chevron
over what Windows drew on `WM_PAINT`. Row height from the font, arrow width from the DPI. Used in
the ticket window, the stage dialog, New ticket, the session toolbar (monitor, script language)
and the dashboard's chat target — which used to draw its own rows at a fixed 20 px. Proved by real
screen captures, closed and OPEN, in `ticketwindowprobe` (`bench-dark-screen.png`,
`dropdown-open-dark.png`); a `DrawToBitmap` picture cannot show any of it, because the border is
painted outside WM_PRINT. The captures repaint the window first: taken straight after showing, a
RoundButton's corners still held whatever was on screen before, which looked like a fault and was
not one.

The New ticket dialog now says "Choose the technician" for a workshop booking before sending it.

The real window, handed tickets at five stages with no server: the buttons are exactly the actions sent; Repairable first, then only the outcomes that follow; Request quote goes to the browser; no status box on a workflow job and one on a General job; nothing past the right edge, no button's words cut, at full size, at the minimum and in dark; the stage dialogs ask for exactly their fields. Pictures of every case, looked at. |

## 46. The workshop ticket as a story, in the portal and the console — 2026-09-27

Clint, after using §44 and §45: *"it needs to be a step by step workflow, not everything on one
screen as it looks confusing. It must pretty much be menu driven"* and *"i do not see an add
Item"*. Then, with screenshots of the system Anywhere uses today: *"the stage transitions at the
top with always a place to post comments through every stage, and then one can scroll through it,
reads like a story."* And the order: *"Inspection Findings before Repairable, and then work done
after repairable."* **§44's bench and §45's layout are superseded by this section**; everything
after the outcome (billing, quote, collection, close) is unchanged.

### The order (commit `1cf714e`)

**Booked in → Inspection findings → Repairable / Not repairable → Work done → Solved to be
invoiced / Quote needed / Do not invoice.** Not repairable goes straight to Invoice inspection fee
/ Do not invoice. In `Workflow.cs`: `inspection` (asks `Details`) moves Booked in to Inspected;
`repairable` and `not-repairable` are plain steps from Inspected; `work-done` (asks `Details`)
moves Repairable to Work done; the endings hang off Work done or Not repairable. Waiting on
customer is available from any bench stage and returns to where it came from. A declined Do not
invoice returns to `@decision` — Not repairable if it was not repairable, otherwise Work done.
**On the bench is retired**: its label is kept for history, and migration `TimelineForms` moves
every ticket (and every Waiting-on-customer return point) sitting there to Inspected.

**Work done is a step now, not entries over time.** `TicketWorkDoneMsg` still exists on the hub
and `mentioncheck` uses it, but neither screen offers it.

**One timeline entry per step.** A step with a form writes ONE note carrying `FormTitle` (the
step's name), `MovedTo` (the stage it moved the job to) and the values as "Label: value" — or,
for `Details`, just what was typed. A step with no form writes a system line. `TicketDetail`
carries `PreviousStageLabel` (from the last note that moved the job to where it is) for the crumb.

### The portal (commit `701a8f5`)

`Ticket.cshtml` hands a workflow ticket to `_Timeline.cshtml`; every other ticket keeps the page
it had. The top: `#N – Subject`, the crumb `Workshop › previous › [stage]`, and a row of
`☞ Step` buttons — only the next steps. A step with fields (or Quote needed, or Machine
collected) opens its form **at the top of the story**, numbered next, with Submit and Cancel; a
step with none posts at once, with a confirm if it closes the job. Under the buttons: Activity,
Photos, Quote (only once there is a quote), Details. Activity is the comment box with "Ask
someone", then the story newest first, ending with the booking as entry 0.

`_QuoteLines.cshtml` is the item list with **Add beside the Item box**, drawn in both the Quote
needed step and the Quote tab (ids prefixed so the two copies do not collide). Typing offers
items; the same words in another order match the existing item without asking; a near miss gets
"Did you mean". `_RequestQuote.cshtml` is the office's step and the hand-over afterwards.

Posting a step or a comment now **redirects** to the ticket, so a refresh cannot post it twice —
walking it in the browser showed `?handler=Act` left in the address bar. The same walk found the
Request quote step drawn twice (its SupplierEmail field made the generic loop draw a second card
with the same id), fixed.

### The console (commit `525c0d4`)

`TicketsForm` draws a workflow ticket the same way: title, crumb with the stage as a `Pill`,
`☞` step buttons, tabs as buttons, the comment box first, the open step's form as a numbered card
at the top of the story, then the notes newest first and the booking as 0. **`StageActionDialog`
and the Repairable toggle are gone.** What is typed into a step or the comment box is kept as it
is typed, so a redraw (somebody else moving the ticket, a quote line added) does not lose it; when
the STAGE moves, the open form closes and its drafts go. Tickets with no workflow keep the plain
layout with the status box.

Request quote and "See them in the browser" open the portal at that place:
`PortalHandoffService.SafePath` now takes `/portal/tickets/<digits>` followed by exactly
`?open=quote-requested` or `?tab=photos`, compared whole — anything else on a ticket path lands
on the queue, as before.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `workflowcheck` | **94 of 94** — the new order, every gate, the one-note-per-step rule. |
| `ticketwire` | **26 of 26** — over real sockets: inspection with its form title, `PreviousStageLabel` "Booked in", repairable → work done, the three endings. |
| `ticketwindowprobe` | **69 of 69** (rewritten). The real window, handed tickets at six stages: the step buttons are exactly the actions; nothing is asked for until a step is pressed, then exactly its fields; an empty Submit says what is missing; a draft survives a redraw and goes when the stage moves; the Add button is on the Item box's line, to its right; Request quote opens no form; tabs; the General ticket's status box; fits at full size, at the minimum and in dark. |
| `handoffcheck` | **44 of 44** — the two suffixes followed, any other query not. |
| `photogate` 38, `quotecheck` 50, `mentioncheck` 27, `mentionwire` 9, `ticketformprobe` 86, `ticketscope` 27, `dashtabs` 72 | passing. |
| by hand, in the browser | on a demo platform: Booked in → Inspection findings → Repairable → Work done → Quote needed (suggestions, the same-words match) as a technician; then as a supervisor, a comment (redirected, clean address) and Request quote through Gmail. Photos, Quote and Details tabs looked at. |

**Seen once and not chased:** the dark screen capture showed a white strip at the right-hand end
of the QUEUE's column header — `HeaderFiller`'s territory, which this work did not touch, and the
2026-09-24 capture of the same window does not have it. If Clint sees it, it is real; until then
it is a capture-timing suspect.

### Not on hardware

Platform restart (migration `TimelineForms`) and `ship-build.ps1 -OnlyTechnician`. No client
reinstall. `TEST-3.6.md` section N, checks 87–94. Any workshop job sitting On the bench when the

### Later the same day: Work done folds into Solved, and a serial number (commits `e6a25cc`, `e977144`)

Clint, after the platform restart: *"After Inspection findings, it should move to the repairable,
not repairable stage. If you click on repairable, it should have the solved to be invoiced, quote
needed, do not invoice options. If once clicks on solved to invoiced, this is where the work done
should come in with the time spent and amount to invoice."* **This replaces the Work done step
described above.**

- **Repairable offers the three endings at once.** The `work-done` action is gone.
  **Solved — to be invoiced asks what was done, the time and the amount, in that order**, and
  writes one entry, `IsWorkDone`. Quote needed and Do not invoice ask for nothing about the work.
  The quote may be edited at Repairable. A declined Do not invoice returns to Repairable.
- **The `work-done` stage is retired like `on-bench`:** its label is kept, nothing moves into it,
  and it still offers the three endings, so any job the 17:28 build left there is not stuck. No
  migration was needed for that.
- **"Copy the work done for the invoice" copies the work alone.** The Solved entry reads *work,
  then "Time spent: …", the amount, the queue line*; `TicketService.WorkDoneText` returns
  everything above "Time spent: " (time is required there, so the line is always present), and the
  server sends it as `TicketNoteInfo.WorkDoneText` so the console copies the same words. An older
  entry with no such line copies whole. The probe checks the REAL clipboard, and puts back what was
  on it.
- **Waiting on customer is drawn after the steps that move the job on**, at every bench stage —
  the buttons are drawn in `Workflow.Actions` order.
- **`ticketwire` had a race that passed by luck:** a refused press is answered with the notice AND
  the ticket, and the harness read the notice, cleared, and then took the late ticket as the answer
  to the next press. It now reads both. Run it three times after touching it.

Then: *"In the quoting section we ask for item, part number and photo, lets also add a field for
serial number."* **`QuoteLine.SerialNumber`** (migration `QuoteLineSerial`, one column), optional,
beside the part number in the portal and the console; listed on the quote, in the timeline entry,
and in the supplier's email after the part number. **Never remembered on the item** the way the
part number is — a serial belongs to one part, and pre-filling it would put last job's serial on
this job's quote.

## 47. The Call out route — 2026-09-27 (stage 3.7, the second category)

Clint's words and his three answers are in `docs/NEXT-SESSION-WORKFLOWS.md` under Call out. In short:
**Call out booked → Work done (work and time) → Ticket completed — to be invoiced / Invoiced — paid
on site (→ Paid cash or Paid card machine → the office closes it) / Needs workshop work (the same
ticket becomes a Workshop job at Booked in).** Commit `7360b42`.

### How it fits the machinery that was there

- **`Workflow.Has` is now Workshop OR Call out**, and `Workflow.FirstFor(category)` says where a new
  one starts. Stage keys are global, so a call out's own stages are `callout-booked`,
  `callout-work-done`, `paid-onsite`, `paid-onsite-to-close`; "Ticket completed — to be invoiced"
  moves to the workshop's own `to-be-invoiced`, and from there it IS the workshop's invoicing route.
- **Sharing those stages is where it could break, and two things had to change.** `@close` sent
  every paid job to Awaiting collection unless a machine had been collected — a call out would have
  waited for ever for a machine that was never in the building. It now closes anything that is not a
  Workshop job. And `ActionsFor` offered "Machine collected" on every `MachineReady` stage; it is now
  Workshop only, and `MarkCollectedAsync` refuses anything else. **`calloutcheck` was proved to catch
  both: 52 → 50 with the old two lines back.**
- **Paid on site** records the amount in `InvoiceAmount` and, new, `Ticket.PaymentMethod` ("cash" /
  "card") and `PaymentReference` (the card machine's). The job's facts then say *Paid on site ·
  1,150.00 · card machine · 004512* instead of "To invoice".
- **Needs workshop work changes the CATEGORY**, so `ActAsync` handles it by name
  (`Workflow.ToWorkshop`). It needs three "as it arrived" photos on the ticket first — the same rule
  as a counter booking — and takes the booking's machine questions as optional `StageField`s
  (`Workflow.Optional`). **The device password is encrypted by the caller** (`ClientService.Protect`,
  in the portal page and the hub): `StageInput.DevicePasswordEnc` is all the service ever sees.
  `/api/portal/photos` now accepts "before" photos on a call out, **at `callout-work-done` only**.
- **Both screens.** The crumb names the category (the portal had "Workshop ›" written in). A call
  out has no Photos tab until it is a workshop job; its story starts with *"booked the call out"*,
  site, appointment and fault, and so does a workshop job that started as one — its machine details
  are in its "Needs workshop work" entry. Details shows the site for anything that started as a call
  out, and the machine for anything that is now a workshop job.

### Migration `CallOutWorkflow`

Two columns (`PaymentMethod`, `PaymentReference`), and call outs on file join the route: Closed stays
closed with its date; everything else — Resolved included, as the workshop migration did with its
Resolved jobs — is at Call out booked, Open, with `ClosedUtc` cleared. `calloutcheck` seeds old rows
by SQL against the table as it stood before, then migrates, and checks each.

## 48. Walk in, Remote support and General — every category has a route (2026-09-27)

Clint's message and his four answers are in `docs/NEXT-SESSION-WORKFLOWS.md`, under the three
categories. Commit `cea4968`. **With this, `Workflow.Has` is true for every category**; a ticket
with no stage is now only one written before the routes that the migrations left closed.

### The routes, and how they share

- **Walk in** — At the counter → Repaired at counter (work, time) → To be invoiced / Invoiced — paid
  at counter / No invoice; or Needs to be booked in (`Workflow.BookInFromWalkIn`, the same category
  change as the call out's `ToWorkshop` — both are in `Workflow.ToWorkshopKeys`). Paid cash and Paid
  card machine are the call out's own two buttons, now from either `paid-onsite` or `paid-counter`;
  their target `@paid` picks the matching "to be closed" stage, so the label is right for each.
- **Remote support** — Remote session → To be invoiced (what was done, amount) / Do not invoice (SLA
  client) → `dni-to-close` with `DoNotInvoiceReason = "SLA client"`, no approval / Do not invoice →
  `dni-approval` / Link to parent ticket (`StageField.ParentTicket`).
- **General** — Open → Done (closes) / Quote needed (the workshop's own `quote-needed` action, now
  also from `general-open`; its items are editable there) / To be invoiced.
- **`@decision`** (where a declined Do not invoice returns) is now per category: the workshop's
  repairable-or-not, the walk in's Repaired at counter, the remote session, and — General's only way
  to Do not invoice is a rejected quote — the rejected quote.
- **`ActionDef.Only`** narrows a shared stage's buttons by category: the rejected quote's "Invoice
  inspection fee" is Workshop only.

### Link to parent ticket

The choices come from `TicketService.ParentChoicesAsync`: the same client, still open, not itself,
not already somebody's child. `ActAsync` checks the same rules again as `SetParentAsync` keeps
(one level, no grandparents), refuses a ticket with no client with *"Link this ticket to a client
first"*, files it under the parent with a note on both, and closes it — Clint's choice, and the only
one that works with the next point.

### Found on the way — read these before touching the same code

- **A job could close through its route with a ticket filed under it still open.** The rule
  (§36/3.6.7) lived in `UpdateAsync`, which a route never calls. `ActAsync` now asks
  `CheckChildrenClosedAsync` of every step that lands on a Done stage — except Abandoned: walking
  away is not claiming the job is done. `ticketpersession` proves both.
- **The console rebuilt the whole ticket side whenever its scrollbar came or went**, ping-ponging
  between the two client widths (the trace showed 1028 ↔ 1002 several times running), and threw
  away what it had just shown: ticketwindowprobe's "Choose the ticket this is part of" vanished the
  instant it appeared, because it was the line that made the scrollbar arrive. Pre-existing since
  §45. `TicketsForm` now redraws on resize only when the panel's OUTER width changes, and
  `ContentWidth` is measured from that width with the scrollbar's room always kept.
- **The 30-minute session reuse** found any ticket that was not closed — so a remote ticket already
  sent to To be invoiced (which is In progress) would have had the next session poured into it.
  `ActiveForDeviceAsync` now only reuses a ticket at `remote-session` (or one with no stage).
- **The Quote tab** showed, empty, on every ticket whose quote could be edited — which would have
  been every open General ticket. It now waits for a quote; the Quote needed step has its own box.
- **Several harnesses assumed General and remote tickets moved by their status.** `ticketscope`'s
  status-permission checks now use deliberately stage-less tickets (the rule still stands for
  those); `ticketpersession` makes its sessions as the hub does — Remote support, not General — and
  closes through the route; `photogate`, `workflowcheck` and `calloutcheck` say what is true now.

### Linking a client at any stage

`TicketService.SetClientAsync` (anybody who may see the ticket; a note in its story). Portal: a
"Client" card on Details, one box with the company's names offered as you type, empty to unlink.
Console: "Link to a client…" / "Change the client…" on Details, opening `LinkDeviceDialog` through
a second constructor — the same window, and a person chosen there becomes the ticket's contact.
New message `TicketSetClientMsg`. The New ticket forms, both of them, no longer require a client for
General (the portal's field's own `required` followed the category too, or the browser would have
refused before the server saw it).

### Migration `EveryCategoryRoute`

No columns. Walk in, Remote support and General tickets on file join their routes; **Closed and
Resolved are closed** — unlike the workshop and call out migrations, which put Resolved back before
its decision. A Resolved remote ticket is a finished session, and there are many; bringing them all
back as open work would have buried the queue.

It caught General's quote items not being editable while Open — fixed. |
| `ticketwindowprobe` | **110 of 110** — the three routes' buttons, the parent picker (and its message, which is how the redraw fault was found), the client card. |
| everything else | `workflowcheck` 100, `calloutcheck` 52, `ticketwire` 28, `ticketpersession` 30, `ticketscope` 27, `photogate` 38, `quotecheck` 54, `mentioncheck` 27, `mentionwire` 9, `handoffcheck` 44, `ticketformprobe` 86, `dashtabs` 72, `contactcheck` 34, `devicelink` 19, `rolecheck` 37. |

## 49. Several people on one ticket — 2026-09-28

Clint, before internal testing with his staff: *"multiple people must be able to be assigned to the
same ticket from the start or added at any stage as sometimes more than one person works on the
same problem at the same time."* Approved with two choices: **everyone on a ticket is equal** (no
lead technician — one control, not two), and **a technician who connects to the machine goes on the
ticket automatically**.

### Stored in the column that held the one name

`Ticket.AssignedTo` (and `Ticket.WorkedBy`, the same way) holds display names joined by `", "`:
"Jason, Ryan". `Services/Assignees.cs` is the one place that parses, joins and asks. **No
migration**: every row ever written holds one name, which is already a valid list, and every screen
that only SHOWS the field shows "Jason, Ryan" untouched. Emptiness still means nobody, so the pool
and the billing queue (`AssignedTo == ""`) did not change.

A join table was the alternative. It was not taken because it means a second source of truth for
display (or `Include` on every list), and a migration, for a set that is two or three names long.
**The price is that a display name may not contain a comma** — `TenantService.AddTechnicianAsync`
refuses one, and a sign-up's contact name has its commas replaced.

### The trap: every "is this person on it?"

`t.AssignedTo == me` is FALSE for Jason on "Jason, Ryan". Every such question was changed:
`VisibleTo`, the "mine" filters (service, portal list, dashboard tile), `Workflow.MayAct` and
`MayMarkCollected`, `QuoteService.MayEditLines`, the photo upload's scope in `Program.cs`, the
workload board (a shared job counts on each person's row; orphans are split per name). In a query
it is `(Assignees.Separator + t.AssignedTo + Assignees.Separator).Contains(Assignees.Tag(me))`,
which SQLite runs as `instr` — **wrapping both sides is what stops "Ryan" matching "Ryan Smith"**,
and it must be guarded with `me != ""`, because the empty tag matches the empty list.
`TicketService.OnIt(q, me)` is the ready-made "tickets I am on". **Anything added later that asks
whether a person is on a ticket must use `Assignees.Has` or `OnIt` — never `==`.**

### Who may change the list

`TicketService.UpdateAsync` takes the WHOLE list wanted afterwards (null leaves it alone) and works
out who came and went. The office administrator, supervisors and the owner may do anything. A
technician has exactly two rights:

- **Join** — put themselves on a BENCH job, taking nobody off. On an unassigned job that is the old
  claim from the pool; on a colleague's it is "I'm helping". They can only reach a colleague's job
  they may already see (asked about it, worked on it), because every caller checks `VisibleTo`.
- **Their own job** — add colleagues to it, and take themselves off. Never take a colleague off, and
  never leave it with nobody: passing on means to somebody.

The story says who: one person to one person keeps its old words (*reassigned from Jason to Ryan*);
anything with more says *added Jason and Ryan to the ticket* / *took Ryan off the ticket*.
Workflow hand-offs carry the whole list: a decision records EVERY person as `WorkedBy`, so all of
them can follow the job through billing, and a job coming back to the bench comes back to all of
them (*Back with Jason and Ryan.*).

### Sessions

`AttachSessionToTicketAsync` puts the starting technician on a reused ticket beside whoever is there
(it used to leave an assigned ticket alone). A second technician joining a session already running
goes on its ticket too (`RunSessionViewerAsync` → `JoinSessionTicketAsync`), with *"… joined the
session on …"* in the story — **only while the ticket is on the bench**, so a job already sent to
billing is not taken out of the office's queue. Both use the server's wide-open `UpdateAsync`
overload: the server is recording a fact, not a person asking. **Not covered by a harness** — it
needs a live session; `TEST-3.6.md` check 115.

### The screens

- **Portal:** `_People.cshtml`, one pill-shaped tick box per person (`PeoplePicker` says which may
  be changed — the service's rule drawn, not a second copy). Used by New ticket, the plain ticket
  page and the workflow ticket's Details tab. A box that may not be changed is greyed and posted
  back as it stands, so saving a note never takes anybody off; `peopleShown` tells "nobody ticked"
  from "no list on this form". A workshop booking with nobody ticked is stopped before sending.
- **Console:** the assignee dropdown in the ticket window and in New ticket is a row of tick boxes
  (`_people` on the dialog — `ticketformprobe` looks for it by that name). `TicketDetail` carries
  `CanAssignToAnyone`, `CanJoin` and `CanPassOn` so the console greys the same boxes the portal does.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `assigncheck` (new) | **49 of 49**, every check through the services, visibility as SQL on a real SQLite file: the list's tidying and the "Ryan Smith" trap; two people from the start; who sees it and "mine"; the office and a supervisor adding and removing, with the story's words; every technician right and every refusal; the workshop route with two on the bench — either presses, both recorded, both follow it, both get it back. **With the old `==` put back in `VisibleTo` and `MayAct` it fails 12 checks and then stops before its tally.** |
| `ticketwindowprobe` | 110 → **123**. The probe's fake connection now has a signed-in name and a team (set by reflection): **its first run after this change drew the "People on it" heading over nothing**, because an empty roster has nobody to draw — every check still passed. New: a box per person, the right ones ticked, a colleague's greyed for a technician on the job, only their own open when they are not, all open for a supervisor, a departed person shown and said so. Picture `people.png`, looked at. |
| `ticketformprobe` | 87 → **91**: a box per person, the booker ticked, two ticked send "Bob Tech, Sue Tech", none sends nothing. |
| everything else | `workflowcheck` 100, `calloutcheck` 52, `routecheck` 53, `ticketscope` 27, `photogate` 38, `quotecheck` 54, `mentioncheck` 27, `ticketpersession` 30, `handoffcheck` 44, `contactcheck` 34, `devicelink` 19, `rolecheck` 37, `themecheck` 40, `appearancecheck` 14, `dashtabs` 72, `ticketwire` 28, `mentionwire` 9. |
| by hand, in the browser | on a `workflowdemo` platform: a General ticket opened with two people ticked (*With Bob Tech and Sue Tech*); as the supervisor, one added and one taken off on Details (*added Sam Supervisor to the ticket, took Bob Tech off the ticket*); as the technician Sue, Sam's box greyed, Bob added — and Sam, greyed, stayed on; the workload board counting the job on all three rows. **The walk found a fault no harness could**: the form's `peopleShown` marker said `1`, a `bool` parameter binds only `true`/`false`, and every change came back as "Nothing changed." It says `true` now. |
