## 50. The monthly health check becomes a tick on the customer — 2026-09-28

Clint: *"not all clients should get the healthchecker. This should only be for sla clients and
clients we choose to have it… the default install is without the healthcheck, but with an option to
add the healthchecker via the console or dashboard after the client app is installed."* Asked which
shape, he chose **a tick on the client, with a right-click override per machine**.

### What decides it

`HealthCheckModes.Wanted(companyAvailable, mode, clientTicked)` in `RemoteSupport.Shared` — the ONE
place, asked by the hub, the portal, the context endpoint and both harnesses:

1. **The company switch** (`Tenant.HealthCheckReady`: the tick on `/portal/healthcheck` AND the mail
   finished). Off, nothing is wanted anywhere. It used to mean "installs from now on get it".
2. **The machine's own choice**, `Device.HealthCheckMode`: 0 as its customer, 1 on, 2 off. 0 is what
   every existing row reads as, and anything unrecognised is read as 0, never as on.
3. **The customer's tick**, `Client.HealthCheck`. Every machine that follows them gets it, including
   machines linked later. An unlinked machine that follows its customer does not get it.

Migration **`ClientHealthCheck`**: that tick, the mode, and what the machine last REPORTED
(`HealthCheckInstalled` null until it says anything, `HealthCheckNote`, `HealthCheckReportedUtc`).

### Who carries it out: the agent service

**Only a SYSTEM service can register a SYSTEM scheduled task.** The tray app runs as the person, and
so does an attended session's host (`HostSpawner` starts it as a plain child of the tray app). So:

- **`Install-Client.ps1` no longer installs the health check.** It copies `healthcheck\` into
  Program Files beside the app — replaced, not merged, so no old script lingers — where it is inert.
  `-HealthCheckSettings` is accepted and ignored so old command lines still work.
- **The hub tells the agent a STATE** (`HealthCheckWantedMsg`) when it connects and whenever any of
  the three inputs change — the portal's tick, the console's right-click, a relink (in
  `RefreshDeviceOwner`), the company switch (`RefreshHealthCheckAvailability`, called by the Health
  check page on save). A machine that was off catches up when it connects; being told twice does
  nothing the second time.
- **`HealthCheckKeeper`** in the agent makes the machine match: runs `Install-HealthCheck.ps1`
  (`-ExistingSettings Keep -PlatformManaged -NoTestRun`, every value a single-quoted literal sent
  with `-EncodedCommand`, so an empty string and "O'Brien IT" both survive) or the new
  **`Uninstall-HealthCheck.ps1`**. An installed copy whose scripts differ from the ones beside the
  app is re-installed — that is how a fixed script reaches a machine now that the client installer
  does not touch it. Only the latest wanted state is acted on, and passes never overlap.
- **It reports what it then FINDS** (`HealthCheckStatusMsg`), never what it was asked. §41's rule:
  the console and portal show the decision AND the report, through `HealthCheckModes.Describe` —
  *"On - waiting for the machine to install it"* is not *"On - installed on the machine"*.
  **Only the agent may report**; a tray app's claim is ignored.
- The installer's own output is kept at `C:\ProgramData\RemoteSupport\healthcheck-agent.log`.

### It removes only what it installed

A health check is **ours** when its `config.json` has a `Platform.BaseUrl` — the standalone toolkit
writes the same folder and never that section (DESKTOP-OPHQIDH has one). Anything else is reported
as *left alone* and never touched: `Uninstall-HealthCheck.ps1` exits 3, and it removes only tasks
that run something out of the install folder — the installer's own rule, for the reason in §17. It
removes the SCHEDULE only; results and `config.json` stay, so switching back on keeps the day.

### The trap that is guarded: a reinstall must never be told "off"

A reinstalled machine arrives with a new device id: no customer, no override, so "off" — until
`PersistDeviceAsync` recognises its hardware a moment later and restores its record. Telling the
agent in that moment would REMOVE the health check and then put it back. `_healthLoaded` holds the
ids whose stored record has been read, and **nothing is sent to an agent until its machine is in
it**. Both sends stay (on registration and at the end of `PersistDeviceAsync`) for §33's reason.

**The harness could not see this at first — 52 of 52 with the guard removed.** On local SQLite,
`PersistDeviceAsync` finishes before the socket is even registered, so the window never opens on a
development machine. `Testing:PersistDeviceDelayMs` (never set in production) slows it on purpose;
with it, removing the guard gives exactly one failure: *sequence: OFF, on*.

### Two faults found on the way, both fixed

- **The monthly run never read the server's answer.** `/api/healthcheck/context` has always sent
  `enabled`; nothing used it, so switching the health check off in the portal stopped no machine. It
  now also sends **`wanted`** for THIS machine, and on an explicit `false` from an authenticated
  answer the run removes its own schedule and stops. An unreachable server never removes anything.
- **"Inspect only" was never obeyed either.** `runMaintenance` was sent every month and ignored, so
  maintenance always ran. The run now skips it when the company has chosen inspection only.

### The screens

- **Portal, client page:** a *Monthly health check* tick above Machines (saves on click), and a
  *Health check* column per machine — *As Zenith Ltd (on)* / *On for this machine* / *Off for this
  machine* — with the machine's own status under it. Walked in the browser on a held
  `healthcheckwire` platform (`HCWIRE_HOLD=1`): the tick and the dropdown both work by real clicks.
- **Portal, Health check settings:** reworded — the company tick *offers* it; which machines is the
  client's tick.
- **Console:** right-click → *Monthly health check* ▸ a greyed status line, then the three choices,
  the current one ticked. Everyone may use it (`Permissions.CanSetHealthCheck`, a question, so it
  can become the owner's alone in one place).

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `healthcheckwire` (new) | **52 of 52** against a platform of its own: the rule in all 12 combinations and the words; the agent told on connect; the company switch, the client tick, the console override, a relink, an unlinked machine switched on, a machine away while it changed, the reinstall that must never hear "off" (**51 with the guard removed**), a tray app's false report ignored, and `/api/healthcheck/context` saying `wanted` per machine and refusing a wrong key. |
| `Test-HealthCheckUninstall.ps1` (new) | **8 of 8** with a scheduled task of its own in a temp folder: somebody else's is left alone (exit 3), ours is removed with its results kept, and running twice is not an error. |
| `dashtabs` | 72 → **79**: the real right-click menu opened on a real row — the status line, *As Zenith Motors (on)*, the unlinked wording, the right choice ticked, and the line moving to *installed* after a report. |
| the agent's command line | generated from the real `HealthCheckKeeper` and parsed: every parameter name exists, "O'Brien IT" and empty values survive, `wss://…/` becomes `https://…`. |
| unchanged | `unattendedwire` 13, `devicelink` 19. |

**Not proved anywhere:** the agent actually registering and removing the task as SYSTEM — that
needs an elevated service on a real machine. `TEST-3.6.md` section R, checks 116–124.

### To ship

**Platform restart (migration `ClientHealthCheck`), a FULL `ship-build.ps1`** (client, agent and
installer all changed), **and a client reinstall** on each machine. A reinstalled machine keeps the
health check only if its client is ticked or it is set On — tick the SLA clients first.

## 51. The health check toolkit brought up to v2.9 — 2026-09-28

Clint fixed the standalone toolkit (`C:\PCHealthCheck`, its own git repository) because it *"wasnt
working correctly"*, and asked for the changes in our copy. We imported it at v2.7 on 2026-09-11
(§17); it is now **v2.9**, and every script prints that. Its `docs/TOOLKIT-HANDOVER.md` is the
toolkit's own account of v2.9 and is worth reading whole; this section is what it meant HERE.

### What v2.9 fixed, in the toolkit's words

- **Drive health comes from the maker's thresholds.** The collector compared bare SMART values with
  50 and 80 as though they were percentages, and never read the threshold column. It now reads the
  drive's life attribute in a fixed order, makes crossing the maker's threshold its own Critical,
  and records `HealthSource`, `Breached` and `AttributesSeen` per drive. Matches CrystalDiskInfo
  (96%, same attribute) on a Crucial SATA SSD. NVMe wear is trusted on NVMe only.
- **The report stops calling a drive "Healthy" on no evidence.** A failing drive was Critical in
  the findings and *Healthy* in the machine table on the same page. The row now says *Failing*, a
  percentage, *No problems reported* (table read, nothing past threshold), Windows' own verdict
  saying that is what it is, or *Not checked*.
- **The backup verdict is reached once, after all the evidence is in.** It used to decide "no
  backup" before the file search ran - a false Critical on a healthy machine - and counted a
  Windows install stick's `boot.wim` and Hyper-V disks as backups. **`Backup.EvidenceFound` now
  means a backup 7 days old or less, without a schema bump.**
- **Email settings are checked after they are read.** The installer's CHANGE-ME guard ran before
  the settings file was loaded, so it never fired. New refusals: an address with no mail server, a
  login with no password, a Client install with no address (the file's address is never used for
  a Client install). New `-ValidateOnly $true`: check, report, change nothing, no admin needed.
- **The email's wording**: *"130 MB"* not *"0.13 GB"*, *"2 things need attention"*, and
  `last-email.txt` beside the run log holds exactly what was sent.
- A new technician diagnostic, `Debug-DriveHealth.ps1`, kept in `healthcheck\src` with the other
  `Debug-*` tools and, like them, **not** shipped to customer machines.

### How it was brought across

`Get-ClientHealthCheck.ps1`, `Invoke-ClientMaintenance.ps1` and `Debug-SfcScan.ps1` were untouched
here since the import, so they are the toolkit's v2.9 byte for byte. `New-ClientReport.ps1`,
`Invoke-MonthlyRun.ps1`, `Install-HealthCheck.ps1` and `DECISIONS.md` carry our changes, so each
was a three-way merge against the toolkit at the import commit (`314b979`). The report's change is
identical to the toolkit's, line for line. The installer had one conflict (both sides added
parameters: keep both).

**The platform needed no change.** The server reads only `Findings` and the maintenance `Tasks`,
neither of which moved; nothing in `src\` reads `EvidenceFound`, `HealthPercent` or `SmartDrives`.

### Where our installer departs from v2.9, on purpose

**The email check sits after the KEPT settings, not straight after the settings file.** The
toolkit has no "keep what is on this machine" step; we do (§50's agent reinstalls with
`-ExistingSettings Keep`). Placed where v2.9 put it, the check would have been v2.9's own fault in
a new place: a reinstall of a Client install that passes no address - the agent never passes one -
refused for having none, and a kept mail section counted as no mail server. It now runs after the
existing install is read, treating a carried Email section as the mail settings. `-ValidateOnly`
never asks the keep question; it reports what an unattended reinstall would do.

### Three faults found on the way, all fixed

- **A kept mail password failed its own round-trip check.** After a Keep reinstall `$SmtpPassword`
  is empty, so comparing the decrypted password with it failed - *after* `config.json` was written
  and *before* the task was registered. Latent: no platform machine stores a password. A kept one
  is now proved by decrypting at all.
- **The installer had no explicit success exit**, so its exit code was whatever its last native
  command returned - and `HealthCheckKeeper` takes that code as the verdict. It ends `exit 0`.
- **`tools\deploy-client-payload.ps1` staged five scripts, not six.** §50 made the installer refuse
  to run without `Uninstall-HealthCheck.ps1` beside it; `build.ps1` staged it and this did not,
  and **`ship-build.ps1` runs this one.** The next full ship would have put an installer on every
  customer machine that stopped at *"These files are missing"*. It also still staged Anywhere IT's
  logo, which `build.ps1` stopped doing on 2026-09-16 (§17); it now removes it. **Keep the two
  lists the same.**

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `Test-HealthCheckValidate.ps1` (new) | **21 of 21**, unelevated: the real installer with `-ValidateOnly $true` - the agent's exact parameters pass; no mail server, no client address, a mistyped address and CHANGE-ME from the file are refused and say why; the file's address never becomes a client's; a kept Client install passes; nothing on disk or in Task Scheduler changes. **17 of 21 against v2.9's own placement of the check** (`-Installer` points it at another copy). |
| `Test-HealthCheckReinstall.ps1` | 17 → **20**: its first install now has a mail server and login (v2.9 refuses an address without one), and the second must keep the encrypted password and exit 0. **Needs an elevated PowerShell, so NOT yet run.** |
| the collector | run on LAPTOP-C3U7E7S6, unelevated: exit 0, schema 1.3, the one collection error BitLocker's expected *access denied*. |
| the report | from that run: *Detailed wear figures could not be read on this check - No problems reported* (NVMe, unelevated). From a July sample with no `Breached` field: no drive marked failing. |
| unchanged | `healthcheckwire` **52 of 52**, `Test-HealthCheckUninstall` **8 of 8**; every script parses in PowerShell 5.1 and is plain ASCII. |

**Not proved anywhere:** v2.9's drive and backup verdicts on a customer's machine, elevated.
`TEST-3.6.md` section S, checks 125-128.

### To ship

**A FULL `ship-build.ps1`** - the scripts are in the client payload. **No platform restart, no
migration.** The scripts reach a machine only through a **client reinstall**, which copies
`healthcheck\` into Program Files - §50 already needs that one. After it, the agent notices the
installed scripts differ from the ones beside the app and re-installs the health check by itself,
on every machine that has it switched on.

## 52. Importing a client list from another program — 2026-09-28

Clint: *"One very important feature that we need to have is the ability to import clients from
another program."* Every IT company that switches to us has a client list somewhere else, and
retyping it is the first thing that would make them give up. His own came out of Xero, 878 rows.

**Where:** Clients → **Import clients** (`/portal/clients/import`). The owner, a supervisor or the
office administrator — `Permissions.CanImportClients`, asked again inside
`ClientImportService.ImportAsync`, so a technician posting the form by hand is refused by the
service and not only by a hidden button (§34). Download the template, upload a `.xlsx` or `.csv`,
see a preview, press Import.

**The format** is one row per contact person: **Client** (required), Contact person, Phone, Email,
Address, Notes. Rows naming the same client become ONE client with several contacts — that is how a
company with three people at it goes in without a second sheet. Headings are matched loosely
(`PhoneNumber`, `Email address`, `Company`, `Mobile`…; `ClientImport.Headings`), several columns may
feed one field (Phone and Mobile are joined with " / "), anything else is ignored and the preview
names it. **`ContactName` is deliberately NOT understood**: Xero means the company by it and most
people mean the person, so either reading files somebody's list wrongly.

The template is written by us (`Spreadsheet.WriteTemplate`) — bold frozen headings, a "How to fill
this in" second sheet, and **the Phone column formatted as Text**, so a number typed into it keeps
its leading zero. Opened in real Excel on this PC: no repair prompt, `0823483295` stays itself.

### Three rules, each a way an import quietly spoils the records it fills

1. **Nothing on file is overwritten.** A client already here (matched by name, case and spacing
   ignored, archived included) only has BLANK fields filled; a contact already on it likewise. The
   same file twice adds nothing the second time, and an old export cannot undo a number somebody
   corrected by hand. The preview says, per client, exactly which blanks it fills.
2. **Nothing is saved before the preview.** Plan and save are ONE walk (`RunAsync(save:)`), so the
   preview cannot describe something the save does not do, and the save plans again against the
   database as it is then. One `SaveChanges`: a thousand clients is one transaction. The parsed rows
   ride from preview to Import inside the form, sealed with Data Protection (two hours, tenant id
   inside) — nothing is held on the server between the two steps.
3. **Repairs are shown, never silent.** Each one is listed on its row in the preview.

### The repairs, and why each is safe

- **Garbled letters** (`Dr AndrÃ© Wiid`, `â€“`): UTF-8 that was read as Windows-1252 and saved.
  `RepairMojibake` turns the text back into Windows-1252 bytes and uses the result ONLY if those
  bytes are valid UTF-8 — correctly written "André" gives a lone 0xE9, which is not, so real text is
  never touched. Clint's file had four of these.
- **Phones, South Africa only** (`Tenant.IsSouthAfrica`), where every local number is 0 + nine
  digits, so the repair is certain: nine digits with no leading 0 get it back (Excel stores
  0823483295 as the NUMBER 823483295 — the reader keeps each cell's "was a number" flag for this);
  `27`, `+27` or Xero's `RSA 27` before nine digits becomes the local form. **The digit count is the
  safeguard** — `083 380 377` is a number with a digit missing and is left alone.
- **Everywhere:** Xero's `UK 44 7781 136389` becomes `+44 7781 136389`; a phone that is only
  country letters (`RSA`) is left blank. **A calling code never starts with 0, and what follows it
  must be at least six digits** — the first version read `RSA 382 1330`, a Knysna number with no
  code, as Montenegro's +382. The harness caught it on Clint's original file.

### Placeholder email addresses

Clint's export had `jason@anywhereit.co.za` on **157 clients** — the IT company's own address,
put in where the customer had none. His call: leave it out. The general rule: any address on
**three or more different clients** (`SharedEmailThreshold`; counted by CLIENT, so one company's
three people sharing the office address do not trip it) is listed in the preview, **ticked to be
left out**, and may be unticked. Left out means off the client AND its contacts.

### Proven

`tools/importcheck` — **98 of 98 given both of Clint's files** at first (115 after the one-value-per-field change below), the real reader, rules and service on a throwaway database with
the real migrations. Give it file paths and it imports each into its own throwaway company and prints
what happened. Clint's fixed list (`Copy of Clients 28 September 2026.xlsx`): **878 clients, 848
contacts, none left out, 21 repairs, nobody has the jason address, garbled letters none, imported
twice = nothing new.** His original list: 875 clients, 451 repairs, 12 phones left for a person.

Then in the browser, on a throwaway platform (`tools/workflowdemo` + `tools/portallink`, port 8195):
the real file uploaded through the real form, the preview, Import, and "morn" finding "Morné
Pienaar" on the Clients page. A technician gets the refusal and no button. It found one fault a
harness had not asked about: "Headings found: none" beside a file whose headings were Contact and
Phone — the message now lists every heading the row had.

**No migration.** A platform restart, nothing else — the portal is the platform. No ship, no
client reinstall. `TEST-3.6.md` section T.

### One value per field — the same day

Clint, looking at the preview: *"the email and contact numbers should be separate fields. In later
updates, we may want to email or text clients when stages change"* — then *"contact should also be
a separate field"* and *"the address field is missing"*.

They always were separate fields in the database (`Client.ContactName/Phone/Email/Address`,
`Contact.Phone/Email`). What was wrong was twofold, and the first half mattered:

1. **The import could put more than one value in a field.** A Phone and a Mobile column were joined
   as `082… / 044…`; two addresses in a cell as `a@x; b@y`; `082 891 9508 (Butch)` went in whole.
   Nothing can be texted or mailed from those. Now **Phone holds ONE number and Email ONE address**,
   and whatever did not fit goes to **Notes word for word** — `Phone as written: 082 891 9508
   (Butch)`, `Other number: …`, `Other email: …`, `Email as written: bob at acme` (an email that is
   not one no longer sits in Email). `ClientImport.SplitPhone`, `SplitEmails`. **The guard**: the
   number is lifted out only when the words around it have no digits of their own, so `1 USA 407
   252 7159` stays whole rather than losing its country code.
2. **The pages showed them run together.** The preview had one "Contact · phone · email" column and
   no address; the Clients list put the email under the name, squeezed beside the Add form so
   addresses broke every few letters; the client page ran them into one line. Now: the preview has
   a column each (Contact person, Phone, Email, Address) with the import's notes on a line under the
   row; the Clients list has the full width with the same four columns and **Add a client folds away
   above it** (open when there are no clients); the client page labels each one.

`importcheck` **115 of 115** with both files (19 new checks for the splitting). On Clint's original
list, the phones not in the plain `0xx xxx xxxx` shape fell from 12 to 7, and every one of the seven
is a foreign number or a genuinely wrong one, kept as written.

## 53. Toolkit v2.11, and the health check install that keeps trying — 2026-09-29

Two things in one session, both about the monthly health check. Clint: *"We have made more changes
to the healthchecker, lets update the system accordingly. Can you also confirm the delays are built
in for the eset approval."* **They were not** - bug 9 had been diagnosed and its fix designed on
2026-09-28, and marked *not yet built*. It is built now.

### The toolkit, v2.9 to v2.11

Same method as §51, against the toolkit at `36d759a` (the v2.9 last synced); now synced to
`fe58b93`. Six scripts untouched here were copied; `New-ClientReport.ps1`, `Invoke-MonthlyRun.ps1`,
`Install-HealthCheck.ps1` and `DECISIONS.md` were three-way merged.

- **The report is one section per machine** (v2.11): page one a summary and a roster of the
  client's machines, then each machine on its own page - its problems, its maintenance, what was
  healthy, what was measured. **Client names match forgivingly** ("Zenith Motors" and "zenith
  motors." are one client), the month is chosen per client, and the PDF no longer prints Edge's
  header and footer - which carried a temp path and the Windows username on every page.
- **The pending-restart finding is in plain words.** Its `Detail` no longer lists Windows' internal
  reasons; `Updates.RebootReasons` still has them. Nothing here parses finding text.
- **Nothing the platform relies on moved**: no script parameter changed, the monthly run still finds
  the report by extension in its own `Reports` folder, and the server builds no report itself.
- The merge of the 559-line report rewrite was clean, and checked rather than trusted: **all 131
  lines we had added are present, none we had removed came back**, and the rewrite added no
  hard-coded branding.
- **One conflict, resolved for this product**: v2.11 changed the installer's closing lines to point
  at `START HERE.bat` options 4 and 5. That menu is the standalone kit's and is never on a customer
  machine, so ours says where a platform install's results go, and how it is removed.

**Rendered and looked at, as the toolkit's v2.11 notes insist** - its five v2.11 faults were visible
only on the printed page. Two machines under two spellings of one client gave one report: five
pages, the roster, a section per machine, the drive row *No problems reported* with the honest
wording, `°C` not `&deg;`. **The first rendering carried Anywhere IT's logo on a report branded
"Test IT Solutions"** - which is the fault §17 fixed. It was the test, not the code: run from the
repo, the report builder's logo search finds `healthcheck\templates\logo.png` one folder up. From a
folder laid out like an install it prints the company name as text, as it must. On a customer
machine nothing can be found: the payload carries no `templates\` and the installer deletes any
`logo.*`. **Anyone checking branding by running the report from the repo will see this and should
not believe it.**

One toolkit wording slip to fix upstream, not here: *"1 days ago"* under Last security update.

### Bug 9: an antivirus holds the install, and nothing ever tried again

The design in `BUGS.md`, built, in two places. **Changes the AGENT and the CONSOLE.**

**The agent keeps trying.** `HealthCheckKeeper.ApplyWithRetriesAsync`: at once, then after **1, 5
and 15 minutes** - four attempts over about 21 minutes. ESET's hold is about a minute; the later
tries cover a slower cloud answer and cost nothing when nothing is wrong.

- **Every failure is reported before the wait, with when the next try is** - *"could not install it
  (exit 1) - trying again in 5 minutes (antivirus often holds new files for a minute)"*. The last
  says it tried four times, where the log is, and that choosing it again in the console tries now.
- **A newer answer ends the wait at once and ends the old retries.** The trap bug 9 named: a
  machine switched OFF during a five-minute wait must not be installed at the end of it. `Want`
  releases `_arrived`; the waiting pass wakes, sees `_pending`, and stops without reporting - the
  newer answer has its own pass queued behind it. The same answer counts as newer, which is what
  makes "On" again mean "try now".
- **What is worth retrying:** an install that did not leave our task in place with current scripts,
  whatever the exit code (a hold looks like anything - an unreadable file, a script stopping half
  way, a timeout), and a removal that left the task. **Not** retried: scripts missing beside the app
  (waiting does not put them there), and somebody else's health check (not a failure).
- **One behaviour change on the way:** an install is now "installed" only if the scripts are also
  current (`!Stale()`), not merely the task present. A refresh that ESET cut short used to report
  *installed* over an old copy; it now reports *could not bring it up to date* and retries.

**The console lets you retry.** `HealthCheckModes.WorthSending` (Shared, so it is testable): a
different choice is always sent, and **the same choice is sent when the machine has not done it** -
wanted and not installed, or installed and not wanted. Before, choosing On again after a failure
did nothing, and the only retry was Off then On, which runs the removal first on a machine whose
files are held. No new control - the menu item that says what you want is the one that retries it.
The hub always passed a repeated choice through; only the console's guard stopped it. **The
portal's per-machine dropdown still cannot retry** (a select only posts on a change); the console
can, which is enough.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `keeperretry` (new) | **31 of 31**, the REAL `Want` -> retry -> report path with a scripted attempt and millisecond delays: ESET's shape (held twice, then installs - three attempts, each failure saying a retry is coming); the same machine with no delays ends failed, which is bug 9; held for good gives up after four with the log and how to retry; missing scripts tried once; **switched OFF mid-wait: the Off is acted on within milliseconds and the old On never tried again**; On again mid-wait tries at once; a leftover wake-up does not shorten a wait. Then `WorthSending` in every case that matters, including that the old rule refused the retry. |
| toolkit v2.11 | every script parses in 5.1 and is ASCII; the collector ran clean on LAPTOP-C3U7E7S6; a two-machine PDF rendered to page images and read. |
| unchanged | `Test-HealthCheckValidate` 21, `Test-HealthCheckUninstall` 8, `healthcheckwire` 52, `dashtabs` 79. |

**Not proved anywhere:** a real ESET hold. The retry is proved on a scripted attempt; whether
ESET's hold is on the scripts at all - Clint saw it name `host.exe`, which the keeper never runs -
is still bug 9's open question, and `healthcheck-agent.log` from that machine answers it. If it is
`host.exe`, that is a separate problem for sessions that this does not touch.

### To ship

**A full `ship-build.ps1`** (agent, console and payload scripts all changed) **and a client
reinstall** on each machine. **No platform restart, no migration** - the hub and protocol messages
are unchanged; `WorthSending` is only called by the console. `TEST-3.6.md` section U, checks
136-140.

## 54. Internal testing: the host crashed on every secure desktop, and a paste gave the old files — 2026-09-29

Clint, during internal testing: *"Control Alt Delete and Copy and paste dont seem to be working on
the gaming laptop... if i copy folders from this laptop to the test machine it works fine, but if i
try copy different folders from the test machine in the same session, it pastes the original files
and folders that i had copied across."* The gaming laptop is **DESKTOP-2N6FVGT**, the test machine
**DESKTOP-OPHQIDH**; DESKTOP-STD8M9C is the newly added internal-testing machine and was not touched.

Two real faults, one on each end, and neither was where it looked.

### Ctrl+Alt+Del worked. The HOST then crashed, every time

Measured first, with `sysactioncheck --observe` (new): a script under the host watches the input
desktop while Ctrl+Alt+Del is sent. On 2N6FVGT it went `Default` → READY → `Winlogon` 1.4 s after
the send — **the policy, the agent and SendSAS were all fine** (policy = 1, agent running). Then the
session ended under us, and `tools/hostinfo/hostcrash.ps1` (new) read Windows' own record of why:

```
RemoteSupport.Host.exe  0xc0000409  ntdll.dll  fault offset 0x8cc4f  subcode 0xa
```

A fast-fail from Control Flow Guard — an indirect call to an invalid target, native, no .NET
exception. Five identical records in an hour: 10:26 (AnthonyTest's session, **a UAC prompt, not
Ctrl+Alt+Del** — nobody but me pressed that button today, per the tickets), then 10:27, 10:29,
10:36, 10:37 (mine). Every one two to four seconds after a switch to the Winlogon desktop, and the
hub records each as `Client disconnected`, which is the HOST's socket going.

**The cause.** A desktop switch costs Desktop Duplication an ACCESS_LOST; `DxgiCapture.Drop`
disposes the output **including its Direct3D device**, and `Create` makes a new one. The H.264
encoder was built on the old device, and `CheckSourceHealth` only called `_encoder.Reset()` — so
the next frame handed a **hardware** encoder a texture from a device it had never seen. Intel Quick
Sync does not throw at that; it takes the process down. **2N6FVGT is the only machine here that
encodes with Quick Sync**; OPHQIDH has no usable encoder and runs on JPEG tiles, which is the whole
reason it never crashed. The idle-release path ten lines above already said *"the encoder goes
first and it is not optional"*. The rebuild path never got the same rule.

**It was never only Ctrl+Alt+Del.** UAC, the lock screen and Ctrl+Alt+Del are all the Winlogon
desktop. On any machine with a working hardware encoder, a session died at the first UAC prompt.

### The fix, and the two things proving it found

- `DropEncoder` — on a rebuild the encoder is **disposed and rebuilt on the new device**, not
  flushed. And a guard in `SendVideo`: **an encoder only ever sees textures from the device it was
  built on** (`_encoderDevice`). The old device is kept alive by the encoder's own reference, so the
  address comparison cannot be fooled by reuse. That also covers a monitor-geometry change, which
  makes a new device without counting a rebuild.
- **Rebuilding exposed a timing refusal.** The encoder is rebuilt on the pass after the duplication
  broke, which can be before the capture thread has followed the user onto the new desktop, and
  Windows refuses a duplication asked for from the desktop that has gone. Without a retry, **five
  sessions of five** then ran on JPEG tiles for the rest of their life. A rebuild now allows five
  retries 750 ms apart before the fall-back is a verdict.
- **The Info tab lied after every UAC prompt.** `SetCodec` stays silent when the codec's name has
  not changed, and a rebuild is H.264 → H.264 — but the report sent while there was no encoder said
  "JPEG tiles". The trace showed H.264 throughout while the console said tiles. A rebuilt encoder
  now always reports itself.

Proved on 2N6FVGT with the new host swapped in (`pushfile` + `swaphost.ps1`; three
`RemoteSupport.Host.old-*.exe` are kept in its install folder):

| | old host | new host |
|---|---|---|
| `sysactioncheck --observe`: the security screen really comes up | yes | yes, 5 of 5 |
| the host survives the trip there and back | **0 of 4**, a crash record each time | **5 of 5**, no crash record since the swap |
| the picture is H.264 again afterwards | — | **5 of 5** (0 of 3 before the retry) |
| `codeccheck DESKTOP-2N6FVGT` | | **11 of 11** |

The control, OPHQIDH, passes on its unchanged host. `sysactioncheck --observe` subscribes to the
picture itself, offering H.264, because its first version did not — and "passed" only because
Clint's console happened to be driving the encoder in the same session (see the traps below).

### Copy and paste: the host was right; the CONSOLE kept the old files

`tools/recopy` (new) does Clint's exact sequence in one session: the technician pastes folder A in,
then the person at the machine — as themselves, through the shell's Copy verb — copies B, then C,
then B and C together. **5 of 5 on OPHQIDH and on 2N6FVGT**: every copy reached the technician with
the right paths, and A was never offered back. Clint's console, which joined that session, fetched
B, C and B+C onto his clipboard correctly (his trace).

So the stale paste is on this side. When the customer copies something **over 50 MB**
(`AutoFetchBytes`, §26), the console offers it on the status bar and **leaves the technician's
clipboard untouched** — and Ctrl+V pastes whatever the technician copied last, which is the folder
they have just sent across. Clint's clipboard held 3 files, 68 MB, at the time. A small copy has the
same gap for as long as the fetch is in flight.

The fix is one call: `ForgetMyClipboardForTheirs` empties the technician's clipboard **the moment
their copy is announced**. Nothing to paste is honest; the wrong files are not. The threshold is
untouched — the delayed-rendering data object is still the right answer eventually (§26).

**`pullcheck` could never have seen this: it emptied the clipboard before every step**, which is
exactly the state in which the fault cannot happen. It now puts the technician's own file on the
clipboard for two new steps — a big set, and a small one held mid-fetch by a gate in the fake host.
**11 of 11; 9 of 11 with the one line removed, and the two failures are Clint's report word for
word:** *"Ctrl+V would paste 'the technician's own.txt'"*.

On 2N6FVGT itself: `usercopy` 3 of 3, `recopy` 5 of 5, `userpaste` 4 of 4 (its first run said 0 of
4 because the user-side task did not start inside its window — its own first check said so; the
second run passed everything).

### Found, not fixed — BUGS #10

2N6FVGT had clipboard sequence **0** all morning: nothing copied since boot. The host's watcher
waits out a zero and then takes the first non-zero value as its baseline, so **the first copy after
a fresh logon is never sent**. It touches the §26 privacy gate and cannot be reproduced until that
machine restarts, so it is written up rather than fixed blind.

### Traps that cost time here

- **The console joins every session started under its own account** — harness sessions included —
  and on coming to the front sends its clipboard. A `recopy` run replaced Clint's clipboard (his
  68 MB copy is gone) and put test folders in his Downloads; `pullcheck`'s leftovers were then
  pushed into three harness sessions. **Empty this laptop's clipboard before running harnesses while
  the console is open**, or close the console.
- **This shell runs inside the Claude app's package sandbox, which virtualises `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.**
  The console trace it shows stops at the sandbox's copy; the real one is
  `\\localhost\C$\Users\Clint\AppData\Local\TheRemoteSupportProgram\technician-trace.log`.
- **Internal testers share the machines** (AnthonyTest, RyanTest, JasonTest). A session in a trace
  is not Clint's until the `Sessions` table says so; the tickets say who pressed what.
- **`runscript` prefers the copy of a script beside its own exe**, which is stale after an edit.
  Pass `tools/hostinfo/<name>.ps1` as a path when the script has just changed.
- **The agent's Information logs never reach the Event Log** (Warning is the default filter), so
  "the agent sent Ctrl+Alt+Del" leaves no record on the machine. The ticket line is the record.

### To ship

**A full `ship-build.ps1`** (the HOST and the CONSOLE both changed) **and a client reinstall** on
each machine — 2N6FVGT already runs this host. **No platform restart, no migration.**
`TEST-3.6.md` section V, checks 141–146.

## 55. Roles are tick boxes — 2026-09-29 (roadmap 3.6.8)

Clint asked for roadmap items 1–3 to be built, most relevant first; this is item 3, done first
because seat pricing (4.7) and payments (4.8) both stand on it. A person used to hold ONE role, so
a one-man shop had to call itself the owner, and "technician and office administrator but not
owner" could not be said at all. Now the People page has four boxes — **Owner, Supervisor,
Technician, Office administrator** — and a person may do the UNION of what theirs allow.

### What changed, and what did not

- **`TenantRole` is `[Flags]`**: Technician 1, Admin (supervisor) 2, Billing (office) 4, Owner 8.
  `OwnerSupervisor` survives as the NAME for Owner | Admin. The old names stay so the ~200 call
  sites and harnesses kept compiling; §34's rule is what made that possible — **nothing compared a
  role, every page asked `Permissions`**, and only `Permissions.cs` changed its answers
  (`role.Has(...)`, i.e. ANY box).
- **Seats**: a person takes a seat if Technician OR Supervisor is ticked — once, however many
  boxes. Owner alone and Office administrator alone are still seat-free. Owner + Technician is one
  seat and opens the console.
- **The owner** stays exactly one person; their Owner box is shown locked and posted hidden, and
  only they may change their own row. `SetOwnerAsync` now ADDS the Owner box to the new owner
  (keeping every box they had) and turns the old owner into a supervisor.
- **At least one box**, refused in the service (`AddTechnicianAsync`, `SetRoleAsync`), and in the
  page's own script before it posts.
- `add-tech` on the command line takes `--technician --admin --billing --owner`, combinable.

### The three traps

1. **The numbers changed, so the migration renumbers** (`RolesAsTickBoxes`, no schema change):
   0→1, 1→2, 2→4, 3→8, 4→10, in ONE `CASE` — a chain of `UPDATE`s would carry 1 to 2 and the new 2
   on to 4.
2. **The cookie carried the old number, and the old fallback was "administrator".** An old cookie's
   1 (supervisor) would now read as a technician, and its 0 as nothing at all — which the old code
   turned into Admin. The claim is renamed (`tenantRoles`); an old `tenantRole` is translated by
   the OLD numbers (`PortalIdentity.FromOldNumber`); a cookie with neither is read from the ASP.NET
   roles it was issued with; anything unreadable is the LEAST. **Never guess upward.**
3. **`TenantRoles.Seated.Contains(t.Role)` in a query compares the whole number** and silently
   misses every combination. `Seated`/`Owners` are MASKS now and queries say
   `(t.Role & TenantRoles.Seated) != 0` (EF translates the `&` for SQLite). They are no longer
   arrays, so any old `Contains` fails to compile rather than quietly lying.

And one in the harness: `rolecheck` seeded an old table with `(int)TenantRole.Admin`, which after
this is 2 — an office administrator in the old numbering. It seeds the literal old numbers now.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `rolecheck` | **72 of 72** (was 37): the union, seats counted by box in memory AND in the database, no box refused, a non-box number refused, hand-over keeps boxes, the page's `Parse`, and seven cookie cases. **67 of 72 with two old lines put back** (`== Billing` in `CanSeeAllTickets`, the Admin fallback). |
| `handoffcheck` | **45 of 45** — its "old cookie is an administrator" check now gives the cookie the role it really carried, plus one that a cookie saying nothing is NOT an administrator. |
| unchanged | `ticketscope` 27, `workflowcheck` 100, `photogate` 38, `assigncheck` 49, `quotecheck` 54, `routecheck` 53, `calloutcheck` 52, `mentioncheck` 27, `importcheck` 107 (0 failed), `ticketpersession` 30, `devicelink` 19. |
| in the browser | On a throwaway platform (`workflowdemo`, port 8195): ticking Office administrator beside Technician saved and kept the seat count; an empty row was refused and nothing changed; a person added with two boxes took one seat; that person saw all 12 tickets and the office's menu, and the People page refused them; the owner ticking Technician took a seat (4 → 5 of 7). |

**The picture found one thing the harnesses could not**: the boxes squeezed the Add card to a
sliver. The People page now gives the card 300 px and the table the rest (`.grid2.people-grid`,
wide screens only), and the reset/remove cell wraps.

### Deploying it

**Platform restart** (migration `RolesAsTickBoxes`). No console or client change — the console
only ever received `isAdmin`. Existing portal sign-ins keep working through the old-claim
translation. `TEST-3.6.md` section W.

## 56. Every clipboard movement reaches the ticket — 2026-09-29 (roadmap 3.5.3)

Roadmap item 2 of the three Clint asked for. **3.5.3 was already built** — inside 3.5.1 on
2026-09-18 (§26, "On the ticket, without burying it"): clipboard TEXT is a `clip-text`
`FileActivityMsg`, a count of characters and never the characters, coalesced per direction per
minute; clipboard FILES are logged by the file-set transfer that moves them. The roadmap was never
told. **But no harness had ever checked that any of it reached a ticket**, and reading the code
for one found that most of it did not.

### Two faults, one on each end

1. **The host only noticed the minute when ANOTHER copy arrived.** The ledger flushed inside
   `NoteClipText`, and only when a movement came 60 s or more after the period began. A session
   with one burst of copies and nothing after it reported nothing while it ran, and its
   end-of-session flush was called after `RunAsync` returned — after the socket had closed.
2. **The server forgot the session's ticket the moment the session ended**, then closed the host
   straight after telling it. So even a host that answered "ended" with its last line was racing
   `_sessionTickets.Remove`, and over any real network it lost.

`tools/clipledger`'s first run passed against fault 2, 20 of 20: **on loopback the fake host's
reply beat the server to the end of `EndSession`.** With 150 ms of reply delay — a machine a
network away — it failed, 18 of 20, and that is the version kept (`ReplyDelayMs`). A harness
about a race that runs on loopback proves nothing about the race.

### The fix

- **`ClipLedger`** (`RemoteSupport.Shared`), out of `HostEngine` so it can be tested: a timer
  reports the minute whether or not anything else happens, the period starts at the first
  movement it covers (a steady trickle cannot postpone it), a refusal is its own line at once, and
  `Flush()` reports what is held now.
- **The host handles `SessionEndedMsg`**: it flushes, then closes its own socket (`CloseAsync`
  drains the send queue first), and after `RunAsync` it waits for that close to finish.
- **The server lets the host say its last**: `EndSession` keeps the ticket on the session
  (`Session.EndedTicketId`), tells the host, and closes it only after `HostLastWords` (3 s) if it
  has not closed itself — an older host that ignores the message costs three seconds, nothing
  more. **"Session ended" is written after the host has gone**, so the ticket reads in order.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/clipledger` (new) | **20 of 20.** Eleven on `ClipLedger` in-process (a one-second period): one copy reported on its own, a burst as one line per direction, Flush, refusals, a trickle. Nine over the wire against its own platform on port 8098 with a fake machine: a mid-session line on the ticket and in the tray, the host's LAST line on the ticket and above "Session ended", and an old host still closed. **18 of 20 against the server before the fix.** |
| `reconnectlocal` | 20 of 20 — its fake host now closes itself on `SessionEndedMsg` as the real one does; before that it was the old host and "closed within 2 s" failed by the 3 s allowance. |
| `ticketpersession` | 30 of 30. |
| `clipcheck --ledger` (new option) | After its usual checks it makes one copy onto the machine and waits 75 s with nothing moving; a `clip-text` line must arrive by itself. **Against the OLD host on DESKTOP-OPHQIDH it failed, as it should**: a line at 10:26:52 (pushed out by a later copy), then nothing for the copy at 10:27:28. |

**On hardware: the new host is on DESKTOP-OPHQIDH** (swapped in 12:23 with a copy of `swaphost.ps1`
carrying its hash; the old one kept as `RemoteSupport.Host.old-20260929-122319.exe`) **but has
not served a session yet** — the session `pushfile` opened was held open by a joined console, and
every harness since joined it and its old host. `pushfile` never ends its session; the tools
deliberately never end one they joined. The run that counts is `clipcheck DESKTOP-OPHQIDH
--ledger` on a fresh session.

### Deploying it

**Platform restart** for the server half, and a **full ship** for the host half (a client
reinstall is how every machine gets the new host). Either half alone is an improvement: the new
host with the old server reports every minute and can still lose the last minute's line; the new
server with an old host changes nothing but waits 3 s before closing it. `TEST-3.6.md` section X.

## 57. Exit in the tray app takes the machine offline — 2026-09-29

Clint: *"even if exit is selected on the client tray app, technicians can still connect to the
machine. this needs to be rectified. It should close the program completely and show as offline on
the dashboard and console"*, and then *"Selecting the shortcut should then put the tray app back in
session."*

### Why it happened

Exit only ever closed the tray app. On a machine with unattended access allowed, the AGENT service
— a separate SYSTEM process — stayed connected, `StartSession` handed sessions to it exactly as §31
designed, and the dot is `Online`, which the agent alone keeps true. On a machine WITHOUT unattended
access Exit already worked, because the tray app was the only host. So the report was true of
precisely the machines where it matters most.

### What Exit means now

- The tray app sends **`ClientClosingMsg`** and closes once it has gone (`DeviceLink.SayClosingAsync`
  — sent FIRST, the reconnect loop cancelled after; cancelling first tore the socket down before
  the message could leave).
- The server (`CloseByUserAsync`) puts the machine in **`_closedByUser`**, stores
  **`Device.ClosedByUserUtc`** (migration `DeviceClosedByUser`), ends any session on it with *"The
  person at X closed the support app."*, cancels a ringing request, and tells every console.
- **`Recompute`** is now the ONE place `Online` and `Unattended` are worked out; a closed machine is
  neither, on the console and in the portal (both read `Online`). **`AgentOnline` stays true** —
  the agent really is connected, and the health check menu and `tools/agentcheck` rely on that
  being said honestly. The monthly health check keeps working.
- `StartSession` refuses a closed machine by every route, and a technician who tries is told
  *"The person at that machine closed the support app… It comes back when they open it again, from
  the desktop shortcut or by signing in to Windows."*
- **Only a CLIENT connection may close a machine**, as with `SetUnattendedMsg`: an agent sending it
  is logged and ignored.
- **The tray app saying hello again reopens it** — the shortcut, or the next logon's autostart —
  in memory at once and in the database in `PersistDeviceAsync`. The agent reconnecting never does,
  which is why the flag is stored: a server restart would otherwise bring every closed machine back.

A crash, a shutdown or a logoff says nothing, so they change nothing: the agent stays reachable,
which is what unattended access is for. Only the menu's Exit closes a machine.

**Known gap:** Exit with no connection to the server (it is down, or the machine is offline) cannot
be told to anyone, and when the agent reconnects the machine is reachable again. Closing that would
need the agent to hold the fact locally; not done.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/trayexit` (new) | **16 of 16**, its own platform on port 8097, a pretend machine with BOTH connections and unattended ticked. The fault first: the tray app simply vanishing leaves it online and a technician gets in through the agent. Then Exit: offline, agent still honestly connected, the running session ended with the reason, a connection refused with the reason, stored; after a server RESTART with the agent back, still offline and refused; the tray app reconnecting brings it back online, clears the database, and a technician gets in; an agent sending the message is ignored. **13 of 16 with the refusal in `StartSession` removed.** |

Also rerun: `unattendedwire`, `unattendedcheck`, `devicelink`, `healthcheckwire`, `clipledger`,
`reconnectlocal`, `ticketpersession` — see the commit.

### Deploying it

**Platform restart** (migration `DeviceClosedByUser`) and a **full ship** — the tray app is the
CLIENT, so every machine needs the reinstall before its Exit says anything. No console change: the
console already shows `Online`. `TEST-3.6.md` section Y.

## 58. Dragging files off the picture — 2026-09-29 (roadmap 3.5.2)

Roadmap item 1 of the three Clint asked for, built in the same batch as §55–§57 so that one
rebuild and one restart carries all of it — his staff are testing the rest meanwhile.

### The gesture

A drag on the picture of their screen is a drag on THEIR screen and is forwarded as one. When the
pointer leaves the session window with the left button still held:

1. **The console already asked**, at the first movement past the drag threshold
   (`OnRemoteDragStarted` → `SelectionRequestMsg`), what the person has selected in the folder
   window in front of them. The host answers (`SelectionMsg`) from a copy of itself running as
   that person — `--get-selection`, the same pattern as §40's `--get-files`, because from SYSTEM
   Explorer's windows are not there at all.
2. **If the answer names files** — Clint's 2026-09-18 rule, *the foreground Explorer selection and
   only that* — the console cancels their drag (Escape down and up, then the left button released
   where it last was: `ScreenView.CancelRemoteDrag`) and starts a drag HERE from those paths, through
   the Files window's own `BeginDragOut` (fetch first, then drag; let go early and they land on the
   clipboard). Nothing more of that gesture reaches their screen.
3. **If it does not**, their drag is left ALONE and the status bar says why in their machine's
   words — *"Nothing to drag here: nothing is selected in "Documents" — click the files there first,
   then drag"*, or *the window in front over there is "Word", not a folder*. Overshooting the edge
   while moving one of their windows must not be cancelled on a guess.
4. **No answer in 3 s**: their drag is left alone and the status bar points at Tools → Files.

Text dropped ONTO the picture goes onto their clipboard with *"on X's clipboard — Ctrl+V to place
it"*, the answer 3.5.0 chose for that one cell (Unicode first: the plain Text format turns "café"
into "caf?"). And the picture refuses our own drag-out as it passes back over it — it would
otherwise send their files straight back to their desktop.

### Where things are

- `Host/ExplorerSelection.cs` — the reader. The window "in front" is the foreground window, or when
  that is ours or the taskbar the first real window below it. `CabinetWClass` is Explorer;
  `Progman`/`WorkerW` is the desktop, read through `IShellWindows.FindWindowSW(SWC_DESKTOP)`.
  **Windows 11 tabs share one window handle**; the tab on screen is the one whose
  `IShellBrowser.GetWindow` is visible. `::{CLSID}` items (This PC, Control Panel) are left out.
- `ScreenView` — `OnRemoteDragStarted`, `OnDragOffPicture`, `CancelRemoteDrag`, and
  **`ButtonsNow`**, the one place the button state is read so a harness can stand in for it. After
  a takeover the shell's drag loop eats the release, so the view notices the button is up by
  itself rather than waiting for a MouseUp that never comes.
- `SessionForm.PictureDragLeft`, `DroppedText`; `BeginDragOut(paths, source)` now serves both.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/dragselcheck` (new) | **11 of 11** on this laptop, as the person: an Explorer window opened on a throwaway folder, items selected through Explorer's own automation, and exactly those read back — `café.txt` and a folder, not the unselected file; nothing selected said in words; the desktop read as the desktop; the taskbar refused as "not a folder"; the helper's JSON read back. |
| `tools/dragoffcheck` (new) | **21 of 21**, the REAL `SessionForm` with no server and synthetic mouse events: a click asks nothing; a drag inside stays theirs; off the picture with files, Escape then the release at the last point, the fetch starts here, and nothing more goes to their screen until the button is up; with nothing selected, their drag is untouched and the reason is shown; no answer waits 3 s and says what to do; text drops; our own drag refused on the way back. **15 of 21 with the cancel moved before the answer is checked** — the "cancel on a guess" mistake. |
| unchanged | `dragoutcheck` 43, `toolbarprobe` 37. |

**Not proved here, and only a person at a machine can:** a real drag across the edge (the OLE drag
loop cannot run without a real button held), **Windows 11 tabs** (they cannot be opened
programmatically), and the helper started from SYSTEM on a customer machine — the same
`UserProcess` path §39 and §40 proved, with a new argument. `TEST-3.6.md` section Z.

### Deploying it

**Full ship and client reinstall** (the HOST changes) **and `-OnlyTechnician` is not enough** for
the same reason. No platform change, no migration.

## 59. Quote requests: the machine, suppliers, BCC and the delivery fee — 2026-09-29

Clint: *"When doing a quote request, the fields are Item, Part Number, Serial Number, and photo.
Can we add fields for Computer or Laptop type plus its serial number ... a quote is needed for a
battery replacement, the quote would ask for the battery replacement for an Asus vivo book 123,
with SN123 ... We also need to be able to add suppliers much like the adding items ... select
multiple suppliers at once ... all the email addresses in bcc rather than the to box ... there
should be a drop down menu where one can select the item."* Then his answers: **one machine per
quote, optional** (parts not for any machine must still be quotable); **all three types** (Desktop,
Laptop, All-in-one) plus make, model and serial; **a supplier setup in the portal, per tenant** —
the company's own To address (Anywhere IT's is accounts@anywhereit.co.za) and **a delivery address,
with every request asking what the delivery fee would be**; supplier records hold name, email,
contact person and phone.

### What was built

- **The machine, once per quote** — `Ticket.QuoteMachine*`, `QuoteService.MachineOf`, `SetMachineAsync`.
  Until somebody saves it, a **workshop** job's quote is for the machine it was booked in with
  (`AssetMake/Model/Serial`; the booking has no type). **Once saved, what was saved is the answer,
  blanks included** (`QuoteMachineSaved`) — otherwise emptying it to say "these parts are not for a
  machine" would let the booking creep back. Edited where the lines are (`MayEditLines`), above the
  items, in the portal's `_QuoteLines` and the console's `MachineEditor` (new `QuoteMachineMsg`;
  `TicketDetail.QuoteMachine` and `MachineTypes` come from the server). What is typed in the console
  survives a redraw through `_drafts` until Save.
- **The request's words** (`QuoteRequestText`): the machine on its own line before the items, the
  make and model in the subject, and always *"Please include the delivery fee"* — *", for delivery
  to:"* and the address when one is set.
- **Suppliers** — `Supplier` table, `/portal/suppliers` (next to Items in the menu), and an **Add a
  supplier** inside Request quote so nobody leaves the ticket for a new one. The item list's guard:
  same words in any order are the same supplier, **one address is never two suppliers**, a
  resembling name gets "did you mean". Removing keeps the row (`RemovedUtc`). Everybody may read the
  list; `Permissions.CanEditSuppliers` (the people who request quotes) changes it and the settings.
- **To and BCC** — `QuoteService.Addressing`, the ONE rule: one supplier → To; several → every one in
  **Bcc**, the company's own address in **To** (`Tenant.QuoteToAddress`, else `SupportEmail`). The
  `.eml` gains a Bcc header only when there is one; Gmail and Outlook on the web get `&bcc=`.
  `StageInput.SupplierEmail` now carries one address or several joined by ", "; `QuoteSupplierNames`
  holds who, for the timeline and the console's facts.
- **The Item box is a dropdown** — `QuoteService.BrowseAsync`: nothing typed is the whole list, by
  name; typing narrows it as before. The portal opens it on click or focus and closes it on blur; the
  console on click or the down arrow. `SuggestAsync` is untouched, so "nothing typed suggests
  nothing" still holds for anything else that asks it.

### Found on the way

- **The §44 trap again, on a new table.** `workflowcheck`, `rolecheck`, `calloutcheck` and `contactcheck` added their
  TENANT through today's model before migrating, so the day Tenants gained two columns all four
  threw. Their tickets were already written by SQL; now the tenant is too, through
  `tools/Common/OldRows.cs` (`Seed.OldTenant`). **Any harness that seeds before a migration must
  seed every table that way, not just the one it is testing.**
- The console's suggestion list came back after a pick (the pick's own TextChanged asked again).
  The debounce now skips while an item is picked.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `quotecheck` | 54 → **108 of 108**: the machine (booking default, three types, tidying, who may, emptying sticks, nothing written for no change), the words (machine, subject, delivery with and without an address), suppliers (who may, duplicates by words and by address, did you mean, rename clash, removal, other company), **To/BCC** (one, several, the support-address fallback, the `.eml` headers, header injection through BCC, both web mail links), several suppliers through `ActAsync` and into the timeline and facts, and the dropdown. **103 with the BCC rule reverted to "everyone in To".** |
| `ticketwire` | 28 → **31**: the whole list over the hub on an empty term, the machine refused to a colleague, saved and carried back in the detail. |
| `ticketwindowprobe` | 123 → **128**: the machine from the booking, the three types, above the items with its own Save, the boxes in the card, a draft surviving a redraw. |
| `workflowcheck` 100, `rolecheck` 72, `calloutcheck` 52, `contactcheck` 34 | passing again after the seeding fix (`contactcheck` was fixed in the follow-up commit — it was not run the first time). |
| unchanged | `routecheck` 53, `handoffcheck` 45, `assigncheck` 49, `ticketformprobe` 91, `photogate` 38, `mentioncheck` 27, `themecheck` 40. |

**Walked in the browser** on a `workflowdemo` platform (8095) as the supervisor: settings saved, two

### Deploying it

## 60. The privacy screen — 2026-09-29 (roadmap 1.7)

Clint asked for roadmap items 4 and 5 of the "build now" list: the privacy screen and session
recording. His choices for this one: **black, with one line naming the IT company.**

### How it works

`Host/PrivacyScreen.cs` puts one black window on every monitor — topmost, click-through
(`WS_EX_LAYERED | WS_EX_TRANSPARENT`, fully opaque), never activating — and marks each
**`WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`** (Windows 10 2004 and later). It is on the customer's screen and NOT in
any capture of it, so the technician's picture is unaffected and their clicks reach what is
underneath. Nothing is installed and nothing about the display changes; the windows belong to the
host, so a host that dies can never leave a machine black. A timer re-asserts topmost every 500 ms,
because a topmost window opened later would otherwise show through.

- **It refuses rather than half-works.** If `SetWindowDisplayAffinity` fails, the technician would
  be blacked out too, so `Show` takes everything down and says why; the console shows the reason
  and the ticket records it. The roadmap's warning was the design: *a technician believing the
  screen is private when it is not.* The console's menu tick follows `PrivacyStateMsg` from the
  host — what the screen IS doing — never the click.
- **Raw Win32 on its own thread, per-monitor DPI aware**, so each monitor is measured and covered in
  real pixels. The host declares no DPI awareness at all; WinForms scaling would have covered part
  of a 150% screen.
- The message is the company's name from the installed `brand.json`, falling back to "Your IT
  company" rather than the branding placeholder "Your Company".
- It goes off when the session ends (`OnSessionEnded`, first thing) and **when every technician has
  left** — a customer must not sit in front of a black screen through a reconnect hold with nobody
  working. A UAC prompt or Ctrl+Alt+Del is another desktop and shows normally: they must see what
  they are asked to approve.
- The server keeps the last state (`Session.LastPrivacy`) for a technician who joins later, and
  writes each change on the ticket. System menu → *Privacy screen — black out their screen*.

### How it was proved

`tools/privacyprobe` — **14 of 14 on this laptop**, the real class against **both** capture paths
(`DxgiCapture` and the GDI `ScreenCapture`) with a MAGENTA window on screen: the control case (the
same windows NOT excluded) captures **black** there, which is what makes the real case capturing
**magenta** mean anything; every monitor covered edge to edge; a click passes through to the
magenta window; a topmost window opened afterwards is pushed back under; `Hide` leaves nothing. Its
first run "failed" the control because the grey letters of the message were sampled — the window
was on top all along; the magenta sits in the top fifth now. The server half is in `sessionextras`
(§61). **Not on hardware**: a customer's machine, two monitors of different scaling, an old Windows.

## 61. Session recording — 2026-09-29 (roadmap 1.6)

Clint's choices: **a Record button; kept on the server with the session's ticket; the customer told
in the tray app and on the ticket.**

### How it works

- **The console records what the technician sees** — their screen and pointer, through
  `ScreenView.RenderFrame` (the pointer drawing is shared with the live picture now) — so it costs
  the customer's machine nothing and survives a codec change, a monitor switch or a reconnect.
  Eight frames a second, their screen's shape up to 1920 wide, into an `.mp4` through Windows' own
  sink writer (`Media/ScreenRecorder.cs`: RGB32 in, H.264 out; **stride set positive**, or Media
  Foundation stores RGB bottom-up and the recording plays upside down).
- **Tools → Record this session.** Not a toolbar button: the toolbar has no room for another control
  at any width this window supports (the same reason Listen moved). While recording, a red
  *"● Recording 03:12 — click to stop"* sits on the status bar the whole time.
- **Stopping** finishes the file and uploads it (`POST /api/recordings?session=…`, bearer token,
  streamed; Kestrel's 30 MB limit lifted for that endpoint only) — off the UI thread; closing the
  window stops and uploads too. The local copy (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\RemoteSupport\recordings`) is
  **deleted once the server has it**; if the upload fails it stays and the technician is told where.
- **The server** (`RecordingService`) finds the ticket through `SessionLog.TicketId`, not the hub,
  because the upload usually arrives after the session has ended. Only somebody who was IN the
  session, or who may see every ticket, may attach one. The bytes must say `ftyp`. Stored under
  `data/recordings/<tenant>/` — **add it to backups** (roadmap 4.5). Migration `SessionRecordings`.
- **Watching**: a *Recordings* card on the ticket (`_Recordings.cshtml`, drawn by BOTH the story
  layout and the classic page), a player that can seek (range requests), and Download. Anybody who
  may see the ticket may watch; **only a supervisor or the owner may delete**
  (`Permissions.CanDeleteRecordings`).
- **Disclosure**: `RecordingStateMsg` goes to the server, which writes *"X started recording the
  session."* on the ticket and sends it on to the tray app, which logs it — with the name the
  SERVER knows, never the one the console claims. The host is never sent it.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/recordcheck` (new) | **11 of 11**: a recording read back through Windows' own decoder (`Mp4Reader`) — the size, every frame, the length, **red at the top and blue at the bottom**. Full HD measured at **10 ms a frame** against a 125 ms budget and **7.5 MB a minute** (≈450 MB an hour). |
| `tools/sessionextras` (new) | **26 of 26**, its own platform on port 8096: the privacy screen's request reaching the host, its answer reaching the technician, the ticket lines (on, off, refused with its reason), the replay to a technician who joins late; recording told to the tray app under the server's name for the technician, and on the ticket, never to the host; uploads — a real one byte for byte on its ticket, not-an-MP4 refused, no token refused, a technician not in the session refused, **40 MB accepted**, one after the session ended still finding its ticket; the ticket page's card, served as `video/mp4`, a 206 for a range, a technician who may not see the ticket gets 404, a technician cannot delete and a supervisor can, file and all. **25 of 26 with the in-the-session check removed.** Its first run found the card only on the classic page — every category has a workflow now, so a remote-support ticket is drawn by `_Timeline`. |

**Not on hardware**: a real session recorded end to end, a long one, and the upload over the
internet rather than a LAN.

### Deploying both

**Platform restart** (migration `SessionRecordings`) and a **full ship with a client reinstall**
(the HOST has the privacy screen; the CLIENT shows the recording line). `TEST-3.6.md` section AB.

## 62. As many workshop photos as the damage needs, and smaller — 2026-09-29

Clint: *"at the upload photos stage, there must be the option to add more photos in case there are
more than three. We just had a broken laptop that came in and we took 14 photos of all of the
damage, so one must have the option at both ends to add as many photos as one likes"* — and then,
*"is there a way that the uploaded photos can be automatically resized that they dont use up so
much space?"*

### What was actually wrong

**Three was always a minimum; nothing counted a maximum.** Two faults made it behave like one:

1. **Every photo picked went up as ONE request**, from the portal and from the console, and the
   server took 30 MB (Kestrel's default). Fourteen phone photos are 40–70 MB, so all fourteen were
   lost at once — "Those photos did not upload" in the portal, "Error while copying content to a
   stream" in the console. `tools/photomany` reproduced it with 14 photos of 4.2 MB: **0 of 14 in
   one upload, 14 of 14 one at a time.** Its first run used 1.3 MB photos and passed — the size is
   the fault, so a harness about it must use real sizes.
2. **After booking in, "as it arrived" could not be added to** — the Photos tab and the console's
   ticket window offered only "as it leaves".

### The fix

- **One photo per request**, portal (`_Timeline`, `NewTicket`) and console (`TechLink.UploadPhotosAsync`),
  with "Uploading 5 of 14…", and one bad photo no longer takes the rest with it.
- **The server takes 400 MB in one upload** on `/api/portal/photos` (`TicketPhotoService.MaxRequestBytes`,
  body and form limits both), so a console that has not been updated yet stops losing photos the
  day the server restarts. Each photo is still capped at 12 MB.
- **Add more, at both ends, while the job is open**: *As it arrived* and *As it leaves* in the
  portal's Photos tab and the console's ticket window. The wording says "at least 3" and "as many as
  you like" everywhere it used to say "3".
- **Smaller before they are sent**: longest side 2048 px, JPEG 85% — `wwwroot/photos.js`
  (`shrinkPhoto`, the portal) and `Technician/PhotoShrink.cs` (the console), the same rule. Done where
  the photo is picked, not on the server, because the server is headed for Linux where .NET's image
  code does not run, and because it makes a phone's upload quicker. A photo already small enough, and
  anything that cannot be opened (a HEIC without a codec), is sent as it is. The console turns a
  sideways phone photo upright first, since re-encoding drops the orientation tag; the browser does
  it through `createImageBitmap(…, { imageOrientation: 'from-image' })`. **Camera details (the date
  taken) are lost**; the ticket still records who uploaded each photo and when. Photos already
  stored are not touched.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/photomany` (new) | **21 of 21**, its own platform on port 8095, fourteen 4.2 MB photos: all 14 in one upload (as old clients send them), one at a time, and through the console's real `TechLink`; what the console stored is ≤ 2048 px and smaller; a 4000×3000 photo tagged sideways comes out 1536×2048, upright, the right way round, 654 → 146 KB; a small one untouched; a workshop job books in with 14; 5 more "as it arrived" after booking, from the portal and the console; 14 "as it leaves"; the Photos tab offers both, the wording, and both pages load `photos.js`. **Against the old code: 0 of 14 in one upload, from the portal and the console.** |
| `photos.js` in a real browser | a 4000×3000 JPEG 1.0 → 0.21 MB at 2048×1536; a 5.6 MB PNG → 0.25 MB; a small one, a text file and a broken image sent unchanged. |
| unchanged | `photogate` 38, `workflowcheck` 100, `calloutcheck` 52, `routecheck` 53. |

**Not on hardware**: a phone's own camera through the portal (HEIC on an iPhone, orientation), and
the Wi-Fi at the counter.

### Deploying it

**Platform restart** for the server limit and the pages; **`-OnlyTechnician`** for the console. No
migration. `TEST-3.6.md` section AC.

## 63. Delivery instead of collection — 2026-09-30 (roadmap 3.7.1)

Clint: *"a machine might be booked in at our offices, but instead of it being collected, it needs to
be delivered so this needs to be added to the workflow after the work is completed and then pretty
much follow the call out process."* His answers are in `docs/NEXT-SESSION-WORKFLOWS.md` ("Fourth
round"): paid before OR on delivery; always a technician; work done is recorded there ("a printer
needs to be installed"); the photos out are taken at the office.

### How it works

- **Out for delivery** (`TicketService.DeliverKey`, `send-for-delivery`) is offered by `ActionsFor`
  wherever Machine collected is — a workshop machine, bench finished, not yet gone — to the same
  people (`Workflow.MayMarkCollected`), behind the same gate (the photos out). It is handled by name
  like `collected` (`SendForDeliveryAsync`) because its performer is "the office OR the technician
  on the job", which no lane expresses. It keeps the billing stage it left in **`StageReturn`** and
  puts the job on the bench with `WorkedBy` — "always a technician".
- **Delivered — work done** [details, time] → *Delivered*. Sets `CollectedUtc`/`CollectedBy` (the
  machine has gone) and the new **`Ticket.Delivered`** (migration `Delivery`), which only changes
  the words: *Delivered* for *Collected*, *Paid on delivery* for *Paid on site*. **Its time is ADDED
  to the bench's**, not put in its place — the browser walk found that; `deliverycheck` asks it now.
  It is a Work done entry, so it is copied into the invoice.
- From *Delivered*, the call out's three: **To be invoiced** [amount] — added to the invoice when
  the job was still at To be invoiced, a new invoice (number cleared) otherwise; **Invoiced — paid on
  delivery** → the call out's own Paid cash / Paid card → Paid on site — to be closed; **Nothing more
  to invoice** → `@return`, back to wherever the billing was, and `@close` then closes outright
  because `CollectedUtc` is set.
- **Not delivered** [why] → `@return`, not gone, and Collected / Out for delivery are offered again.
- **`TicketService.Offered`** is the one place a step's offer depends on more than its stage: To be
  invoiced is not offered after a delivery that left from *Invoiced — awaiting payment*, and
  `ActAsync` refuses it with the reason. A second "to be invoiced" there would overwrite the unpaid
  invoice's amount and number and lose track of it.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/deliverycheck` (new) | **48 of 48**, through the service: paid before, paid on delivery (card), an invoice out and unpaid, the delivery's work added to an unsent invoice (650 + 300 = 950) and as its own after payment, not delivered, the quote route (Parts fitted → Complete closes), a call out never offered it, a machine still on the bench refused, Machine collected unchanged, abandoned from Out for delivery. **44 of 48 with `Offered` always true** (43 of 47 before the time check was added). |
| unchanged | `workflowcheck` 100, `calloutcheck` 52, `routecheck` 53, `photogate` 38, `quotecheck` 108, `assigncheck` 49, `ticketwindowprobe` 128. `ticketwire` 31 after its "Machine collected is her only button" became "…and Out for delivery". |
| the portal, walked | on a `workflowdemo` platform: Invoiced — awaiting payment → Out for delivery → Delivered (form wording) → only Paid on delivery and Nothing more to invoice → Paid cash "R 450,00" → billing queue, Details reading *Paid on delivery 450.00 · cash* and *Delivered*. |

**Starting a throwaway platform on a demo folder**: `RSP_Platform__DataDirectory=<folder>` in the
environment and `run` as the first argument. A `--Platform:DataDirectory` argument is IGNORED (the
folder is read before the arguments are), and the platform quietly opens `bin\Debug\...\data`.

**Not on hardware.** Platform restart (migration `Delivery`) and `-OnlyTechnician`.
`TEST-3.6.md` section AD, checks 193–199.

## 64. Several machines booked in at once — 2026-09-30 (roadmap 3.7.1)

Clint: *"sometimes a client may bring in more that one machine to the office at the same time, so at
the beginning of the workflow, there must be an option to add machine with it's fault description
and ask for the same details as the original."* His answers: **one ticket per machine**, linked;
paying and leaving together OR separately; *"there's always a chance of one or two of them being
abandoned."*

### How it works

- **Add another machine** (`TicketService.AddMachineKey`) is a step at **Booked in**, not a
  repeating block on the New ticket form. It is offered by `ActionsFor` (ahead of Abandoned) to the
  office and the people on the job, and handled by name (`AddMachineAsync`) because it moves nothing:
  the job it was pressed on stays at Booked in. Being a step, its form is drawn by the SAME generic
  step-form code in the portal and the console — only the photo picker is its own.
- It asks **the fault first**, then the booking's questions (`AddMachineFields`), and needs **three
  photos of THAT machine**, staged as they are picked (`StageInput.PhotoStageId`,
  `TicketActMsg.PhotoStageId`) and checked by the booking's own rule
  (`TicketPhotoService.CheckBookInAsync`) — photos staged by somebody else do not count.
- The new ticket gets the same client, contact, people, priority and site; its subject is the
  machine and the fault's first line. **Every ticket of one booking carries the same
  `Ticket.BookingId` — the first ticket's id** (migration `BookedTogether`), whichever ticket the
  machine was added from. They are equals: no parent, nothing waits for its siblings, each can be
  abandoned alone. `BookedWithAsync` lists the others with their stage; the portal shows *Booked in
  with:* under the header, the console a row of buttons that open each one.
- The portal keeps the photos' stage id across a refused submit (`MachineStageId`, posted back as
  `photoStage`), and uploads without reloading so nothing typed is lost. The console closes the form
  when a new machine appears in `BookedWith` — the stage does not move, so "the stage changed" (how
  every other step's form closes) never fires.
- It is not offered once work has started; pressing it then says to book the machine in as a new
  ticket.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/machinescheck` (new) | **36 of 36**: who is offered it and in what order; the fault, no photos, two photos and somebody else's photos each refused, and a refusal makes no ticket; the new ticket's category, stage, client, contact, people, priority, subject, fault, machine details and encrypted password; its photos its own; both stories; one booking id; a third added from the SECOND ticket joins the same booking; each lists the others; the console's detail carries the list; they move and are abandoned independently; call outs and General never offered it. **33 of 36 when a machine added from the second ticket starts a booking of its own.** |
| the portal, walked | on a `workflowdemo` platform as a technician on #1: the three buttons, the form's wording, three photos pushed through the page's own picker (canvas JPEGs → `shrinkPhoto` → staged, count "3 added so far" without a reload), Submit → #13 created, *Booked in with: #13 …* under #1's header, #1's story line; then #13: its subject, *Booked in with: #1*, Photos (3 in), its booking card. |
| unchanged | `deliverycheck` 48, `workflowcheck` 100, `calloutcheck` 52, `routecheck` 53, `photogate` 38, `quotecheck` 108, `assigncheck` 49, `ticketwindowprobe` 128, `ticketformprobe` 91. `ticketwire` 31 once its Booked-in button list included Add another machine. |

**Not on hardware.** Platform restart (migration `BookedTogether`) and `-OnlyTechnician`.
`TEST-3.6.md` section AE, checks 200–205.
