## 76. Internal testing, 2 October: attended sessions run as SYSTEM, the console waits visibly — 2026-10-02

Clint brought six faults from internal testing, with screenshots. **Five had one cause between
them, or two causes each — none of them was where it looked.**

### 1. UAC black, Task Manager will not open, DISM "error 740" — attended sessions ran as the person

The Info window of the screenshot (item 3, see below) was not blank: it said, unreadably, *Host
running as: the logged-on user*. That is the whole of item 1. `StartSession` offered the agent only
when there was a call or unattended permission (`mayUseAgent`, §31), so **every technician-initiated
attended session was hosted by the tray app**, as the person: it cannot open the Winlogon desktop
(UAC black, §4), cannot send input to an elevated window (Task Manager is elevated for an
administrator), and its scripts are not elevated (DISM: 740 = *elevation required*). And `taskmgr.exe`
started with `UseShellExecute = false` as an administrator's account fails outright with 740, which
the console showed only as a status line.

**The permission was never about which process hosts — it is about whether anybody is ASKED.** So now:
without permission, an agent that says it can ask (`HelloMsg.Can` contains `DeviceCan.AskConsent`) is
handed the session with `StartSessionMsg.AskConsent`; it launches its SYSTEM host with
`--consent ask`, on `winsta0\default`, so the same prompt is in front of the person and nothing is
captured until they allow it. **An agent that has not said so is never offered an attended session —
it would start one without asking** — and the tray app hosts as before. Such a session is
`Unattended = false` (after a restart somebody must say yes again), and the tray app is told a
technician is connected only on the yes (`Session.TellTrayWhenAllowed`).

Where the tray app still hosts (no agent connected, or an old one), it is now said, not discovered:
`SessionInfo.HostedByApp` puts one dismissable yellow line in the session window (full text in its
tooltip; the banner's *Close* closes the WINDOW, so notices have their own *OK*), Info's *Host running
as* says what it costs, a script ending 740 says why under the error, and Task Manager's refusal says
why. **Whether those test machines' agents are connected was not measured** — `agentcheck` against
the live server got a 401 with `tools/rs-credentials.json` as it stands.

### 4 and 5. Nothing while the customer decides; a blank window when they did not

The console drew a session only once its host connected, and an asking host used to ask **before
connecting**, so for up to a minute the technician saw nothing (item 4). On a timeout the host then
connected only to send `DeclineSessionMsg` — and `RunSessionHostAsync` marked the session
`HostConnected` and broadcast it *before* reading that message, so the console opened a window for a
session that was ending. The window's viewer socket arrived after `EndSession` had unregistered the
session, and **`/ws/session` answered a session it no longer knew with a bare 404** — which
`SessionLink` reads as "not yet", so it dialled for 120 s and said *"Could not get back to the session
after 124 seconds"* (item 5, the screenshot). The "that session has ended" branch in
`RunSessionViewerAsync` existed and was unreachable once a session had left the registry.

Now:

- **The host connects FIRST** with `consent=asking&secs=N` on its address, runs its receive pump, and
  acts on nothing until the answer (`_consented`; `OnMessage`/`OnBinary` ignore everything except
  `SessionEndedMsg`, which withdraws the prompt). Yes → `ConsentGrantedMsg`; no → `DeclineSessionMsg`
  with *declined* or *nobody answered within N seconds* told apart (`ConsentAnswer`).
- **The hub** keeps such a session `HostConnected = false, AwaitingConsent = true` (so an OLDER console
  still waits, as it always did), passes nothing from a viewer to that host, and on the yes flips both
  and writes *"The person at X allowed the connection."* on the ticket.
- `EndSession` sets **`SessionInfo.Ended` and `EndReason`** — a session that ended before anybody
  joined used to look exactly like one not started yet — and remembers the reason for ten minutes
  (`_endedReasons`). **A viewer for an unknown session is answered by its own company's hub** with
  `SessionEndedMsg` and that reason, never a 404.
- **The console** shows `ConsentWaitForm` for a session the technician started: *Connecting…* (only
  if still waiting after 1.5 s, so unattended sessions do not flash it), then *Waiting for X to accept*
  with the time left and *Cancel* (ends the session; the host takes the prompt down), then either it
  closes and the session window opens, or it says why it did not. `StartSessionOnAsync` (Reconnect)
  waits as long as the person is still deciding, and is answered "no" at once if they decline.

### 2. The microphone question, under a Windows notification

The tray app asked on the corner banner AND showed a balloon — and Windows put the balloon on top of
the banner's buttons. The question is now `MicQuestion`, a window in the middle of the screen, top-most,
**no default button** (an Enter meant for something else must not answer it), X = *Not now*; no
balloon when asking. The banner still says what is happening and its buttons still work.

### 3. Tools → Info "opens a blank window"

A `ListBox` with the theme's ink on Windows' default white: in the dark theme **#EEF3F8 on #FFFFFF,
1.1:1**. Now a read-only, wrapping `RichTextBox` on `Surface`, like the Sound report.

### 6. The sign-in window

§30 again: the console is per-monitor DPI aware, the fonts grow with Windows' scaling and the label
heights were written as 26 px. At 150% *Password* needs 28 and had 22. Every height is measured now
and the window's height is the sum of its parts. *Forgot your password?* was `AutoSize`, so it was as
wide as its text and *MiddleCenter* had no middle; it spans the card and sits under the button.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/consentwire` | **New, 34.** A real hub on a throwaway platform: the attended route to an agent that can ask, nothing reaching an unanswered host, the tray app told only on the yes, an older agent never offered one, unattended unchanged, *nobody answered* arriving as `Ended` with its reason and never as under way, a viewer dialling in afterwards answered rather than refused, Cancel withdrawing the question — and **the real `RemoteSupport.Host.exe`** with a 5 s brand.json, left to time out and then cancelled (its prompt shows on the screen for a few seconds; nothing to click). **Against the old hub: 7 of 14 in part 1, including the 404.** |
| `tools/fitprobe` | **New, 68.** The real sign-in, waiting, microphone and session windows, at this screen's scaling (150% here), light and dark: every label holds its text, the link spans and centres, Info is readable and wraps, the microphone window is centred with no default button. PNGs to look at. **Against the old LoginForm and SessionForm: 54 of 68** — the clipped labels, the 183 px link, the 1.1:1 Info. |
| re-run | `unattendedwire` 13, `voicewire` 37, `websupportcheck` 64, `trayexit` 16, `sessionextras` 26, `ticketpersession` 30. |

**Not proved: the SYSTEM host's prompt on a real customer machine**, and UAC/Task Manager/DISM in an
attended session through it — `TEST-3.6.md` section AR, checks 293–302.

**Platform deploy (no migration), a FULL ship, and a client reinstall** — the agent must say it can
ask, or nothing changes for item 1.

## 77. An unattended password, for somebody's own machine — 2026-10-02

Clint: *"A good feature to have would be to set unattended passwords. This is especially handy if
someone wanted to connect to their own personal machine from the office."* His answers when asked:
**set in the tray app, by whoever is at the machine** (the person, or a technician working on it in a
session); **nobody gets in without it — the owner and supervisors included**; set at the machine only.

### What it is

With unattended access on and no password, every technician at the company can connect. With one,
a technician-started connection to that machine needs it.

- **The tray app**: under *Allow unattended access*, **Unattended password…** (reads *Unattended
  password — set…* once there is one). `UnattendedPasswordDialog`: typed twice, eight characters at
  least (`UnattendedPasswords.Problem` in Shared — the ONE rule, asked by the tray app and the
  server), *Remove password* when one is set. It can be set before unattended access is switched on;
  it only matters while it is on. The chat log says when it is set or removed.
- **The server** keeps only a PBKDF2 hash and salt (`Device.UnattendedPasswordHash/Salt/ChangedUtc/
  ChangedBy`, migration `UnattendedPassword`; the same `Passwords` derivation as a technician's), held
  in memory in `TenantHub._unattendedPw` — **never in `DeviceInfo`, which is broadcast**; that carries
  only `UnattendedPassword` (one is set). **Only the CLIENT connection may set it** (§31's rule).
  It stays with the machine through a reinstall (the hardware-matched row carries it).
- **The console**: Connect on such a machine puts a password box under the reason, in the same
  `ReasonDialog`. A refusal comes back as `ErrorMsg { NeedsPassword, DeviceId }`, and the console
  reopens that window with the reason kept and the server's words in it. The password is kept in
  memory for the run, beside the reason, so a restart's reconnect does not ask again; it is forgotten
  the moment the server refuses it. An OLDER console gets the same refusal as plain words ("update the
  console").

### The rules, and where they live

All in `TenantHub`: `NeedsUnattendedPassword` (unattended allowed AND a password set), `PasswordLets`,
and the gate in `ConnectDevice` — the one door a technician-started session comes through.

- **A call never needs it**: the person asked and is there. **Attended machines are untouched**: the
  person is asked to Allow, as ever, password or not.
- **Nobody joins a session opened with it without typing it** (`Session.Admitted`, technician ids).
  Without this a colleague could open the running session from the Sessions list, which is what
  "nobody without it" would otherwise have meant. `RunSessionViewerAsync` refuses them with words that
  send them to Connect; Connect on the machine asks them and then hands them the running session.
- **Blank is not a guess.** An empty password is refused without counting, so a console's reconnect
  loop can never lock a machine. **Five wrong ones lock the MACHINE for 15 minutes** — the right one
  included — across every console; in memory, as `SignInGuard`. Setting or removing the password
  clears the count. Every wrong one is logged with who typed it.
- **No way round it from the office, on purpose.** There is no portal or console control to see,
  reset or clear it. A forgotten one is removed at the machine. Do not add an override for supervisors
  — Clint was asked and said no.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/unattendedpw` | **New, 33.** A real hub on a throwaway platform, two real sign-ins (a technician and an OWNER): too short refused by the server, the agent cannot set it, consoles told it is set and never the password; missing / wrong (*4 more tries*) / right (unattended, nobody asked); the owner refused; a colleague refused at the session socket, then let in by Connect with it; ten blanks lock nothing; five wrong lock even the right one; a new password lifts the lockout and the old stops working; removing it; attended and a call untouched; **and after a server restart** still set, still enforced. **With the Connect gate taken out: 12 of 28. With the session-join guard taken out: 32 of 33** (the colleague walks in). |
| `tools/fitprobe` | **126** (was 68): the Connect window with the password and a refusal showing, and the tray app's window set and change, light and dark, at 150%. It found a real fault the first time — *Remove password* ran off the left of a 480 px window, each button fitting its own words — and now checks every button is inside the window. |
| re-run | `unattendedwire` 13, `consentwire` 26 (`--no-host`), `unattendedcheck` 40, `dashtabs` 98. |

**Not on hardware.** `TEST-3.6.md` section AS, checks 303–310. **Platform deploy (migration
`UnattendedPassword`), a FULL ship (tray app and console) and a client reinstall.** The agent and
host are unchanged.

Not built, and worth knowing: the person at the machine is not told when somebody types a wrong
password (only the server log says so), and the portal's device page does not show that a machine has
one.

## 78. Two machines on ONE job — a data transfer — 2026-10-02

Clint: *"An example of when we get two machines for one ticket would be when we need to do a data
transfer. the client would bring in their old and new machines which needs to be booked in together
under one ticket."* §64 had built the other case only — one ticket per machine, linked by
`BookingId` — from his 30 September answer, which was about machines with faults of their own.
Shown both, he chose **both kinds**. Recorded in `NEXT-SESSION-WORKFLOWS.md`, "Fifth round".

### How it works

- **One control.** *Add another machine* (still only at Booked in) asks first **Is it part of this
  job?** — `StageField.SameJob`, first in `AddMachineFields`. *No — a separate job* is the default
  and does exactly what §64 did. *Yes* puts the machine on THIS ticket. Portal: two radio choices,
  and the box under them relabels itself; console: a dropdown, same words.
- **Same job** (`TicketService.AddMachineToJobAsync`): the booking's questions and **three photos of
  that machine** (the same `CheckBookInAsync`), but no fault of its own — the job's is written, so the
  box asks what the machine is FOR and may be empty. It becomes a **`TicketMachine`** row (migration
  `MachinesOnOneJob`): purpose, make, model, serial, accessories, password (encrypted like the
  ticket's own), who and when. **The ticket's own `Asset*` columns stay machine 1**; rows are 2, 3….
  Its photos are attached with **`TicketPhoto.MachineId`** (null = the ticket's own machine). The
  story gets *Another machine on this job*, written like a booking.
- **One route, one invoice, leaving together.** Nothing else in the route changed. **Photos out are
  three of EACH machine** (`PhotosOutRequiredAsync`, both *Machine collected* and *Out for
  delivery*), counted together and worded "3 of each of the 2 machines" so nobody takes six of one.
- **Shown**: the portal's Details tab has a card per machine (each password behind its own Show), the
  Photos tab groups *As it arrived* by machine, the booking card says *Machine 1*. The console gets
  `TicketDetail.Machines` (passwords decrypted by the hub, `FillWorkflowAsync(..., reveal)`) and
  `PhotosOutRequired`, and draws the same.
- **A refused form keeps the choice** — `SameJobChosen` in the portal, `_drafts["add-machine:SameJob"]`
  in the console. Without it a refusal (no photos yet) redrew the form on *separate job*, and the next
  Submit would have made a ticket nobody chose. The console closes the form when `Machines` grows,
  because a same-job machine makes no new linked ticket for the old signal to see.

### Not built

Photos added later from the Photos tab (*Add more photos as it arrived*) go to machine 1 — there is
no machine picker there. Photos out are not tied to a machine at all, only counted. A machine added
by mistake cannot be removed (abandon and rebook, or note it). An OLDER console shows the new
`SameJob` field as a text box called "SameJob" and wants something typed in it; ship
`-OnlyTechnician` with the platform.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/machinescheck` | **56** (was 36): the field order; same job refused without its photos; same job with nothing typed accepted; NO new ticket; the `TicketMachine` row with the answers and the encrypted password; its photos on this ticket and marked as its own; the story entry; no `BookingId`, stage unchanged; a third added by a technician; the console's `Machines`, passwords only through the caller's decryption, photos per machine, `PhotosOutRequired` 9; the job moved on as one; no adding after inspection; 3 photos out refused for 3 machines (collection AND delivery), 9 accepted, "All 3 machines collected"; a separate job still the default and still needs its fault. **With the old three-photo rule back: 52 of 56.** |
| `tools/ticketwindowprobe` | **146** (was 128): the REAL console ticket window — the dropdown first with *separate* chosen, a separate job's missing fault named, *same job* relabelling the box, **a redraw keeping the same-job choice** (145 of 146 with the console's memory of it taken out), collection asking for 6 "as they leave", *Machine 1* on the booking with its own photos, a card per machine in Details with its own password button, the Photos pane's 6. Pictures in its `shots` folder. |
| the portal, walked | on a `workflowdemo` platform as Sue on #1 at Booked in: the two choices, *Yes* relabelling the box and dropping `required`; Submit with no photos refused **and still on Yes**; three canvas JPEGs through the page's own picker ("3 added so far"); Submit → no new ticket, no *Booked in with*, *Photos (6 in · 0 out)*, the story entry; Details with *Machine 1* and *Machine 2*, the password shown by its own Show; Photos grouped by machine, *At least 6 (3 of each machine)*. It found that *Add more photos … as it arrived* would silently go to machine 1; it now says *machine 1*. |
| unchanged | `workflowcheck` 100, `deliverycheck` 48, `photogate` 38, `photomany` 21, `routecheck` 53, `calloutcheck` 52, `quotecheck` 110, `ticketwire` 31, `ticketformprobe` 91. |

**Not on hardware.** `TEST-3.6.md` section AT, checks 311–317. **Platform deploy (migration

## 79. Tickets by email and by a contact form — 2026-10-05

Clint: *"someone sends an email to support@anywhereit.co.za, it automatically creates a ticket using
the email address, subject and body ... check the email address against the client database, and
automatically link to the client if the email address exists. The same would work from the contact
form. The system should then auto reply to the email address given with the ticket reference number
and a short message saying a ticket has been opened."* His three answers, the same day (roadmap
3.8.4): **(1)** any mail host, *"explaining the possible issues they may face"*, and a form a company
makes for its website from the portal — **Microsoft 365's own sign-in is LATER, by his decision**;
**(2)** an unknown sender opens a ticket with **no client**; **(3)** client known but person not:
**say so, and suggest adding them as a contact first** so the ticket links correctly.

### What it is

- **Portal → Tickets by email** (`/portal/mailintake`, owner and supervisors — it holds a mailbox
  password, so it is on the admin page list in `Program.cs` like Health check). Off by default.
  **One button for email: Save and test.** A status line, a *What can go wrong* section per host
  (cPanel/xneelo, Google, Microsoft 365, Zoho, anything else), the contact form's settings with the
  line to paste and a live preview, and **every message looked at, with what happened and why** —
  nothing is dropped quietly.
- **Two ways in.** *We check your mailbox* — IMAP with server, username, password; *Fill in for*
  buttons (cPanel = `mail.<their domain>`, Gmail, Zoho; Microsoft switches to forwarding). *You
  forward it to us* — their server forwards support@ to ONE mailbox on our domain (Owner → Mail,
  *Forwarding mailbox*, or `forwarding-mailbox set` with `RSP_INTAKE_PASSWORD`), which the platform
  reads and **sorts by the address each message was sent to** (To, Cc, Delivered-To, X-Original-To…).
  A forwarded address must be **confirmed by a link mailed to it** (`/mail-confirm`; the GET shows,
  the POST confirms — §73's rule), and one confirmed address belongs to one company. **Gmail's own
  forwarding confirmation code** arrives in OUR mailbox, not theirs, so it is put on their page.
- **A ticket**: General, `TicketSource.Email` or `Form`, subject and text (HTML mail made text,
  attachments named but not copied), **`Ticket.RequesterEmail`** (migration `TicketsByEmail`), and a
  story line saying who it came from and what the client check found.
- **Who is it** — `TicketIntake.MatchAsync`, the one rule, asked by the intake AND by the ticket page
  every time it is drawn: a contact with that exact address → client and person; a client with it →
  the client; **on two or more → linked to neither, and named**; otherwise the **domain** — if it is on
  1 or 2 clients they are SUGGESTED (answer 3), never linked; a domain on **3+ clients** is an
  internet provider's and suggests nobody; **free mail** (`TicketIntake.FreeMail`, incl. SA ISPs) and
  **the company's own domains** (support address, its people, ours) never suggest anybody. The form's
  Company box naming a client exactly suggests it too.
- **The notice** (`Pages/Portal/_Sender.cshtml`, in BOTH the story page and the classic page): the
  note, the sender's name filled in, the client (or a choice), and **one button: Add as a contact and
  link this ticket** (`AddSenderAsContactAsync`). A sender put on file anywhere else links their
  waiting ticket the next time it is opened, with a story line.
- **The auto-reply**: `[Ticket #N] their subject`, their words with {name} {number} {subject}
  {company}; **from their own server** (same login by default — cPanel's arrangement) so it is really
  from support@, or from ours in their name with Reply-To support@; **if theirs fails it goes from
  ours** and the page says why. `Auto-Submitted: auto-replied`, `In-Reply-To` theirs, and a
  **Message-ID that carries the ticket** (`rsp.{tenant}.{number}.…@`).
- **A reply goes on the same ticket** — found by that Message-ID in References first (survives a
  rewritten subject), then `[Ticket #N]`; **only from the address it was opened for or a contact of
  the same client** (anyone can type a number); added as the customer's words with the quoted history
  cut (`StripQuoted`) and **no @mention processing** (`AddNoteAsync(..., mentions: false)`); never
  answered. A reply to a CLOSED ticket opens a new one that says so.
- **Left alone, with the reason logged**: out-of-office (Auto-Submitted, X-Autoreply, "Automatic
  reply:"), bounces, newsletters (List-Id/List-Unsubscribe/Precedence), the server's spam mark,
  no-reply senders, **mail FROM their own support address** (a loop, or an Outlook rule that forwards
  and replaces the sender — the reason says to forward on the server), over **5 per sender per hour**
  or 200 per company, over 15 MB, the same Message-ID again.
- **A website's existing contact form that emails support@** works with nothing else: a form robot
  (wordpress@, noreply@, website@ their own domain) with a Reply-To is read as the customer.
- **The contact form**: `/contact/{slug}` (a page to link to) and `<script src=".../contactform/{slug}.js"
  async>` which puts it in a frame where it is pasted and sizes the frame by `postMessage`. Heading,
  intro, phone off/optional/required, company, thank-you words. **No antiforgery token on purpose**
  (in a frame it is a third-party cookie Safari discards) — a hidden field, three seconds open, and
  10 per internet address an hour stand in front of it instead. The portal's preview sends nothing.
  `/contact` joins `/webchat` as the only paths another site may frame.

### The rules that matter, and why

- **The mailbox is opened READ-ONLY (EXAMINE) and messages fetched with BODY.PEEK.** Nothing in a
  company's mailbox is marked read, moved or deleted. Mail is found **by UID, never by "unread"** —
  somebody reading support@ in Outlook first must not stop it becoming a ticket.
- **Only new mail.** The first look notes where the folder is up to (UIDVALIDITY + last UID) and
  makes nothing of what is already there; another server/user/folder starts again. **The trap, found
  by the harness and fixed:** "last UID 0" is an EMPTY mailbox, not "never looked at" — treating it as
  the latter re-took the starting point every minute, so **a new mailbox's first message was always
  lost**. Only a missing or changed UIDVALIDITY means "start again".
- **A refused password is tried ONCE, then checking stops** (`Paused`) until the form is saved. cPanel's
  cPHulk blocks an address that keeps failing, and that address is OUR server — one company's typo
  would lock out every company on the same host. Other failures back off 2, 4, 8 … 30 minutes.
- **Plain IMAP/SMTP only to loopback** (`MailServer.Socket`), which is where the harness's fake
  servers live; every real server is SSL or STARTTLS whatever the form says.
- **MailKit (MIT) is the second library brought in**, after QRCoder: reading mail from the internet is
  a parser for hostile input. It is confined to `Services/MailWire.cs`.

### Where it lives

`Services/MailWire.cs` (MailKit, reading, sending, `Explain` — every failure in words: Google → app
password, Microsoft → forwarding, cPanel → full address and the mailbox's own password, a certificate
for another name → the name to use, a port/security mismatch, a server that is not there).
`Services/TicketIntake.cs` (every rule). `Services/TicketIntakeSweep.cs` (once a minute, four at a
time, 90 s each; `Testing:IntakeSeconds` shortens it for the harness). `Data`: `TicketIntakeSettings`,
`InboundMail`, `Ticket.RequesterEmail`, `PlatformSettings.Intake*`, `TicketSource.Email`/`Form`.
Pages: `Portal/MailIntake`, `Portal/_Sender`, `ContactForm`, `MailConfirm`, `Owner/Mail` (forwarding).
`wwwroot/contactform-embed.js`. The consoles hear new tickets through `TicketIntake.TicketMade`.

### Not built

~~Microsoft 365 sign-in (OAuth) — later, by Clint's decision~~ — **built 2026-10-19: §151**, Sign in with Microsoft. Attachments are named on the ticket, not
copied. ~~Staff cannot reply to the customer FROM the ticket~~ — **they can since 2026-10-09: §123**, a
comment emailed to the client from the ticket, and the customer's answer comes back onto the ticket. The console shows the story line about the sender but
not the Add-as-contact button — that is the portal's, like Request quote. The auto-reply is plain text.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/mailintakecheck` | **135 of 135**. A real platform, and a **fake IMAP server and fake SMTP server inside the harness** — the real timer reads real mail, the real auto-reply is caught as bytes and read with MimeKit. The rules (automatic, spam, HTML, recipients, the robot's Reply-To, quoted replies cut, the ticket number found, failures in words); who is it (contact, client, two clients, the domain suggestion, a two-client domain, a provider's domain, Gmail, our own domain, the form's company box); the portal page as owner and refused to a technician (by heading, §34); **a wrong password said once and NOT retried over three ticks**; Save and test; old mail left alone; Jane's ticket linked, the reply from support@ through its own login, subject, words, `Auto-Submitted`, `In-Reply-To`, Message-ID; her reply onto the SAME ticket without the history and unanswered; **Eve typing her number gets her own ticket**; Bob at Acme unlinked with the notice and one press linking him; a stranger, then put on file, linking itself; six kinds left alone, unanswered and listed; a WordPress form's Reply-To; one Message-ID twice is one ticket; HTML only; the flood limit; **only EXAMINE and BODY.PEEK in 117 IMAP commands**; the reply from ours, and from ours when theirs is refused; a console's `TicketChangedMsg`; forwarding — the link, nothing sorted before it is used, opening it confirms nothing, Confirm does, once; the right company only; no squatting; Gmail's code on the page; the form — script, frame allowed, no token, too fast, honeypot, a required phone keeping the words, a ticket with the phone and the reply, a company named, the preview, switched off. **132 of 134 with the sender check on replies removed; 133 of 134 with the empty-mailbox fault put back.** |
| the portal, walked | on a throwaway platform as the owner: the page in dark (it found the radio buttons stretched full width by `.form input` — fixed), the form's preview, a real form sent as Bob at an Acme domain, the ticket's notice, one press → linked to Acme and Bob with a story line. It found the thank-you claiming *we have emailed you a copy* when no reply had gone — it now says so only when one did. |
| unchanged | `routecheck` 53, `ticketwire` 31, `contactcheck` 34, `securitycheck` 75, `webchatcheck` 80. |

**Not on hardware, and not against a real mail server yet.** `TEST-3.6.md` section AV, checks
320–331 — **320 is Anywhere IT's own cPanel mailbox, and is the one that matters.** **Platform deploy
(migration `TicketsByEmail`)**; no ship — neither the console nor the client changed. For forwarding:
create `tickets@theremotesupportprogram.com` on the domain's mail and set it on Owner → Mail
(`GO-LIVE.md`).

## 80. A knowledge base — 2026-10-05 (roadmap 3.8.5)

Clint: *"There should be an option on all user's dashboards to click on their dashboard and access
and edit/create in the knowledgebase. There should also be an option once a ticket is completed with
the option to commit to the knowledgebase that then opens it as an editable item, so that it can be
worded correctly. Knowledgebase options should be able to be linked to clients ... The knowledgebase
would have a General section and clients section."* His six answers were *"go with your
recommendations"* — they are in the roadmap, 3.8.5, and each is a section of `kbcheck`.

### What it is

- **Portal → Knowledge base** (`/portal/kb`), on every role's menu and as a card on the owner's
  dashboard: a **General** section and a **Clients** section (each client with articles under its
  name, "This client only" → `?client=N`; `?client=0` is General only). The search narrows as you type
  by asking the page itself — the Clients page's way (§59) — across titles, words and client names.
- **An article** (`/portal/kb/{id}`): title, General or ONE client, the words drawn as a page, who
  wrote and updated it, the ticket it came from, **Edit**, **History** (every save, each viewable,
  **Put this version back** — itself a new version), **Delete** (supervisor or owner only).
- **The editor** (`/portal/kb/edit/{id?}`, `?ticket=N` to write a ticket up, `?client=N` for a new one
  under a client): title, the client picker (`clientpick.js`, empty = General), a toolbar (1. Step,
  • Bullet, Heading, Bold, Commands, Add a picture, Preview), **screenshots pasted or dropped straight
  into the box** (made smaller by `photos.js`, as workshop photos are), a live password warning, and
  a warning before leaving with changes unsaved.
- **On a ticket** (`Pages/Portal/_Knowledge.cshtml`, in BOTH layouts per §61): *📘 Knowledge base for
  Acme (3)* when its client has articles, *Written up: …* for each article made from it, and **Add to
  knowledge base** (then *Add another…*) when this person is offered it. The ticket's story gets
  *Written up in the knowledge base: …*. The client's own page has the count and *New article for them*.
- **The console**: a **Knowledge base** header button; the ticket window draws the same line from
  `TicketDetail.Knowledge` (`KnowledgeInfo`); a session window asks `KnowledgeCountRequestMsg` for its
  machine as it opens and shows *📘 Knowledge base for Acme (3)* on the status bar and on Tools. All of
  them open the portal through the hand-off (`PortalHandoffService.SafePath` allows `/portal/kb`,
  `?client=N`, `/N`, `/edit`, `/edit?ticket=N|client=N` — digits only, compared whole).

### The rules, and where they live

Every rule is **`Services/KnowledgeBaseService.cs`**; the pages and the hub only ask.

- **When a ticket offers the write-up** (`WorkIsDone`): a Work done entry, the technician's decision on
  how it ends (any `Outcome`), or Resolved/Closed. Not Closed alone — **a technician never closes
  anything**, so waiting for Closed would hide it from the person who did the work. **To whom**
  (`Offered`): anybody in `AssignedTo` or `WorkedBy` (a job in billing has nobody assigned — WorkedBy
  is what keeps the technician on it), and supervisors and the owner (`Permissions.CanWriteUpAnyTicket`).
  Not the office administrator, who was not on it. Reading a ticket for a draft goes through
  `TicketService.VisibleTo` like every other read.
- **The draft** (`DraftFromTicketAsync`): the subject as title, the ticket's client, *# What was
  needed* (the description), and *# Step by step* — each line of every Work done entry's
  `TicketService.WorkDoneText` (so never the time or amount) as a numbered step, old marks stripped.
  **Nothing is saved until Save**; pressing the button twice makes nothing twice.
- **Everybody writes and edits** (`Permissions.CanWriteKnowledge`); **only a supervisor or the owner
  deletes** (`CanDeleteKnowledge`), and deleting keeps the row (`DeletedUtc`) and its history.
- **Two people saving the same version**: the editor sends the version it opened; a save against an
  older one is refused with who saved and when, and **what was typed comes back in the box**.
  `KbArticle.Version` is also an EF concurrency token, so two saves in the same instant cannot both land.
- **One client per article, or General.** A client of another company is "not found", both ways.
- **Never a password** (`KbText.LooksLikePassword`): *Password: x*, *pwd = x*, *PIN 1234*, *wifi key is x*
  — a nudge, never a refusal. The article page warns everybody who opens it, with the secret shown as
  •••••• — never repeated. Sentences ABOUT passwords (*reset the password for the user*, *User must
  change password at next logon*) are left alone.
- **Staff only.** Nothing here is ever shown to a customer.

### The words: `KbText`, our own small markup

`1.` a numbered step (an indented line under it belongs to it), `-` a bullet, `#` a heading, a line of
three backticks above and below a block of commands, `**bold**`, `` `code` ``, `[image:N]` on its own
line, and web addresses as links. **Everything typed is HTML-encoded before anything else**, and the
only tags in the output are the renderer's own — that is why this is not a rich-text editor storing
HTML: everybody edits, everybody reads, so stored HTML would let one account run script in every
colleague's browser. Only http/https become links, and a quote cannot break out of one. Preview asks
the server (`/api/portal/kb/preview`), so what is previewed is what is saved.

**Pictures** go up the moment they are pasted (`/api/portal/kb/images`, one per request), are
identified by their first bytes (JPEG, PNG, WEBP — the photo service's `SniffType`), stored under
`data/knowledge/{tenant}/` (inside `data/`, so in the nightly backup), served only to the same company
(`/portal/kb/image/{id}`), and **never deleted** — an old version may still show one. Both portal
writes need the `X-Kb: 1` header as well as the cookie, as office chat's need `X-Chat`.

### What building it found — read these before the next form or header

- **A Razor form with an `action` written out does NOT get its antiforgery token by itself.** The
  editor's form names its action (so a refused write-up does not post the ticket number again), and
  Save was refused in a real browser — a blank page. **`kbcheck` had passed 108 of 108 against it**,
  because its form helper took the token from ANYWHERE on the page, and the menu's Sign out form
  always has one. Fixed with `asp-antiforgery="true"`; the harness now takes the token only from
  **the form being posted** (`FormOf`), and drops to 70 of 108 with the attribute out. Any harness
  that posts a form should do the same.
- **The console's header was already full.** `dashtabs` measured it: a seventh button put the
  left-most one over the company's name at 1366 px. `BrandHeader` now has `TextLimit` (its words end in
  "…" before the first button) and `TextRight`; `LayoutHeader` lets **Light/Dark step out of the header
  when there is no room**, and it is on the tray menu always, so it is never lost.
- **A status-bar pill capped at a number of pixels** cut its words off at 150% scaling ("Knowledge
  base fo"). It is capped at a third of the bar, and a client name too long for that leaves the pill
  saying *Knowledge base (3)* — the Tools line has the full name. **Docking puts the LAST-added
  left-most**, so the pill is moved to index 1 (just above the Fill label) to sit after the
  connection pill, not before it.
- **Razor writes 📘, • and — as character references**, so a harness comparing page text must decode
  it first (and keep the raw page for injection checks).
- The story layout titles a ticket with `tk-title`, not an `<h1>` — `kbcheck`'s first run asserted an h1.

## 81. Processes and Performance, without connecting — 2026-10-05

Clint: right-click a machine in the console, **Processes** or **Performance**, *"so that the
technician can see performance before even connecting"*. His answers when asked: **straight through on
every online machine, attended or unattended — no consent prompt and no unattended password**, because
it is *"just to give one an idea before deciding on connecting or not"* (he first said "ask on
attended", then changed it); **look only** — no End task; **nothing logged, no ticket**. Then, while it
was being built: the Network card must say whether the machine is on a **Private or Public** network
(*"this can solve quite a few problems at a glance"*) **and its IP address**.

Same day, smaller: the machine list's right-click has **Chat** (points the one chat card at that
machine and puts the cursor in the message box; `dashtabs`).

### What it is

- **Not the customer's Task Manager.** That is a window on their screen; showing it would be a session.
  The console draws its own two pages from figures the machine sends once a second, so nothing appears
  on the customer's screen. `MachineWatchForm`: one window per machine with both pages — the menu item
  only chooses the page it opens on; a second click on the same machine brings that window forward.
- **Processes**: name, PID, user, CPU (share of the whole machine, as Task Manager), memory (private
  working set, Task Manager's column). Sorted busiest first; any heading sorts. Rows are updated in
  place, so selection and scroll survive each refresh.
- **Performance**: four cards with the last minute drawn — Processor, Memory, Disk (busiest physical
  disk's active time, read/write), Network (receive + send) — and **one line per connected network**:
  *Private network · 192.168.1.115 · Wi-Fi "AnywhereIT"*. **Public is amber and says "sharing off"**:
  a network Windows calls Public has file sharing and discovery off by default, and nothing else on
  screen would say so. Hover the card for the lines uncut. Uptime, processes and threads underneath.
- **It says when the figures stop** — *"X went offline"*, *"closed the support app"*, *"no figures for
  N seconds"* — and never leaves a frozen graph looking live. It starts again by itself when the
  machine comes back or the console reconnects.

### How it works, and the rules

- `Shared/MachineWatcher.cs` measures, **once however many technicians look**, and only while somebody
  does. Processes come from ONE `NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation)` call, which gives
  every process's times and memory **without opening it** — so a protected or other-account process
  still shows CPU and memory (`Process.GetProcesses` cannot: its CPU time opens a handle). Disk through
  PDH by ENGLISH counter names. Networks through the **Network List Manager's typed COM interfaces** —
  late binding (`dynamic`) was tried first and Windows refused it with E_INVALIDARG; `watchcheck`
  measured that, and a swallowed failure had shown "Not connected to any network" on a connected PC.
- `DeviceLink.OfferWatch()` — ONE place, called by the agent AND the tray app — says `DeviceCan.Watch`
  and runs the watcher on `WatchRunMsg`; it stops the moment the connection goes.
- `Hub/TenantHub.Watch.cs`: the first console to open a machine sends `WatchRunMsg{On}`, the last to
  close sends Off; a console that disappears is taken off everything (`ForgetWatcher`). **The agent
  sends where connected** (as SYSTEM it names every process's account; the tray app sees only its own
  person's), the tray app otherwise, and **takes over** if the agent restarts. Figures go ONLY to the
  consoles that opened that machine, with `DeviceId` filled in by the server; **figures from a
  connection that was not asked are dropped and it is told to stop**. Exit in the tray app ends a look
  like a session. `DeviceInfo.CanWatch` greys the menu items with *(update the support client)* on an
  older client — never a blank window — and an older client is never sent a message it cannot read.
- **Deliberately absent**: any message that changes the machine, any consent or password check, any
  ticket or session row. Do not add an End task without asking Clint; it was asked and he said no.

### Found while building it

- **Column widths written as numbers** cut PID and CPU to "117…" at 150% (§30 again); measured from the
  font now, Name takes what is left. `Themed()` ListViews now right-align a column added with
  `HorizontalAlignment.Right` (no existing list had one).
- **Black corners on the tab buttons** in this window only — the rounded button paints into a buffer
  and nothing filled the square outside the rounding. `TabButton` fills it with what it sits on. Found
  by enlarging the picture; `watchprobe` reads the corner pixel now. Its first version read the wrong
  pixel and passed — the check that the capture is of the window at all is there because of that.
- `dashtabs`' Chat test clicked a menu item and left activation elsewhere, so a later screen-reading
  check read another window; it now waits and re-activates.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/watchcheck` | **New, 57.** Part 1 measures THIS PC with the real watcher against independent answers: memory vs .NET, process count vs .NET, its own PID, name, memory and owner, lsass listed without being opened, PID 4 = System/SYSTEM, a thread spinning 1.5 s showing as one core (12.0% of 12.5%), and **every network's Private/Public, adapter and IP against `Get-NetConnectionProfile`/`Get-NetIPAddress`**. Part 2, a platform of its own with two technicians: attended straight through with nobody asked, no session, only the opener gets figures, two watchers measure once, last out stops it; unattended WITH a password — Connect refused, a look allowed; agent preferred, stray figures dropped and stopped, tray app takes over, offline said; an older client answered with what to do; a console vanishing stops the machine; Exit ends it; **no ticket and no session row**. **50 of 53 with the stray guard and `ForgetWatcher` taken out.** |
| `tools/watchprobe` | **New, 68.** The real window with real figures from this PC, light and dark, at 150%: asking → live → stopped wording, one row per process, busiest first, selection kept, Name sorts, every column holds its widest entry, tab corners the window's colour, four cards with room, the real network line with its address, a Public network amber, the address readable at the opening size with two networks. PNGs beside it. |
| `dashtabs` | 110 → **120**: Chat, and Processes/Performance enabled / *(update the support client)* / *(offline)*, one window per machine, closing forgets it. |
| re-run | `trayexit`, `unattendedwire`, `unattendedpw`, `consentwire --no-host`. |

**Not proved: the agent measuring as SYSTEM on a real customer machine** (process owners filled in,
the Network List Manager answering in session 0). Every harness here ran as the person.

### Deploying it

**Platform deploy (no migration), a FULL ship and a client reinstall** — the figures come from the
agent and the tray app, so a machine shows *(update the support client)* until it is reinstalled. On
the live instance: `deploy\Publish-Platform.ps1 -Server 154.65.110.136`, technicians re-download the
console from `/tech/anywhereit`, customers reinstall from their download link. `TEST-3.6.md` section
AY, checks 343–349.

## 82. One sign-in at a time — 2026-10-05

Clint: *"The system must also not allow more than one simultaneous sign in. If they log into a second
machine it must automatically log them out of the first machine and request a code again incase it
someone trying to hack the system."* Asked whether a console plus a portal counts as two, he chose
**one console and one browser per person**, the console's own Tickets hand-off not counting as a new
sign-in. The decision is recorded in `PRICING.md`, "Decided 2026-10-05".

### What it is

- **Consoles.** Every console sign-in revokes every OTHER console token of that person
  (`AuthService.ReplaceConsoles`) and the hub closes those consoles and their session windows
  (`TenantHub.SignOutTechnician(..., keepToken)`), saying why. Tokens are in memory, as before.
- **Browsers.** `Technician.BrowserSignIn` names the one browser sign-in; the cookie carries it as
  the `signin` claim, `b:{id}`. A sign-in on another browser replaces it, and the old cookie is
  refused on its next page (`CookieCheckAsync`, the same 15-second cache as the stamp). The sign-in
  page says why, once (the `rsp_out` cookie). Portal **Sign out** empties the slot.
- **The Tickets hand-off** is `c:{id}`: good while the console that made it is signed in, never
  touching `BrowserSignIn`. A cookie from before this has no claim and stays good until the person
  next signs in on a browser.
- **Somewhere else.** Each console (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\RemoteSupport\console-id`, per Windows user) and
  each browser (`rsp_device` cookie, a year) sends a random id of its own. Neither is a secret; they
  only decide whether a sign-in already held is on THIS machine. Signing in when another machine
  holds the slot: **the code is asked even with a good trust token**, with a notice (`SignInResult.Notice`,
  `notice` on `/api/login`; the console's code window shows it in ink, not red), and on completion
  **`Technician.TrustStamp` moves**, voiding every 7-day trust on every machine — so the first PC is
  asked for the code too. The trust token is bound to `SecurityStamp + TrustStamp`; with no
  `TrustStamp` yet that is exactly the old binding, so the deploy itself voids nobody's trust.
- **Exit and Sign out in the console** call `POST /api/logout` (new, Bearer), so signing in on another
  PC afterwards pushes nobody off and asks no extra code.
- **The same PC** signing in again (a second copy, Sign out and back) closes the old console with
  *"…on this computer…"*, asks no code, and voids no trust.

### The traps

- **A page that re-issues the portal cookie must carry the `signin` claim over**
  (`PortalIdentity.SignInOf`) — `Account` and `Appearance` do. Without it the re-issued cookie has no
  claim, which is refused as soon as the person has a browser sign-in: the page would sign itself out.
- **Live-server harnesses now sign the console out.** Anything that signs in with
  `tools/rs-credentials.json` against the live server ends the console of whoever that account is.
  Keep that file on a test account, not Clint's.
- **An old console** (before this) sends no device id, so EVERY sign-in from it while another console
  of that person is live counts as somewhere else and asks the code. The `-OnlyTechnician` ship (or the
  re-download) fixes that.
- **The rule is per person, not per seat.** It stops one login being shared; it does not count seats.
  Seats are the next piece of work (`PRICING.md`).

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/onesignin` (new) | **42 of 42**, a platform of its own with two-factor ON. The same PC again (no code, old console closed with "this computer"); another PC (code asked over a good trust token, the notice, nobody signed out while it is only asked, the old console told and closed in ~330 ms, its token dead); Exit via `/api/logout`, then the first PC's old trust asks the code, and a third PC with the NEW trust goes straight in; browsers (same browser again fine, another asked the code with the notice, the first lands on sign-in saying why — once — and is asked the code, the console untouched throughout, the console's trust voided too); the Tickets hand-off (not a new browser sign-in, dies with its console). **With the three guards out — the code on a trusted PC, closing the other consoles, the browser check — it drops to 28.** |
| the self-contained harnesses | **27 re-run.** 23 passed untouched (signincheck 20, handoffcheck 45, rolecheck 72, techdownload 22, dashtabs 120, chatcheck 51, clipledger 20, consentwire 34, devicelink 20, healthcheckwire 52, invitecheck 51, kbcheck 108, mailintakecheck 135, mentionwire 9, sessionextras 26, ticketwire 31, trayexit 16, unattendedpw 33, unattendedwire 13, voicewire 37, watchcheck 57, webchatcheck 80, websupportcheck 64). **Four signed the same person in twice and went on using the first token** — exactly what the rule now closes — and were changed to use the latest, as a real console does: `securitycheck` (now **76**: every console sign-in from one harness PC, and the People-page sign-out watched on the console signed in last), `appearancecheck` 14, `photomany` 21, `reconnectlocal` 20 (its session windows now reuse the console's token instead of signing in for each). |

**Not on hardware.** Platform deploy (**migration `OneSignInAtATime`**) and the console re-download
(`-OnlyTechnician` locally). No client reinstall. `TEST-3.6.md` section AZ, checks 350–356.

## 83. Seats are a price the owner agrees to — 2026-10-05 (roadmap 4.7)

Clint: *"When adding users, the system seems to allow as many as one wants without changing the
pricing. When one adds more than the allotted amount of users, it should prompt them and show an
increase in the price which they must accept or reject. If they reject, it must not add the extra
users."* His answers are in `PRICING.md`, "Decided 2026-10-05": any role costs the same extra seat;
only the owner accepts; a change shows on the NEXT bill; existing companies keep everybody; Anywhere
IT is not billed.

### What was measured first

Seats **were** capped — but only Technician and Supervisor counted (`TenantRoles.Seated`). Office
administrators and an owner-only login were free and unlimited, and the People page said so. That is
what "as many as one wants" was. The price itself knew two regions (`IsSouthAfrica ? R500 : $49`)
and never added anything for extra people.

### What it is now

- **`Services/Pricing.cs` is the one place the prices live** (and `landing/index.html`'s `PRICES`
  for the public page — change both). Five regions: ZA R500 + R300; US and **CA** $49 + $20 (Canada
  pays in US dollars — assumed, in `PRICING.md`); UK £49 + £20; EU €49 + €20. `BillFor` does the
  sum; `RiseIf` says what a change would do; `PriceRise.Token` ("ZA:8:800") is what an agreement
  must name.
- **`Tenant.Seats` is the seats IN THE PACKAGE** (7), no longer a cap. **`Tenant.Region`** is what the
  company pays in, for life; signup works it out from the country (`RegionOfCountry`) until the
  country-first signup exists; the Owner → Tenants country picker and `set-brand country` keep it in
  step. **`Tenant.NotBilled`**: no price, nothing asked — Owner → Tenants, *Not billed* / *Bill them*,
  or `set-brand <slug> not-billed true`.
- **Every role takes a seat** except an owner-only login: `TenantRoles.Paid` (Technician | Admin |
  Billing), which is what `Technician.UsesSeat` asks now. **`TenantRoles.Seated` still means the
  console** — an office administrator pays for a seat and still never reaches it. Do not merge them.
- **The gate is in the service.** `AddTechnicianAsync` and `SetRoleAsync` take `asker` and
  `agreed`: a person past the package must be the owner (`Permissions.CanAcceptPrice`) AND name the
  exact token they were shown — a stale Accept, a supervisor posting the figure, a yes to a different
  figure all add nobody. **`asker` null is the platform's command line and the harnesses** — not asked,
  but the rise is still recorded. `NewPersonProblemAsync` runs the add's own checks first, so nobody is
  asked to agree a price for a person who would be refused anyway.
- **Every yes is a `SeatAgreement` row** (who, what, before → after, when), saved with the change, never
  edited; the Billing page lists them. `SetOwnerAsync` (command line) records the seat an owner-only
  old owner now takes.
- **The People page** asks `PriceRiseAsync` first and, for the owner, draws the question at the top:
  Now / After with the sum, *Accept R… a month* (re-posts the same change with `agreed`) and *Don't do
  it* (`Decline` — "Nobody was added"). A supervisor gets the service's refusal. The heading counts
  seats against the package; past it, a note says what the next person costs. **The Billing page**
  shows the true total, the people in seats by name, and the agreements.
- **The migration `SeatsAndPrice`**: Region from each Country (the same rules in SQL — a blank country
  is ZA, as a command-line company was always meant to be), Seats raised to 7 where lower, NotBilled for
  slug `anywhereit`.

### The traps

- **"Next bill" is only words until 4.8.** Nothing invoices; the Billing total is what the next invoice
  should say. When PayFast arrives, it reads `BillFor` at billing time — do not store a second copy of
  the price on the tenant.
- **A harness that seeds before the migrations gets its seats raised to 7** — `rolecheck` puts its
  company back to 3 after migrating so its checks still fill a package.
- **Razor encodes "×" and "→" from C# strings as entities** (no `WebEncoderOptions` here). A browser
  shows them; a harness must `WebUtility.HtmlDecode` what it reads, as `seatcheck` does.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/seatcheck` (new) | **44 of 44.** The migration on companies written as the product wrote them before it (regions from six countries incl. blank and Australia, packages 7 with one at 10 kept, only `anywhereit` not billed); the sums in all five regions; the service (a supervisor refused with the figure, the owner refused until naming the exact figure, a yes to another figure refused, a yes not reusable, the agreement recorded, an office administrator costing a seat, the owner's own seat gated, removing lowers it, a company not billed never asked); and the pages through a platform of its own (the question, Don't do it, Accept, Billing's total and record, a supervisor told to ask, a supervisor forging the figure refused, a stale Accept refused, not billed). **With the service's gate out and office administrators free again it drops to 21.** Walked in the browser pane at desktop and phone width — which moved the sum under the amount (it was a third column, one word per line on a phone). |
| `rolecheck` | **74** — its cap checks rewritten as price checks (refused until agreed; a supervisor cannot add an office administrator past the package; handing over from the command line works and is recorded). |

**Not on hardware.** **Platform deploy (migration `SeatsAndPrice`)** only — no console download, no
client reinstall. `TEST-3.6.md` section BA, checks 357–364.

## 84. Signup: country first, the region's terms, then the company — 2026-10-05

Clint: *"when signing up, the system must first ask what country they are from with the 5 options we
currently have. this will determine pricing and also add that tenant to the relevant server. The idea
is to have a server in every country … it must also have a country relevant disclaimer including
things like popia act, we are not responsible for loss of data etc etc which the client must
acknowledge before they can set up their tenant."* His answers: a region with no server yet gets a
**waiting list** (never a place on another country's server); **Claude drafts the terms, his lawyer
reviews**, and they say DRAFT until then.

### What it is

- **`/signup` is three steps** (`Pages/Signup.cshtml`): **where** (five cards, each with its price,
  from `Pricing.Regions`), **the terms** for that region (read in a box, one tick — "on behalf of my
  company"), **the company** (the password is typed here only, so it is never carried between steps).
  The region and the terms' **SHA-256** travel in hidden fields; `TenantService.SignupAsync` checks
  both again — not ticked, other terms, or a region this server does not hold, and nothing is made.
  The company, its owner and the acceptance are one transaction.
- **Servers per region** (`Services/RegionServers.cs`): `Platform:Region` is what this server holds
  (`ZA`); `Platform:RegionServers:{code}` is another region's https address. A region here → terms;
  one with a server → a button to its own `/signup?region=`; one with none → the **waiting list**
  (`WaitingListEntry`, the same email in a region updated not duplicated), shown on Owner →
  Approvals with Remove. GO-LIVE.md says how a new region's server is set up.
- **The terms** (`Services/Terms.cs`): `Terms/core.txt` (service, fees, the customer's duties incl.
  permission for every computer, **section 4: we are not responsible for loss of data — keep backups**,
  privacy, security, as-is, liability capped at 12 months' fees, indemnity, ending and deletion,
  changes, law) and `Terms/{ZA,US,CA,UK,EU}.txt` (the privacy law — POPIA operator/responsible party;
  UK GDPR and GDPR Article 28 processor terms; CCPA service provider; PIPEDA — the tax, the governing
  law). **Embedded in the program**, written in `KbText` markup, **[square brackets] for the lawyer**.
  `Terms.Version` and `Terms.Draft` — move the version on any change; set Draft false once approved.
- **What was accepted is kept word for word** (`TermsAcceptance`: text, fingerprint, version, draft,
  who, address, when). The company's Billing page has *Terms accepted on … by …* to unfold.
  `/terms/{region}` shows today's text to anybody.
- **Europe** asks the country (`Pricing.EuropeanCountries`); the others are the region's own name.
  `Region.In` says "the United Kingdom" inside a sentence.

### The traps

- **Walking it in the browser found that the company form looped for ever**: with no handler it
  posted to the address the terms step left (`?handler=Terms`), which ran the terms step again. It
  has its own (`Create`) now, and `signupcheck` checks the form's action. **Any multi-step Razor page
  whose forms post to different handlers must name every handler** — the address bar is not neutral.
- **Signups are still OFF on the live server** (`Platform:SignupsEnabled=false`, and Caddy serves the
  holding page on `/signup`). None of this is public until both change.
- **These terms are a draft by Claude, not legal advice.** Every `[bracket]` needs an answer: VAT in
  or out, the Information Officer and registration, the ICO number, the EU representative, the
  governing law and courts outside South Africa, the notice periods, the deletion period, the address.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/signupcheck` (new) | **39 of 39.** The five regions and prices; the US sent to a configured server; the UK a waiting list (one entry for one email); South Africa's terms (DRAFT, version, POPIA, the data-loss clause in bold, rand and VAT); every region's text whole, with its own law and money; `/terms`; Continue refused without the tick and for stale terms; the company form's own handler; nothing made unticked, with other terms, or for a region not held here; the company made with all three, a duplicate refused with nothing half-made; the region, country, owner, and the terms kept **word for word** with fingerprint, version, draft, who and from where; the Billing page showing them once approved; Europe requiring a European country, and a Europe server refusing South Africa. **With the two service checks and the form's handler out it drops to 34.** Walked in the browser pane. |
| `seatcheck` 44, `rolecheck` 74 | re-run on the new migration chain. |

**Not on hardware.** **Platform deploy (migration `SignupTermsAndWaitingList`)**. No console, no
client. Nothing is visible to the public while signups are off. `TEST-3.6.md` section BB, 365–371.

## 85. Every time in the company's own time zone — 2026-10-05

Clint: *"I see the time zone for Anywhere I.T has changed again. Why is this?"* Then, once the fix was
proposed: *"Time zone should be selected at the start of creating the tenant, because selecting the us
as location still could have different time zones."*

### What was measured

- **There was no company time zone to change.** Every portal time was the SERVER's local time —
  `ToLocalTime()` in 63 places, `DateTime.Now` for "today" and month starts. On the office PC (Windows,
  set to South Africa) that looked right; **the live server is `Etc/UTC`** (Clint ran `timedatectl`), so
  live it was two hours behind. Hence "again": it moved whenever he switched between the two.
- **Nine places printed raw UTC even on the office PC** — Sessions, People's last sign-in and two-factor
  date, pending signups and the waiting list, trial end dates, Billing's agreements and terms.
- **Typed times were read in the server's zone too**: the portal's New Ticket appointment and the ticket
  list's date filter. **Appointments typed on the live portal since 2026-10-01 were saved two hours
  early** (09:00 SAST stored as 09:00 UTC) — they now show two hours late. The console's were right (it
  converts on the PC). They cannot be told apart in the data; check upcoming ones by eye.
- **On Windows no IANA zone could be found at all**: the platform is built with
  `InvariantGlobalization`, and `FindSystemTimeZoneById("Africa/Johannesburg")` throws there (measured
  with a probe). `WebSupportHours.Zone` caught it and used **UTC** — so web chat and browser support
  hours were two hours out whenever the platform ran on Windows. Linux knows the names.

### What it is now

- **`Tenant.TimeZone`** (IANA). **Chosen at signup** on the company step where the region has several —
  the US (incl. Alaska, Hawaii, Arizona), Canada (incl. Newfoundland, Saskatchewan), Europe — and filled
  in for South Africa and the UK (`CompanyClock.MustChoose`, `For(region)`); the service refuses a
  missing or foreign one. Changeable on **Branding**. `set-brand <slug> time-zone <id>` on the CLI.
  Migration `CompanyTimeZone` gives every company its region's zone (Anywhere IT: South Africa).
- **`Services/CompanyClock.cs` is the one clock.** `x.Local()` to show, `CompanyClock.ToUtc(typed)` to
  store, `CompanyClock.Now` for today. Which company is set per request (Program.cs middleware, from the
  signed-in person) and at each hub entry (`TenantHub.UseCompanyClockAsync` — console, machine, session
  and browser-caller sockets). No company (owner pages): `ServerDefault`, this server's region.
  **`Find` tries the IANA name, then the Windows name** carried in `Zones`; an unknown name is South
  Africa, never a silent UTC. `WebSupportHours.Zone`/`Zones` now use it.
- **Never write `ToLocalTime()` or `DateTime.Now` in the platform again.** The console is different: it
  runs on the technician's PC, whose clock is theirs, and keeps `ToLocalTime()`.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/clockcheck` (new) | **33 of 33**, built with `InvariantGlobalization` like the platform. Every offered zone found on Windows with its real offset (Newfoundland −3:30, Hawaii −10…); unknown → South Africa; to the company's time and back; the skipped spring hour read, not refused; web chat hours open at 08:30 SAST (06:30 UTC); the migration's six regions; signup — the US with no zone or a foreign zone refused, US Central kept, South Africa filled in; **the pages on a server whose own clock is South African, for a company in New York**: last sign-in in New York time (not SAST, not UTC), an appointment typed 09:00 stored 13:00 UTC and shown 09:00, Branding switches to London and the page follows at once. **With the request's clock out it drops to 29; without the Windows names, to 23.** (Its first run without `InvariantGlobalization` passed the zone checks against the fault — a harness must be built as the program is.) |

372–376.

## 86. Call outs reschedule; the office is told when a job reaches billing — 2026-10-05

Clint: *"Two things need amending. Call outs need the option to reschedule and when something is
assigned to billing, all office administrators should be notified."* His answers: Reschedule asks the
new date and time **and why**; the office gets **a badge and a pop-up**. In his words in
`docs/NEXT-SESSION-WORKFLOWS.md`, under Call out.

### Reschedule

- **A step in the route, not a field on Details** — `Workflow.Reschedule` (`callout-reschedule`), from
  Call out booked only (after Work done somebody has been out), asking the new **`StageField.Appointment`**
  and a Reason. It goes to **`@stay`**: recorded, and the job stays where it is. Its timeline form has
  **no `MovedTo`** (a step that moved nothing gets no arrow, and the crumb's "came from" is untouched).
  The form reads *New appointment … / Was … / Reason …*; `TicketService.Appointment` is the format, in
  the company's clock.
- **Refused**: no date, a time already passed, the time it is booked for already, no reason.
- **Who**: the people on the job and supervisors (the bench) **and the office** — the customer phones
  the office to move it. That is the new **`ActionDef.OfficeToo`**, asked through **`Workflow.MayPress`**,
  which `ActionsFor` and `ActAsync` now both use instead of `MayAct` directly.
- **Portal**: date and time inputs starting at the current appointment, read with
  `CompanyClock.ToUtc` (`yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, invariant); a refusal keeps what was typed
  (`RescheduleDate/Time`). **Console**: two `DateTimePicker`s, the PC's clock to UTC as New ticket does,
  kept in `_drafts`; `TicketActMsg.AppointmentUtc`. An older console simply never sends one — the server
  then refuses "Choose the new date and time".

### The billing queue tells the office

- **Who is told is `Permissions.HearsOfBilling(role, companyHasOfficeAdmin)`**: every office
  administrator; in a company with none, supervisors and the owner (answer 16). **Never both** — a
  supervisor beside an office administrator would be told of somebody else's work.
- **The badge counts jobs in the Office lane NOT on hold** (`TicketService.BillingWaitingAsync`): the
  ones the office must DO something with. Awaiting payment, waiting on a supplier, awaiting collection are
  in the queue but waiting on somebody else — counting them would light the badge for weeks (account
  customers sit on Awaiting payment, answer 13). So it is not the same number as the Billing queue
  list, which shows those too, on purpose.
- **`ActAsync` is still the only thing that moves a stage**, so it is where the news starts: after the
  save, any step touching the Office lane raises **`TicketService.BillingChanged`** with a
  **`BillingNews`** (count, who is told, and — only when the job came INTO the lane from outside — a
  `BillingArrival`). `SendForDeliveryAsync` raises it too (it leaves the lane). Listeners never pop the
  arrival at the person who caused it (`Arrived.By`).
- **Portal**: the badge is `#billingBadge` beside *Billing queue* in `_Layout` (`BillingBadgeForAsync`;
  null = not one of the people told, no badge). The live stream `/api/portal/chat/stream` carries
  `event: billing`; `chat.js` moves the badge and draws `.bill-pops` top right (clear of the chat
  corner), amber, staying until closed or opened, four at most, a browser notification when the tab is
  behind.
- **Console**: `BillingQueueMsg` (`billing_queue`) — at sign-in (`PushBillingCountAsync`) and on every
  change (`PushBilling`, wired in `HubRegistry`). **One count on the Tickets button** (mentions + billing,
  Clint's one-control rule; the tooltip says which), and it opens on the billing queue when there is no
  reply waiting. `BillingPopup` sits bottom right, never takes the keyboard (`ShowWithoutActivation`),
  heights measured from its fonts (§30). An older console ignores the message.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `calloutcheck` | **68 of 68** (52 before). Reschedule offered to the technician on it, the office and a supervisor, not a colleague, and refused when pressed anyway; refused without a time, with a past time, with the same time, without a reason, and none of those changed anything; accepted: stays at Call out booked with the same people, ONE form with new/was/reason and no arrow; the office moves it again; gone after Work done, refused if pressed. |
| `tools/billingwire` (new) | **37 of 37**, a platform of its own: the rule (office administrators; supervisors only with none; never a technician); Oscar's console (office administrator + technician) and **Olive's PORTAL page** (office administrator only, signed in through the form) told the count at sign-in; Reschedule from Sue's console crosses the socket to the minute, a past one refused in words, and tells the office nothing; Work done tells nobody; to be invoiced pops up on Oscar's console AND Olive's stream with the job, number, stage and sender — not Sam (supervisor), not Sue; Olive's page then says *1 to do*; Oscar invoices it — count 0, no pop-up, on both; a company with no office administrator tells its supervisor, and company A hears nothing of B; a supervisor who sends one himself gets the count without a pop-up. **With the pop-up on every move into the lane, and the supervisors' fallback out, it drops to 30.** |
| everything else | `workflowcheck` 100, `routecheck` 53, `deliverycheck` 48, `machinescheck` 56, `ticketwire` 31, `mentionwire` 9, `chatcheck` 51, `ticketwindowprobe` 156, `dashtabs` 120. **The console's Reschedule form (the two date pickers) and `BillingPopup` are drawn by no probe** — TEST-3.6.md 379 and 383. |

(A browser keeps the old `chat.js` until the `?v=` build stamp moves, i.e. the next commit.) |

## 87. Outside help, step 1: the switches and the customer's code — 2026-10-06 (roadmap 3.9)

Clint was asked how a customer of ours gets help from somebody OUTSIDE the IT company — their
accounting firm — and suggested *"the client generate[s] a code"*; then widened it to another company
on the platform, with the local technicians able to watch and end it. His four answers are in roadmap
3.9. **Step 1 of 4: who may make a code, and the code itself. Nothing can be connected to with one
yet** — the hub still refuses any viewer from another company (`/ws/session`), and a guest has no way
in at all. Step 2 (another company with a code) is next.

### The rule — `OutsiderAccess` (Shared), the ONE place

- **Allowed = the machine set On, or the machine "as the company" and the company switch on.** The
  company switch (`Tenant.OutsidersAllowed`) is **off by default**; a machine's own choice
  (`Device.OutsiderMode`: 0 as the company, 1 on, 2 off) overrides it **either way** — Clint: *"off
  being default, but can be toggled per machine."* So a company can keep it off and open one machine.
  This differs on purpose from the health check (§50), whose company switch wins over everything.
- **Who may switch it: a supervisor or the owner** (`Permissions.CanAllowOutsiders`) — company and per
  machine. It decides whether outsiders can reach the machines the company looks after. My choice,
  not Clint's; widen it in that one method if he wants technicians to.
- **A code**: nine digits from `RandomNumberGenerator`, ten minutes, **used once**, unique among live
  codes on the server (it is typed with no company beside it). `Format` reads it in threes; `Clean`
  takes spaces and dashes. Who it is for is required — it is shown when it is used.

### The server

- **`OutsiderCodeService`** holds the codes; the hub holds the switches. **Only a SHA-256 hash (with a
  fixed pepper) is stored** (`OutsiderCodes` table, migration `OutsideHelp`); the digits exist only in
  the one reply that made them. Rows are KEPT after use or stop — the record of who was let in. A new
  code stops the machine's live one (*replaced*); one machine, one code.
- **Spending a code** (`RedeemAsync`) is written and proved now, used by nothing until step 2. It is a
  conditional update, so two people typing it at once get one machine between them. **The guess limit
  is on the GUESSER** (five wrong in fifteen minutes, keyed by whatever step 2 passes — an account or an
  address), because a wrong code names no machine to lock, unlike §77. Blanks never count. Every
  failure has the same words, so a guesser learns nothing about which numbers were once real.
- **`TenantHub.Outsiders.cs`**: `ApplyOutsider` (like `ApplyHealth`), `TellDeviceItsOutsiderStateAsync`
  (on connect — from the registered-connection point, §33 — and after the stored record loads, and
  after every change). **Only the CLIENT connection may make or stop a code** (§31's rule; the agent is
  refused and logged). `SetDeviceOutsiderModeAsync` is the ONE write path for a machine (console and
  portal); `RefreshOutsidersAsync` follows the company switch. **Switching it off — for a machine or
  the company — stops every code it no longer allows, at once**, recording who.
  `HubRegistry.Outsiders` is set by Program.cs like `Knowledge`. The mode survives a reinstall with the
  machine's row (`PersistDeviceAsync`).
- `OutsiderStateMsg` tells the tray app *allowed*, and who the live code is for and until when — never
  the digits again.

### The screens

- **Tray app**: *Let someone else connect…* under the unattended items, **hidden, not greyed**, where it
  is not allowed — off for most machines, and a greyed item nobody can use is a question nobody can
  answer. `OutsiderCodeDialog`, two faces: **the scam warning first** (*"Nobody legitimate phones you
  out of the blue and asks for a code"*) and *Who is it for?*; then the code, large, in threes, with the
  minutes left, *Stop this code*, *Make a new code*, and *"you will be asked to Allow them, by name… press
  Deny"*. Not modal — the code arrives from the server into it. Told when the code stops elsewhere.
- **Console**: right-click a machine → *Outside help* (a now-line, *As the company (on/off)*, *On / Off
  for this machine*), beside the health check. The console does not know the role, so the server
  refuses a technician in words.
- **Portal → Outside help** (owner and supervisors; added to the admin page list in Program.cs): the
  company switch, every machine with its own setting (a dropdown that saves on change), and the last 25
  codes with what became of each. It says plainly that connecting is still being built.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/outsidercode` (new) | **53 of 53.** The rule (all four combinations, unknown modes, the format, who may switch); the codes in-process — nine digits, ten minutes, hash only (the digits nowhere in the row), replaced stops the old, typed with spaces works and is recorded as used by whom, ONCE, the same words for spent and never-existed, stop, expiry, **five wrong lock the guesser and not someone else, blanks are not guesses, six people racing one code → exactly one**; the wire on a platform of its own — the tray app told *not allowed* by default and refused a code; a technician refused in words; the supervisor's per-machine On reaches the tray app at once and every console's list; the AGENT cannot make a code; the code, the live line without the digits, who made it; stop; **Off for the machine with a code live stops it, saying who**; the portal page for a supervisor and NOT a technician (the heading asserted, §34); company on → the following machine told, the Off machine not; company off → told, live code stopped; the page lists the codes. **With the agent let through and the switch-off stop removed: 50.** |
| `tools/fitprobe` | **164** (was 126): both faces of the code window, light and dark, at this PC's scaling — every label fits, nothing overlaps, every button inside the window. Looked at, too: it found the buttons touching (a right-to-left row's gap belongs on the RIGHT margin) and an empty band on the code face, now the Deny line. |
| re-run | `unattendedpw` 33, `unattendedwire` 13, `unattendedcheck` 40, `healthcheckwire` 52, `devicelink` 20, `dashtabs` 120, `trayexit` 16, `billingwire` 37, `calloutcheck` 68. |

**Not on hardware.** **Platform deploy (migration `OutsideHelp`), re-download the console, and a client
reinstall** for the tray app. `TEST-3.6.md` section BE, 385–391. Nothing it adds lets anybody connect.
