## 88. Terms, refunds and privacy on the landing page, for PayFast — 2026-10-06

Clint: *"Payfast is asking that we have a terms and conditions section on our current landing page."*
PayFast checks a merchant's site for **terms and conditions linked from the home page, a refund
policy, a privacy policy (POPIA), and the business's contact details and address**. His answers:
**cancel any time, no part-month refunds, a payment in error refunded in full within 30 days**; **not
VAT registered**; **publish South Africa's terms as final** (his lawyer may revise them later as a new
version); **the Information Officer is Clint, not yet registered** with the Information Regulator.

### What it is

- **South Africa's terms are final** (`Terms.IsDraft("ZA")` false, version `2026-10-06`): every
  [bracket] answered — no VAT, 14 days' late payment, 30 days' notice, 60 days to delete data, the
  Western Cape High Court, 19 Tide Street (the CIPC registered office), queries@ and 078 131 5618.
  Section 11 is now **Cancelling, refunds and ending the agreement**. The other regions stay DRAFT
  with their brackets until they open. Signup shows the version under the heading now.
- **A privacy policy**, `Terms/privacy-ZA.txt` (`Terms.PrivacyHtml`): what is collected and why
  (the site sets no cookies and loads nothing from elsewhere; the region choice stays in the
  visitor's browser), who else sees it (xneelo, PayFast, the mail provider), how long, how it is
  protected, POPIA rights, the Information Officer, the Information Regulator.
- **The landing page's LEGAL block** — company, registration number, address, five refund points,
  and the terms and the privacy policy folded under their headings — is **written, never hand-edited**:
  `RemoteSupport.Platform landing-legal <full path to landing\index.html>` (`Services/LandingLegal.cs`)
  rewrites what sits between the `LEGAL:BEGIN`/`LEGAL:END` markers from the same `Terms/` files signup
  shows. The footer names the company and links **Terms and conditions**, **Refund policy** and
  **Privacy policy**; a click opens the folded part.
- **`Publish-Platform.ps1 -LandingOnly`** puts just the page live: renders it as a full deploy does,
  copies the one file to `/var/www/landing/index.html`, restarts nothing. A full deploy carries it too.

### The traps

- **Never run `Publish-Landing.ps1 -Server` against the live server.** It is from before the platform
  went live: it rewrites `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile` for a landing-only site (cutting the platform off) and
  installs Caddy from the expired apt repository. Its header says so now.
- **Change `Terms/` → run `landing-legal` → commit both.** `legalcheck` fails until the page matches.
  `dotnet run` does not resolve a relative path for it; give the full path.
- **Public promises to keep true**: the privacy policy says the servers are backed up nightly and
  encrypted (`go-live.sh` step 6 — **confirm it is running on the live server**: `ls /var/backups/rsp`),
  and that enquiries are answered within 30 days. There is **no cancel button** in the portal, so the
  terms say cancel by email or phone; add one before saying otherwise.
- **Register the Information Officer** on the Information Regulator's eServices portal (free), then add
  the registration number to `Terms/ZA.txt` and the privacy policy.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/legalcheck` (new) | **16 of 16.** The page's block is exactly what `landing-legal` writes today (it **failed** when the privacy text changed until the page was regenerated); no [bracket] or {{placeholder}} in South Africa's terms or the privacy policy; ZA final and the others draft; only the contact placeholders Publish-Landing fills; PayFast's list — the three footer links each landing on something that exists, the company/registration/address, email and phone, the refund points and the terms' own refund section saying the same, the data-loss clause, POPIA/Information Officer/Regulator/PayFast in the privacy policy, rand with no VAT. Walked in the browser pane, desktop and phone (no sideways scroll), which found "cancel … from your account" — there is no such button — and the remembered currency the privacy policy had not mentioned. |
| `signupcheck` | **39** — South Africa's terms final, with the version shown and no VAT. |

**Not on hardware.** `deploy\Publish-Platform.ps1 -Server 154.65.110.136 -LandingOnly` for the page
alone, or a full deploy. `TEST-3.6.md` section BF, 392–395 (renumbered 2026-10-06: it had been given BD and 377–380, already the call out checks of §86).

## 89. Outside help, step 2: another company connects with a code — 2026-10-06 (roadmap 3.9)

Clint: *"Two signed up tenants may compliment each other in the work they do, so cross tenant option
would be good using the same principle. This would still need to be a multiple connection option, so
that the local tech can watch what is going on and terminate the connection if necessary."* Step 2 of
4: a technician of ANOTHER company on this server, in their own console, signed in as themselves,
connects to a customer's machine with the code that customer made (§87). **This is the first time the
hub lets anybody from outside a company into one of its sessions; read this section before touching
`/ws/session`, `RunSessionViewerAsync`, the host relay or `StartSession`.**

### The path

1. **The visitor's console**: *Connect with a code…* beside Connect (`CodeEntryDialog`, digits only, the
   server's own reading) → `OutsiderConnectMsg` to THEIR company's hub.
2. **Their hub** (`ConnectWithCodeAsync`) spends the code through `OutsiderCodeService.RedeemAsync` with
   a **check that runs BEFORE it is spent** — so a refusal leaves the code working: a code for the
   visitor's OWN company (*"that is what Connect is for"*), a machine no longer allowed, closed, offline,
   already in a session (joining one would skip the Allow), or whose app might not ask (below). The
   guess limit is keyed on `tech:{tenant}:{technician}`.
3. **The machine's hub** (`StartVisitAsync`, reached through `HubRegistry.Get`) starts the session
   itself — **never `StartSession`**, whose unattended path hands an agent a session WITHOUT asking.
   `PickVisitHost`: an agent that says `AskConsent`, else a tray app that says the new
   **`DeviceCan.AlwaysAsk`**. `StartSessionMsg` carries `AskConsent = true` and **`VisitorCompany`**.
   The agent fallback (`FallBackToClientAsync`) keeps both, and ends the session if no tray app can ask.
4. **The person is ALWAYS asked.** This found a real hole: **the tray app asked only when the company's
   BRANDING had Require consent on** (`_brand.RequireConsent`). It now asks when the server says so too
   (`RequireConsent || AskConsent`), and says `AlwaysAsk` so the server knows it will. An older tray app
   is never handed a visit (*"too old for this"*). The prompt (`ConsentPrompt`, `--visitor` from both the
   tray app and the agent) says *"… They are NOT from {company}"*, that they can see and control but not
   copy files or run anything, that the company is told, and *"If you did not give them a code, press
   Deny"* — the old text promised file transfer and scripts.

### Who gets in, and what they may do

- **`/ws/session` (Program.cs)** lets a viewer from another company through ONLY if
  `hub.AdmitsVisitor(id, who)`: that session's `Visitor`, same company AND same technician.
  `RunSessionViewerAsync` asks again (`IsTheVisitor`) — two locks. A colleague of the visitor, or
  anybody else, is refused.
- **Labels, not names.** Everywhere this company sees the visitor — `StartedBy`, `Technicians`,
  `Visitor`, the ticket, the prompt — it says *"Victor Visitor (Smith & Co IT)"*. The visitor's OWN
  console is sent a copy (`TellVisitor`, from `BroadcastTechs`) with `StartedBy` = their bare name and
  `Visiting = true`, because the console opens what `StartedBy` says it started — and a technician HERE
  with the same name would otherwise have had the session open on their screen.
- **Two allow-lists**, so a message added to the protocol later is the visitor's only when somebody
  decides: **`VisitorMaySend`** — Subscribe, Quality, Mouse, Key, Ping (End is handled first); their
  binary is dropped (it is files and voice). **`VisitorMaySee`** — Monitors, SysInfo, Cursor, Privacy
  state, Participants, Error, Ping, Ended; binary only `Tiles`, `Video`, `Cursor` by its first byte. So
  the visitor never receives a file or the clipboard this company's own technician asked for, nor the
  machine's sound. **The customer's chat and Ctrl+Alt+Del results skip the visitor too** (`RouteChat`
  and the `SysActionResult` relay). A refused message is logged once per kind per session. **Files on
  the customer's tick (Clint's answer 2) are NOT built: files are simply off.**
- **The session window** (`SessionForm.ApplyVisiting`) hides every tool but Info, and the system-action
  button, and says whose computer it is. The server enforces it either way.

### The machine's own company

- **`OutsiderVisitMsg`** to every console: `VisitorPopup` (red, bottom right, never takes the keyboard,
  stacks) — who, which machine, whose code and for whom; *Watch* opens the session alongside (the
  ordinary join; whoever of theirs joins goes on the ticket, §49); *End it* ends it for everybody; it
  follows the session to *allowed* and *Ended: …* and stays until dismissed.
- **The visitor's going ends it.** Their End ends the session even with this company's technician still
  watching — the Allow was for the visitor, not for a session somebody else carries on. A dropped
  connection gets the grace period (`VisitorMayReturn`, its own token), then ends it.
- **Switching outside help off** — for the machine or the company — ends a visit in progress
  (`EndVisitsNoLongerAllowed`), as well as stopping codes (§87).
- **The ticket**: the machine's open one, or *"Outside help: {visitor}"*; **never assigned to the
  visitor**; with *"… connected to ANN-PC with a code {who} made for "{for whom}""*, the Allow, and the end.

### The visiting company's record

**A line on their own Sessions page** (`RecordForVisitorAsync`, from `LogSessionAsync`): their tenant,
*"ANN-PC ({company}'s customer)"*, their technician, start and end. **No ticket** in their portal — the
roadmap's open question, settled this way for now: they have no client record for that machine, and a
ticket they did not ask for is noise. One step to change if Clint wants one.

### Also fixed on the way

`BillingPopup` (§86) had `AutoEllipsis` on its two-line labels — which in WinForms stops a label
wrapping and cuts it to ONE line (the incoming call alert's own comments say so). Off, with the stage
line given two lines; `fitprobe` now measures it.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/outsidervisit` (new) | **54 of 54**, three companies on a platform of their own, standing in for the customer's tray app and the host. Refused AND unspent: an unknown code, a code for the visitor's own company, a tray app that might not ask, a machine gone offline, a machine already in a session. The visit: the tray app told to host and to ASK, with the visitor's name and company; the visitor's console sees it as his (bare name, visiting); this company's consoles see the label and get the pop-up, the visitor does not, a third company hears nothing; spent, by whom, not twice; waiting → allowed. **The visitor gets in; his colleague and a stranger do not; this company's technician does.** What he may send: mouse, keyboard, subscribe reach the machine — clipboard, a file request, a script, a restart, voice, a file chunk and chat do NOT; this company's technician's clipboard still does. What he is shown: the picture and the pointer — not the file the other technician pulled, the sound, the clipboard, a file list, or the customer's chat. The records: this company's ticket without him on it, saying who / whose code / for whom and the Allow; his company's Sessions line. Ended by the supervisor (he cannot get back in); **his End ends it with somebody still watching**; switched Off ends it; a busy machine refuses a second code unspent; Deny reaches him with why. **With four faults back — the socket check opened, the send list removed, the binary filter removed, AskConsent false — 44.** |
| `tools/fitprobe` | **198** (was 164): the console's code box, the visit pop-up and the billing pop-up, light and dark. **It found that a long name, or a long ticket subject, needed THREE lines** where both pop-ups had two — now three, and a billing subject past 110 characters is cut at a word with an ellipsis. |
| re-run | `consentwire` 34, `unattendedpw` 33, `unattendedwire` 13, `sessionextras` 26, `voicewire` 37, `websupportcheck` 64, `watchcheck` 57, `ticketpersession` 30, `assigncheck` 58, `trayexit` 16, `outsidercode` 53, `billingwire` 37, `dashtabs` 120, `viewonlyprobe` 18, `toolbarprobe` 50. |

**Not on hardware, and the customer's prompt has not been looked at by eye** (it is drawn by the host,
only in a real session). **Platform deploy (no migration), a FULL ship — host, agent and tray app all
changed — and a client reinstall**; both companies' consoles re-downloaded. `TEST-3.6.md` section BG,
396–404. Steps 3 (the guest console) and 4 (the browser viewer) are not built; nor are files on a tick.

## 90. Outside help, step 3: a guest with no account — the guest console — 2026-10-06 (roadmap 3.9)

Clint's original case: a customer's **accounting firm**, who have no account here. Step 3 of 4: the
**guest console** — Clint: *"a generic technician installer that links to that code."* It is the SAME
console .exe again (one file, one signature), from a public page, and it belongs to no company.

### The download

- **`/guest`** — a public page (Pages/Guest.cshtml): what it is, four steps, and **Download the guest
  console** → **`/guest/console.exe`**, the payload's `RemoteSupport.Technician.exe` served as
  **`remote-support-guest.exe`** (`DownloadIdentity.GuestFileName`). With no console built it is a plain
  404 that says so. `/guest` is not on Caddy's holding-page list, so it reaches the platform live.
- **The console recognises a guest copy BEFORE the downloaded-console set-up** (Program.Main →
  `GuestForm.GuestServer`): `--guest [--server URL]`, a Zone.Identifier HostUrl ending
  `/guest/console.exe` (`DownloadIdentity.GuestServerFromZoneIdentifier` — which also gives the
  server), or the guest file name. Otherwise the set-up would try to work out whose console it is and
  ask for a company code. **Nothing is installed**: it runs where it was saved.

### The guest window and the server

- **`GuestForm`**: *Your name* (required), *Your company (if any)*, *The code*, Connect. The rules are
  the server's (`GuestRules.Problem`, `CodeEntryDialog.Problem`). It talks to **`/ws/guest`**; waiting →
  allowed (it opens the ordinary `SessionForm` with `Visiting`, so the tools are hidden) → ended.
- **`GuestVisitor`** (Hub): spends the code with the same pre-spend check as §89 (refused codes are
  kept), **the guess limit keyed on the guest's ADDRESS** (`guest:{ip}`; behind Caddy that is the real
  one, §72's forwarded headers), then starts the visit through the same **`StartVisitAsync`** — so the
  person is always asked, the allow-lists, the pop-up with Watch/End, leaving ends it, and switching
  off ends it are all §89's, unchanged.
- **Who a guest is, is what they typed — and everything says so.** Company = *"Smith & Co Accountants,
  a guest — not checked"* (`GuestRules.CompanyLabel`; *"a guest — not checked"* with no company). That
  label is what the customer's prompt (*"… They are NOT from …"*), the company's pop-up, the ticket and
  the code's record show.
- **A guest's only credential is a token** (`HubRegistry.AddGuest`, `GuestFromToken`): made when their
  code works, sent as `GuestTicketMsg`, accepted by `/ws/session` (after `auth.FromToken`) and then only
  by **`AdmitsVisitor`** for the session their code started — a guest is tenant 0 with a NEGATIVE
  technician id, never a real one. **It dies when their guest connection closes.**
- **No record for the guest's side**: a guest belongs to no company (`RecordForVisitorAsync` returns for
  tenant 0). The machine's company's ticket is the record.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/guestcheck` (new) | **30 of 30.** A guest copy known by where it came from and by its name (a browser's " (2)" too) — a company's console, or a file from elsewhere, never taken for one; a name required, company optional, *not checked* either way. A platform of its own: `/guest` public (heading asserted, §34) and `/guest/console.exe` a plain 404 here, never a sign-in. A real guest: no name refused and the code kept; the token; ANN-PC's app told to ASK with *"…, a guest — not checked"*; the company's pop-up and the code's record say the same; the guest's console sees it as theirs; allowed. **The token opens that session; a made-up token, and a SECOND guest's token, do not**; the company's technician can watch. Mouse through, script and clipboard not; the customer's clipboard and a file not sent. The ticket names the guest as not checked and does not put them on it; **no record for tenant 0**. **Closing the guest connection kills the token**; the guest's End ends it for the watching technician. **Five wrong codes from one address lock it, the right one included, and the real code stays unspent.** With three faults back (the token not revoked, "not checked" dropped, the tenant-0 guard out): **22**. |
| `tools/fitprobe` | **218** (was 198): the guest window, light and dark; guest mode from `--guest` and the file name and NOT for a company's console; its rules are the server's. |
| re-run | `outsidervisit` 54, `outsidercode` 53, `consentwire` 34, `consoleexecheck` 31 (the downloaded console still sets itself up — the guest branch runs first and takes only guest copies), `securitycheck` 76, `onesignin` 42, `unattendedpw` 33. |

**Not driven by any harness: the guest window's own connection** — typing the code in `GuestForm` and

Clint's answer 3: *"both options should be available"* — the guest console (§90) **and a browser page,
installing nothing.** Step 4 of 4. **No server code changed**: the page speaks exactly what the guest

  (±120); keys by **`e.code` → Windows key code**, with the "extended" set (the right-hand Ctrl/Alt, the
  arrows and their block, numpad Enter and /, the Windows keys); keys held are released when the picture
  loses focus. Ctrl+Alt+Del and Windows-key shortcuts stay with the guest's own computer, and the page

Walked in the browser pane against **`tools/guestwebdemo`** (new): a platform of its own with two
machines — **REAL-PC hosted by the real `RemoteSupport.Host.exe` on this PC**, and FAKE-PC hosted by the
tool, which paints a picture and prints every click and key it is sent.

## 92. Outside help: files when the customer ticks it — 2026-10-06 (roadmap 3.9, the last piece)

Clint's answer 2: an outsider gets the screen and control, and **"file transfer only if the customer
ticks it"** for that session. Until now files were simply off for anybody from outside (§89).

### What it is

- **The tick is in the Allow prompt** (`ConsentPrompt`, the host's own window), and only in the prompt
  for somebody from outside: **"Also let them copy files to and from this computer" — unticked** unless
  the person ticks it. The text says *"They cannot run anything, and cannot copy files unless you tick
  the box below."* The person decides once, at the moment they are deciding anyway; nothing else turns
  it on, and it lasts for that session only.
- **`ConsentPrompt.Ask` returns the tick with the answer**; the host sends **`ConsentGrantedMsg.Files`**.
  An older host cannot send it, and absent is no.
- **The hub** keeps it on the session as **`SessionInfo.VisitorFiles`** — only for a session with a

  and the file-set ones) and **file chunks by their first byte, both ways** (`VisitorMaySendBinary`,
  `MaySeeBinary`). **Never the clipboard, scripts, restarts, sound or voice — files are files.** With
  files ticked a visitor can also receive the chunks of a file the company's own watching technician
  pulls: the machine's own files, which the person has just let them copy anyway.
- **What everyone is told**: the ticket — *"…allowed the connection — and ticked that they may copy
  files."* or *"…, without files."*; the company's pop-up — *"allowed it — and ticked that they may copy
  files"*; the visitor's console shows **Files** under Tools (`ApplyVisiting`) and says so in its banner.
  **The browser viewer (§91) has no file tool**: it says files were allowed and to use the guest console.

`fitprobe` now builds the host's real Allow prompt (private, so by reflection; `tools/fitprobe` references

## 93. BUGS #10 fixed: the first copy after a fresh logon reaches the technician — 2026-10-06

Clint asked for the three items left at the bottom of the roadmap; this is the first of them.

### What it was

`ClipboardAccess.WatchPump` waited while the clipboard sequence number read 0 and took the first
non-zero value as its **starting point**. On a machine where nothing had been copied since logon the
counter really is 0, so that first non-zero value **is the person's first copy** — and it was taken as
"where things started" rather than as a change. The second copy got through; the first, the one a
technician asks for first, never did.

The wait was there for a different zero — clipmirror found the first read at process start can come
back 0 while the clipboard is NOT empty — and treating every 0-to-something as a copy would send
whatever was already on the clipboard (§26: the password copied at nine this morning).

### The fix: tell the two zeros apart

A zero is believed — and the change that ends it reported as a copy — only when it **lasted
`RealZeroMs` (2 s)** and **`CountClipboardFormats()` read 0 throughout** (nothing on the clipboard; it
needs no open, like the counter). The start-up blink is one read with something on the clipboard, so it
still only sets the starting point. The host's own write during the zero (a technician's paste, or the
`--put-files` helper, both through `Writing()`) re-bases `_lastSeq` and ends the wait without a report;
the loop reads the counter **before** the flags so a write landing in between is never mistaken for
theirs. The wait now polls every 250 ms rather than every second, so the first copy is as quick as any.

A copy made within two seconds of the host starting on an unused clipboard is still taken as the
starting point — the conservative side: a lost copy, never a leaked one.

### How it is proved

The fault needs a clipboard nobody has used, which is a fresh logon. **A new window station is one**, but
making one needs elevation (`CreateWindowStation` → win32 5 from this unelevated console). So:

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/clipfirst` | **11 of 11**, simulated: the REAL watcher, handed a counter and a format count it drives (`ClipboardAccess(sequence, formats)`, the harness parameters — `null` is Windows'). Unused clipboard then a copy → reported, and the next; the start-up blink → not reported; a long zero WITH formats → not reported; a zero under 2 s → not; something there before the session → not, the next copy is; the host's own write first → not, the person's next copy is. **With the new rule switched off: 9 of 11 — the first copy is lost, which is BUGS #10.** |
| `tools/clipfirst --station` | The same against Windows itself, each case in a fresh window station with a copy of the harness started inside it. **9 of 9, run elevated by Clint 2026-10-06** (`tools\Run-ElevatedChecks.ps1`): a fresh window station really does start at sequence 0, and its first copy is reported. |
| `tools/clipmirror` | 18 of 18 — the watcher and its echo guard unchanged on this laptop's own clipboard. |

**Not on hardware.** **A FULL ship (the host) and a client reinstall; no platform restart.**
`TEST-3.6.md` section BK, 421–422.

## 94. Wake-on-LAN, through another of the customer's machines — 2026-10-06 (roadmap 1.8)

Clint asked for the last roadmap items; for Wake-on-LAN he chose **"via another of their PCs"** —
no setup on the customer's router. (Microsoft 365 sign-in for email tickets: **"leave it for now"**.)

### What it is

- **Right-click an OFFLINE machine → Wake up**, straight under Connect. Hidden on a machine that is on;
  greyed with *(its network card is not known yet)* when the server has never been told its card.
  The answer is a message box: *"The wake-up was sent from HELPER-PC. SLEEPER-PC should turn green
  within a couple of minutes. If it does not, Wake-on-LAN is probably switched off in its BIOS or
  network card settings — or it is on Wi-Fi only, which seldom wakes."* — or why not, in words.
- **Every machine reports its network cards at every connect** (`HelloMsg.Cards`, `WakeOnLan.Cards()`):
  the MAC of each physical cable or Wi-Fi card, connected or not (a laptop on Wi-Fi is woken through
  its cable card), and the IPv4 networks it is on (`192.168.1.0/24`). Virtual adapters and locally
  administered MACs are left out. The server keeps them, and **the address the machine connected
  from** — its site's internet address, the real one behind Caddy — on the `Device` row
  (`NetworkCardsJson`, `PublicAddress`; migration **`WakeOnLan`**), because the machine is off when
  anybody needs them. `DeviceInfo.CanWake` says the server knows enough.

### Who sends it — `Hub/TenantHub.Wake.cs`

- A machine connected **from the same internet address** as the sleeping one last was, **sharing one of
  its networks** — either alone is not enough (every office has a 192.168.1.0/24; a building can share
  an address) — that says **`DeviceCan.Wake`** (an older client is never asked) and was not closed by its
  person. **The same customer's machine**, when the sleeping one is linked to a customer; an unlinked one
  may be woken by any of the company's machines at that place. **The agent first.**
- **The sender is handed MAC addresses only** (`WakeSendMsg`), never an address to send to.
  `WakeOnLan.Send` broadcasts the magic packet (FF×6, the MAC ×16) on ITS OWN networks: from a socket
  bound to each of its IPv4 addresses, to 255.255.255.255 and that network's broadcast, ports 9 and 7.
  **A wake request cannot be turned into traffic aimed anywhere.**
- `DeviceLink.OfferWake()` — one place, called by the agent and the tray app — answers `WakeSentMsg`.
  **Only the connection that was asked may answer** (`w.From != dc` drops anything else); no answer in
  15 s and the technician is told so; only the technician who asked hears any of it.
- Any technician may ask. **Nothing is logged, no ticket** — a wake-up changes nothing but whether the
  machine is on, like its power button.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/wakecheck` | **New, 50.** Part 1, this PC: the magic packet's bytes; MACs and networks written one way; **this PC's cards against `Get-NetAdapter -Physical`** and its networks against `Get-NetIPAddress`; the sender's packets captured before they leave — every network, both broadcasts, ports 9 and 7, only broadcast addresses, a rubbish MAC dropped, no MAC refused; one real send. Part 2, a platform of its own on port 8131, pretend machines each claiming an internet address through X-Forwarded-For (as Caddy sets it): can/can't wake, already on, nobody there, an older client's machine; **another customer's PC on the same network, the customer's PC at another site, on another network, on an older client — none asked**; the right one asked with the MAC only and the technician told which machine sent it; the agent first; a sender's error passed on; **an answer from a machine not asked ignored**; no answer → told after 15 s, and the late answer dropped; an unlinked machine; **a server restart keeps the card**; no ticket, no session row. **With the same-customer rule out: 32 of 42 (it stops). With the stray-answer guard out: 48 of 50.** |
| `tools/dashtabs` | **124** (was 120): no Wake up on an online machine; greyed, saying why, when the card is not known; offered straight under Connect when it is. |

**Not on hardware** — it needs two machines at one place, one switched off with Wake-on-LAN enabled.
**Platform deploy (migration `WakeOnLan`), a FULL ship and a client reinstall** (every machine must
report its card once before it can be woken). `TEST-3.6.md` section BL, 423–426.

## 95. Remote printing, both directions — 2026-10-06 (roadmap 1.8)

Clint chose **both**: the customer's prints on the technician's printer (what TeamViewer and AnyDesk
call remote printing) AND a technician's file on the customer's printer.

### Their print → the technician's printer

- **Tools → Print on my printer** (a tick). Windows' own Print window asks which of the technician's
  printers; the host then adds a printer on the customer's machine named **"Sue Tech's printer
  (Coastal IT Remote Support)"** (`PrintRedirect.PrinterName`: no comma or backslash, ≤ 120 chars).
  The status bar says what it is called there and where it comes out.
- It is **Windows' own "Microsoft Print To PDF" driver on a FILE port** (`Spooler.AddPort` through
  `XcvData`, `AddPrinter` level 2) — no driver of ours. **The XPS writer is NOT an option**: it is absent
  on Windows 11 25H2 (this laptop). The port file is in the PERSON's temp (`…\Temp\RemoteSupport\print\out`)
  because since PrintDemon (CVE-2020-1048) the spooler writes it **as the person who printed**.
- The host polls four times a second: the queue (for the document's name) and the port file; when the
  spooler has closed it and it has stopped growing it is moved aside (`job-….pdf`) and announced
  (`RemotePrintJobMsg`, with the technician's name). **The named technician's console pulls it with the
  ordinary single-file pull** (file id `print-…`; every other console ignores a `print-` offer, so a
  colleague in the same session never saves somebody else's print) and prints it with
  `DocumentPrinter` on the printer chosen. The pull is not also written as a copy (`IsJobFile`), and the
  file is deleted once sent.
- **The known limit, said rather than hidden**: the file port writes the same file for every job, so two
  documents printed within a moment can arrive as one. Every job seen in the queue is counted; one that
  never became a file is told to the technician (*"1 print job was printed too close together and did
  not arrive — ask them to print it again"*).
- The printer goes when it is switched off, when its technician leaves the session (`KeepOnly` on
  `ParticipantsMsg`), when everybody has, at session end, and — **for a host that was killed** — at the
  next host's start (`SweepLeftovers`: recognised by its PORT being a file in the print folder, never by
  name alone).

### The technician's file → their printer

- **Tools → Print a file on their printer…** — an Open window; the file goes with the ordinary
  single-file send to `%PRINT%` (`RemotePaths.PrintStaging` → a folder of its own per job under the
  person's temp), then `PrintFileMsg` asks for it to be printed. **The host prints ONLY from that folder**
  (`HostPaths.IsPrintStaging`: not elsewhere, not climbing out with "..", not a folder whose name merely
  starts the same) — never a file a technician merely names.
- It is printed by **`RemoteSupport.Host.exe --print-file <file> <answer.json>` running AS THE PERSON**
  (`UserProcess`, as `--put-files`): the default printer is per user, and as SYSTEM there is often none.
  It answers in writing — which printer, how many pages, or why not — and `PrintFileResultMsg` brings it
  to the status bar of the console that asked (only that one).

### Printing a document with nothing bought in — `RemoteSupport.Media`

- **`PdfPages`**: Windows' own PDF renderer, **`Windows.Data.Pdf`, called through its vtables by hand.**
  The C#/WinRT projection would mean targeting `net8.0-windows10.0.x` and shipping the ~20 MB Windows SDK
  assembly in the console download and the customer's installer, for four interfaces. **The interface IDs
  and method order were read from `C:\Windows\System32\WinMetadata\*.winmd`** (a throwaway reader), not
  from memory. Async calls are polled through `IAsyncInfo`. **Windows draws at the display's zoom** (1.4 on
  this laptop) — the first page measures it and the rest are asked for divided by it; every bitmap's
  resolution is set so it is the page's real size.
- **`DocumentPrinter`**: PDF (every page at 200 dpi, landscape pages landscape), pictures (fitted,
  never enlarged), plain text (paginated); anything else through the program Windows prints it with
  (`printto`, else `print` on the default printer) — or refused: *"nothing on this computer prints .xyz
  files — send it as a PDF"*.

### What everyone is told

Both directions are `FileActivityMsg` lines, kinds **`print-out`** and **`print-in`**, with a new
`Printer` field: on the ticket and in the person's tray app, like a file copy. *"“Invoice-1042” was
printed on RECEPTION-01 to Sue Tech's printer."* / *"Sue Tech printed “letter.pdf” on RECEPTION-01's
printer, HP LaserJet M404 (2 pages)."* **Nobody from outside the company** (3.9) is sent or may send any
print message — the allow-lists, with files ticked or not.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/printcheck` | **New, 32** without elevation, against Windows' "Microsoft Print to PDF" told to write to a FILE (nothing on paper): a 4-page text printed, the PDF Windows made opened with `PdfPages` — page count, A4, drawn at the size asked once the zoom is out, ink on it; **that PDF printed again** (what the console does with a customer's job) — every page, the same ink; a wide picture on a landscape page; refusals (unknown kind, no such printer, not a PDF); the printer's name rules; the print-folder guard (elsewhere, "..", a look-alike folder); the job-file test; **the real helper exe** refusing an unprintable file in writing; the two ticket lines. **`--elevated`** adds the real spooler: add, listed on its file port, printed to by name, the PDF picked up for the right technician with the program's document name and every page, two quick jobs each arrive or are said lost, removed, and a printer from a host that died swept. |
| `tools/sessionextras` | **35** (was 26): through the server — the switch reaches the host, its answer the technician, a job is announced, both ticket lines (and a failure with its reason), the tray app told, a print request and its answer. |
| `tools/outsidervisit` | **65** (was 62): a visitor's printer request and print request never reach the machine — with files ticked too — and a visitor is never shown somebody else's print or printer. |
| `tools/toolbarprobe` | 50 — both items on the Tools menu, which still fits. |

**Not on hardware.** **A FULL ship (host, console, client) and a client reinstall; no platform restart.**
`tools\Run-ElevatedChecks.ps1` (one UAC prompt) runs the spooler half and `clipfirst --station` — **run by Clint 2026-10-06: `printcheck --elevated` 43 of 43** (the real spooler: the printer added on its file port, a 4-page document picked up whole for the right technician with the program's name for it, two quick jobs BOTH arrived, removed, a dead host's printer swept) **and `clipfirst --station` 9 of 9.**
`TEST-3.6.md` section BM, 427–433.

## 96. Several photos per quote item; knowledge base folders; link buttons — 2026-10-06

Clint, three requests in one sitting: *"When requesting quotes, uploading photos only allows for one
photo. Can we change this to allow for multiple photos."* — *"on the knowledgebase, it would be nice to
be able to create folders and subfolders ... This must be under general and clients."* — and, while it
was being built, *"click here buttons ... one can add the url, save it and it shows as a button instead
of the url as some urls can be extremely long and would look messy."*

### Several photos of one part

- **A photo now names its line, not the other way round**: `TicketPhoto.QuoteLineId`. A line has as
  many as were taken, up to **`QuoteService.MaxPhotosPerLine` (12)** so one request email stays a size a
  supplier's server takes; each photo belongs to ONE line. `QuoteLine.PhotoId` is kept only because the
  migration read it — **nothing reads or writes it any more**; `QuoteLine.PhotoIds` (not stored) is filled
  by `LinesAsync`, the one place a line's photos are found.
- `AddLineAsync` takes `IEnumerable<long>? photoIds`; **`AddLinePhotosAsync`** adds more to a line
  already on the quote. Both claim through `ClaimPhotosAsync`: a Part photo, on THIS ticket, on no other
  line, duplicates ignored. Removing a line frees its photos (`QuoteLineId = null`) for another.
- **The portal** (`_QuoteLines`): the photo box is `multiple` (and lost `capture=environment`, which on a
  phone forbids picking several). Its script makes each photo smaller (`photos.js`) and sends it **on its
  own to `/api/portal/photos` with `kind=part`** — §62's rule, because several phone photos in the AddLine
  form itself would pass 30 MB — then posts the line naming their ids. Without script the files go with
  the form (`List<IFormFile> photo`). Each line has **Add photos**; "Did you mean" carries the uploaded
  ids (`PendingPhotos`) so a near-miss never loses them.
- **Found on the way:** `/api/portal/photos` refused `kind=part` on every non-workshop ticket — so the
  CONSOLE could never attach a part photo to a **General** job's quote (General asks for quotes too). Part
  photos are allowed on any category now, and to the technician in `WorkedBy` (who may still edit the
  lines, `MayEditLines`). The console's part photo was also never made smaller; it goes through
  `UploadPhotoIdsAsync` (the same loop as `UploadPhotosAsync`, handing back ids) now.
- **The console**: *Photos of the part…* picks several; each line has **Add photos** (`QuoteLinePhotosMsg`,
  checked to be on the named ticket like Remove). `QuoteLineAddMsg.PhotoIds`, with `PhotoId` still sent
  as the first so an older server keeps one; the hub takes either from an older console.
  `QuoteLineInfo.PhotoCount`, with `HasPhoto` still set for older consoles.
- **The request**: *"(3 photos attached)"*; the .eml attaches every photo, **named for the item's number
  in the email** (`QuoteService.PhotoFileName`: `item-2.jpg`, or `item-2-photo-3.jpg`), and web mail's
  download buttons use the same names.

### Folders in the knowledge base

- **`KbFolder`** (`TenantId`, `ClientId` — null is General, `ParentId`, `Name`). **A folder belongs to ONE
  section, and so does everything in it**: a subfolder takes its parent's section; an article may only be
  in a folder of its own section (`CheckFolderAsync`). `KbArticle.FolderId`, and `KbRevision.FolderId` so
  **putting a version back puts it back where it was** (or the top, if that folder is gone or in another
  section). No foreign keys: the service is the only thing that removes a folder.
- Rules, all in `KnowledgeBaseService`: names tidied, unique among siblings in any case, no `›`;
  **six deep at most** (`MaxFolderDepth`); rename and move in one (`EditFolderAsync`) — never into itself
  or a folder inside it, never into another section. **Removing a folder loses nothing** — what was in it
  moves up to where it was (a moved subfolder whose name is already there gets *"(from X)"*). **Anybody who
  writes may remove an EMPTY folder; one with something in it is a supervisor's or the owner's**, the same
  people who delete an article. Moving an article (`MoveArticleAsync`) is a new version, *"Moved to X"*.
- **The page** (`/portal/kb`, `?folder=N` — its section follows from the folder): a section's top or a
  folder shows what is directly in it, **folders first, then articles**, like a folder on a PC, with
  *Knowledge base › General › Printers › HP* above. Everything (`/portal/kb`) shows each section's top.
  **A search looks through everything below where you are** and each match says where it lives
  (*📁 Printers › HP*). *New folder (inside)*, *Rename or move*, *Remove folder*; *New article here*
  (`/portal/kb/edit?folder=N`). An article whose folder has gone astray is shown at its section's top
  (`FolderOf`) — never hidden.
- **The editor** has a **Folder** box of the chosen section's folders; choosing another client refills it
  from `/api/portal/kb/folders?client=N`. For that, **`clientpick.js` now raises `change` on its hidden
  input** when the choice changes, and emptying the box clears what was chosen (typing the same name back
  is then a new choice, not a silent return to a value no longer held). The article page has a **Folder**
  box beside Edit (moves within its section; another client is the editor's job), and deleting returns
  to the folder it was in.

### Link buttons — `KbText`

- **`[button: words | address]`** is a button with those words; **an address alone on a line** is a button
  named after its site (*Open hp.com*); an address inside a sentence stays a link, shown as *site/…* when
  longer than 50 characters (the whole address on hover). The editor's **Link button** asks for the
  address (adds `https://` to *hp.com/…*) and the words, and writes the tag on a line of its own.
- Buttons are made BEFORE the address rule and set aside, so their address is not linked twice; the
  set-aside marks (`\u0001N\u0002`) are stripped from typed text first. Words and address are encoded like
  everything else; only http/https make one. The snippet reads a button as its words.

### What building it found

- **A harness marker can match the Light/Dark switch.** `kbcheck` took a refused folder form by
  `handler=NewFolder` — and found the theme switch's form first, because its *returnUrl* is the page's own
  address, which after a refused POST contains `handler=NewFolder`. Find a form by something only it has
  (its box's `aria-label`). A GET that carries `?handler=NewFolder` back (that switch's return) renders the
  page normally — walked.
- **The site's `nav` rules centre a `<nav>` on a phone.** The breadcrumb is a `<nav>`, so `nav.kb-crumbs`
  puts the alignment and link colours back; the floated *New article* button now has its own line on a
  phone (`.kb-new`) instead of sitting on the breadcrumb.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/quotecheck` | 110 → **129**: three photos on one item, oldest first, the story says how many; a photo already on another item refused; the same photo twice is one; Add photos; not by a colleague; never an "as it arrived" photo or another ticket's; the 12 limit and a refusal changing nothing; the request's *(5 photos attached)*; the file names; removing frees all five; **the migration carrying an old line's one photo across** — an old database at `WakeOnLan` seeded by SQL (`Seed.OldRow`, new in `tools/Common/OldRows.cs`), then migrated. **122 of 129 with the "already on another item" guard and the backfill out.** |
| `tools/kbcheck` | 108 → **151**: link buttons (words, a bare address, a long address in a sentence, no words, inside a step, injection, typed marks, the snippet); folders — made in General with its name tidied, a subfolder, a duplicate refused with the name kept, the breadcrumb, a client's own folders and not General's, the Folder box's API, six deep and no deeper, New article here, saved in the folder, the folder above counting it, a search inside a folder saying where, an Acme article refused a General folder, Move to the top and back as versions, never across sections, a restore putting it back where it was, rename and move in one, no loop, no cross-section move, a technician refused a full folder and not shown the button, an empty one removed by a technician, a supervisor removing a full one with nothing lost, another company seeing and making nothing. **147 of 151 with the section and loop guards out.** Two older checks changed with the page: the client heading is now the breadcrumb, and a delete lands back in the client's section. |
| `tools/ticketwindowprobe` | 156 → **161**: *Photos of the part…*, an older server's HasPhoto still saying *photo*, *Add photos* on the line beside Remove and inside the window, *3 photos*. |
| unchanged | `ticketwire` 31, `photomany` 21 (the console's reshaped upload loop). |
| **walked** | on a `workflowdemo` platform: Sue made Printers › HP, wrote an article in HP with a Link button and a bare address (both buttons, breadcrumb, Folder box); three images (4000×3000, 1200×900, 3000×4000) on one quote item went up one at a time, made 2048 px; Add photos added a fourth; the office requested the quote — the .eml had `item-1-photo-1…4`, the words *(4 photos attached)*, the Gmail page four named downloads. Phone width: found and fixed the two layout faults above. |

**Not on hardware**: a phone's own camera picking several photos at once (iOS and Android differ).

### Deploying it

**Platform deploy (migration `KbFoldersQuotePhotos`: `KbFolders`, `KbArticles.FolderId`,
`KbRevisions.FolderId`, `TicketPhotos.QuoteLineId`, and the backfill) FIRST, then the console
re-download** (`-OnlyTechnician` locally). No client reinstall. An older console keeps working: it
sends one photo as before and draws a line with photos as *photo*. `TEST-3.6.md` section BN, 434–442.

## 97. Quote requests: stock, ETA and signatures — 2026-10-06

Clint: *"When creating the quote to the suppliers, can we add to the template that it asks for eta, and
also have an option to upload a signature or multiple signatures that one can select before sending in
case there is more than one person in the organization that requests quotes. In the case of multiple
signatures, the system should first ask which signature to use before requesting the quote."* Asked what
a signature is: *"text and or image. Some cases just an image is required. With text, font, size and color
selection should be available."* Then, while it was being built: *"also add stock availability to the
template"*, and *"the text will be above the image, so for example our text may read Kind Regards, with
the signature image directly below."* The one already ticked: the one the person used last (his answer).

### The words

`QuoteService.AskDeliveryStockEta` is the one sentence: *"Please include the delivery fee, whether each
item is in stock, and the ETA (how soon each item can be delivered)"*, then *", for delivery to:"* and the
address when one is set. The Request quote form and the Suppliers page say the same.

**A signature with words is the WHOLE closing.** The request now ends at *"Our reference: job #N."*
(`QuoteRequestWords`); with no signature (or an image-only one, in the plain words) `QuoteRequestText`
adds *"Thank you,"*, the person's name and the company's, exactly as before. With a signature, ours
would have read *"Thank you, / Kind regards"* — so the editor says to start with your sign-off.

### Signatures — `Services/QuoteSignatures.cs`

- **`QuoteSignature`** (one row per signature, migration `QuoteRequestSignatures`): a name for the picker;
  **lines** as JSON (`QuoteSignatures.Line`: text, font, size, colour, style) — **never HTML**; an optional
  image kept IN the row (PNG, JPEG or GIF by the bytes — WebP and HEIC are not on it because Outlook draws
  neither; 1 MB); the image's width in the email (its own, at most 400 to start; 40–800); above or below
  the text (below is the default — Clint's *Kind regards* then the picture). Removing one is a soft delete:
  a ticket signed with it downloads again the same.
- **Every style comes from a list** (`Fonts` — eleven every mail program draws, each with fall-backs —
  `Sizes`, `Styles`, `#rrggbb`); `Clean` puts anything else back to the default, and every word is
  encoded. Nothing typed reaches a supplier's inbox as markup.
- **Who**: the people who keep suppliers (`Permissions.CanEditSuppliers` — office administrator,
  supervisor, owner), on the **Suppliers page**, card *Signatures*: a line per row (font, size, colour
  picker, Normal/Bold/Italic/Bold italic), *Add a line*, the image, and a live *How it will look*.
- **Choosing** (`QuoteSignatureService.ChooseAsync`): none on the list → none; ONE → that one, nothing
  asked (the form says *Signed with X*); several → the form asks **Which signature?** with each drawn, the
  person's last ticked (`Technician.LastQuoteSignatureId`, `Preselected`), and the server **refuses an
  unchosen one before the job moves** — never a guess. Afterwards `RememberAsync` keeps it on the ticket
  (`Ticket.QuoteSignatureId`) and on the person.

### Into the email

- **Desktop mail**: the draft becomes `mixed { alternative { plain, related { html, image } }, photos… }`
  (`QuoteRequestEml`'s `html` and `inline`); the image is `cid:signature@rsp`, `Content-Disposition:
  inline`, so it shows in the email rather than as an attachment. With no signature the file is
  what it always was.
- **Gmail / Outlook on the web** take plain words through a link and nothing more. With a signature the
  link's words stop at *Our reference*, and **pressing Open the email copies the signature, drawn**, to
  paste under it (*Copy the signature again* beside it). **Copy by selection first** (`execCommand`), the
  clipboard API second: the API's `write` was refused outright in the app's built-in browser even on a real
  click (*"Write permission denied"*), while the selection copy put the formatted signature on the Windows
  clipboard. If both fail it says to select and copy it by hand.
- **The image's public address** `/quote-signature/{token}` — no sign-in, because web mail fetches the
  pasted image and so does the supplier's mail program. The token is 128 random bits, new with every new
  image (cached a year, `nosniff`); a replaced image's old address serves nothing, so a web-mail request
  already sent with the old picture loses it. Desktop drafts carry their own copy.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/quotecheck` | 129 → **190**: the stock/ETA sentence both ways; unsigned as before; Clean (font, colour, style, size, newlines); trailing blank lines; PNG/JPEG/GIF sniffed and their widths read; WebP/SVG refused; who may add; no name, empty, over 1 MB refused; duplicate name; image-only at 400 from 1200; the token; the public address and a malformed one; a new image's new token; width without re-upload, held to 800; another company's; choosing with none/one/several, never a guess; last used ticked; removed still found and served; Remember on the ticket and the person; a signature as the whole closing; web mail's words; **Clint's Kind regards with the image directly below**; HTML styles and encoding; the draft read back by **MimeKit** — plain and HTML, the image inline by Content-ID byte for byte, the photo still attached. **185 of 188 with the never-guess guard and the encoding out.** |
| **walked** | on a `workflowdemo` platform as the supervisor: a two-line signature (*Kind regards* Calibri 14, *Clint Smith* bold 18 blue) with a 600 px image — preview text above image, saved, image served at 600×160 drawn 400, reachable with no cookie, a made-up token 404; an image-only *Office banner*; Request quote asked *Which signature?* with both drawn and the first ticked; banner + desktop mail → the draft re-downloaded with the image inline and drawn under *Our reference*; next time the banner was ticked; *Clint — Accounts* + Gmail → the link stopped at *Our reference*, and the copy (after the fix above) put the formatted signature on the clipboard. |

**Not on hardware**: pasting into real Gmail and Outlook on the web, and Outlook desktop opening the
signed draft.

### Deploying it

**Platform deploy (migration `QuoteRequestSignatures`)** only — the console sends Request quote to the
browser, and the customer app is untouched. Then add the signatures on the Suppliers page. `TEST-3.6.md`
section BO, 443–449.

## 98. One look in the console and the customer's app: rounded, no black corners, one colour rule — 2026-10-06

Clint: *"Everywhere in the console, tickets, remote support and including where the technician signs in,
there is no conformity. Some boxes are round edges, some have round and square edges and some have black
lines sticking out etc… the tickets button in the console is blue, the rest are not… All edges must be
rounded with no visible black lines. this needs to be fixed in light and dark mode."* Then, during the
work: *"Is this also fixing the client app because that also has similar issues"* — yes: it is the same
library, and the customer's windows are now held to the same harness.

### The black lines were a paint fault, not a drawing one

**Windows' `Button` marks itself `ControlStyles.Opaque`** — measured, not remembered: `GetStyle(Opaque)` is
true on a Flat button, and neither `ButtonBase` nor `Button` overrides `OnPaintBackground`. Opaque tells
WinForms "I paint every pixel myself", so it never paints a button's background; that is
`ButtonBase.OnPaint`'s job, and `RoundButton` replaces `OnPaint`. The corners outside the rounded shape
were painted by NOTHING.

With `OptimizedDoubleBuffer` an unpainted pixel is not left as the screen had it: the control paints into
an off-screen buffer and copies the whole of it. **WinForms shares ONE buffer for anything up to 225×96
(`BufferedGraphicsManager.Current.MaximumBuffer`)**, so a small button's corners showed a piece of the
last control drawn there — the blue corner on *Photos*, the border stubs under *Open in browser*, the
right ends that looked square. A bigger button gets a new buffer, which starts **black** — *Sign In*,
*Connect*, *Create ticket*, *Finish setting up*. One line fixes every one: `SetStyle(ControlStyles.Opaque,
false)` in `RoundButton`, and in the new `RoundCheck` (a `CheckBox`, so a `ButtonBase` too).

**Never give a control derived from `ButtonBase` its own `OnPaint` without that line.**

### What else was square or in Windows' colours, and what replaced it

All in `RemoteSupport.UI` (`Controls.cs`, new `RoundControls.cs`, `NativeDark.cs`), so the console, the
customer's app and the host's Allow prompt all have it:

- **Dropdowns** (`ThemedCombo`) were drawn square on purpose (2026-09-24). Now `Ground.Round` paints the
  corners outside the rounded shape in the colour behind the control — `Ground.Behind` walks up to the
  first `Card` (its `Fill`), `CanvasPanel` (`ColourAt`, the gradient at that point) or solid `BackColor` —
  and draws the border round, smooth, over Windows' own.
- **`FieldFrame`**: a rounded field round any control Windows draws square — the two-factor key, code and
  recovery-code boxes, the script box and the script output (on its own dark `Slate`), New ticket's client
  search list, a quote's item suggestions, the customer's chat reply box. **What shows and hides is the
  FRAME** (`_matchesFrame`, `_suggestFrame`): a control's `Visible` reads false while its parent is hidden,
  so asking the inner list would never have said true.
- **`ListBox.Themed(t)`**: rows drawn by us, the chosen one the palette's raised row, not Windows' blue bar.
- **`RoundCheck`** for every tick box (people on a job, Book an appointment, password protected, Control,
  the installer's unattended box, the Allow prompt's files box). An empty box's edge is `Muted`, not the
  field border, which all but vanished on the dark card. `CheckAlign = TopLeft` puts the box beside the
  first of several lines.
- **`DateBox` + `CalendarView`** (our own month, in the palette) and **`TimeBox`** (a quarter-hour
  dropdown) replace `DateTimePicker`, which is white on the dark console whatever it is told. **A time
  not on a quarter hour is inserted, never rounded**, so opening a ticket never moves its appointment.
- **`NumberBox`** (an `InputBox`; Up and Down count) replaces the quantity `NumericUpDown`; **`RoundSlider`**
  the session's Quality `TrackBar`; **`RoundProgress`** the transfer bar.
- **Menus**: `.Themed(t)` on every `ContextMenuStrip` (console: machine right-click, tray, System, Tools;
  customer: tray). `ThemedMenuRenderer` paints the palette with a rounded hover row; on Windows 11 DWM
  rounds the window and draws its border in `FieldBorder` (`DWMWA_WINDOW_CORNER_PREFERENCE`,
  `DWMWA_BORDER_COLOR`); Windows 10 gets a square border in the same colour.
- **Lists**: `HeaderFiller` now runs in the LIGHT theme too (the band stopped short of the list's edge,
  white beyond), is attached by `UiExt.Themed` on the list's own `HandleCreated` (a tool window's list is
  made after `NativeDark.Apply` has run), and is kept alive in a table — a `NativeWindow` that only the
  window procedure knows about can be collected. **`EmptyFiller`** paints the space under the last row,
  where the Explorer style's column rules showed, so a list keeps the dark scrollbar that `NoColumnRules`
  costs. Lists with groups (the dashboard's) still use `NoColumnRules`.
- The session toolbar's **Monitor** label grows over its dropdown's top edge at 150%; the fields are now
  in front of their labels.

### One colour rule — the portal's

`BtnStyle` says what a button is FOR. **Accent** (filled, the tenant's colour) is the ONE main action of an
area, and the chosen tab of a set; **Ghost and Neutral are now ONE look**, the portal's `.btn` — outlined,
the signature colour for the words (`RoundButton.LookOf`); **Danger** is outlined red; **Success** stays
green (Accept call, Run). The console had three looks on one toolbar — a grey pill, an outline and a
fill. The dashboard's **Tickets** is outlined like its neighbours, and still turns red with a count, as
Office chat and Website chat do.

**The light palette's signature is the tenant's accent**, deepened to read on white (`Theme.Light`:
`Grape`, `Purple`, `SurfaceAltText`), as `BrandPalette` does for the portal. It was our purple #7C3AED
whatever the tenant, so Anywhere IT's blue buttons had purple outlines and purple focus rings beside them.

### How it is proved — `tools/lookprobe` (new)

Every window, light and dark — the console's 18 and the customer's 10 (tray window, chat, installer,
request, microphone, outside help, unattended password, banner, Allow, Allow from outside) — the real
classes, no server. Per window: no square-bordered box; nothing left in Windows' own look; every menu
themed; every pixel painted (a magenta flood, then a full repaint); **every rounded control's corners show
what is behind it** (each corner pixel against the pixel just outside it); list headers run to the edge
and nothing is drawn under the last row; the dashboard header and the session toolbar each have one look.

**163 of 250 on the old code; 330 of 330 now** (the customer's 80 were added after the fix; one of the old
code's 87 failures was the harness's own, item 3). Three things
it took to make it honest, worth knowing before the next harness that reads pixels:

1. **The magenta flood could not see the fault, and passed every window.** The pixels come from the
   off-screen buffer, not from what was on the screen. The corner check asks from where Clint stands.
2. **It runs on a desktop somebody is using**: the first runs read the Claude app for half the windows,
   and the session window for every tool window. `TopMost` alone is not enough; it now retries until
   `WindowFromPoint` at the middle and four corners is the window, and **a flood that cannot be read
   back fails the window** instead of passing it. `PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)` did NOT return what
   GDI had drawn, so it reads the screen.
3. It once guessed a tool window's palette and failed a correct header; it reads the header's own first
   cell now.

Unchanged and still passing, run after the change: `toolbarprobe` 50, `ticketwindowprobe` 161, `ticketformprobe`
91, `fitprobe` 244, `chatprobe` 24, `dashtabs` 124, `webchatprobe` 32, `watchprobe` 68, `staffchatprobe` 18,
`callprobe` 25, `themecheck` 40. Two needed a line each: `ticketwindowprobe`'s dark quantity check asks the
`NumberBox`, and `ticketformprobe` shows the client list by its frame. **Run window harnesses one at a
time**: `dashtabs` failed 3 while another harness had a window up, and passed 124 alone.

### Deploying it

It changes the CONSOLE, the CUSTOMER'S APP and the HOST's prompt, not the platform's code: **a
`Publish-Platform.ps1` deploy (it carries both downloads), then technicians re-download the console and
customers reinstall** for theirs. No migration. `TEST-3.6.md` section BP, 450–457.

## 99. A program opened or closed shows only after Refresh — the colour converter was asked once — 2026-10-06

Internal testing, Clint: on one test machine of three, a program opened or closed through a session did
not appear on the console until **Refresh**. He suspected Windows 10 Pro against Home. **It is the
graphics card, not the edition.** The machine's Info tab (DESKTOP-STD8M9C, Windows 10 19045, 1366x768):
*"H.264 — Intel Quick Sync … **with a GPU colour conversion**"*. The other two, and this laptop, take the
frame as BGRA and never use the converter.

**The fault.** `GpuColourConverter.Convert` called `ProcessOutput` ONCE per frame. Windows' Video
Processor MFT does not count a frame as finished until `ProcessOutput` has answered
`MF_E_TRANSFORM_NEED_MORE_INPUT`; until then it refuses the next frame as busy (`H264Encoder.Dropped`).
A refused frame on a screen that then goes still is never replaced — Desktop Duplication has nothing new
to hand over, so the host never calls the encoder again — and the last frame of a window opening or
closing is exactly that frame. Refresh rebuilt the encoder and forced a key frame, which is why it fixed
it. Now `Convert` asks until the transform says it wants more input (bounded at 4, newest kept).
**The Info tab's "Frames the encoder was too busy for" could not show it**: Info is a snapshot taken when
the encoder is built, when the count is 0.

**`codecbench --tail`** (new, `tools/codecbench/Tail.cs`): the host's loop exactly — a burst of change
ending in one large change (the "program appearing"), then a still screen — decoded as the console does
and compared with the screen, then a forced key frame (Refresh) and compared again. `--nv12` forces the
colour-conversion path (`H264Encoder.ForceColourConversion`, bench only) on a machine that would not
need it; `--hold N` makes the encoder behave N frames late, and must FAIL before Refresh — **its first
version passed that simulated fault**, because it froze a moving field and two neighbouring frames of
that are near enough alike; the burst now ends on `SceneKind.Colour`.

On this laptop (Quick Sync, Windows 11): `--tail --nv12` **FAIL 94.7 of 255 before, and AFTER Refresh
too** on the old code (the converter took 1 frame and refused 16) — **PASS 2.3 / 1.6 with the fix**, twice;
`--tail` PASS 2.1; `--tail --hold 1` FAIL 89.9 then PASS 1.7 (the harness can still see a fault);
`--mfpipe` PASS 0.5. Not yet run on DESKTOP-STD8M9C. `tools/encoderstate.ps1` (new, read-only, for a
session's Scripts tab or `runscript`) prints the graphics card, its driver and the host's capture/codec
trace lines.

### Deploying it

It changes the HOST only (RemoteSupport.Media's converter is used by the encoder alone): **a
`Publish-Platform.ps1` deploy, then reinstall the client on DESKTOP-STD8M9C**. No migration, no console
re-download. `TEST-3.6.md` check 458.

## 100. Remembered unattended passwords, per technician per machine — 2026-10-06

Clint, while describing the free version: *"once the technician enters the password once, it should
remember it for that machine. The same should apply for the full version. entering a password remembers
it, but only for the particular technician that entered it."* His answers are in
`NEXT-SESSION-FREE.md` (the decisions table): **kept on the server**, so it works from any PC they sign
in on; **forgotten** when the password is changed or removed at the machine, when the technician is
removed, or by right-click → *Forget saved password*; a **supervisor or the owner** sees who has it saved
(names only) and clears one or all. This is Stage A of the free version, and is in both versions.

**It loosens §77 on purpose, and only this far**: each technician still types it ONCE. A colleague who
never has is asked; a session opened with it still admits nobody without it (`Session.Admitted`) — a
remembered one counts as typed. §77's "no override" stands: nobody can see or reset the password itself.

### What it is

- **A row, not a password**: `SavedUnattendedPassword` (migration `RememberedUnattendedPasswords`) —
  technician, device ROW (`Device.Id`, which a reinstall keeps; the password survives a reinstall the same
  way), when, and **the machine's password salt at that moment**. Never the password, never its hash. A
  password set or removed at the machine has a new salt, so every older row is dead; the hub deletes them
  then too (`ForgetEveryoneAsync`), so the who-list is never a list of the stale. Cascades from Device and
  Technician — technician ids are AUTOINCREMENT, never reused, so a removed person's memory row can never
  become somebody else's.
- **The hub** (`Hub/TenantHub.SavedPasswords.cs`): `_savedPw` (machine → technician → salt), loaded at
  start, reloaded when a machine's row comes back under a new device id. `PasswordLets` asks
  `RemembersPassword` FIRST — **ahead of the lockout**: the lockout stops guessing, and somebody else
  guessing must not lock out the people who already know it. A right password typed calls
  `RememberPassword` (memory at once, the row after).
- **The console**: `SavedPasswordsMsg` (its own machines, and `MayManage`) at sign-in and after any
  change. Connect leaves the password box out for those; the server still decides, and a stale list only
  means one refusal and the box, by the path that already existed. Right-click: *Forget saved password*
  (one's own); *Saved passwords ▸* for a supervisor or the owner (`Permissions.CanClearSavedPasswords`),
  filled when the server answers — *Clear Pat Technician's (saved 6 Oct 2026)*, *Clear everybody's*
  (asks first). The tooltip on a passworded machine says whether yours is saved.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/unattendedpw` | **64** (was 33). Sections 1–7 as before, with the guessing in section 4 moved to two technicians who never typed it (a remembered one gets in whatever is typed); plus: told it is saved, never the password, not offered others'; let in during another's lockout; a new password forgets everybody's and their consoles are told; and a new **section 8** through a second restart — told at sign-in, in with nothing typed, the owner not remembered and still asked, a technician refused the list and clear-all, the owner sees names only, Forget, the owner clearing Pat's (Pat told), a removed technician gone from the list, Clear everybody's. **With the remembered check and the forget-everyone call taken out: 60 of 64.** |
| re-run | `unattendedwire` 13, `dashtabs` 124. |

**Not on hardware, and the right-click menu has not been looked at.** **Platform deploy (migration
`RememberedUnattendedPasswords`) and the console re-download.** No client change. `TEST-3.6.md`
section BR, 459–464.

## 101. The free version's limits, at the hub — 2026-10-06 (Stage B of NEXT-SESSION-FREE.md)

Nothing a customer can see yet: there is no way to sign up for the free version until Stage C, and the
console and portal still draw everything until Stage F. What exists is **the rule, enforced where it
cannot be got round**, and a command to make a free company: `set-brand <slug> plan free` (or `full`).

### What it is

- **`Tenant.Plan`** already existed and only ever said "five-user". **"free" is the free version**;
  anything else is the full one. Ask **`FreePlan.Is`** (Shared/FreePlan.cs) — never compare the string.
  `FreePlan` is the ONE place the limits live: two machines, two removals a calendar month, the words,
  and the session allow-list.
- **One person** (`TenantService`): `NewPersonProblem` refuses anybody past the first; `SetRoleAsync`
  refuses anything but Owner + Technician (`FreeRole`). The CLI has no set-role, so that half is proved
  only by reading — Stage F's portal check will drive it.
- **Two machines** (`Hub/TenantHub.Free.cs`, `FreeRefusesHello`): checked in the SAME lock that adds a
  machine, so two arriving together cannot both take the last place. Refused with
  `ErrorMsg.NotAdmitted` (new — "trying again will not change this") and closed. **Counted as machines,
  not install ids** (`MachineCount`, by hardware fingerprint): a reinstall is the same computer.
- **A reinstall's old id no longer lingers** (`ForgetReinstalledId`, called from `PersistDeviceAsync`'s
  takeover): before this it sat in every console's list as an offline twin until a server restart — in
  BOTH versions. On the free version it would have read as a third machine, and removing it would have
  spent one of the month's two removals on nothing. `DeviceGoneMsg` (new) tells the consoles; an older
  console ignores it (unknown message types are dropped by `WsConnection`), as before.
- **Remove** (`RemoveDeviceAsync`, `DeviceRemoveMsg` from the console): free only. The row goes (and
  with it everybody's remembered password, §100, by cascade), a **`DeviceRemoval`** row is written
  (migration `FreeVersionRemovals`), its sessions end, its connections are told and closed, and **that
  install id is refused if it says hello again** — its agent is still running over there and would put
  itself straight back. A fresh install on the same computer is a new machine. The third removal in a
  calendar month (company time) is refused with the date of the next.
- **Unattended only, with a password**: `ConnectDevice` refuses unattended-off and no-password in words;
  `StartSession` offers only the agent (never a consent prompt, never the tray app); a call and an
  outside-help code from a machine are refused; web support and website chat read as off.
- **No reason asked and no ticket**: `ConnectDevice` skips the reason; `AttachSessionToTicketAsync`
  returns at once. Session history (`SessionLog`) is still written.
- **The session allow-list** (`FreePlan.MaySend`/`MaySendBinary`): control, the System menu
  (Ctrl+Alt+Del, restart, lock — **an assumption**: an unattended machine in another office cannot be
  looked after without restart), Files and drag-off, clipboard, both printing directions, file chunks.
  Not scripts, sound, voice, recording, the privacy screen, chat or the Info tab.
- **The console allow-list** (`ConsoleMaySendOnFree`): Connect, End, saved passwords, Remove, the
  portal link. Everything else gets *"That is part of the full version, not the free version."*
- `StateMsg.Free` tells the console; nothing draws from it yet (Stage F). No health check is offered.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/freecheck` (new) | **42 of 42**, a platform of its own with a free company and a full one beside it: one person; a third machine refused with words and closed, a reinstall not a third, a full company taking three; unattended-off and no-password refused, in with the password and no reason; in a session the allowed messages reach the host and scripts, Listen, Talk and the privacy screen do not, a file chunk does and voice does not; no ticket written (read from the database); a call and an outside-help code refused, a tray app never asked to host; tickets, Processes, office chat and Wake up refused from the console while a full company's tickets still come; Remove (told, closed, refused on return, place freed), a third removal refused with the date, recorded; after a restart, a removed install still refused and the count read from what is stored; a reinstall's old id taken off the list. **With four guards out (hello, session list, console list, the twin): 30 of 42.** |
| re-run | `unattendedpw` 64, `unattendedwire` 13, `consentwire` 34, `outsidervisit` 65. |

**Platform deploy (migration `FreeVersionRemovals`) and the console re-download** (it drops removed and
reinstalled rows). Nothing is visible until Stage C, so there is no hardware check for this stage alone.

## 102. Signing up for the free version; no terms say DRAFT — 2026-10-06 (Stage C of NEXT-SESSION-FREE.md)

### Free or full, at signup

- **`/signup` asks Free or Full after the country** (`Step == "plan"`, two cards, `?plan=free|full`),
  before the terms, because the two have different terms. The plan travels as a hidden field to every
  step; `Route()` sends a missing one back to the choice. Region rules (§84) unchanged.
- **The free terms** = the region's own with **`Terms/free.txt`** put in ahead of section 1
  (`Terms.ForFree`, `Terms.For(region, free)`): own computers only, two computers, no fees (section 2
  and refunds do not apply), two removals a month, 30 days' notice of changes, and that section 3 still
  applies — with *"Being controlled remotely"* on screen (Stage E delivers that). A different fingerprint
  from the full terms, so ticking one never makes the other. `/terms/ZA?plan=free` shows them.
- **The free form**: company name optional (blank → the person's name, and the slug from it), contact
  number optional, **no colours** (ignored even if a doctored form sends them — our defaults). The one
  person is **Owner + Technician** (`TenantService.FreeRole`), not OwnerSupervisor: they connect.
- **Approval**: still Pending until the platform owner approves — **an assumption, not asked**; then
  **Active, with no trial** (`ApproveAsync`), because there is nothing to run out. If Clint wants free
  signups to start at once, it is one line in `SignupAsync`.
- **The landing page is NOT changed**: it is the PUBLIC holding page (`Publish-Platform.ps1 -LandingOnly`),
  and a line about a free version nobody can sign up for yet was taken back out. Add it with the real site.

### No terms say DRAFT

Clint, the same day: *"lets remove draft from the consent forms. lets assume they are correct as is. I
will get a lawyer to check them and give you any changes if they are found."* `Terms.IsDraft` is false
for every region and for the free section; the free section's one lawyer question was taken out (30
days' notice kept). **The regions not yet open (US, CA, UK, EU) still hold `[to be confirmed]` facts** —
tax, governing law, the ICO number, the EU representative — which only Clint can supply before each
opens; nobody can sign up there today. A lawyer's change is an edit to `Terms/` and a new
`Terms.Version`, then `landing-legal` (§88).
