## 103. Installing a free computer: the password at install, no tray app — 2026-10-06 (Stage D)

Clint's answers: the unattended password is chosen when the computer is installed, unattended access is
switched on then, **nothing of ours stays on the screen** (no tray app), and changing the password is
installing again.

### What it is

- **`Branding.Free`** (from `Tenant.Plan`, in `brand.json`) tells a downloaded copy the company is free.
  It then shows **`FreeInstallForm`** instead of `LauncherForm`: no *Get help now* (no attended access),
  only *Add this computer* (*Change password* when it is already installed), the password typed twice
  (`UnattendedPasswordDialog.Problem`, the server's rule), and a note that *"Being controlled remotely"*
  shows on screen while connected.
- **Three steps, as the person at the machine, never elevated** (`Shared/FreeSetup.cs`):
  1. **`MayAddAsync`** — `GET /download/{slug}/may-add?hw=<fingerprint>` asks the hub
     (`FreeWouldRefuse`, the same rule as the hello) BEFORE anything is installed, so a third computer is
     told why and nothing is left behind. The hello stays the rule for two installs racing.
  2. **`Install-Client.ps1 -Free`** — the agent service only: no shortcuts, no Run key, no tray app; a
     tray app left by an earlier full install is stopped and taken out of logon. **A dead agent fails the
     install** (`throw`): on the free version there is nothing else to reach the computer by.
  3. **`SetPasswordAsync`** — waits for the agent's `ProgramData\RemoteSupport\device.json` (read, never
     created: a second identity would be a second machine), connects ONCE as this machine's **client**,
     switches unattended on and sends the password. **It has to be the client** — §31 and §77: only a
     client connection may change either, so the agent can never unlock itself. Without a tray app, this
     one connection is the client.
- **`SetUnattendedPasswordMsg.RequestId`, echoed in `UnattendedStateMsg.RequestId`** (new). A machine is
  told its state TWICE as it connects (from memory, then the stored record — §33's fix), so an installer
  changing the password could take the old *"has a password"* for the answer to its new one. Only the
  state carrying its own id answers it. Older tray apps send none and are answered as before.
- **An installed copy on a free computer is never a tray app**: opened by hand it says how the computer is
  reached and how to change the password; at logon it says nothing (`Program.Main`).
- **`DeviceLink` waits 15 minutes** after `ErrorMsg.NotAdmitted` (a removed or third computer) instead
  of 30 seconds: asking again changes nothing until a place is freed.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/freeinstall` (new) | **16 of 16**, a platform of its own, the REAL `FreeSetup`: brand.json free and not; may-add yes on an empty account, yes for THIS PC by its real fingerprint, no — in the hub's words — for a third, yes for one of the two, always yes for a full company; a refused password refused before sending; set, with unattended on, answered for this request; the console sees it unattended with a password and connects with it; installing again with a new password — the old refused (and the remembered one gone), the new working; a third computer refused in the hub's words; a new identity on one of the two let on. **With the hub's echo taken out: 13 of 16** (the setup waits for its own answer and never gets it). |
| `fitprobe` 284, `lookprobe` 338 | the new window, add and change, at 150%, light and dark — looked at too. |
| re-run | `oneexecheck` 61 (the real packed .exe), `unattendedpw` 64, `unattendedwire` 13, `unattendedcheck` 40, `freecheck` 42. |

**The install itself is not driven by any harness** — it needs an administrator and a real service. That
is check 469. **A FULL ship** (the client, the installer and the payload change), **a platform deploy**,
and then a free company's download. `TEST-3.6.md` section BT, 469–474.

## 104. "Being controlled remotely" on a free computer's screen — 2026-10-06 (Stage E)

Clint, asked whether a free computer (no tray app) should show anything during a session: *"Lets add
Being Controlled Remotely."*

### What it is

- **`Host/ControlledNotice.cs`**, a sibling of the privacy screen (§60): one amber bar, white words, at
  the **top centre of every monitor** — *"Being controlled remotely by Fran Free"* (everyone connected,
  by name). Raw Win32 on its own thread, per-monitor DPI aware, sized from each monitor; **topmost** (kept
  there every 500 ms), **click-through**, **never activated**, rounded, and **`WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`**
  so it is not in the technician's picture and never covers what they are working on. **Unlike the
  privacy screen it does not refuse** when Windows cannot exclude it: the person being told matters
  more than a strip of the technician's view.
- **It follows the participants** (`HostEngine.FollowNotice`, from the hub's `ParticipantsMsg`): named
  while anybody is connected, re-worded when somebody joins or leaves, gone when nobody is and when the
  session ends. The host going takes it with it.
- **Asked for by the hub only on the free version**: `StartSessionMsg.ShowNotice = Free` →
  `AgentService.HostArguments` (now static) adds `--notice` → the host. A full company's tray app
  already says so, so it gets none.
- **And the free version never falls back to a tray app** when the agent's host does not connect: the
  session ends saying the computer's support service did not start it (`TenantHub`, the fallback timer).
- **Not on the secure desktop**: a UAC prompt or Ctrl+Alt+Del is another desktop and shows without it,
  as with the privacy screen. Said rather than half-done.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/noticeprobe` (new) | **21 of 21**, on this laptop, as `privacyprobe` does: the words for one and two technicians; the agent's REAL command line with `--notice` for a session asking and without for one not; a magenta window under the bar — **control** (not excluded): GDI and Desktop Duplication both see the AMBER bar over it, with amber either side of the white words (they fit) — **test** (as shipped): both see THROUGH it to magenta; one bar per monitor, top centre, inside it; topmost, click-through, never activated; a click reaches the window underneath; a topmost window opened later pushed back under; re-worded for a second technician with the first bars gone; nothing left when nobody is. The control's picture is kept as `notice-control.png` and was looked at. |
| `freecheck` 43 | a free session asks for the notice. |
| `unattendedpw` 65 | a full company's does not. |
| re-run | `privacyprobe` 14. `codeccheck` needs a remote machine and was not run. |

**A FULL ship** (host, agent), a **platform deploy**, and the free computer reinstalled. `TEST-3.6.md`
section BU, 475–478.

## 105. The free version's portal and console — 2026-10-06 (Stage F)

Clint's answer: a small portal (My account, Downloads, its machines, Upgrade — Upgrade is Stage G) and
no tickets, clients, people or knowledge base; a console with only what the free version has.

### The portal

- **ONE rule, `Services/FreePortal.cs`, asked by a middleware in front of every `/portal` and
  `/api/portal` address** (Program.cs, after the company clock): a free company may open Computers,
  Downloads, My account, Upgrade, the light/dark switch and the console's hand-off, nothing else. A
  refused page goes to Computers with *"That is part of the full version"*; an API gets 403. **A page
  added next year is refused to a free company until somebody adds it to the list** — that is the point.
- **`/portal/machines` — Your computers** (new): its computers, online or not, *N of 2*, removals left,
  **Remove** through the hub's own rule (§101), and *Add a computer* (the `/download/{slug}` link) while
  there is room. **Post, then redirect, and never words in the address**: the result comes back as
  `?removed=<install id>` (the name read from the `DeviceRemoval` on record) or `?refused=month|other`, so
  a crafted link cannot put a sentence on the page — and the light/dark switch's way back is never a
  form post. A full company opening it is sent to Devices.
- **The menu** (`_Layout`): Computers, Downloads, My account; no office chat script (one person).
- **Downloads**: the console, and the installer link for its computers — nothing for customers or
  technicians. **`/get/{slug}`** for a free company: *Add a computer to …*, one download.

### The console

- **`StateMsg.Free` → `DashboardForm.ApplyFree`**, with every state: no Tickets, Office chat, Website
  chat, Knowledge base or New ticket (the header closes up — `LayoutHeader` now places only what it
  shows), no customer chat, no incoming calls, no *Connect with a code*, **no tabs at all** (one kind of
  computer), *Your computers (N of 2, M online)* as the heading, no *Technicians online*. A full
  company's state puts everything back, so an upgrade needs only a sign-in.
- **Right-click**: Connect, Forget saved password, **Remove this computer…** (asked first; the server
  refuses past the month's two, in words).
- **Connect asks no reason** (no tickets): with the password saved it goes straight in; otherwise
  `ReasonDialog(askReason: false)` asks the password alone.
- **The session window** (`SessionForm(free: true)`): Tools is Files and the two printing items
  (`FreePlan.Tools`); System keeps Ctrl+Alt+Del, Task Manager, lock and restart, without the privacy screen.

## 106. Removing a machine on the full version, with a reason; Uninstall from the tray app — 2026-10-06

Clint, while the free version was being built: *"The full system also needs a remove option for devices, both
via console and portal with a reason why. this is important for when machines get upgraded, replaced or a
person has been using their own private device."* His answers: **a supervisor or the owner**
(`Permissions.CanRemoveDevices`); **a reason picked from a list with a note, required for Other**
(`RemovalReasons`, Shared — Upgraded, Replaced, Private device, No longer a customer, Other); **the history
kept**; **a machine that is online uninstalls itself**. Then: *"there should also be an uninstall option of the
client app tray for someone who no longer wants to use the product."*

### What it is

- **ONE removal, both versions** (`TenantHub.Free.cs`): `RemoveDeviceAsync(deviceId, who, role, reason,
  note)` does the version's checks — free: twice a calendar month, no reason; full: a supervisor/owner and a
  valid reason, no limit — then `RemoveCoreAsync`: the row goes (**tickets, sessions and reports keep their
  DeviceId and stay**), a `DeviceRemoval` is written **with `Reason` and `Note`** (migration
  `DeviceRemovalReasons`), sessions end, connections are told and closed, every console drops the row.
- **The removed install is refused on return on BOTH versions now** — it was free-only, which on the full
  version would have let an agent still running over there put the machine straight back.
- **An online agent uninstalls itself**: `ErrorMsg.Uninstall` to the AGENT connection only →
  `DeviceLink.OnRemoved` → `AgentService.UninstallSelf`: our health check off first
  (`HealthCheckKeeper.RemoveForUninstall`; one this app did not install is left alone), then the SAME
  `Uninstall-Client.ps1` a person would run, **copied out with its branding** (`Shared/ClientUninstall.cs` —
  it deletes the folder it would run from) and started on its own (it stops the service on its way).
  **The installer now keeps `Uninstall-Client.ps1` in Program Files** for this; an install made before
  cannot uninstall itself, says so in the agent's log, and stays refused. An offline machine is refused when
  it returns and is never told to uninstall — Clint's answer.
- **The console**: `StateMsg.MayRemoveDevices` → right-click **Remove this computer…** → `RemoveDeviceDialog`
  (says whether it will uninstall itself; Why?, Note; the rule checked before sending, the hub decides).
- **The portal**: **Remove** beside each machine on Devices for a supervisor/owner → `/portal/removedevice`
  (page policy *Tenant* AND the hub's check; posts to its own address, so the light/dark switch's way back is
  a page) → back on Devices, *"Removed X."* — named from the record, never from the address. Devices ends
  with **Removed machines**: when, by whom, why and the note.
- **Uninstall… in the tray app** (above Exit): asked once, then `Uninstall-Client.ps1` run **with
  administrator permission** (Windows asks; No changes nothing). Only once Windows has said yes is the server
  told (`ClientUninstallingMsg`, **CLIENT connection only**), so the machine leaves the list as
  **"Uninstalled at the machine"** by *"{user} at {machine}"* — and the agent is not told to run a second
  uninstaller. If the tray app is not connected at that moment the server is not told; the machine simply
  goes offline. Not offered on the free version, which has no tray app.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/removecheck` (new) | **31 of 31**: the uninstall command copied out with its branding (and *none* for an old install); the owner may and a technician may not (state and refusal); no reason / Other without a note / an unknown reason all refused with nothing removed; Replaced with a note — every console told, the AGENT told to uninstall, the tray app only refused, the ticket kept, reason/note/who recorded, the install refused on return and not told again; three more the same month (no limit), offline, refused on return and never told to uninstall; the tray app's Uninstall recorded as *Uninstalled at the machine* by *probe at HOME-PC*, an agent saying it ignored, the agent not told to uninstall; the portal — Remove for the owner not a technician, the page refusing a technician, the removed list, a reason required, Private device named on Devices and the agent told. **With the permission check and the client-only check out: 25 of 31.** |
| `fitprobe` 324, `lookprobe` 346 | the Remove window (online and offline) and the free version's password-only Connect, at 150%, light and dark. |
| re-run | `freecheck` 43 (its "full has no Remove" now "full asks a reason"), `freeportal` 32, `freeinstall` 16, `dashtabs` 132. |

**Not driven by any harness: the agent and the tray app really running the uninstaller** — it needs a real
install and administrator rights. Checks 487 and 490.

**Platform deploy (migration `DeviceRemovalReasons`), a FULL ship (agent, tray app, installer) and a client
reinstall** — an install made before this keeps no uninstaller and cannot remove itself. `TEST-3.6.md`
section BW, 485–491.

## 107. Upgrading from the free version, in place — 2026-10-06 (Stage G). THE FREE VERSION IS BUILT.

Clint's answer: *"Yes, in place"* — the same account, the same two computers, the same saved passwords; a
normal company once the owner accepts the full terms and price.

### What it is

- **`/portal/upgrade`** (in `FreePortal`'s list; *Upgrade* on the free menu, an **Upgrade** button on the
  free console's header that signs straight in to it, and a link on Your computers when it is full): what the
  full version adds, the price — **free → R500 a month** (the region's package for the people in seats, one),
  after a **14-day free trial** — and the region's **FULL** terms. One tick, one button. A full company
  opening it is sent to Billing.
- **The rule, `TenantService.UpgradeAsync`**: free only; **the owner only** (`Permissions.CanAcceptPrice`);
  the terms by their fingerprint, ticked; **the exact price token shown** (`UpgradeQuote`, a
  `Pricing.PriceRise` from nothing to the package — §83's rule, so a figure changed in the meantime is asked
  again). Then `Plan` → full ("five-user"), **Status Trial for 14 days** (it was approved already, so nobody
  approves it again — an assumption; it is the trial a new signup gets), the FULL terms kept word for word
  (`TermsAcceptance`), the price agreed recorded (`SeatAgreement`, *Upgraded from the free version*,
  0 → 500). Nothing else changes: the owner stays Owner + Technician, the machines, rows and saved
  passwords are untouched.
- **The hub, `PlanChangedAsync`**: the full version's rules from that moment, and **every open console is
  sent its state again** (`StateFor`, now the one place a console's state is built), so it becomes the full
  console without signing in. The page lands on **Billing**, which says the trial has started.
- **The free computers keep running as they are**: agent only, no tray app (their installed `brand.json`
  still says free, so the installed copy does not become a tray app). Installing the support program on them
  again gives them the full version's tray app.

The page: Upgrade on the menu, the price from free to R500 after a 14-day trial, the FULL terms (not the free section); no tick, other terms, a price not the one shown — each refused, still free. Upgrading: on Billing saying so; full, in a 14-day trial; the full terms kept by fingerprint; *0>500, Upgraded from the free version, by the owner*. Then: the open console told at once (full, may remove), both computers, the remembered password — connecting without typing it; a third computer let on; tickets answer (the session held after had one); the full portal; Upgrade again goes to Billing. **With the hub not told: 16 of 21.** |

### The free version, all of it

Stages A–G of `docs/NEXT-SESSION-FREE.md` are built: remembered passwords (§100), the limits at the hub

and the upgrade (§107) — and, asked for along the way, removing machines on the full version and the tray

## 108. Recurring tasks — a sixth ticket category — 2026-10-07

Clint: *"we need to have an option for recurring tasks. An option to select, daily, weekly, or monthly and on
what day. Some cases are for maintenance, some are for billing, some are for readings so it would very much be
a category of its own ... setup the task once assign it to the correct person/persons and forget about it, but
it should also have a cancel task option if the task becomes obsolete."* His five answers are in
`docs/NEXT-SESSION-WORKFLOWS.md`, "Recurring task".

### What it is

- **A schedule, not a ticket.** `RecurringTask` (Data): title, details, type, optional client, people
  (`Assignees`' "Jason, Ryan"), priority, and the calendar — `Repeats` Daily (`WeekdaysOnly`), Weekly (`Days`,
  one bit per `DayOfWeek`) or Monthly (`MonthDay` 1–31, **0 = last day**; the 31st in a short month is its
  last day, never skipped). `NextDue` and `LastOpenedFor` are company DATES. Cancelled is a mark
  (`CancelledUtc`/`By`/`Reason`), never a delete.
- **Each due day opens an ordinary ticket**, `TicketCategory.Recurring` (**5**, offered LAST), source
  `TicketSource.Recurring` (6), with `Ticket.RecurringTaskId` and `Ticket.DueOn`, already assigned, its story
  starting *"Maintenance — due Wednesday 7 October 2026. Every Wednesday, for Zenith. Assigned to Sue."*
- **When: 06:00 in the company's own zone** (answer 5; `RecurringTaskService.MorningHour`). `RecurringTaskSweep`
  asks once a minute and at start-up. Set up for today after 06:00, today's opens at once. **The next opens
  even if the last is open** (answer 3) — `IsOverdue` is a ticket still at Due after its day; shown on the
  ticket, the list and the console. A day missed while the server was down opens late rather than never (a
  monthly billing run must not vanish), at most `CatchUpLimit` (31) per schedule per pass. Free and suspended
  companies open nothing. One ticket per schedule per day, whatever races.
- **The route: Due → Done (closes) / To be invoiced** (answer 2) — `recurring-done` and `recurring-invoice`,
  General's two steps with keys of their own because they are **`OfficeToo`**: a billing or readings task is
  often the office administrator's, and the bench's rule would leave them unable to finish their own task.
  So *Who it goes to* offers **everybody**, the office too — not the console's seated roster.
- **Who** (answer 4, `MayChange`): anybody sets one up; the people on it, a supervisor or the owner change or
  cancel it. A technician sees only the ones they are on (`MaySee`); the office and supervisors see all.
- **Types** (answer 1): `RecurringKind`, Maintenance / Billing / Readings written the first time anybody asks,
  then the company's own, with the item list's duplicate guard (`QuoteService.MatchKey`: "toner printer" is
  "Printer toner").
- **Cancel** stops future tickets only; an open one stays open and is told in its story.

### Where

- **Every rule: `Services/RecurringTaskService.cs`** (calendar, `Problem`, `MayChange`/`MaySee`,
  create/update/cancel, `OpenDueAsync`, `InfoAsync`, and the sweep).
- **Portal**: `/portal/recurring` (list), `/portal/recurring/new` and `/portal/recurring/{id}` (one form for
  set up and change, Cancel below, the tickets it opened); New ticket's *Recurring task…* goes there (and a
  posted Category 5 is sent there — the form never makes one by hand); a *Recurring tasks* button on Tickets;
  `_Recurring.cshtml` on BOTH ticket layouts (§61); *Due … Overdue* in the ticket list. Not in `FreePortal`'s
  list, so the free version never sees it.
- **Console**: New ticket → *Recurring task* (type, how often, the days; the office's names arrive by
  `RecurringKindsMsg` and show only for this type — `FitOfficePeople` grows the window once for their line);
  the ticket window's *Recurring task* card with *Change in the browser* and *Cancel the task…* (asks why in
  the window). New messages `RecurringKindsRequestMsg`/`RecurringKindsMsg`, `RecurringSetMsg`,
  `RecurringCancelMsg` — refused on the free version by its allow-list. `Hub/TenantHub.Recurring.cs`;
  `HubRegistry.Recurring` tells every console of a ticket the sweep opened.

### Found on the way — read before storing a DATE

**`PlatformDb` converts every `DateTime` not marked UTC with `ToUniversalTime()`, which asks the SERVER's
zone.** A company date (midnight, no zone) written as Unspecified came back on this PC (South Africa) as 22:00
the day before — the ticket due on Wednesday said Tuesday, and a schedule set up at 05:00 opened at once. The
live server runs on UTC, which would have hidden it there and nowhere else. `RecurringTaskService.AsDate`
stores a date as midnight **marked UTC** — not because it is a UTC time, but so the converter leaves it alone.
`recurringcheck` saw it on its first run: **82 of 98 with it, 98 of 98 without.**

And in the console: the office's names arrive after the New ticket window is sized, and their extra line
brought in a scrollbar that cut the right column's Type box off. `ticketformprobe`'s "inside the window" could
not see that (the box WAS inside the window, behind the scroller); a check that the full-size window needs no
scrollbar does — **125 of 126 without `FitOfficePeople`.**

And the console's *Change in the browser* would have landed on the ticket queue: the one-use sign-in link takes
only the addresses `PortalHandoffService.SafePath` lists, and `/portal/recurring/{n}` was not one. It is now —
digits only, as tickets are. Seen while adding recurring checks to `ticketwire`, which now holds it.

Built with `InvariantGlobalization` like the platform. **82 with the date fault back.** |

## 109. A ding for a chat message, a ring for somebody waiting — 2026-10-07

Clint: *"When someone receives a chat message, I would like it to play a sound. A simple ding ding type sound.
Also when we get incoming support call requests, this should also play a sound, more like a constant ringing
which is not overly intrusive."* Before this, Windows' own Asterisk played once for a customer's chat line and
Exclamation once for a call, then nothing; office chat, website chat, the tray app and the portal played
nothing at all, and a machine with its system sounds off played nothing anywhere.

### What it is

- **Two sounds of our own, made in code: `Shared/Chimes.cs`.** `Ding()` is two soft bell notes rising (C6
  then E6, 1.15 s, peak 0.40); `Ring()` is ONE ring, two warm bursts (G5+B5, a gentle 12 Hz warble, peak
  0.26), played every `RingEverySeconds` (4) while somebody waits — about a second of sound and three of
  quiet, which is what keeps it from being intrusive. WAV bytes, the same everywhere: the console, the tray
  app, and the platform, which serves them at **`/sounds/ding.wav`** and **`/sounds/ring.wav`** (public; the
  visitor pages use them).
- **`UI/Sounds.cs` plays them** in the console and the tray app: `Ding()` (several within 1.2 s ding once)
  and `Ringing(bool)` — told the TRUTH whenever the waiting changes, never "start"/"stop"; "on" again does
  not restart it. One sound at a time (Windows plays one per process), so a ding mid-ring cuts that ring.
  **Muted is per Windows user, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RemoteSupport\sounds.json`, not on the server** — chosen
  so no migration collided with the session building §108 at the same time; it does not follow a person to
  another PC. `Sounds.Played` and `IsRinging` exist for the harness.
- **When it rings (console, `DashboardForm.UpdateRinging`)**: any call `Ringing` that THIS person has not
  dismissed, or any website visitor nobody has answered (`_webWaiting`). Asked from `UpdatePopup` (every call
  change, and `LoadState` — signing in while somebody waits rings) and from website chat's `WaitingChanged`.
  Answered anywhere, cancelled, or dismissed here: it stops.
- **When it dings**: a customer's line in the session chat card (**never the `RecentChat` a (re)connect hands
  back** — `AppendChat(…, live: false)`; it used to replay the Asterisk AND the tray balloons for history);
  office chat, every message somebody else sends that reaches me, Everyone's too; website chat, a line from
  the visitor *I* am answering (one nobody has answered is ringing already); the tray app, a technician's
  message (devices are never sent old chat, so no replay guard is needed there).
- **The portal (`wwwroot/sounds.js`, `window.rspSounds`)**: the same rules for office chat and website chat in
  `chat.js`; mute per browser in localStorage, a **🔔 Mute sounds** button beside Light/Dark (`#soundToggle`,
  not on the free version). **Support requests do not ring in the portal** — a call can only be answered in
  the console, and the portal ringing for one it cannot take would be noise. A browser plays nothing on a page
  nobody has clicked since it loaded; that is the browser's rule, and a refused play is skipped.
- **The visitor pages ding on a reply**: the website chat frame (`webchat.js`, live lines only — not the
  `hello` replay) and browser support (`help.js`). No mute there; they are the customer's.
- **The console's header has a bell (🔔, 🔕 while muted), not words.** "Mute sounds" in words pushed
  Light/Dark off the header at 1920 px on Clint's 150% screen. Square from its own font's height (§30);
  tooltip and the tray menu carry the words. When room runs out Light/Dark steps out first, then the bell;
  both are on the tray menu. Hidden on the free version, which has no chat and no calls.

### Found on the way — read before laying out the header

**`LayoutHeader` must never read a control's `Visible` back.** It runs once before the window is on screen,
when `Visible` reads false for every control; the first version decided Light/Dark's place from
`_soundBtn.Visible`, so a console opened at its size and never resized lost Light/Dark for good. `dashtabs`
found it — **131 of 133**, "it is showing (light/dark)" at 1600 px — and it looked at first like the bell
taking the room. It now keeps `soundShown`/`modeShown` flags, as `_webChatShown` already did; the header's
`TextLimit` read `_modeBtn.Visible` the same way and does not any more. `soundcheck` now asks the never-resized
case itself.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/soundcheck` (new) | **52 of 52.** The sounds: valid WAVs whose sizes add up, about a second, nothing clipped, silent at the end, C6 then E6 in the ding, two bursts and a silent gap in the ring, the ring quieter than the ding, more rest than sound. The REAL `DashboardForm`, `WebChatForm` and `StaffChatForm` fed the hub's messages: history never dings; a customer dings, my own does not, three at once ding once; a call rings at once and again 4 s later; answered, both dismissed, cancelled → stops; one of two dismissed → still rings; signing in with somebody waiting rings, a reconnect with nobody stops it; a waiting visitor rings, their lines do not ding over it, answering stops it, the visitor I answer dings, a colleague's does not; office chat to me and to Everyone ding, mine does not; the bell mutes (🔕, file written), muted plays nothing but still knows somebody waits, unmuting from the tray rings the waiting call again; the header at 1920 and 1366, Light/Dark stepping out first, the glyph actually drawn, the never-resized window; the free version without it. Plays the sounds aloud. **`--save <folder>`** writes ding.wav, ring.wav and ringing-12-seconds.wav to listen to. |
| re-run | `dashtabs` **133** (131 with the `Visible` read-back), `lookprobe` 346, `staffchatprobe` 18, `webchatprobe` 32. |
| walked in the browser | a throwaway platform (`workflowdemo`, `.claude/launch.json` "platform-sounds"), every `play()` recorded: Bob's office chat to Sue → `ding.wav`, *playing*; Sue's own → nothing; muted (🔕, `rsp.sounds=off`) → the message shown, nothing played; website chat switched on, a visitor in a second tab → `ring.wav` at 22.9, 26.9, 30.9 s; Sam's reply → no ring in the 9 s after, and the visitor's page played `ding.wav`; the visitor's answer → Sam's `ding.wav`. `/sounds/nope.wav` is a 404. |

**Not walked**: browser support's ding (`help.js`, one line, the same call as `webchat.js`'s), and the tray
app's (one line in `MainForm`'s chat handler). **Not on hardware.** No migration. **Platform deploy, then the
console re-downloaded and the client reinstalled** for the tray app's ding. `TEST-3.6.md` section BZ, 506–512.

## 110. Windows shortcuts go to their machine — 2026-10-07

Clint: *"When doing remote support, we notice that windows shortcuts dont work. The idea is that while doing
remote support on a machine, using windows shortcuts works within that session from the technician machine.
Can we make this happen without affecting the way control c and control v currently work?"* Then: *"build it
without the on off switch."*

### Why they did not work

The picture forwards keys from `ScreenView.OnKeyDown`/`OnKeyUp` — the ordinary key messages. Windows never
sends those for the keys it keeps: **the Windows key and everything pressed with it, Alt+Tab, Alt+Esc,
Ctrl+Esc, Ctrl+Shift+Esc, Print Screen.** It acts on them first, so they opened the Start menu, Run, the task
switcher or Task Manager on the TECHNICIAN's machine. The host was never the problem: `InputInjector` replays
a Windows key like any other.

### What it is — `Technician/ScreenView.Shortcuts.cs`

- **A low-level keyboard hook (`WH_KEYBOARD_LL`) that exists only while the picture has the keyboard focus**:
  installed in `OnGotFocus`, removed in `OnLostFocus` and `Dispose`. Click a tool window, the toolbar or
  another program and the shortcuts are the technician's own again. **No on/off switch, by Clint's
  decision** — do not add one.
- **It takes only those keys and lets everything else through untouched** (`Catch`): the Windows keys; any
  key while a Windows key it took is held; Print Screen; Tab with Alt; Escape with Ctrl or Alt. Only when
  Control is ticked, the picture is live (not `Stale`), focused, and its window is in front. A key's release
  goes the way its press went (`_taken`), so Win+E with Win let go first still sends E's release.
- **Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V do not pass through it** — they arrive by the ordinary path exactly as before, and the
  clipboard mirroring never depended on the keys anyway (it watches the clipboards). `shortcutcheck` asserts
  the hook's counter does not move for them.
- **A held modifier goes first.** The hook is called AHEAD of the window's queued key messages, so for a quick
  Alt+Tab the hook sees Tab before the window has handled Alt, and their machine got Tab then Alt — measured:
  `shortcutcheck` 36 of 39 without the line. Any of Ctrl/Shift/Alt that is held but not yet sent
  (`_remoteDown`, now kept by `OnKeyDown`/`OnKeyUp`) is sent down first; the ordinary message then arrives
  as a second key-down, which their machine takes as auto-repeat.
- **The focus leaving lets go of everything still held over there** — the hook's keys and the ordinary path's
  (`RemoveShortcutHook`). The release of a key held as the focus left goes to whatever has the focus now, so
  their machine used to go on holding Ctrl or Alt. This is new for ordinary keys too.
- `IsExtended` now includes LWin, RWin and Apps, as real keyboards send them.

**Windows will not let any program take two:** Ctrl+Alt+Del (the toolbar's button) and **Win+L, which locks the
technician's own PC** (the toolbar's Lock locks theirs). The hook is silently removed by Windows if this
thread ever stops answering for longer than `LowLevelHooksTimeout`; the next focus puts it back.

The browser guest (`guestview.js`, §91) is unchanged: a browser cannot take these keys.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/shortcutcheck` (new) | **39 of 39.** The REAL `SessionForm` with no server; keys pressed for REAL by `SendInput` from another thread, so they go through Windows and the hook as a keyboard's would; refuses to press anything unless its own window is in front with the picture focused. A, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V by the ordinary path, hook untouched; Win, Win+R, Win+Shift+S, Win+E (Win released first), Alt+Tab typed and in one burst, Alt+Shift+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Esc, Ctrl+Esc, Alt+Esc, Print Screen sent in order and balanced — **and this machine's window still in front after each** (the Start menu, Run, the snipping bar, Explorer, Task Manager or the switcher would have taken it); plain Escape and Tab ordinary; Control unticked / connection down → left here; clicking away removes the hook and releases the Windows key AND Ctrl over there; focus back puts it back. **36 of 39 with the held-modifier line out.** |

**Not on hardware** — nobody has yet watched the Start menu open on a customer's machine. Console only:
**`Publish-Platform.ps1` (the console rides in the server package; no server code changed), then the console re-downloaded; no client reinstall.**
`TEST-3.6.md` section CA, 513–518.

## 111. A reinstalled machine waits for the office; passwords at 600,000 rounds — 2026-10-07

Roadmap 4.4, §72's "Left for soon after" items 1 and 2, taken up by Clint (*"lets do 1"*).

### The hole, and why the agreed fix was not enough

A machine that comes back with a new install (an uninstall deletes `device.json`) is matched to its old row by
its hardware fingerprint (`PersistDeviceAsync`), so its client link, history, password and tick follow it. The
fingerprint is the board's SMBIOS UUID and Windows' **MachineGuid — both readable by any program on the
machine, no administrator needed**. With those and the company's public tenant key, a stranger's PC could say
"I am that machine, reinstalled" and take the row; a technician would then connect to the wrong computer,
clipboard and files and all.

§72 agreed: *a takeover clears `UnattendedEnabled` until the customer ticks it again.* Reading the code showed
that stops accidents and not an impostor — **the impostor holds the tray app, so they tick it straight back
(and set their own password)**. Asked, Clint chose: **the office confirms it.**

### What it is

- **`Device.ReinstallUnconfirmed`** (migration `ReinstallConfirm`, with `ReinstallConfirmedBy`/`Utc`), set on
  every takeover, carried to consoles as `DeviceInfo.ReinstallUnconfirmed`. **The tick is KEPT** — it was the
  real customer's, and the impostor's tick proves nothing either way.
- **`TenantHub.MayGoUnattended(info)` = the tick AND not unconfirmed — THE question for every unattended door**
  (`Recompute`, `NeedsUnattendedPassword`, `StartSession`'s `mayUseAgent`, the free version's gate). **Never ask
  `UnattendedEnabled` alone again.** Unconfirmed, a technician's connection goes ATTENDED (the agent's
  AskConsent, or the tray app) — the person is asked, no password wanted; the free version (no attended) is
  refused in words.
- **`TenantHub.ConfirmReinstallAsync`** (`Hub/TenantHub.Reinstall.cs`) is the one rule:
  `Permissions.CanConfirmReinstall` (supervisor or owner; the free version's one person is its owner). Console:
  right-click → **Confirm it is the same machine…** (top of the menu while it waits; greyed with whose it is for
  anybody else), `StateMsg.MayConfirmReinstall`, `ConfirmReinstallMsg`. Portal: a *reinstalled — not confirmed*
  pill and **Confirm same machine** on Devices; **It is mine** on the free version's Your computers.
- **Said everywhere**: the console row reads *"NAME — reinstalled, not confirmed"* with the amber dot and counts
  as *not ready* on the Unattended tab (`DeviceList.ClaimsUnattendedButCannot`); the tray app's note says the IT
  company must confirm it (`UnattendedStateMsg.AwaitingConfirm`, `UnattendedWording`); the free installer ends
  by saying to confirm it (`FreeSetup.SetPasswordAsync(awaitingConfirm:)`).
- **Found and fixed on the way — and it bit the free version's reinstall every time on a real database:** a tick
  or a password from the client connection that arrived after the hello but BEFORE `PersistDeviceAsync` had read
  the stored record was made to a fresh in-memory record, not stored (the row had no new device id yet), then
  overwritten by the stored one. The free installer sends both in exactly that gap, so a reinstalled free
  computer lost its tick and could never be reached; a brand-new one could lose its password while the
  installer said "done". Now `_recordRead` (a TaskCompletionSource per hello) and **`WhenRecordReadAsync` (10 s
  at most) hold `SetUnattendedAsync` and `SetUnattendedPasswordAsync` until the record is in.**
- The portal's Devices page **never showed its `Error`** — a refused Link vanished. It does now (`devicesError`).

### Passwords at 600,000 rounds

`Passwords.Rounds` = 600,000 (OWASP); **the rounds travel in the salt**, `"600000$<base64>"`, so no column was
added and a bare base64 salt is an old hash at `OldRounds` (120,000) — still verified. **At a person's next
sign-in** (`AuthService.PasswordAsync`, after the password is proved) an old hash is made again; **the security
stamp does NOT move** (it would sign them out everywhere for signing in). **A machine's unattended password is
NOT upgraded on verify**: remembered passwords (§100) are keyed on its salt, and re-making it would forget
everybody's — it moves to 600,000 when somebody at the machine next sets one. `RemoteSupport.Server` (the old
LAN server) is untouched.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/reinstallcheck` (new) | **33 of 33**, a real hub on a platform of its own with `PersistDeviceDelayMs` 1500 so the gap is open: the owner may confirm, a technician may not; before, unattended; reinstalled — marked, one row, tick kept, NOT unattended, the tray app told; the owner's connection ATTENDED with no password; the tray ticking off and on changes nothing; a technician refused in words; the owner confirms — every console, the tray app, recorded, unattended again; a plain reconnect is not a reinstall; **the flag survives a server restart**; **a tick and a password sent in the gap are both kept**; the portal's pill, Confirm for the owner only, a technician's post refused on the page, the owner's confirming; **the free version**: installer told, console refused, *It is mine*, then unattended. **30 of 33 with `MayGoUnattended` back to the tick alone; 28 of 33 with the record-read wait out — two of the five are the free reinstall itself.** |
| `tools/hashcheck` (new) | **15 of 15**: a new password says `600000$`, verifies, a wrong one does not; an OLD hash — worked out in the harness by the 120,000-round formula, not by `Passwords` — verifies and is read as needing an upgrade; bad salts verify nothing and throw nothing; then a real sign-in against an account rewritten to the old format by SQL: a wrong password upgrades nothing, the right one signs in and leaves a `600000$` hash, **the security stamp unmoved**, and signs in again. One verify takes 83 ms on this laptop. |
| re-run | `unattendedcheck` 40, `unattendedpw` 65, `unattendedwire` 13, `freeinstall` 16, `removecheck` 31, `consentwire` 34, `dashtabs` 133 — and **`freecheck` 45, which found a fault**: the free console's allow-list (`ConsoleMaySendOnFree`) refused `ConfirmReinstallMsg`, so a free owner's right-click would have answered *"part of the full version"*. Added; `freecheck` now confirms from the console (its own reinstall of BRANCH-A is a takeover too, so it asserts the mark first). |

**Not on hardware.** **`Publish-Platform.ps1` (migration `ReinstallConfirm`), the console re-downloaded; a FULL
ship and a client reinstall for the tray app's note and the free installer's words** (an older tray app and
installer work, they just do not say why). Existing rows are NOT marked — only takeovers from now on.
`TEST-3.6.md` section CB, 519–524.

## 112. End-to-end encryption of sessions — 2026-10-07

Roadmap 4.4, §72's "Left for soon after" item 4. Clint: *"Can we do this?"* — and three answers: **encrypt AND
pin machine keys; older apps allowed but clearly marked; the browser routes included.** The design and its
reasoning are `docs/NEXT-SESSION-E2E.md`; read it before changing anything here.

### Why

TLS ends at Caddy, so every session was plaintext INSIDE our server: the picture, every key typed on a customer's
machine (passwords included), the clipboard, file contents, sound, voice, scripts and output. Now the host and
each console agree a key the server never sees and the CONTENT travels sealed (AES-256-GCM). The server still
relays it, still knows who connected to what, and still writes the audit trail.

### What it is

- **`Shared/SessionSeal.cs`** — one per session socket at each END, never on the server. **Everything is sealed
  except `ClearTypes`, the short list the hub ACTS on** (consent, the disclosures, the audit lines, chat,
  Ctrl+Alt+Del, the microphone rule, the handshake) — safe by default: a new message is sealed unless somebody
  decides the server must read it. **Add to that list only for something the HUB acts on**, and change
  `wwwroot/e2e.js`'s copy with it (`e2ecore` fails until you do).
- **Frames**: a sealed message is `[7][tagLen][tag][sender][counter][ct+tag]` (its JSON type visible); sealed
  binary is `[kind|0x80][sender][counter][ct+tag]`. **Every drop rule and allow-list asks `BinKind.Of(b[0])`,
  never `b[0]`** — `WsConnection`, `BinaryRelay`, the visitor and free allow-lists all changed for it. The
  header and the session id are the associated data; nonce = sender ‖ counter; replays refused. **The receiver
  refuses a sealed message whose type is not its tag, or is a clear type** — so the hub's allow-lists, which
  judge the visible tag (`SessionSeal.Probe`), still hold.
- **`WsConnection.Seal`** does it as frames are queued and arrive: the host's thirty-odd send sites, the console,
  the recorder — untouched. **A connection with no seal (the server's) passes sealed frames through untouched.**
- **The key** (`E2eHandshake`): the host makes K; each viewer says `E2eHelloMsg` (its ephemeral P-256 key) on
  joining and on `E2eReadyMsg`; the host answers `E2eKeyMsg` — K wrapped under HKDF(ECDH), **signed by the
  machine's identity** over session, viewer key, host key and sender number. One answer per viewer key, ever (a
  second would restart its counter).
- **The identity** (`Host/MachineIdentityStore.cs`): ECDSA P-256 in `%ProgramData%\RemoteSupport\identity.key`,
  SYSTEM and Administrators only, DPAPI machine scope (a copied disk opens it nowhere else). Made the first time a
  host runs as SYSTEM; a host running as the person signs nothing. **Uninstall deletes it: a reinstall is a new
  identity.** A key that cannot be read is NOT replaced (every console would cry "changed" for a local fault).
- **The pins** (`Shared/MachinePins.cs`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RemoteSupport\machine-keys.json`): by device id AND by
  machine name + whose it is (a reinstall or impostor arrives with a NEW id). Changed — **or a pinned machine
  answering unsigned** (a server pretending to be the host would just leave the signature out) — holds the
  session: nothing opened, nothing sent, until the technician answers *"Is this the same computer?"* (No is the
  default and ends it). TOFU on first contact, said plainly in the brief.
- **Mode** (`Hub/TenantHub.E2e.cs`): the hub tells the host `E2eModeMsg` — sealed while every viewer said hello,
  CLEAR once one has been in for 5 s without (an older console). In sealed mode the host refuses clear content
  (only the server could have sent it). **Each console's badge says what ACTUALLY arrived** — so a server forcing
  clear is visible: 🔒 End-to-end encrypted (green) / 🔒 Encrypted — identity not checked (amber: tray-hosted, or
  browser support) / Not end-to-end encrypted (amber, for the rest of the session) / Identity changed — waiting.
- **The ticket keeps its script line**: the console sends `ScriptAuditMsg` (language, FIRST line) beside the sealed
  script while keyed; the hub writes it and never passes it on. Unkeyed, the hub reads the clear script as before —
  never both.
- **The browser** (`wwwroot/e2e.js`, loaded by `/guest/web` and `/help/{slug}`): the same frames and handshake in
  WebCrypto, opened and sent through ordered promise chains (async decryption would otherwise reorder counters).
  The guest page shows the lock under its status; browser support is a HOST that signs nothing. **WebCrypto needs
  a secure page: https (live) or localhost — a plain http LAN address falls back to not encrypted.**

### What it does not do (say it when asked)

A taken-over server can still START a session — it authorises technicians and the agent obeys it. Pinning stops
it reading or hijacking a REAL technician's session. The audit trail (who, file NAMES, a script's first line,
reboots) is readable on purpose. Chat is the customer's record and stays on the ticket.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/e2ecore` (new) | **48 of 48**: tags and the clear list — **and e2e.js's copy word for word**; the handshake (signed; another viewer's, another session's, a renumbered sender, a swapped identity, a removed signature all refused; a server answering as the host can only use its own identity); the seal (no plaintext in a frame, kind visible, altered / replayed / older / other session / wrong key refused; frames built BY HAND: a tag that lies and a clear type sealed refused); the pins (first time, matches, changed by id and by name under a new id, unsigned-when-pinned, kept on disk, a damaged file forgets); two real WebSockets (sealed and opened, clear list clear, a seal-less end relays untouched, a sealing host refuses clear content, a console counts it). **43 of 47 with the tag and replay checks out.** |
| `tools/e2ewire` (new) | **31 of 31** through a REAL hub, the REAL `SessionLink`, and a stand-in host that keeps every frame as relayed: four host markers and three console markers arrive opened and appear **nowhere in what the server relayed and nowhere in the platform's database**; the ticket still names the script (once); clear types sent sealed by a rogue console never reach the host; an older console joins → CLEAR, it can read, the new badge says so, it leaves → sealed again; identity changed → asked, **nothing opened before the answer**, yes re-pins; pinned but unsigned → asked, no keeps it shut; the free version's allow-list drops a sealed script by its tag. **Fails with the hub's clear-type refusal out, and with the identity hold out (27 of 31).** |
| `tools/e2einterop` (new) + the built-in browser | `guestwebdemo`'s FAKE-PC now seals like the real host; `/guest/web` walked: the lock shown, the sealed picture drawn, a click and a key arriving sealed (opened 3, clear 0, refused 0). In the page, `rspE2e.host` against `rspE2e.viewer` (replay refused, no plaintext in the frames); and **the browser host's answer and frames opened by the C# viewer, a C# frame opened by the browser host** — the browser-support pairing no harness can drive. |
| re-run | `outsidervisit` 65, `freecheck` 45, `consentwire` 34, `sessionextras` 35, `voicewire` 37, `websupportcheck` 64, `guestcheck` 33, `clipledger` 20, `ticketpersession` 30, `toolbarprobe` 53, `fitprobe` 324, `viewonlyprobe` 18. |

**Not driven by any harness: the real `HostEngine`'s wiring** (it is small — a seal, `E2eReadyMsg` after the yes,
`AnswerViewer`, `E2eModeMsg`) and **the identity file as SYSTEM**. Both are checks 525–527 and 530. **Not on
hardware.** `Publish-Platform.ps1` (no migration), the console re-downloaded, a FULL ship and client reinstall
for the host; until then a machine's sessions say *Not end-to-end encrypted*. `TEST-3.6.md` section CC, 525–534.

## 113. Branding reaches installed machines — 2026-10-07

Roadmap 4.6, **the settings half** (the binary half still waits for code signing). Clint: *"At the moment, a company
that changes its logo or colours only sees it on new downloads. The hub should send the current brand.json when a
machine connects. This doesn't need signing. Can we do this?"*

### What it is

- **`Shared/BrandRefresh.cs` is the one rule.** What travels is **`BrandLook`**: the name, product name, support
  email and phone, colours, welcome text, light/dark for both apps, the three consent settings and the logo. **Never
  the server address, the company key, `Free` or the health check settings — they are not in the type**, so no
  message can point a machine somewhere else. `BrandRefresh.Hash` is the look plus the logo's bytes.
- **The wire.** `HelloMsg.BrandHash` says which look a machine has (empty = the installed one); a link that says
  `DeviceCan.Branding` and has another is sent **`BrandingMsg`** (look, hash, logo bytes) once it is registered
  (`TenantHub.Branding.cs`). Saving Portal → Branding raises `TenantService.BrandingChanged` and every connected
  machine with another look is sent it. **The page saves the words and the logo apart: 1.5 s settle, one message.**
  Per connection, `DeviceConn.BrandHash` is what it has, so nothing is sent twice. The command line (`set-brand`,
  `set-logo`) is another process: it reaches a machine at its next connect (the built look is trusted for a minute).
  The hub's name follows a rename (`Rename`).
- **On the machine it is kept in `branding\live\`, beside the installed `brand.json`, which is NEVER rewritten** —
  `Uninstall-Client.ps1` finds the shortcuts by the company and product names in it, and a renamed company would
  leave them behind. `Branding.Load`/`LoadFrom` lay `live\look.json` over it (`BrandRefresh.Overlay`), so the tray
  app, the consent prompt and `--write-icon` read the new look without knowing. A kept look whose logo has gone is
  ignored (and its hash not said, so it is sent again).
- **The logo gets a new name each time (`logo-{hash}.png`)**: `Image.FromFile` keeps the file locked while it is
  shown, so a running tray app would make an overwrite fail. Old ones are deleted when nothing holds them.
- **The agent keeps it** (SYSTEM, the only thing that can write in Program Files): `AgentService.TakeBranding` saves,
  `BrandRefresh.Reapply`s its own branding (the consent setting for the next session), moves `link.BrandHash`, and
  redraws `branding\app-shortcut.ico` with `RemoteSupport.Client.exe --write-icon` — only where the installer made
  one (the free version has no shortcuts).
- **The tray app restarts into it, quietly, only when nobody is using it** (`MainForm.OnBranding`/`BrandTick`): no
  session, no request waiting, and **no window showing — asked of Windows (`EnumThreadWindows`, visible and not
  minimised)**. It restarts for what is ON DISK, never for the message: in Program Files only the agent can keep it,
  and restarting into the old look would restart for ever. It looks for 10 minutes for the agent to have kept it,
  then waits for idle with no deadline. The new copy is `--tray --after <pid>` (it waits for the old one to let go
  of the single-instance mutex); the server is NOT told the machine is closing — that is Exit. A downloaded "Get
  help now" copy does not take part: it fetched its branding as it started.
- **A reinstall starts from the download**: `Install-Client.ps1` deletes `branding\live`.

### Found on the way — read before asking "is anything on screen"

**The tray app started in the tray is "visible" to Windows the whole time** — minimised at -32000 (measured:
`WindowsForms10.Window… 'Old Look — Old Product' -21333,-21333 158x26`). `IsWindowVisible` alone said a window was
showing for ever and the restart never came; visible AND `!IsIconic` is the question. And a test that closes the
window from outside must post `WM_SYSCOMMAND SC_CLOSE` (what the X sends): a bare `WM_CLOSE` from another process
reads as Task Manager closing the app, and it exits.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/brandpush` (new) | **45 of 45.** On disk: kept beside, read back over; server address, key and health check still the installed ones; `brand.json` untouched byte for byte; a logo name with a path writes nowhere but `live\` under our name; colours that are not colours keep the last good; timeout 0 → 10; no fingerprint / a logo over 4 MB refused, the kept look stays; a held-open logo does not stop the next; a missing logo → installed look; `Reapply`. On the wire (own platform, port 8098): sent once, name and logo byte for byte, no key or server address in the raw frame; the same look → nothing; an older build → nothing; another company's machine gets its own; the REAL `DeviceLink` + `BrandRefresh` keep it and a starting app says so in its real hello; **the portal's save → one message with a 1.9 MB logo whole**, the tray app too, the old build and the other company nothing; saving again unchanged → nothing; the command line → at the next connect. **40 of 44 with the per-connection check and the settle taken out.** |
| the real tray app, by hand (scratch scripts) | Against brandpush's server from a folder of its own: **restarted 7.5 s after connecting, once, into the new look, and asked for nothing more** (three runs). With its window open: **not restarted in 20 s; restarted 3.1 s after the X**. |
| the real agent, as a console program | In a folder laid out like an install, against a company with a logo: kept the look and the logo byte for byte, `brand.json` untouched, **`app-shortcut.ico` redrawn (7 frames)**. |
| re-run | `e2ecore` 48, `trayexit` 16, `freecheck` 45. |

**Not proved: the agent as SYSTEM writing in Program Files, and whether Explorer redraws the desktop shortcut at once
or only when it next refreshes its icon cache.** Checks 535–541. One unexplained double send in an early tray run
(not seen in four since; `link.BrandHash` now moves the moment the look is on disk, closing the likeliest cause). **Not
on hardware.** `Publish-Platform.ps1` (no migration), a FULL ship and client reinstall. **Two things not covered:** the
console (it is re-downloaded whenever it changes, and its own sign-in could carry the same look later), and **an
installed monthly health check**, which copied the logo, name and colours into its own folder when it was installed
(`Install-HealthCheck.ps1`) and keeps them until it is installed again.

## 114. The console's windows carry the company's icon — 2026-10-07

Clint: *"The technician app does not show the tenant icon when open. It shows like a normal windows icon. It does
show correctly in the tray."* True, and measured before the fix: the console's sign-in window answered
`WM_GETICON` with **no icon at all**.

### What was wrong — two things

- **Only the main window was given the logo.** `DashboardForm.BuildTray` set `Icon` on itself and the tray. The
  sign-in window, every session window, Tickets, office chat, website chat, Processes/Performance and every tool
  window kept WinForms' own default — twenty-odd forms, plus the ones built inline.
- **The console's shortcuts named the .exe as their icon** (`ConsoleDownload.Shortcut`, `exe,0`), and the .exe has
  no icon of its own — it is the same file for every company, so it cannot (`BrandIcon`'s remarks). A shortcut,
  and a taskbar button PINNED from it, is drawn from that, not from the window.

### The fix

- **`BrandIcon.UseForEveryWindow(brand)`**, called in `Program.Main` before the sign-in window: the logo becomes
  the DEFAULT icon of every window in the process. WinForms has no public setter, so it sets the static field behind
  `Form.DefaultIcon` (`s_defaultIcon`) by reflection; if a future .NET renames it, it returns false, the trace says
  so, and windows simply keep the old default — `tools/iconcheck` will fail first.
- **Two traps, both measured.** (1) WinForms gives a **`FixedDialog` no icon unless one is set on it**, default or
  not — and the sign-in window is one, in the taskbar. The fixed dialogs that show in the taskbar set it themselves:
  `LoginForm`, `ReasonDialog`, `RemoveDeviceDialog`, Tickets' "Did you mean…" (`BrandIcon.Current`). (2) Setting a
  window's `Icon` to **the default object itself counts as a reset** — so the default is a CLONE, or those dialogs
  lost it again (`iconcheck` caught this one: "no icon").
- **The console's set-up writes `console.ico`** (`BrandIcon.WriteIcoFile`, seven frames) in its folder and points
  the Start menu and desktop shortcuts at it. No logo → the .exe, as before.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/iconcheck` | **24 of 24** (was 19). New CHECK 3 asks a fresh window by `WM_GETICON` and compares pixels: before, WinForms' default; after `UseForEveryWindow`, the company's; a bare fixed dialog none (why they set it); one given `BrandIcon.Current`, the company's — **"no icon" with the default not cloned.** |
| `tools/consoleexecheck` | **32 of 32** (was 31): the harness company now has a logo (`set-logo`), and the downloaded console's shortcut carries `console.ico`. |
| the real console | Started from the new build: its sign-in window carries Anywhere IT's logo by `WM_GETICON`. The 13:05 build of the same day: no icon. |

**Not on hardware.** Console only: `Publish-Platform.ps1` (no migration), then re-download the console — the
re-download is also what rewrites the shortcuts. No client reinstall. **A pinned taskbar button made before the
re-download keeps its old picture: unpin it and pin it again.** `TEST-3.6.md` section CE, 542–545.

## 115. A load test: how much one server carries — 2026-10-07

Somebody told Clint the system was "not enterprise ready" and that SQLite would be a problem; the goal is
10,000 companies. Measure first: **`tools/loadtest`** is thousands of pretend machines (`/ws/device`, a
hello and a ping every 15 s like `DeviceLink`, `--agents` for the second socket), pretend technicians
(`/api/login`, `/ws/tech`) and pretend sessions (ConnectDeviceMsg → a host on `/ws/session` → the viewer
subscribes → H.264-sized frames at `--kbps`, default 200, the scrolling figure from §2.2), raised in
stages (machines, sign-in, sessions, hold), reading every 5 s: connect, sign-in, machine list, session
start, first picture, video relayed against expected, `/health` and one database read
(`/api/branding`). It ends with a VERDICT and says when the LOAD box, not the server, was the limit.
`Link` is a light socket of its own on purpose — WsConnection's 64 KB receive buffer each would make
the load box run out first. net8.0 and Shared only, so it publishes as one Linux file.

- **`loadtest local`** builds a throwaway platform on port 8131, seeds it and runs a small test:
  400 machines / 20 technicians / 40 sessions, 97% of the picture relayed, VERDICT comfortable.
  `--wal` and `--env NAME=VALUE` exist to measure one change at a time.
- **`seed-loadtest <companies> <people> <file>`** (`Services/LoadTestSeed.cs`, hooked before `Cli` in
  Program.cs) fills a server with `load-00001`… companies, one password hashed ONCE. **It refuses any
  database holding a company that is not its own, and one already seeded** — it cannot run on live.
- **`deploy/loadtest/`** is the xneelo run, one command each: `Prepare-LoadServer.ps1` (the platform
  as live has it via Publish-Platform, then two-factor off, the seed, the stats script; refuses the live
  address and IP; `-MoreThreads`), `Prepare-LoadBox.ps1`, `Start-LoadRun.ps1` (`-Part 1/2` with two
  boxes), `Watch-LoadServer.ps1` (`rsp-loadstats.sh` — **unrun: it reads /proc, so only on Linux**).
  Its README is the step-by-step. `out/` (the seed holds keys and a password) is ignored by git.
  For Clint, no addresses typed twice: `Save-Addresses.ps1` keeps them in `out/servers.json`
  (`Servers.ps1`), and **`Run-LoadStep.ps1 -Step A`…`E`** opens the three windows (server watch + both
  boxes) itself.
  **Windows PowerShell mangles double quotes in an argument to ssh** — none in the remote scripts.

**The first finding, BUGS #11:** 5,000 machines connecting in 30 s stalled even `/health` for up to 13 s
at 7% processor — thread-pool starvation. 512 threads ready from the start (`DOTNET_ThreadPool_ForceMinWorkerThreads=200`,
hex) took connect from a 5 s median to 2 ms. WAL mode and quieter logging changed nothing. Which call
blocks is not yet proved; Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's synchronous "async" is the leading suspect.

## 116. Five seats, ten at most — 2026-10-08 (supersedes §83 on the count)

Clint: *"I think we are giving away too much for free. I would like to change the system to a 5 user
license with Owner only still being a free seat ... the system must only allow for a maximum of 10 seats
and one owner. If more than one owner is selected, this must be considered a seat taken even if no extra
roles are assigned."* His four answers are in `PRICING.md`, "Changed 2026-10-08": R500 / $49 stays the
price of the five; **one owner-only login free, everybody else a seat**; the limit is for **every**
company, Anywhere IT and the command line included, no override; the free version untouched.

### What it is now

- **`Pricing.IncludedSeats` is 5** (and `Platform:DefaultSeats` in `appsettings.json` — signup reads
  THAT, not the constant; `signupcheck` caught it). **`Pricing.MaxSeats` is 10**; `BillFor` never counts a
  package above it, and Owner → Tenants clamps to it.
- **`Pricing.SeatsFor(roles)` is THE rule**: a paid box (`TenantRoles.Paid`) is one seat however many,
  and of the owner-only logins ONE is free and every other a seat. `PeopleInSeats`, `SeatsIf` (the seats
  after a change) and `InSeats` (the names, for Billing — the earliest owner-only login is the free one)
  all go through it. **`Technician.UsesSeat` is only what a person's own boxes say** — never count seats
  with it; a second owner-only login is only visible in the whole list.
- **`RiseIf` takes the role AFTER, not a bool**, and compares seats before and after — so a change that
  adds no seat is never priced, whoever it is.
- **`Pricing.LimitProblem` is the limit**, asked by `NewPersonProblem` (so the People page never asks a
  price for an eleventh), `SetRoleAsync` and `SetOwnerAsync`, for every asker including null (the
  command line). It refuses only a change that ADDS a seat, so a company above ten from before keeps
  everybody and can still change boxes that cost nothing. `PriceRiseAsync` answers null at the limit:
  there is no price to agree, only a refusal.
- **The People page** says *"· 10 at most"* in its pill and, at ten, replaces the Add form with
  `#seatsLimit` (the add-form script now survives the form's absence). Billing says *"up to 10 seats"*.
- **The migration `FiveSeatPackage`** sets EVERY company's package to 5 (data only; Down puts 5 back to
  7). Nobody is removed. Signups were off and Anywhere IT is not billed, so nobody paying was on seven.
- **The words**: South Africa's terms (`Terms/core.txt`, **version 2026-10-08**) say five seats, one
  owner-only login free, ten at most; `landing-legal` re-run; the holding page's price card is now
  *Owner — free / 5 any mix / 10 at most*; signup, the portal's first-steps card and the held-back
  `/` and `/pricing` pages match.

### Still one owner

**`TenantService` still refuses a second owner** ("There is only ever one"). The seat rule already
counts a second owner-only login, so allowing several owners would be lifting that refusal and checking
the 16 `IsOwner` call sites (`CanChangeOwner`, removing the owner, handing over) — not asked for yet.

### How it was proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/seatcheck` (rewritten) | **72 of 72.** Both migrations (seven, then five — the company given ten included); the rule (two owner-only logins = 1, an owner-tech beside an owner-only = 1, three boxes = 1); the sums (R2,000 at ten, a package of 50 counted as 10); the service at five (sixth refused to a supervisor, owner refused until the exact figure, R1,100 for an office administrator); **the limit**: no price question for an eleventh, the owner naming R2,300 refused, the command line refused, the owner unticking frees a seat somebody else takes, ticking it back at ten refused, a no-seat box allowed at ten, a company not billed refused at eleven, handing over at ten; the pages (the question, Accept, Billing's names without the owner, a supervisor and a forged figure refused, the CLI's eleventh refused with the reason, the Add form gone at ten, a forced post refused). **With the limit out and a second owner free again it drops to 58.** |
| `rolecheck` 74, `signupcheck` 51, `legalcheck` 16, `upgradecheck` 21, `freecheck` 45 | Unchanged counts; rolecheck and signupcheck now expect five. |

**Not on hardware.** **`Publish-Platform.ps1` (migration `FiveSeatPackage`)** only — no console
re-download, no client reinstall. `TEST-3.6.md` section CF, 546–550.
