## 152. The tray app never restarted into an update — it read its own old version — 2026-10-19

Clint: *"The auto updates do not seem to be working then. Two of our test machines are on different versions and they are on
all the time"* — the console showing DESKTOP-2N6FVGT at `2026.10.16.932` and DESKTOP-OPHQIDH at `2026.10.18.629`, with the
server handing out `2026.10.19.1126`.

**Measured first, from three places.** (1) `/owner/updates` history: **both AGENTS had taken every release by themselves** —
2N6FVGT 10.16.1107, 10.18.629, 10.19.1108 and 10.19.1126, each *Offered → Downloading → Downloaded, waiting until nobody is
connected → Installing → Updated 11 files* in about 20 s, no rollback. The automatic half of §148 works on hardware.
(2) **`tools/updatestate.ps1` (new)**, run on 2N6FVGT through Scripts: every file in the install folder 10.19.1126 and signed by
us, `apply.log` clean for all four, a `healthy-<version>` for each — and **the tray app, pid 4868, running since 16 Oct 11:51**.
The console's Version column is the OLDER of agent and tray app (`AppVersion.Oldest`), so the stuck half was the tray app.
(3) **Reproduced on this PC** with a real tray app built as 10.16.932, started `--tray`, the agent's swap done by hand (renamed
aside, 10.19.1126 copied in): no restart in 2½ minutes, nobody connected, no window showing. A temporary log in `UpdateTick`
said it in one line: **`onDisk=2026.10.16.932`** — the file on disk was 10.19.1126.

**The cause:** `UpdateTrust.FileVersion` is `FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo`, and **Windows answers it from a module already
loaded at that path. A running program renamed aside still goes by its ORIGINAL path** (§148 measured that, and the swap
depends on it) — so the tray app asking about `RemoteSupport.Client.exe` was told its own version, every minute, for ever. The
check `onDisk > Current` could never be true; nothing else was wrong. The agent and console never hit it: they only ever read a
downloaded or unpacked copy, which is not loaded.

**The fix:** `UpdateTrust.FileVersionOnDisk` reads VS_FIXEDFILEINFO from the file's own bytes (PE headers → section table →
RT_VERSION → the fixed info; 64 KB at most; "" for anything that is not a program, an exception for a cut-off one, which the tick
already catches). `MainForm.UpdateTick` uses it. **Never use `FileVersion` on a path the asking program was started from.**
The same reproduction with the fix: read 10.19.1126 and restarted `--tray --after <pid>` within the minute.

**`tools/trayversion` (new) 14 of 14; 13 with `--old`** (the old read — fails exactly on its own path). It does to itself what the
agent does to the tray app — renames its running .exe aside, copies a stamped release program in — then checks the byte read
agrees with Windows on every dist program and on 64- and 32-bit Windows files, and gives nothing for a text file or a cut-off
program. It carries a Windows 10 `supportedOS` manifest: **without one, Windows tells a program its system files are 6.2** (the
compatibility version lie), and the byte read — which is honest — looks wrong.

**What it means in the field: every installed tray app is still the build it started with, and the running ones CANNOT notice an
update** — the old code is the fault. After the deploy carrying this, the agent swaps the fixed tray app in as usual, but the old
one keeps running until the person **signs out and in, or the machine restarts**; from then on it restarts into every update by
itself. Nothing stops working meanwhile; the tray app is only behind. (An agent that could end a stuck old tray app and start the
new one as the person, when nobody is using it, would close that gap without a restart — not built.)

**Also found:** the console's Scripts tool — the big dark box is the OUTPUT (read-only, no right-click menu), the box to type in
is the small one below it, and nothing says so. Clint pasted into the big one, then ran *Update this machine* (harmless: same
version reinstalled over itself, 20 s). Not changed yet. And `updatestate.ps1` has no `param()` block on purpose: the Scripts tool
puts a line of its own ahead of every script, and `param()` must come first.

**Deploy:** a signed `Publish-Platform.ps1` (no migration). Machines take the fixed tray app by themselves; restart each one
once (the test machines now) to start it. `TEST-3.6.md` section DI, 761–764.

## 153. Five seats and no more; ending a pilot; five companies at a time — 2026-10-22

Clint, in one message: *"We need an option to revoke pilot licenses. The two pilot companies have had their licenses for a week
now and have done absolutely nothing ... I have decided to make this product a 5 license only product, with no option to have
extra seats. I want to make this available to small I.T companies only ... My thought process is allow 5 companies in at a time
and rather test it that way."* His answers: both endings for a pilot, suspended first and closed 30 days later; R500 for five,
one owner-only login still free on top; **Anywhere IT is always excluded — "it can have as many seats as it wants"**; keep the
free version; count only paying companies; the website says honestly when it is full; the wording is his vision, *"to make proper
I.T support more affordable for smaller I.T companies"*. **The real site and live PayFast go on on 1 November 2026, not before.**

### Five seats and no more (supersedes §83's price and §116's ten)

- **`Pricing.MaxSeats` = `IncludedSeats` = 5**; `Region` has no extra-seat price any more. `Pricing.Limited(t)` = not billed is
  never limited (that is Anywhere IT). `Pricing.SeatsAllowed(t)` = the package (`Tenant.Seats`, clamped 1..5) — the platform owner
  can still set FEWER on All companies. `LimitProblem(t, …)` takes the tenant now.
- **`RiseIf`, `PriceRiseAsync`, the People page's price question (Accept / Don't do it) and the `agreed` parameters are GONE.** A
  sixth seat is simply refused, to everybody, the command line included. `PriceRise` stays for the free version's upgrade only, and
  `SeatAgreement` rows already agreed stay on Billing. `Bill` has no `Extra`.
- The People page: *"n of 5 seats in use"* (*"not limited"* for Anywhere IT), the Add form replaced by the reason at five. Billing:
  *"A company has 5 seats and no more"*. `Pricing.WhyFive` is the one sentence every page uses for why.
- **Terms version 2026-10-22**: core section 2 says five and no more, with the reason; `{{EXTRA}}` is gone; `landing-legal` re-run.

### Ending a pilot (`PilotService`, Owner → Pilots)

- **The pilots accepted terms that end the agreement as section 11 says — 30 days' notice.** So ending one is a NOTICE: a day
  (30 days ahead offered; an earlier one asks "only if the company has agreed"), and what follows — **close** (suspended through
  `AdminCompanies`, its people signed out and machines turned away, then **Closed 30 days later** with the 60-days-to-deletion
  email) or **pay** (no longer a pilot, a 14-day `Trial` on the standard price, the trial notices and *Add your card* as for any
  trial). Nothing changes until the day; **Withdraw notice** puts it back. A day of today ends it at once.
- `Tenant.PilotEndsUtc` (the start of that day in the company's zone), `PilotAfter` (`close`/`pay`), `PilotEndedUtc`.
  **`PilotSweep`** (every 10 minutes, `Platform:PilotSweepSeconds`) ends due pilots and closes the closing ones — only once each
  (the end updates only a row still `Pilot`). The owners get the notice, the ending and the closing by email (`AdminCompanies.NoticeAsync`).
- Owner → Pilots now lists the pilot companies first with **people · machines · tickets · sessions · last sign-in**, so "did nothing"
  is a reading, not a feeling. Their Billing page says when the pilot ends and what follows.
- **The pilot terms for NEW pilots** (`Terms/pilot.txt`) now say this outright: free *while you are a pilot company*, ended by 30
  days' notice by email to the standard price or the end. The two existing pilots accepted the 2026-10-15 wording — still 30 days.

### Five companies at a time (`OpenPlaces`, Owner → Approvals)

- **What takes a place** (`OpenPlaces.Taking`, THE rule): billed, not a pilot, not the free version, and Active, Trial or Suspended
  — or Pending for under 3 days (an abandoned PayFast checkout lets its place go; if PayFast's notice comes later it is let in anyway).
  Plus every offer from the waiting list not used or expired. `PlatformSettings.OpenPlaces` (5; the migration writes **5**, not 0,
  into the existing row — 0 means no limit) is set on Owner → Approvals for each server (`ControlServers.Dispatch` `places`).
- **Full**: the plan card says *All places taken*; choosing the full version shows the waiting list (`Step == "full"`), not the
  terms; `SignupAsync` refuses a full-version signup too (`OpenPlaces.IsFullRefusal`), so a forged post makes nothing. The free
  version never waits. Joining is a `WaitingListEntry` with `Full`.
- **Offer a place** (Approvals, `offer-place`): a link, once, 7 days, SHA-256 only (`PlaceTokenHash`), emailed — shown on the page
  ONLY when the email did not go, and **never written to the admin log** (a remote server's answer is logged without it). It is
  `/signup?region=ZA&plan=full&place=…`, carried through every step in a hidden `Place`, and **spent in the same save as the company
  by a conditional update** (the pilot link's shape). Two strangers in the same second for the last open place can both get in —
  one company over, not worth a lock.
- `ServerReport.Places` and `WaitingRow.Full/PlaceUntilUtc/PlaceUsed` — optional, so an older server's report still reads.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/seatcheck` (rewritten) | **54 of 54** (50 on PostgreSQL, which skips the old-migration part); 8 fail with `Pricing.Limited` answering true for Anywhere IT. The rule and migrations as before; the sums (R500/$49/£49/€49 whatever the count, a package above five is five, set to three is three); a sixth refused to a supervisor, the owner and the command line, before anything is done; a second owner-only login and the owner ticking Technician refused at five; removing frees a seat; Anywhere IT takes twelve; the pages (5 of 5, no Add form, a forced post and an old Accept refused, Billing, the form back after a removal, not billed → not limited). |
| `tools/pilotcheck` (extended) | **57 of 57 on both databases** (was 42): the new pilot terms; five free, a sixth refused; then over HTTP as an admin: the companies with their use, notice with the day stored at 00:00 company time, the company's Billing saying so, withdrawn, a bad ending refused, a day of today ending it at once (Suspended, people signed out), the sweep closing it after 30 days; a pay notice whose day comes → a 14-day trial at R500. |
| `tools/placescheck` (new) | **26 of 26 on SQLite and PostgreSQL** (21 with `SignupAsync`'s own refusal out — the page turns a full signup away first, so the service is also asked directly): what counts (8 kinds of company), two signups filling the last places, full (plan card, waiting list not terms, a forged Create making nothing, free still open, the entry kept), Approvals 5 of 5, an offer (shown once, fingerprint only, never in the log, holding a place), three at once on the link → ONE company, the link again refused, an expired one said, 0 = no limit, the number logged. |
| re-run | **All 85 database harnesses pass on SQLite**; on PostgreSQL the eleven touched. `signuppaycheck` 72 (stage C now proves an R800 subscription from before is brought to R500, and that people send PayFast nothing), `pgcheck` 20, `legalcheck` 16, and `rolecheck`, `signupcheck`, `upgradecheck`, `clockcheck`, `admincheck`, `controlcheck`, `freecheck`, `legalcheck`, `sitecheck` (the pricing page: five and no more; `up to ten` and `R300` now stale claims). |

**Not on hardware.** **Signed `Publish-Platform.ps1` (migration `PilotEndingAndOpenPlaces`, both databases)** — no ship, no console
re-download, no client reinstall. Then Owner → Pilots → End the pilot. `TEST-3.6.md` section DL, 773–782.

## 154. A company takes its data with it — 2026-10-22 (roadmap 4.9)

Clint, 2026-10-22: *"the ability for companies to export their clients, tickets and knowledgebase."* Section 11 of the terms
already promised it — *"Ask us before then for an export of your data"*, within the 60 days after an agreement ends — and until now
that meant somebody on the server by hand. **Every rule is `Services/CompanyExport.cs` (`CompanyExportService`).**

### Clint's four answers (all the recommendation)

1. **Who: the owner and supervisors** — `Permissions.CanExportCompany` (= supervises, an owner-only login included). Asked by the
   service AND by the page's policy (`/Portal/Export` is in Program.cs's "Tenant" list). Not a technician, not the office
   administrator alone: it is everything the company holds, at once.
2. **A company that cannot sign in is exported BY US.** Suspended and Closed companies cannot sign in at all (`IsServiceEnabled`), and
   letting them back in to fetch a zip would reopen what was shut. So Owner → All companies has **Export their data** (a Manager or
   above, a `with recordings` tick) — action `export` in `ControlServers.Dispatch`, so it reaches whichever server holds the company —
   and when it is made, **the owners (`AdminCompanies.OwnersAsync`) are emailed a link** `/export/{token}` that needs no sign-in. The
   terms' "ask us" stays true word for word; no terms change.
3. **A zip of Excel workbooks and the files themselves.** Excel, not CSV: a CSV opened in Excel loses a phone's leading 0 (§52). Every
   cell is TEXT. `clients.xlsx`'s first sheet is EXACTLY `ClientImport.TemplateHeaders`, so it goes straight back into Import clients
   — here or into another program.
4. **Session recordings: a tick, off by default.** Always listed in `ticket-files.xlsx`; copied in only when ticked.

### What is in the zip

| | |
|---|---|
| `README.txt` | What each file is, who asked, what is in it, any file missing on the server. |
| `clients.xlsx` | Sheet 1 *Clients*: Import's six columns, one row per contact person, live clients and contacts only (`ImportRows`, below). Sheet 2 *Every client and contact*: everything, archived too, contact roles and notes, health check. |
| `tickets.xlsx` | One row per ticket (44 columns: category, stage in words, client, people, machine, money, time, parent, booking…); sheet 2 the further machines on a job (`TicketMachine`). |
| `ticket-story.xlsx` | Every `TicketNote` in order: when, who, stage, step (`FormTitle`), moved to, kind (Comment / Step / Automatic / From the customer / Work done / Went back), gone back over, words, its files' paths. |
| `quote-lines.xlsx` | Item, part number, serial, quantity, its photos' paths. |
| `ticket-files.xlsx` | Every photo, comment file and recording, and where it is in the zip — or *missing on the server*, or *not included*. |
| `tickets/<n>/` | `story.txt` (the ticket as a person reads it, every word — the cell limit never cuts it), `photos/` (*arrived 1.jpg*, *went out 1.jpg*, *part 1.jpg*, *screen 1.png*), `files/` (their own names), `recordings/`. |
| `knowledge-base.xlsx`, `knowledge-base/` | Articles (section, folder path, file, from ticket, version, who) and folders. `General/` and `Clients/<client>/` with the folders as in the portal; each article as `.html` (drawn by `KbText.Render`, the portal's own renderer — everything typed encoded — pictures pointed at `pictures/`) and `.txt` as written. |

**Left out on purpose:** device passwords (the ticket's and a second machine's — only *Password protected: Yes*), deleted articles and
older versions, staged photos never attached, files picked for a comment never posted, other companies (every query is by `TenantId`).

### How it runs

- **A background job, never one request.** A `CompanyExport` row (migration `CompanyExports`, both databases): Waiting → Making →
  Ready / Failed → Expired. `CompanyExportSweep` makes them one at a time, woken at once by a start (a semaphore), else every
  `Platform:ExportSweepSeconds` (60). **One at a time per company**: asking while one is in flight answers with that one.
- Written to `data/exports/{company}/<generated>.zip.part`, renamed when complete — a half-made zip is never offered. A restart part
  way: `RecoverAsync` (at start) sets it Waiting again and deletes the `.part`. Workbooks are written row by row
  (`Spreadsheet.Workbook`, new: streaming, every cell text, a cell over Excel's 32,767 characters cut with a note saying where the
  whole is, a sheet past Excel's last row carried on in "(2)"), so four thousand tickets' story is never held in memory.
  `Spreadsheet.ReadXlsx(bytes, index)` reads any sheet back; Import still reads only the first.
- **Kept `KeepDays` (7) days**; a newer one replaces the older (marked Expired, file deleted). The supervisor who asked is emailed
  when it is ready; for one of ours, the owners get the link (`LinkHash` = SHA-256 of a 256-bit token; the token is never stored or
  logged). **Opening the link downloads nothing** — a page with a button (a POST): mail filters open every link. The admin log has
  *Export started* and *Export ready … link emailed to …* (or *NOT emailed: why*).
- **It refuses rather than fills the disk**: the files' sizes plus 512 MB must be free, or it fails saying so.
- **`deploy/rsp-backup.sh` leaves `exports` out** — a zip of what is already in the backup.
- The free version has no Export (not in `FreePortal`'s allow-list); we can still make one for a free company.

### `ImportRows` — the one subtle part

Import fills a client's own Contact person / Phone / Email / Address / Notes from the FIRST row that has each, and adds a contact
person for every row that names one. So a client with no contact people is one row of its own details; otherwise the client's own
person comes first, and **when the client's own phone or email is not that person's (a switchboard), a row with NO contact person
carries them ahead of everybody** — so nobody is made up. Notes go on the first row only; the address on every row. **What comes back
exactly: names, addresses, notes and every contact person's name, phone and email; the client's own fields wherever they are set.**
A BLANK client phone or email cannot travel — Import fills it from the first person (as it does with any file), so re-importing into
the same company adds no client and no person, but may fill such a blank. Do not "fix" that in the export.

### How it is proved

`tools/exportcheck` (new) — **92 of 92 on SQLite and on PostgreSQL**; **88 with three guards out** (the page policy, the company check
on download, the link's GET counting nothing). A real platform and a fake mail server; two companies seeded with every kind of record
and a file on disk for each: who (technician and office administrator refused, page and start — the SERVICE still refused the start
with the page policy out; owner-only and supervisor in; another company's owner cannot download by number), one at a time, made and
emailed, every file the very bytes on the server, a missing file said, no device password and nothing of the other company anywhere
(the workbooks' insides searched too), **clients.xlsx through the real Import into an EMPTY database made by `HarnessDb.MigrateAsync`**
(same clients, addresses, notes, people), back into its own company (nothing added), tickets / story / quote lines / knowledge base
read back equal (a 40,000-character entry cut in the cell and whole in story.txt; the article's picture resolved inside the zip;
`<script>` encoded), recordings only when ticked, a newer replacing the older, a suspended company exported by an admin with the link
mailed, opened (no download), used (download, no sign-in), refused when wrong or expired, the sweep deleting it, and a restart part way
made again. Re-run: `pgcheck`, `importcheck`, `controlcheck`, `admincheck`, `backupcheck`, `freeportal`, `rolecheck`.

**Not on hardware.** **Signed `Publish-Platform.ps1` (migration `CompanyExports`)** — no ship, no console re-download.
`TEST-3.6.md` section DM, 783–791.

## 155. A technician asks for outside help — 2026-10-22 (roadmap 3.9.3)

Clint: *"What would be nice is for a technician to also be able to ask for outside help. In the console for example under tools
when connected to a machine, there is a get outside help option. This generates a code, plus links to the browser and guest account
download, that they can then copy or share via their whatsapp or email. Sometimes it happens that I tech needs the outside
assistance rather than the client."* He took every recommendation, and on the one question left: *"the customer should be told."*
Everything §87–§92 built — the codes, the guest console, the browser page, the allow-lists, the red pop-up — is reused; what is new
is **who makes the code, who lets them in, and that the session is the company's, not the visitor's.**

### The rules (each Clint's answer or the recommendation he took)

- **Any technician IN the session** may make one (`TenantHub.InviteProblem`: in `ViewerIds`, the session under way, not a browser
  session, nobody from outside in it or waiting). **The machine's outside-help switch (§87) is the CUSTOMER's and is not asked.** The
  company has its own switch, **`Tenant.TechnicianInvitesAllowed`, ON by default** (the migration sets every company on), on Portal →
  Outside help, a supervisor's or the owner's (`CanAllowOutsiders`); off stops every such code and removes anybody let in that way
  (`RefreshInvitesAsync`). Not on the free version (refused at the hub; the menu item has no socket to send on).
- **The code is for that SESSION** (`OutsiderCode.SessionId`, `InvitedById`; `CreateForSessionAsync`). One per session; the
  customer's own codes are the rows with no session — **neither kind stops the other**, and `LiveAsync` (the tray app's line) reads
  only the customer's. It stops when the session ends (`InviteSessionEnded`) or when its maker leaves the session.
- **Whoever types it waits for the technician who made it** (`JoinInvitedAsync` → `OutsiderJoinAskMsg` to that technician's
  consoles only). **Only the maker may answer** (`AnswerJoin`). Unanswered for two minutes (`Testing:OutsiderJoinAskSeconds`), they
  are turned away. The visitor's console, guest console and browser page say *Waiting for {technician} to let you in*
  (`SessionInfo.AwaitingTechnician`, in a COPY of the session only the visitor gets — `TellVisitorWaiting`).
- **The person at the machine is TOLD, never asked**: `OutsiderJoinedMsg` to the tray app — the log and a balloon, joined and left. No
  consent prompt, no new session: the visitor joins the session already running, as the session's single `Visitor`, so **§89's
  allow-lists apply unchanged**; files only if the technician ticked it (`SessionInfo.VisitorFiles`).
- **The session is the company's.** The visitor's Leave, their lost connection (after the grace), the red pop-up's **Remove** (any
  technician of the company) and the session window's *Remove them* take ONLY them out (`RemoveInvited`); the session goes on. **When
  nobody of the company is left in it — a dropped connection included — they go at once** (`InviteViewerLeft`); and a company
  technician's deliberate Leave with only the outsider left **ends the session** (the `last` test in the viewer's `EndSessionMsg`).
  Nobody from outside is ever on a customer's machine alone.
- Recorded: the ticket has made / typed / let in (with or without files, *the person at the machine was told*) / left; the red pop-up
  says *Brought in by {technician}*; the visiting company's Sessions line ends when they leave, not when the session does.

### Where it is

- **`Hub/TenantHub.Invite.cs`** — every rule above. `CheckCode` / `ArriveWithCodeAsync` are now what `/ws/guest` and *Connect with a
  code* call; they pick the customer's visit (§89, `StartVisitAsync`) or this by the code's `SessionId`.
- **`Session.InvitedBy` is the switch every old visitor path asks**: the visitor's End, `VisitorMayReturn`, `EndVisitsNoLongerAllowed`
  (the customer's switch never ends an invited visit). **`NoLongerTheVisitor`**: a removed visitor's socket stays in `VisitorSockets`
  (so the filters still hold) but is taken out of `Viewers` at once, and anything it still sends goes nowhere — **including a late
  Leave, which would otherwise have ended the company's session** (the §89 path).
- Console: **`SessionForm.OutsideHelp.cs`**, `OutsideHelpForm` (who for → the code, the message, Copy / WhatsApp / Email, Stop or Make
  a new code, Remove them), `OutsiderAllowDialog` (brought to the front with `ComeForward`). All on the **dashboard's** signed-in
  socket (`TechLink.Send`), never the session socket — that is sealed end to end and the hub could not read the ask; so **nothing was
  added to `SessionSeal`'s clear list or `e2e.js`**.
- **`OutsideHelpMessage`** (Shared) is the message and the links, once. **The browser link puts the code after `#`** — a browser never
  sends that part, so the code is in no server log and opening the link spends nothing; `guestview.js` fills the box and takes it out
  of the address bar. WhatsApp is `wa.me/?text=`, email a `mailto:`.
- `/guest` and `/guest/web` now say *whoever gave you the code lets you in* (it was always the person at the computer).

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/helpcheck` (new) | **77 of 77, on SQLite and on PostgreSQL.** Two companies and a guest against the real hub. ## 156. The installer asks who the computer is for — 2026-10-23

Clint: *"Would it be possible that during the client install, the client has to put in their name, surname and email address?
This will then be the default name that shows up in the console and when they then request support, that is also the default name
that get filled into their user field? And then if one links said user to a client, it automatically registers it as a contact
under that client in the portal."* §150 already made the name typed at a support request the machine's name until it is linked;
this starts that at the install, with an email, and makes linking file the person. **His eight answers, all the recommendations:**

1. **Required in the installer window** (name, surname, email; the email only has to look like one, nothing is sent to it).
   **A scripted install** (`Install-Client.ps1` run by hand, no window) **asks nothing** and behaves as before.
2. **The latest name still wins** (§150): the install's is the starting point; a support request with another name replaces it.
3. **Request Support starts with** the name this Windows user last sent, else **the install's**, else Windows' username.
4. **Request Support asks the email too** — optional, filled in, refused only when it is half an address.
5. **Linking to a client adds them as a contact there with their email**, and links the machine to them: **by email first** (the
   same address at that client is that person — Jane who married), **then by name** (`CreateAsync`'s rule); a blank email on file
   is filled, never one overwritten. **A tick, ticked by default**, to say no — a shared reception PC belongs to the company.
6. **An email never links anything by itself** — anybody can type anybody's address; a person still chooses.
7. **New installs only** — older machines get the email as their people ask for help.
8. **Not the free version** (the owner's own machines; `FreeInstallForm` is untouched).

Assumed and said: name and surname are two boxes but ONE name, *"Jane Smith"*, as contacts have always been; the window says
why in one line (*"So {company} knows who you are when you ask for help"*).

### How it travels

- **`Shared/GivenPerson.cs` is the one rule**: `Problem` (the installer's three), `Join`, `LooksLikeEmail`/`CleanEmail` (the
  platform's `TicketIntake` shape), `Make`, and the file. **`LauncherForm`** has Name, Surname, Email address in the Install card,
  checked BEFORE anything is staged or Windows asks; an Update starts with what is on file (`Program` reads the installed
  `person.json`). The window writes **`person.json` into the staged folder** — Install-Client.ps1 copies `*`, so it lands in
  Program Files beside the apps with no change to the script, and an auto-update (§148) never touches it (not a release file).
- **Every hello says it** (`HelloMsg.InstalledForId/Name/Email`; `DeviceLink.InstalledFor`, set by the agent AND the tray app from
  `GivenPerson.Installed()`). **The server keeps it ONCE per id** (`Device.InstalledForId`, `ContactService.KeepInstalledFor`) —
  **this is the trap**: a hello repeats it at every reconnect, and keeping it each time would put the installer's name back over
  a later request's for ever (`installedfor` fails two checks without the guard). It is applied in `PersistDeviceAsync`, where the
  stored record is read and a first install's two hellos are already taken in turn (§127's `RecordGate`). **The id stays the same
  when an Update leaves the boxes as they were** (`GivenPerson.Make`), so updating does not undo a later request either; a name
  retyped in another case is a change.
- **The email belongs to the name beside it** (`ContactService.Given`, used by requests and the install alike): another name with
  no email clears the old one (it was somebody else's); the same name with none keeps it — an older tray app sends none.
  `Device.RequestedByEmail`, `DeviceInfo.RequestedByEmail`, `RequestCallMsg.ContactEmail`. The tray app's `LastContact` keeps the
  email beside the name (`EmailFor`: the one sent with THAT name, else the install's for the install's name — never another
  person's).
- **Linking**: `ContactService.LinkDeviceToNewContactAsync` takes the email **from the machine's record, only while the name being
  added IS the given name** — never from the caller, so the console and portal send a name, not an address. Console:
  `LinkDeviceDialog` has the tick (*"Add {name} ({email}) as a contact when I choose a customer"*) whenever the machine has a given
  name and **no person** — so a machine linked to a client alone gets it too; choosing a COMPANY row with it on sends
  `NewContactName`; hidden during the *Which customer is {name} at?* step. Portal: the same tick on the Set form
  (`addGiven`, `DevicesModel.OffersGiven`), `OnPostAssignAsync` choosing `LinkDeviceToNewContactAsync` for a client with it on.
  Tooltips in both say the email.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/installedfor` (new) | **48 of 48, on SQLite and on PostgreSQL.** The installer's rule and the file; the server's email rule and once-per-id; then pretend agents and tray apps against a real platform: a first install's two hellos at once (the RecordGate gap open), every console told name and email, the row and its id; Mary asks from Jane's PC and wins, Jane's email not left beside her; **both reconnect still saying Jane — NOT put back**; an email from a request kept, a blank from an older tray app keeps it, half an address not; a reinstall typed again wins; a scripted install unchanged; a restart; linking — a new contact with the email, **the same email at that client is that person**, the same name with a blank email filled, a different name never borrows it, the tick off adds nobody; the portal's tick (there, and on a client-only machine, not on a person's), its token, Set with it on and off. **With the once-per-id guard out: 46; with email-first out: 47.** |
| `tools/oneexecheck` | **39** — the three boxes in the Install card, empty, labelled, inside it; an Update filled in; Install refused with them empty or a bad email (nothing run), then it installs with the person kept. **It found the boxes sitting over their labels' foot** (placed from the font's line, not the label's height — §30 again). |
| `tools/callprobe` | **77** — the email box filled in under the name, half an address refused in the window, blank fine; `LastContact` with the install's name and email, never another person's email. **It found the complaint cut off at "…or leave it"** — shortened. |
| `tools/dashtabs` | **155** — the Link window's tick: words, email, fits, hidden at the which-customer step, a company with it on adds, off does not, a person chosen adds nobody, absent with no given name, present on a client-only machine. |
| re-run | `requestedname` 43 (both databases), `contactcheck` 34, `devicelink` 20, `requestwire` 20, `firsthello` 9, `pgcheck` 20, `lookprobe` 348. |

**Not on hardware.** **One signed `Publish-Platform.ps1` (migration `InstalledForPerson`, both databases)** carries all of it: the
console updates itself, installed machines update themselves (§148 — the tray app's email box once it restarts), and every new
download has the new installer window. No reinstall is needed; a machine gets an install name only from an install through the new
window. `TEST-3.6.md` section DO, 805–812.

## 157. A free account from the owner pages, with the links sent and a technician copied — 2026-10-23

Clint, after being given three server commands to set a client up on the free version: *"Can we rather have a button that i can
create the client in the portal from and send the links directly from there?"* — then, mid-build: *"I need an option to cc the
tech in when sending the links so that he can help her set it up."*

### What it is

- **Owner → Free version** (`/owner/free`, `Pages/Owner/Free.cshtml`), beside Pilots. Any admin sees the list; **a Manager or
  above** makes one and sends links (refused in the service, not only by a missing button). **Every rule is
  `Services/FreeCompanies.cs`.**
- **Their name and email** (the login, and where the links go); company and phone optional — their own name stands in for a
  company, as at the free signup (§102). The company is made **Active on the free plan at once — approved, no trial**, in this
  server's region and its time zone (a region with several asks; the EU asks the country). Its one person is **Owner +
  Technician** (`TenantService.FreeRole`) with **no password** (`AwaitingSetup`) — made in ONE transaction with the company. An
  email already registered anywhere is refused and names where. Logged by name on Owner → Log.
- **One email** (`FreeCompanies.Invitation`, chosen inside `AccountLinks.Compose` by `IsTheirFirstInvite`): from *The Remote
  Support Program* (the company is the person, so never "Jane Smith has added you"), with (1) the set-up link — `AccountLinks`,
  72 hours, once, (2) the installer for up to two computers, `/download/{slug}`, and (3) the console, `/tech/{slug}`.
- **Copy to a technician** (optional; several separated by commas, five at most, `CcProblem`): a **visible Cc**, and **Reply-To**,
  and the body says who has it. **They get the set-up link too — on purpose**: that is how they help. Our own copy-to address is
  NOT added (`copyOwner: false`, as for every set-up link). `PlatformMailService.SendAsync` takes `cc` now.
- **Send the links again** per row, with its own Cc box (the Cc is not stored — no migration): not set up yet → a NEW set-up link
  (the old one stops working; `AccountLinks` keeps one per person); set up → the two download links alone
  (`FreeCompanies.DownloadsEmail`). A full-version company is refused (its people come from its own People page).
- **No mailbox, or a refused send**: the account is still made, and the set-up link is shown ONCE on the page to pass on.
- **The free terms are still accepted, word for word.** §84's rule — nothing is made unless the very text shown was ticked — cannot
  be met by us typing their details, so **the set-up page asks instead, before the password**: an owner of a free company with no
  `TermsAcceptance` (`FreeCompanies.TermsDueAsync`) sees the free terms and a tick; no tick, or another text's fingerprint, is
  refused and **spends nothing**; ticked, the password is set and the terms kept (`AcceptTermsAsync`, the same row signup writes).
  The page does not autofocus the password while there are terms to read. A full company's invitation is unchanged.
- **No migration.** The command-line way (`create-tenant`, `set-brand … plan free`, `invite … --owner --technician`) still works,
  and its owner is now asked for the terms at set-up too.

### What building it found

- Walking the set-up page: *"Welcome, Lerato Mokoena. Lerato Mokoena has added you."* — the company IS the person. Its own words
  now, and a check.
- The password box's autofocus scrolled the page past the terms on arrival.

| `tools/freeaccount` (new) | **40 of 40, on SQLite and on PostgreSQL**, a real platform with signups off and a fake SMTP server: refused (no name, a bad copy address, an email already registered) with nothing made; made — free, Active, approved, no trial, her name for the company, ZA and Johannesburg, Owner + Technician with no password, no terms yet, logged; the email to her, the technician in **Cc and Reply-To**, from us, not to our copy-to, with the set-up link, installer and console and the line saying who has it; the set-up page with the FREE terms and its own welcome, no autofocus; no tick, and the full terms' fingerprint, refused with the link unspent and no password; ticked → password, terms kept word for word, link dead after; again → set up: download links alone with the NEW copy; not set up: a new link, the old one dead; no copy → no Cc; a full company refused, and its invitation shows no terms; no mail → still made, link shown once and not again. **With the terms check and the Cc taken out: 33 of 38.** |

## 158. The outside security review (Daniel, 19 October) — what was real and what was fixed — 2026-10-23

Clint brought a pentest report on the live site (`Downloads\Pentest report.html`, not in the repo), external and signed in as a
company owner. **It found no way into another company's data and no account takeover.** Each finding was checked against the code
before anything changed. **Read this before "fixing" any of F1, F2, F11 or F12 again — they were already right.**

### Already right, and why the report could not see it

- **F1, "no limit per address"**: there is one — `SignInGuard.PerAddress`, 30 failures in 15 minutes — behind the per-account 5.
  The tester tried ONE new address after seven failures. (`securitycheck` has proved it since §72.)
- **F2, "/forgot has no throttle"**: `AccountLinks.ForgotAsync` allows 3 an hour per address and 10 per caller, and over the limit
  sends nothing **while saying the same thing** — by design, so it cannot be used to ask which addresses exist. From outside that
  looks unlimited.
- **F11, "all twelve marketing pages are the same page"**: that is the holding page, on purpose until 1 November (`go-live.sh`
  `@holding`; `-RealSite`).
- **F12, "the runtime patch level is unknown"**: the platform is published **self-contained** (`build.ps1`), so the server's
  `dotnet --list-runtimes` says nothing — its runtime rides in the package. The build's `RemoteSupport.Platform.deps.json` names
  **`runtimepack.Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64` 10.0.13**, the version the report gives as fixed. `dotnet list package
  --vulnerable --include-transitive` on the platform: none. **That deps.json line is the way to answer this question next time**,
  and an `apt install` on the server would change nothing. `UseRequestLocalization` (F4.3) is not used.
- **F10's robots.txt / sitemap** "contradiction": before go-live robots.txt says `Disallow: /` and does not name the sitemap;
  `sitecheck` expects exactly that. Left alone.
- **F5** (`includeSubDomains; preload`): left alone on purpose — `mail.` and `smtp.` are on xneelo's shared hosting, and the preload
  list is hard to leave. **F8** (one id sequence across companies): the number people see is per company
  (`TicketService.CreateAsync`); the database id shows in the address bar, so a company can estimate the platform's volume. Every
  page asks the ticket's company first. Not changed here — briefed as `docs/NEXT-SESSION-ADDRESSES.md`, to build before go-live.
  **Built the same day: §159** — every portal address names things by the company's own number, files by a token.

### What was fixed

- **F1, the lockout lever.** The fair half: anybody who knew an address could keep its owner out for good, five wrong passwords
  every fifteen minutes. **A machine holding the person's trust token** (their code typed on it within `TwoFactorTrustDays`) **is now
  counted on its own** — `SignInGuard`'s `k:` key beside `a:` — so a stranger's failures never lock it, and its own five still do.
  The token is Data Protection's and bound to the stamps (`AuthService.Trusted`), so it cannot be made by a guesser; that is why the
  device id (`rsp_device`, `console-id`) is NOT used for this — it is only a random string the caller sends. The address is now
  checked first, before the database is asked (`SignInGuard.AddressWait`). The same for platform admins (`PlatformAdmins.PasswordAsync`).
  The pending code step carries it (`Pending.Known`), for the "signed in elsewhere" case. **A person away longer than a week has no
  token, and can still be locked out from outside** — the address limit and the lock's 15 minutes are what is left.
- **F3**: `go-live.sh` gives the holding page (served by Caddy itself, so it had none of the platform's headers) the same five; the
  policy is `frame-ancestors 'none'` only, because the page has an inline script. It reaches the server with the next full deploy —
  `Publish-Platform.ps1` runs go-live.sh.
- **F4**: a full policy sent **report-only** beside the enforced `frame-ancestors 'none'` (`Services/CspReports.cs`): 45 pages
  still carry inline script or `onclick=`, so enforcing it would break them. Browsers report what it would have blocked to
  **`POST /api/csp-report`** (no token, 30 an hour per address, 8 KB), logged as `CSP report from …`. **That log is the list of inline
  scripts to move into files; then the header's name changes and the policy is enforced.** It allows PayFast's and Microsoft's
  sign-in hosts in `form-action`; framed paths (web chat, the contact form) leave out `frame-ancestors`, as the enforced one does.
- **F6**: a ticket (and a knowledge base article) that is not there, or not yours, still says so but as a **404**.
- **F7**: a photo, a knowledge base picture and a quote signature's image must **hold together**, not only start right —
  `TicketPhotoService.WholeImageType` walks JPEG's segments to a frame header with a width, PNG's chunks IHDR → IDAT → IEND, WebP's
  RIFF and first chunk, HEIC's boxes from ftyp to a meta; `QuoteSignatures.WholeImage` adds GIF. Nothing is decoded — no library
  (ImageSharp is licensed) and image work stays off the server (§62). `SniffType` alone still labels a file when it is SERVED, and
  comment attachments (any file) are unchanged. **Harnesses that fed the store a JPEG's first four bytes and zeros now use
  `tools/Common/TestImages.cs`** — a new harness that stores a photo must too.
- **F9**: `/health` is `{"ok":true}` — every check that asks reads only the status. **F10**: `/.well-known/security.txt` (RFC 9116),
  queries@, an `Expires` a year from the day it is asked (`SitePages.SecurityTxt`).

### What building it found

- **A 404 page is still a page** — `kbcheck` and `ticketeditcheck` read it with `GetStringAsync`, which throws on a 404. Both now
  read the status (kbcheck asserts the 404 and the words; ticketeditcheck's form helper takes the token from the 404 page, which
  still carries one). A harness that opens a ticket or article that may not be there must do the same.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/securitycheck` | **87 of 87** (78 before): a stranger's five wrong passwords lock the account to anybody without its trust, but NOT a machine holding it, whose own five still lock it; the report-only policy and its report taken without a token; a missing ticket a 404 still saying so; `/health` is `{"ok":true}`; security.txt. **With the known-device line taken out: 86 of 87** — exactly that check. |
| `tools/photogate` | 41 (37 before): a PNG signature and junk refused, a JPEG's first bytes and zeros refused, a WebP and a HEIC whose boxes hold together accepted and refused cut short. |
| every database harness, SQLite | **89 of 89** after the two fixes above (`tools/Run-DbHarnesses.ps1`): kbcheck 151, ticketeditcheck 60, quotecheck 190, calloutcheck 68, workflowcheck 100, sitecheck 95. |

**Not on hardware, and the policy has not yet reported anything from a real browser.** Not run on PostgreSQL (nothing here touches
the database). **One signed `Publish-Platform.ps1`, no migration, nothing to ship to machines** — it also rewrites the Caddyfile,
which is what puts F3 live. `TEST-3.6.md` section DQ, 820–826.

### Still to ask of the tester

Their own §8: the database had one company, so **cross-company access was never tried**, nor a technician reaching owner pages.
Give them a second company (a pilot link) and a technician login, and have those re-run.

## 159. Portal addresses name things by the company's own number, not the database id — 2026-10-23 (the review's F8)

The outside review (§158) found that every ticket, client, knowledge base article and photo took its id from ONE sequence shared by
every company, and that the portal showed it: `/portal/tickets/129` for a company's ticket #2. Nobody could reach another
company's data that way — every page asks the company first — but the gap between two of a company's own tickets told it how many
the whole platform had made in between. Clint: fix it before go-live, *"would fixing it after going live not be more riskier?"* —
today only Anywhere IT and the two pilots hold old links. The brief was `docs/NEXT-SESSION-ADDRESSES.md`; its "Decided" list was
followed, and this section wins over it.

### What a page shows now

| | new | old (still answered) |
|---|---|---|
| a ticket | `/portal/t/{number}` (`?tab=`, `?open=`, `?sent=` as before) | `/portal/tickets/{id}` |
| a client | `/portal/c/{number}` | `/portal/clients/{id}` |
| an article, its editor | `/portal/a/{number}`, `/portal/a/{number}/edit` | `/portal/kb/{id}`, `/portal/kb/edit/{id}` |
| a recurring task | `/portal/r/{number}`, `/portal/r/new` | `/portal/recurring/{id}`, `/portal/recurring/new` |
| one client's articles / tickets | `/portal/kb?c={number}`, `/portal/tickets?c={number}` (`c=0` is General) | `?client={id}` |
| writing up a ticket, a new article for a client | `/portal/kb/edit?t={number}`, `?c={number}` | `?ticket={id}`, `?client={id}` |
| a photo, a comment's file, an article's picture, a recording | `/portal/p/{token}`, `/portal/f/{token}`, `/portal/i/{token}`, `/portal/v/{token}` | `/portal/photo/{id}`, `/portal/attachment/{id}`, `/portal/kb/image/{id}`, `/portal/recordings/{id}` |

- **Every address and every lookup is `Services/PortalAddresses.cs`** — one per kind, `(company, number) → id` and back, and
  `(company, token) → id`, **always with the company in the same query**. A number or token of another company is 0, which every
  caller answers exactly as it answers one that does not exist.
- **Tickets already had their number** (`Ticket.Number`). **Clients, articles and recurring tasks now have one**: `Number`, a unique
  index on (TenantId, Number), **given on save by `PlatformDb` itself** (`Data/PlatformDb.Numbers.cs`, `ICompanyNumbered`): the
  company's highest + 1, under one lock for the process, as `TicketService`'s `NumberLock`. In the context rather than the services
  because a client is made in four places (Add a client, the import, a ticket's sender, the console) and **every harness seeds rows
  straight into the tables** — a 0 left behind would break the unique index the second time.
- **Recurring tasks were the brief's open question** (`which` was the database id), so they got the same treatment; the list's
  "it is set up" notice now says `?n={number}`.
- **Stored files got a random token, not "its place on the ticket"**: a photo staged on New ticket has no ticket yet, and a place
  moves when one is removed. `Token` on `TicketPhoto`, `TicketAttachment`, `KbImage`, `SessionRecording` — 24 hex characters
  (`FileToken.New()`), a property initialiser, so every new row has one. **Not a secret**: every route still asks the signed-in
  company and looks the token up within it. Comment files and recordings were not in the brief; they had the same leak, so they
  are done too.
- **The migration, `PerCompanyAddresses`, on both databases**, adds the columns, numbers every existing client, article and
  recurring task 1, 2, 3 per company in id order, gives every stored file a token (SQLite `randomblob`, PostgreSQL `md5(random…)`),
  and only then makes the unique indexes.
- **The ticket page's `?sent=` names the comment by its place in the story** (1 is the first entry), not the note's id.
- **An article's pictures**: the stored markup is still `[image:{id}]`; `KbText.Render` takes the address of each from
  `KnowledgeBaseService.ImageAddressesAsync` (this company's only — another's is drawn as missing), on the article page and in the
  editor's Preview. Left out, it gives the old id address, which the export relies on.
- **The billing pop-up** (`chat.js`) is sent the number only and opens `/portal/t/{number}`; the upload APIs take
  `ticketNumber` from the portal (the console still sends `ticketId`), and `/api/portal/photos` answers each photo's `token`;
  `/api/portal/clients` answers `number` beside `id`, for the Clients page's "already on file" buttons.
- **The menu's tab** reads `/portal/t|c|a|r/…` as Tickets, Clients, Knowledge base, Recurring (`_Layout`'s script).

### The old addresses, and why they keep working

- **The pages have their old route as a second one with `SuppressLinkGeneration`** (Program.cs, `OldAddress`). Routed to the
  same page, which asks `PortalPage.AddressedIdAsync`: a company's own id is sent on to its number, query kept — **302 for a GET,
  307 for a POST** (a page left open since before the deploy still posts, and lands); anybody else's is the page's own "not found",
  **a 404, word for word the page a missing number gets**. **Never `Conventions.AddPageRoute` for this**: it suppresses the
  page's own route and makes the ADDED one the address every link is built with — exactly backwards.
- **A page's handlers are given the id from the number in its address** (`OnPageHandlerExecutionAsync` on Ticket, Client,
  KnowledgeArticle, KnowledgeEdit, RecurringEdit). **The hidden `id` fields are gone** from the ticket and client pages, and
  whatever a form posts as `id` is overwritten before any handler runs — a forged one is never read.
- **An old query** (`?client=`, `?ticket=`) is translated by `PortalPage.FromOldQueryAsync` on the knowledge base, its editor and
  the ticket list, for a post as well as a GET; one that names nothing of this company's goes to the page with no query — the same
  answer whether it is another company's id or nobody's.
- **Old file addresses** are minimal routes (`OldFileAddress`): this company's own → 302 to the token; anybody else's a 404, as
  a token that does not exist.
- **Everything goes through one translator, `PortalAddresses.FromOldAsync`** — the pages, the file routes and the hand-off.
- **The console**: `TicketsForm` and `SessionForm` send the new shapes (`Technician/Portal.cs` for a ticket); the protocol gained
  ADDITIVE fields for it (`AttachmentInfo.Token`, `TicketDetail.ScreenshotTokens`, `KnowledgeInfo.ClientNumber`,
  `KnowledgeRefInfo.Number`, `KnowledgeCountMsg.ClientNumber`, `RecurringInfo.TaskNumber`) and falls back to the old shape when
  a field is empty. **`/portal/enter` translates an old console's path for the signed-in company before it redirects**, so the
  browser lands straight on the number and never shows the id; nothing of theirs → the queue. `PortalHandoffService.SafePath`
  allows the new shapes, spelled out whole, digits or 24 hex characters only, **and keeps the old ones for good**.

### Out of scope, on purpose

- **Ids in the portal's background calls (`/api/portal/…` JSON) and in the console↔server protocol** (`Shared/Protocol.cs`).
  Reading those takes developer tools or taking the console apart, and gives only a rough platform-wide count; closing them too
  would mean ids that are never sequential at all — a much bigger change.
- **What comes FROM those calls**: the client picker's hidden value (`clientpick.js`, modes `id`/`owner` — `clientId`, `c:{id}`,
  `p:{id}`, filled from `/api/portal/clients`) once a client is chosen, the photo ids a refused quote line carries back
  (`photoIds`), a picked comment file's id (`attach`). Those are the API's ids, round-tripped.
- **The `[image:{id}]` an article's words hold**, as the editor shows them; folder ids (`?folder=`); contact, quote-line, note
  and item ids in hidden fields. None names a ticket, client, article or photo in an address.
- `/owner` (our own platform admins), which names companies by id.

### What building it found

- **`addresscheck`'s first run found a link still naming the client by id**: a ticket's *Knowledge base for …* (`_Knowledge`).
- **The console's comment-file buttons had never worked**: `/portal/attachment/{id}` was not on the hand-off's allow-list, so
  they opened the ticket queue. Both its shapes are on it now.
- **A not-found page carries its own address** (the light/dark switch's `returnUrl`), so "the same page" means the same page
  with its own address set aside — which is what the harness compares.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/addresscheck` (new) | **122 of 122**. Two companies, the OTHER seeded first so the first one's ids are not its numbers. The backfill on a database of its own, stood at the migration before, rows written by SQL interleaved between two companies: numbered 1, 2, 3 per company in id order, every file a distinct token. New rows numbered by whatever made them (Add a client, several in one save for two companies, an article), a duplicate refused by the unique index. The translator for every kind, both companies; the hand-off's allow-list. Then a platform: each company's `/portal/t|c|a|r/1` is its own; every old address 302s to the new one with its query; another company's old id, number or token is a 404 identical to a missing one's; files open by token; **18 pages searched for a database id** (old-shape addresses, `?client=`/`?ticket=`, `name="id"` holding one of the company's ids, `ticketId`) — dashboard, lists, a ticket in the story AND the classic page, a client, the knowledge base, an article with a picture, its editor, a write-up, recurring, devices, workload; a comment posted at `/portal/t/1` with a forged id lands on #1, another company's forged post lands on its own #1, a number it lacks is a 404; an old-address post 307s and lands; a client saved by number; a write-up by `?t=`; a photo uploaded by `ticketNumber`; the console's hand-off with old and new shapes. **Guards out: the company in the ticket lookup 107 of 122; the company in the old-address lookup 118 of 122; the ticket page's "id from the number" line 109 of 122.** |
| on PostgreSQL | **`addresscheck` 122 of 122 there too** — its backfill runs the PostgreSQL migration's own SQL — and 23 more that touch clients, articles, ticket pages or files: kbcheck 154, ticketstepcheck 129, webchatcheck 127, securitycheck 87, healthcheckwire 61, routecheck 61, pilotcheck 57, mailintakecheck 135, quotecheck 187, importcheck 107 and the rest: **24 of 24**. `pgcheck` 20 of 20 (both migration sets match the model; PgInitial untouched). |
| every database harness, SQLite | **90 of 90** (`tools/Run-DbHarnesses.ps1`). Six needed changing, all for the same reason — they asserted or scraped the old shapes: **kbcheck** (154, 151 before: its link checks name the new addresses, and three hand-off checks added — an old console's link now lands on the number), **ticketstepcheck** and **sessionextras** (a file's and a recording's token), **devicelink** and **healthcheckwire** (they read a client's id out of the Clients page's links; it comes from `/api/portal/clients` now, which keeps ids), **pilotcheck** (its browser does not follow redirects, so it opens the new address). |
| walked | in the built-in browser on `addresscheck -- --hold`'s platform: the list, a ticket, its photos and file by token, an article with a picture, an old `/portal/clients/{id}` bookmark landing on `/portal/c/1` with the Clients tab lit; a person added, a folder made in a client's section (`?c=1&done=made`), a new article saved to `/portal/a/5`, a comment, a recurring task saved (`?done=changed&n=1`); then signed in as the other company: Acme's old ticket address is *Ticket not found* (404), and `/portal/t/1` is its own. |

**Not on hardware.** **One signed `Publish-Platform.ps1` — migration `PerCompanyAddresses` on both databases, which numbers what is
there before the unique indexes are made** — then the console updates itself (§148); an old console keeps working through the

## 160. Five seats; more on request — we allow it per company, the owner agrees the price, PayFast charges it — 2026-10-25

Clint, three days after §153: *"I know i said we should only allow the tenants 5 seats, but can i have an option in the owner portal
where i can right click on a registered tenant with an option to allow more seats. When this option is selected, the tenant owner then
get the add more seats option in their portal and adding them adds to the payfast order so that rather than me having to bill them
independently, it gets done via payfast."* He took every recommendation — R300 a seat; a number per company that we set (not a
switch); from the next payment, no part-months; a pilot's extras invoiced (PayFast cannot hold R0); a sentence in the terms — and
changed the last: the website says **"five seats; more on request"**. **§160 supersedes §153's "no more"**; §153's pilots and open
places are untouched.

### What it is

- **`Tenant.MostSeats`** (0 = the package and no more — every company until we say otherwise) and **`Pricing.MostSeatsFor(t)`**,
  the ONE number the limit asks: never below the package, never above **`Pricing.MostAllowed` (50)**. `SeatsAllowed` is still the
  PACKAGE (≤ 5); `LimitProblem` now asks `MostSeatsFor`, and its words say an owner can ask on Billing.
- **The extra-seat price is back**: `Region.ExtraSeat` (R300 / $20 / $20 / £20 / €20), `Bill.Extra`/`ExtraText`, `BillFor` charging
  `package + extra × ExtraSeat` — a pilot's package R0, its extras not. **`RiseIf`, `PriceRiseAsync`, `PriceRefusal` and the People
  page's Now / After / Accept / Don't do it are restored from before `b2c6fe0`**, as they were: the owner names the exact figure
  (`PriceRise.Token`) or nobody is added; a supervisor is refused with the figure; the command line is not asked but is recorded; every
  yes is a `SeatAgreement` on Billing. Without an allowance there is no price question at all — the sixth is refused before it.
- **PayFast needed nothing new**: `CompanyBilling.OwedCents` is `BillFor`, and `PeopleChanged` already sends the new amount at once
  (§136). Changing the package on All companies now raises it too (`TenantService.PriceMayHaveChanged`), since fewer in the package can
  make seats extras.
- **Asking**: Billing → *More seats* (`#moreSeats`), owner only — `TenantService.AskForSeatsAsync`: more than they may have, 50 at most,
  500 characters of reason; never the free version (it upgrades) or a company not billed. Kept on the company (`SeatsAskedFor`,
  `SeatsAskedUtc`, `SeatsAskedNote`, `SeatsAskedBy`; a newer ask replaces it). `AdminCompanies.TellUsOfSeatRequestAsync` emails every
  Full admin and Owner **of that server** and logs it; Approvals lists it whether or not the mail went.
- **Answering** — through `AdminCompanies`, by `ControlServers.Dispatch` (`allow-seats` with `most`, `decline-seats` with `reason`), so
  a company on another server is answered the same way: **Owner → Approvals → *More seats asked for*** (Allow up to N, prefilled with what
  they asked; Decline with an optional reason for them), and **Owner → All companies → *Allow up to*** beside *Seats in package*, any
  time — the package's number takes it back. Each clears the ask, logs by name and emails the owners (`SeatsAllowedMail`,
  `SeatsDeclinedMail`). **Taking it back removes nobody**; nobody more can be added until they are below it, and giving a seat back is
  always allowed. Clint asked for a right-click; the owner pages are web pages, so it is a box on the row (said to him before building).
- `ServerReport` carries `MostSeats`, the ask, `InSeats` and `Pilot` — optional, so an older server's report still reads (as 0).
- `set-brand <slug> most-seats N` on the command line.
- **The words**: `Pricing.WhyFive` (*"every company starts with five seats, and more are on request"*); core terms section 2 with
  `{{EXTRA}}` (filled by `Terms.For`) and the pilot section — **version 2026-10-25, `landing-legal` re-run**; `/pricing` (*Five people;
  more on request*, a fact card with R300), `/support`, the holding page (the `+ More on request` row; `PRICES` carries `extra`, switched
  with the region), both guides (reprinted).

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/seatcheck` (rewritten) | **99 of 99.** The sums (R300/$20/£20/€20, R1,100 for seven written out, £89, a pilot's sixth R300, PayFast's 110000 cents, the allowance held 5..50); at five a sixth refused to supervisor, owner naming a price, command line, with how to ask; asking (owner only, more than they have, ≤ 50, not free, not unbilled; changes nothing); allowed seven: R500 → R800, supervisor refused with the figure, owner refused without and with the wrong figure, added with it and recorded, the owner's own tick the seventh at R1,100, an eighth refused, removal lowers it, the command line recorded, taken back keeps everybody. Pages: the way to ask, Billing's ask form (a supervisor's forced ask refused), Owner → Approvals, Allow seven, All companies and the log, Now / After, Don't do it, Accept, Billing R800 with the extra row, a supervisor told R800 → R1,100, a second ask declined, the allowance taken back from All companies, not billed. **96 of 99 with the owner's price gate out; 97 with the owner-only ask out.** 95 of 95 on PostgreSQL (the old-migration part is SQLite's). |
| re-run | **All 90 database harnesses pass on SQLite** once five that asserted "no more" / "no R300" were moved to the new words — `pilotcheck` 57, `placescheck` 26, `rolecheck` 105, `signuppaycheck` 72, `sitecheck` 96 (which now treats *"no extra seats"* and *"and no more"* as stale claims). `brandpush` and `versioncheck` failed once on timing (a late message; a reset connection at login) and passed unchanged on the re-run. On PostgreSQL the 19 that touch seats, prices, terms or the owner pages: 19 of 19. `pgcheck` 20, `legalcheck` 16. |

**Not on hardware.** **Signed `Publish-Platform.ps1` (migration `MoreSeatsOnRequest`, both databases)** — no console re-download, no
client reinstall. `TEST-3.6.md` section DS, 836–844.

## 161. No free version: the Basic Version for Remote Workers, R50 a month, three computers — and a page for remote workers — 2026-10-25

Clint: *"I have decided to no longer have a free version. I would like to change the free version to a R50 per month version and set
its maximum amount of machines to 3. All the usual rules for the free version would still apply."* He took every recommendation and
named it himself: **The Basic Version for Remote Workers**. Then, while it was being built: *"we have a limitation of tenants signing
up, but that should not apply to the basic version"* (it never did — now proved), and *"we also need to add as many keywords as
possible for remote working for when the site goes live"* (a page, below). **§161 supersedes §100–§107 on the price and the count;
every other rule of the free version stands.**

### What changed, and what did not

- **The code keeps `FreePlan` and the stored plan `"free"` ON PURPOSE** — renaming them would touch every guard in the hub
  (`TenantHub.Free.cs`, the allow-lists) and every row for nothing a person sees. **What a person reads never says "free version"
  now**: `FreePlan.FullName` (*The Basic Version for Remote Workers*), `ShortName` (*Basic*), `TheName` (*the Basic version*).
  `sitecheck` treats "free version" on a public page as a stale claim.
- **`FreePlan.MaxMachines` = 3** (was 2); removals stay two a month. Everything that counts machines asks it, so the hub, `may-add`,
  the portal's count and the console's header followed by themselves.
- **The price**: `Pricing.Region.Basic` (R50 / $5 / $5 / £5 / €5); `BillFor` gives a Basic company `Bill.Basic`, one person, no extras.
  `OwedCents` follows, so **PayFast's amount sync and the late-payment checks no longer skip the free plan** (they did:
  `CompanyBilling.SyncAmountAsync`, `CompanyBilling.Late`), and **`CompanyBilling.Refusal` no longer refuses it** ("nothing to pay").
- **Signup**: Basic goes on to PayFast exactly like the full version (`SignupModel.OnPostCreateAsync` lost its `!Free`) — R0 now, R50
  from 14 days on, switched on by PayFast's notice. Approved by hand (where card payment does not apply) it starts a **14-day trial**,
  no longer Active-for-ever (`TenantService.ApproveAsync`). **The five places never apply to it** (`OpenPlaces.Taking` and
  `SignupAsync` already excluded it; `basiccheck` fills every place and shows Basic still signing up).
- **Its portal** gains **Billing** (`FreePortal` allow-list and the menu): the plan as *The Basic Version for Remote Workers* and R50,
  no seats, no tickets link, the card, cancelling, payments.
- **Upgrading** (`TenantService.UpgradeQuote`, `UpgradeTrialEnd`): R50 → the package; **no new trial for a company already paying by
  card** (PayFast would charge R500 inside it) — the full price from its next payment, PayFast told at once (`Counted`); the trial it is
  on, if any; else 14 days (a free account from before). The Upgrade page says which.
- **The free accounts from before** — their terms promise *"at least 30 days"* by email. **Owner → Basic version** (was Free version)
  marks each running account with no card *Free — needs notice*; **Give notice** / **Give every one notice**
  (`FreeCompanies.GiveNoticeAsync`) puts it on the TRIAL machinery, ending at midnight 30 days on in its own time — one conditional
  update, so two admins give one notice — and emails the owners (`NoticeEmail`), logged. From there the existing parts do the rest:
  Billing's *Add your card*, the portal's trial banner, the trial notices at 7, 1 and 0 days (**`TrialNoticeService.ComposeBasic`**,
  its own words: no "technicians", no "support software"), and on the day, with no card, its computers are refused until the card goes
  in. **Nothing is sent by itself: the notices go when an admin presses the button.**
- **Accounts made from Owner → Basic version** start a 14-day trial; the invitation says R50 after 14 days and to add the card; the
  set-up page says so too.
- **The terms**: `Terms/basic.txt` (was `free.txt`, `git mv`): R50 (`{{BASIC}}`), three computers (`{{BASIC_MACHINES}}`), **"computers
  you own, or whose owner has allowed you to reach them"** (a remote worker's office PC is usually the employer's — the old "own"
  would have forbidden the very use in the name), section 2's paying rules apply, section 11 in full. Version 2026-10-25 (not yet
  deployed, so the morning's seat change and this share it); `landing-legal` re-run.
- **The words**: signup (plan card, terms, what happens next), `/pricing` (the Basic card, R50), the home page's section and its
  schema.org offer, the footer, approvals, the owner pages' pills, the hub's refusals, the console's Remove question, the emails, both
  guides (reprinted). **The guides' screenshot of the Basic console still shows "of 2"** — remake it with `tools/siteshots` when next
  touched.

### A page for remote workers (`/remote-workers`)

Search engines read what a page SAYS; a hidden keyword list does little. So **`Pages/RemoteWorkers.cshtml`** says it — *work from home
on your office computer*, remote access to the work PC, unattended remote desktop, hybrid work, branch offices, after hours, printing and
files from home, secure (two-factor, end to end, POPIA), the price, a TeamViewer/AnyDesk alternative for one person — **every claim true
of the Basic version**. It carries a `keywords` meta (the layout writes one from `ViewData["Keywords"]`; the home and pricing pages
have one too), schema.org `SoftwareApplication` + **`FAQPage`** (the questions can show as answers in Google), and links from the home
page, the pricing card and the footer. **It is in `SitePages.Public` AND go-live.sh's `@holding` list** — behind the holding page until
1 November like the rest; `sitecheck` fails otherwise.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/basiccheck` (new) | **36 of 36 on SQLite and PostgreSQL.** The rules: R50/$5/£5/€5, one person, nothing extra, 5000 cents; three machines; it may pay by card (rand only); its terms (R50, three, "allowed you to reach them", nothing unfilled); Billing on its allow-list, tickets not; upgrading R50 → R500 and the three cases of when it starts; the approval and notice emails. The pages: an old free account needs notice → Give notice → a trial ending at midnight 30 days on in its own time, logged, never twice; an account made from Owner → Basic version → a 14-day trial; the Basic owner's Billing, menu and refused tickets; Upgrade (Now R50, After R500, the trial carried) and the yes on record; **every place taken: the full version waits, Basic goes straight to its terms**; the plan card. **34 of 36 with the old "nothing to pay" refusal back; 35 with a card-paying upgrade given a new trial.** |
| moved to the new rules | `freecheck` 45 (a fourth refused, not a third), `freeinstall` 16, `freeportal` 31 (Billing allowed, three listed), `freeaccount` 40 (a trial, the email's R50 and card), `signupcheck` 51 (its terms; approved by hand → a trial), `signuppaycheck` 73 (**Basic to PayFast: R0.00 now, R50.00 from 14 days on; Approve refused while the card is awaited**), `upgradecheck` 21 (R50 → R500, "50>500"), `sitecheck` 103 (no "free version" anywhere; the remote-workers page's heading, keywords, R50, FAQ data). |
| re-run | **All 91 database harnesses on SQLite pass** — `brandpush` failed 2 of 45 in the full run (as it did in the morning's, before any Basic change) and passed 45 of 45 alone: a timing flake under load, not this. **23 of 23 related on PostgreSQL**, `pgcheck` 20, `legalcheck` 16. Both guides reprinted and measured page by page (two screenshots made smaller to keep A4). |

**Not on hardware.** **Signed `Publish-Platform.ps1`, no migration** — the apps update themselves (one console sentence). Before 1 November
nothing is public; **pressing Give notice on the live server emails the real free accounts — only on Clint's word.** `TEST-3.6.md` section DT,
845–855.

## 163. The Free version is back beside the Basic version, and the Basic version connects attended too — 2026-10-25

Clint, the same evening as §161: *"I think that we should have a free version as well. The free version should only allow one
connection for unattended access with password as it was previously. The basic version we should change to allow attended and
unattended, but still only a maximum of 20 machines. Does this make sense?"* Told it did, with guard rails so Basic could not stand in
for the full version at a one-person IT shop (attended only on installed computers that count toward the 20, no "Get help now", no
Request Support, one person, no tickets or branding, the bar always on), and that the old free accounts would keep two computers until
they removed one: *"yes build it. will the free then have the option to upgrade to basic and full, and does basic have the option to
upgrade to full and downgrade to free?"* — yes to all of it. **§163 supersedes §161's "no free version"; Basic's price, card, extra
computers and places stand.**

### Three plans, two stored names

- **`Tenant.Plan` is `"free"` (the Free version) or `"basic"` (the Basic version)**, anything else the full version. **`FreePlan.Is`
  now means EITHER** — every shared one-person rule (one person, no tickets, the hub's allow-lists, two removals a month, the bar)
  kept asking it unchanged — and **`IsFree` / `IsBasic` / `Attended(plan)`** decide the rest. **`MachinesFor(plan, paid)` and
  `TooManyFor(plan, n)` take the plan now**: the Free version 1 (`FreeMachines`), the Basic version 3..20. Words by plan:
  `FullNameOf` / `ShortNameOf` / `TheNameOf` (*The Free Version*, *Free*, *the Free version*). The class keeps the name `FreePlan`.
- **Migration `FreeVersionBack`** (data only, both databases): a company stored `"free"` that has a trial end, extra computers, or a
  PayFast subscription that is not a test becomes `"basic"` — those were made as Basic this morning; the old free accounts have none
  and stay Free. Down puts every `"basic"` back to `"free"`.
- **The old free accounts keep the computers they have.** The hub only ever refuses a NEW computer past the limit (`FreeRefusesHello`),
  so one with two keeps both until it removes one. **Owner → Basic version's *Give notice* is gone** (and `GiveNoticeAsync`,
  `NoticeEmail`), so nothing can email them that their account is becoming R50.

### The Basic version, attended — through the agent alone

- **`StartSession`**: a one-person plan goes unattended only with the permission AND a password; without both, the Basic version is
  handed to an agent that can ask (`AskConsent`, §76) — **and never to a tray app** (`if (Free && hostConn == null) return null` sits
  ahead of the tray-app fallback; `FallBackToClientAsync` already ended a one-person session). The Free version's
  `ConnectDevice` refusals (unattended only, a password) now ask `UnattendedOnly`, not `Free`. `ShowNotice` stays on for both.
- **Nothing on the computer asks for help**: Request Support and an outside-help code are refused on both (`FreePlan.NoAskingFor`,
  each in its own plan's words); there is still no tray app on a Free or Basic computer, so there is nowhere to press them.
- **The installer** (`FreeInstallForm`, told by `Branding.Basic`): on Basic the password is OPTIONAL — both boxes blank installs the
  agent and **`FreeSetup.SetAttendedOnlyAsync`** connects once as the client and switches unattended OFF (waiting for an "off" after
  its own request — an earlier "on" is the stored old one). Running it again with a password makes the computer unattended again.
  The Free version still requires one.
- **The console**: `StateMsg.Basic`; on either one-person plan the machine list is ONE list of everything (**`DeviceTab.All`**) —
  the Free view had shown only the Unattended tab, which would have hidden every attended Basic computer. Connecting to one without a
  password goes straight to *Waiting for … to accept*, as on the full version.

### Moving between them

- **`/portal/upgrade` is the one page for all of it** (`?to=basic|full|free`): the Free version with nothing named is asked which
  (Basic or full, each card with its price); Basic goes to the full version by default, or **down** with `?to=free`. Each shows the
  terms of where it goes and the price, ticked by the owner. Up: `TenantService.UpgradeAsync(..., to)` — Free → Basic is R0 → R50, a
  14-day trial, three computers, on to PayFast for the card; Free → full and Basic → full as before. `UpgradesFrom(plan)` says where.
- **Down, Basic → Free: `CompanyBilling.DowngradeToFreeAsync` is the one way.** `TenantService.DowngradeProblemAsync` first (the owner;
  the Free terms by fingerprint; **no more than one computer installed**, by hardware as the hub counts — the owner removes the others
  first, so nothing is cut off by surprise); then PayFast is told to cancel (if it will not, nothing changes) and ours is marked
  **ended today** — never "service until the end of the month", because the service carries on free, and `CloseEndedAsync` must not
  close it (PayFast's own CANCELLED notice finds `EndsOn` already set and does nothing); then `DowngradeToFreeAsync`: Active, no trial,
  `BasicMachines` 0, the Free terms kept word for word, *Moved down …* on Billing. No refund of the month paid (the terms say so).
- **Billing**: the Free version shows *nothing to pay* and Upgrade; Basic shows *Move to the Free version*. `CompanyBilling.Refusal`
  says the Free version has nothing to pay again, and the amount sync and late checks skip it.
