## 164. Latest activity: every update on the tickets, as it is posted — 2026-10-26

Clint, raised by one of his technicians: *"a latest activity button. So in the dashboard if one clicks on latest activity, it will show
any updates on all tickets as they are posted or when stages change ... for all tickets, with the option to only check latest activity
on one's own tickets ... An example of this, is i asked technicians for updates, they updated, but i had no way of seeing that there
was updates posted unless i actually went back into that ticket. It should show newest to oldest, but should also be able to be sorted
by client, technician, and all tickets."* Eight questions put to him with a recommendation each; his answer: *"lets go with your
recommendations"*. Then, mid-build: *"would this also include when a ticket is assigned to you. so for example, i assign a ticket to
Ryan, it shows up in his recent activity?"* — yes, and it says *assigned it to you*.

What he took: a button in the portal (a tab beside Tickets, every role, and a card on the dashboard) and in the console (beside
Tickets); comments, stage changes, customer replies, files, edits, assignments and new tickets — **a session's own lines left out
unless ticked**; your own posts hidden unless ticked; **Mine = on it, worked on it, opened it, or @mentioned on it**; client and
"posted by" as FILTERS on one newest-first list ("posted by", not "assigned to" — *"show me everything Sipho posted today"*); a count
of what is new since you last looked, per person, live, no pop-up and no sound; each line opens the ticket at that entry; 50 at a time
with *Show older*; closed tickets included; everybody gets it.

### Nothing new is written to make the list

- **The entries ARE the tickets' stories** (`TicketNote`) **and the tickets themselves** (a "New ticket" line from `Ticket.CreatedUtc`
  / `OpenedBy`). Every rule is **`Services/TicketActivityService.cs`**: `ListAsync` (a page), `NewCountAsync` (the badge), `Scope`
  (who sees what), `FromNote` / `FromTicket` (what one line says — the ONE place that decides a line's kind), `AssignsTo`.
- **Who sees what is `TicketService.VisibleTo`, asked first** — exactly the ticket list's boundary. A technician's *All* is their own
  work and the unassigned pool, never a colleague's job. **Mine narrows; it never widens.** The owner-only login sees everything (it
  oversees); the office administrator too.
- **`TicketNote.Automatic` (new)**: a line written by itself while something ELSE happened — the hub's session lines (connected, ended,
  clipboard, scripts, recordings, privacy screen, the customer's chat during a session: everything through `LogToTicketAsync`), the
  "Customer requested support" / web-support / website-chat / outsider lines, and **each ticket's own "…ticket opened" line** (portal
  New ticket, console New ticket, email and contact form intake, recurring tasks, *Add another machine*) — because the "New ticket"
  line already says it. **Not the same as `IsSystem`**: *"reassigned from Sue to Ryan"* is system-worded but is news, and stays in.
  `AddNoteAsync(..., automatic: true)` is how a writer says so. **The migration marked every old `IsSystem` line Automatic** — the past
  shows less rather than a session's every line. **A new writer of a session-style line must pass `automatic: true`**, or it will
  appear in everybody's list and count on everybody's badge.
- **"assigned it to you"** is read from the words `TicketService.UpdateAsync` writes for a hand-off (*reassigned from X to Y*, *assigned
  to … (was …)*, *added … to the ticket*) — those words ARE the record of it; a display name holds no comma (§49), so a list of names
  splits cleanly. A new ticket booked straight to you says it too; an @mention says *asked you*.

### What is new, and telling people

- **`Technician.ActivitySeenUtc`** — the newest page, opened with *mark seen*, sets it to the moment the list was READ (an entry saved
  while it was being read stays new). Null until the first look; the badge then counts the last day (`FirstLook`).
  **`Technician.ActivityMine`** — All or Mine, remembered on the server from that same look, so the badge counts what the person chose
  and the portal and the console follow each other. *Show older* is not a look.
- The count never includes your own posts or automatic lines; at most 99, said *99+* (`ActivityWords`, Shared).
- **`PlatformDb.TicketActivitySaved`** (static, in `PlatformDb.Numbers.cs`) is raised after ANY save that adds a `TicketNote` or a
  `Ticket` — the one place, because there are thirty-odd writers and a count that missed one would be this feature's own fault.
  `TicketActivityService` turns it into **`Changed(tenant)`, at most once per 700 ms per company** (a step writes two or three lines),
  and a look into **`SeenChanged(tenant, person)`**.
- **Console**: `ActivityRequestMsg` → `ActivityListMsg`; `ActivityCountMsg` at sign-in and whenever it moves (`Shared/Activity.cs`;
  `Hub/TenantHub.Activity.cs`, wired by `HubRegistry.Activity` like `Knowledge`). Never sent to, and never answered for, the one-person
  plans (their consoles may not ask: `ConsoleMaySendOnFree`).
- **Portal**: the existing live stream (`/api/portal/chat/stream`) sends `event: activity` with this person's count; `chat.js` moves the
  tab's badge (`#activityBadge`) and the dashboard card (`[data-activity-count]`) and raises `rsp-activity` on the page.
- **The loop that must not happen**: a look sends a count of nought; **a window or page refetches only on a count ABOVE nought**, or its
  own look would answer itself for ever. Both the console's `ActivityForm.CountChanged` and the page's script say so.

### The two places it is drawn

- **Portal `/portal/activity`** (`Pages/Portal/Activity.cshtml`, the list in `_ActivityList.cshtml`, refreshed alone by `?handler=List`):
  All / My tickets as tabs; Client by **`clientpick.js`** (§75) — the picker's id arrives as `client=` and is **turned into `c={number}`
  by a redirect at once**, so no id stays in the address (§159); Posted by; the two ticks; *Show older* by `before={ticks}`. A line is a
  link to **`/portal/t/{number}#note-{id}`** — the ticket's story (both `_Timeline` and the classic page) now gives every entry
  `id="note-{id}"`, outlined when it is the target (`site.css`). Not in `FreePortal`'s allow-list, so a one-person plan is refused it.
- **Console `ActivityForm`**: All / My tickets (tinted `RoundButton`s), Client by part of a name (the Clients page's own `SearchAsync` on
  the server — a filter needs no picker), Posted by, the ticks, an owner-drawn list (a stripe by kind, *new* tinted, *assigned it to you*
  in red), *Show older*. A click opens the ticket in the console's ticket window. **Seen only while on screen** (shown and not
  minimised); minimised, it waits and the count stays. One window, hidden on close. The header button sits **beside Tickets and is never
  red** — an update is the ordinary run of a day; what is waiting on you is the Tickets button's count.

### How it is proved

|---|---|
| `tools/activitycheck` (new) | **83 of 83 on SQLite and on PostgreSQL** (the 83rd from the browser walk, below). In-process: both comments newest first with the three new tickets; never another company's; an automatic line out, in with the tick; a line's ticket, client, who, what and words; **a technician sees nothing of a colleague's ticket**, the office and an owner-only login everything; own posts out, in with the tick, *Posted by* me / Ryan / Sue; one client by id, by words, by a contact's name, none, not this company's; a step *Call out booked → Work done*, Back and the step marked, a customer's reply; **Clint's Ryan case**: before, he cannot see it; after Olga's reassign it is in his list as *assigned it to you* by Olga, in his Mine, and plain for anybody else; *added … to the ticket*; booked straight to him; the hand-off words read seven ways; an @mention *asked you*; Mine's four ways in; the count — the last day, nought after a look, one after a colleague's post, never his own, automatic, another company's or a ticket he cannot see, Mine remembered and counted, *Show older* not a look; four posts told once; a look told to that person; 74 entries paged to the end, none twice, newest first. ## 165. A deploy cuts every connection once, not twice; the server report shows Caddy's memory — 2026-10-26

Clint asked whether Caddy's memory grows deploy after deploy (§126's restart grew it 2.18 → 3.98 GB and it kept it).
**It cannot pile up across deploys: every `Publish-Platform.ps1` runs `go-live.sh`, and step 4 restarts Caddy.** §126's
storm restarted the PLATFORM alone, which a deploy never does; only a platform-only restart (a crash systemd restarts,
or one by hand) leaves Caddy holding what it grew.

Reading live (Clint, by hand: platform up 43:07, Caddy 43:05) showed what that restart cost instead: **step 3 started
the platform and step 4 restarted Caddy two seconds later**, so every machine and console was cut off, reconnected, and
was cut off again — two reconnect rushes per deploy, where §126 measured one. Now step 3 only ENABLES the platform;
it starts after `systemctl restart caddy`, and **a `trap … EXIT` starts it should anything in between fail** (Caddy
refusing its new configuration included) — a failed deploy must never leave the platform down. Caddy's own upgrade in
step 1 (only when `CADDY_VERSION` changes) still restarts it separately; that is rare and left alone.

`server-report.sh` (`Get-ServerReport.ps1`) has a `Caddy using` line: its memory and since when. It should stay near
the same figure between deploys while the machines do; climbing on its own is the growth. The baseline on 2026-10-26,
~14 machines: Caddy 59 MB, platform 376 MB, 950 MB used of 7.9 GB.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `unixsockcheck` | **18 of 18** (16 with the old go-live back): the platform starts after Caddy restarts and never by `enable --now`; the trap is set after the stop, before Caddy, and cleared after the start |
| the real lines against stubs | the step 3 → 4 slice of go-live.sh with stand-in `systemctl`/`caddy`: in order enable → validate → restart caddy → start, once; with Caddy's validate refusing, the script stops AND the platform is started by the trap |
| `bash -n` | go-live.sh and server-report.sh parse |

**Not on the server yet.** It takes effect from the next signed `Publish-Platform.ps1` — that deploy runs the NEW
go-live.sh, so it is already the first with one cut. No migration, nothing for the apps.

## 165. Sort the ticket list by any column; a due date on every ticket — 2026-10-26

Clint, with a screenshot of SuperOps' ticket list: *"you can see all the tickets at a glance. Every column (Status, Subject, Company,
Tech, Priority, Last Updated, Due Date) can be sorted by simply clicking on Last Updated, for example. Can we do something similar?"*
Six recommendations put to him (click to sort, the Sort box gone; Group by customer a tick; Due shown from what tickets had; Customer
replied in orange; the console's queue too; saved "ticket views" left for later), and the one decision his: a real due date on every
ticket now or later. His answer: *"Lets go with your suggestions and add a due date now as well"*.

### Every column sorts, on the server

- **`Shared/TicketSort.cs`** is the one rule for both ends. A key is a column and its direction: `"due"` (its own first way —
  **`FirstDescending`**: number, last updated and priority start newest / highest / most urgent; everything else A–Z, the soonest due
  first), `"due:asc"`, `"due:desc"`. `Toggle` turns the column in use round; `Arrow` says ▲/▼; `Parse` gives the column. **The four
  keys of §130's Sort box (`updated`, `newest`, `oldest`, `appointment`) keep their old meaning** — an older console still sends them,
  and `ticketeditcheck` still proves them.
- **`TicketService.Sorted`** sorts every column BEFORE the first 500 are taken. Text in lower case (SQLite and PostgreSQL agree);
  **Type by its NAME** (a CASE, because the stored numbers are in the order categories were added); Status by status then stage;
  **blanks LAST whichever way round** — no client, nobody on it, no due date — so turning a list round never brings the empty ones to
  the top. Ties: newest update, then the number.
- **Portal `/portal/tickets`**: every heading a link (`SortLink` keeps the filter, search, dates, client and machine), `aria-sort` and
  the arrow on the one in use; **the Sort box is gone**; **Group by customer is a tick** (its own cookie `rsp_ticket_group`; the old
  sort cookie's `customer` still means grouped), and grouped, the headings sort within each customer, Machine standing for Client. New
  columns **Priority** (word + dot), **Last updated** (*2 min ago*, the time on hover) and **Due**. Both views are drawn by ONE pair of
  functions at the bottom of `Tickets.cshtml` (`SortRow`, `TicketRow`, every value encoded). **On a phone the headings fold away with the
  table**, so a small *Sort by* box (`t-phone-sort`) stands in for them there only.
- **Console queue** (`TicketsForm`): columns #, Subject, Where it is, Due, Priority, Client, Assigned to, Updated (`ListColumns`, most
  needed first); a heading click sorts, ▲/▼ in the heading, remembered in `ticketsort.txt` (the full key now). **The queue takes what the
  window can spare and no more**: the ticket side keeps the room it had (`ticketRoom`, `_line * 74`) — widening it unconditionally broke
  three `ticketwindowprobe` checks (buttons wrapping, long names running off) — and Subject is never below two fifths of it; in a narrow
  queue the later columns scroll in from the right.

### "Customer replied"

- **`TicketService.CustomerRepliedAsync`**: the tickets whose NEWEST entry (not counting automatic lines — §164's `Automatic`) is the
  customer's emailed reply. The portal shows an orange *Customer replied* in Status; the console says it first in *Where it is*, in amber.
  Anybody's comment or step after it is the answer.
- `TicketSummary.CustomerReplied`, filled for the console's list, and **for every `TicketChangedMsg` in `TenantHub.BroadcastTechs`** —
  fourteen places send one, so it is asked there once (a `_replyAsked` set stops the second pass asking again).

### A due date on every ticket

- **`Ticket.DueDate`** (migration **`TicketDueDate`**, both databases): a DAY, stored as `RecurringTaskService.AsDate` stores one (§108).
  **Kept apart from `DueOn`**, which is a recurring SCHEDULE's day and what stops it opening that day twice — moving a due date must not
  open another ticket. A recurring task's ticket is given its day (and the migration copies `DueOn` into `DueDate` for those).
- **Every rule is `Services/TicketDue.cs`**: `TryRead` (a date box's `yyyy-MM-dd`), `Problem` (**never a day already gone** — a day
  already on the ticket stays as it is), `IsOverdue` (**past its day, still the bench's, not resolved or closed** — §108's recurring
  overdue, widened to every ticket; once it has gone to be invoiced the people on it have done their part), `Effective` (the due date,
  else a call out's appointment — what Due shows and sorts by), `Say` (*Tue 4 Nov 2026*).
- **Set** at New ticket (portal: *Due date (optional)* beside Priority; console: a *Due date* tick beside Priority, on the SAME two rows —
  `ticketformprobe` found the window needing a scrollbar when it took two rows of its own). **Changed** in Edit the ticket (portal and
  console: `TicketEdit.DueGiven` / `DueDate`, `TicketEditMsg` likewise — an older console sends neither and changes nothing), said in the
  story as *Due: … (was …)* / *Due date removed (was …)*, refused on a closed job. **Shown** first in the ticket's facts (*Due …* and
  *— overdue*) and in both lists; overdue in red with *Overdue*.
- **A console sends the DAY at midnight marked UTC** — never its local midnight, which the JSON carries with an offset and the server turns
  into its own (UTC) time, the day before. Said on `TicketCreateMsg.DueDate`.

### How it is proved

|---|---|
| `tools/ticketsortcheck` (new) | **61 of 61 on SQLite and on PostgreSQL.** The keys (first directions, nonsense, Toggle, Arrow, the four old ones); **all nine columns both ways** on four tickets chosen so every tie and blank shows (subject with mixed capitals, no client, nobody, no due date, a call out's appointment standing in), the old keys as before, sorted before the take; the due date read, refused in the past, set / same day / refused with NOTHING applied / left alone / removed, each said in the story, a closed job's kept; overdue on the bench, not in the office, not closed, not on its own day; the facts; a recurring task's ticket due on its day; Customer replied set by the reply, kept over an automatic line, cleared by a comment. Then a platform: `?sort=priority`, the heading's ▼ and its turn-round link, every heading a link that keeps the filter, remembered; Due with the appointment and 📅, Overdue in red, Priority's dot, *min ago*; Customer replied on that ticket only; Group by customer, remembered, unticked, **an old `customer` cookie still grouped**; the Sort box gone; New ticket with a due date and refusing a past one; Edit setting it, the form and the facts saying it; **the console**: a column sort and its echo, CustomerReplied / DueDate / Overdue on the summaries, New ticket keeping the DAY sent, a past day refused, Edit removing it, an older console's edit leaving it, an old Sort-box key. **57 of 61 with blanks-last taken out of Client and the past-day check out of Edit.** |

## 166. Job types, stage A: the rule and the service — 2026-10-27

Clint: *"there may be companies that wont want all the categories, or in some instances may not want all the stages of a category.
For example one I.T company might not want to have the before and after photos ... deselect stages they dont want without breaking
the flow."* Ten questions, every answer *"lets go with your suggestions"*; the brief is **`docs/NEXT-SESSION-JOBTYPES.md`** and holds
them all — do not re-ask them. **This is stage A of four: the rule and the service. There is no page yet (stage B), so nothing can be
switched off on any server — deploying it changes nothing a company sees.**

### What a company can switch off

- **24 switches**, every one in **`Services/JobTypes.cs`** (`JobTypes.Switches`: key, label, kind, card, what happens with it off).
  Four **categories** (Workshop, Call out, Walk in, Recurring task — **Remote support and General are locked on**: sessions, calls,
  emails, website chats and forms open them by themselves); two **rules** (photos in, photos out); the rest **steps** — skipped
  (Inspection findings, Ask suppliers, Payment before ordering, Track payment, Supervisor approval for Do not invoice) or one **choice**
  among several taken away (Damage report, Inspection fee, Waiting on customer, Out for delivery, Add another machine, Quote needed,
  Reschedule, Paid on site, Needs workshop work, Needs to be booked in, Paid at counter, SLA, Link to parent). **Anything not in the list
  is locked** — the first stages, each category's main way of billing, Do not invoice, Machine collected, Abandoned, Back.
- **Stored as what is OFF**: `Tenant.JobTypesOff`, comma-separated, so a switch added later is ON for every company. Written ONLY by
  **`TenantService.SetJobTypesAsync`** (`Permissions.CanSetJobTypes` — supervisor or owner, the owner-only login too), which
  **`JobTypes.Clean`s** it (unknown keys out; a switched-off category's own steps out, so switching it on again brings it back whole;
  the page's order) and then asks **`JobTypes.Problem`**. With who and when (`JobTypesChosenBy`, `JobTypesChosenUtc`).

### A job finishes the route it started on

- **`Ticket.RouteOff`** is a copy of the company's list **made in `TicketService.CreateAsync` and never changed**. Empty — every ticket
  before today — is everything on. The machines booked in with a job copy ITS list, not the company's (`AddMachineAsync`).
- **Steps are asked of the ticket's copy; categories of the company, live** (`TicketService.CategoryRefusalAsync`,
  `JobTypes.CategoryRefusal`): New ticket (portal and hub — an older console still offers every category), Edit's category change,
  a new recurring schedule, and **Needs workshop work / Needs to be booked in, which a call out opened while Workshop was on still SHOWS
  but is refused with words** (the brief: never hidden without saying why).
- Recurring task off: **`OpenDueAsync` lets the days pass without opening them** (and without moving `LastOpenedFor`), so switched on
  again the next one opens on its own day — never a pile of the days missed. The schedules are kept.

### One rule for the buttons, the refusal and the judge

- **`TicketService.RouteSteps(t)`** (now public) is what the route offers from where a ticket is: `JobTypes.FromHere` (a step's own
  stages, plus the ones a skipped step leaves it to answer — Repairable/Not repairable from Booked in, Quote sent from Quote needed),
  the category, **`JobTypes.Allows`** (its switch, by step key — `StepSwitch`), and `Offered`. **`ActionsFor` and `ActAsync` both ask
  it**; `ActAsync` REFUSES a switched-off step in words (*"… is switched off for this job (Job types)"*), so a stale page or an old
  console cannot walk round it. Out for delivery and Add another machine are asked in their own places, with their own words.
- **Where a skipped step sends a job is `JobTypes.ToOf`**, read by `TargetOf` (now public) before it resolves the `@` words: Do not
  invoice → `dni-to-close` (no approval); Client invoiced → `@close` (no tracking payment); and **with payment before ordering off,
  Quote accepted → `order-parts` and Parts fitted → `to-be-invoiced`**. Two new stages for that road, `Workflow.OrderParts` (*Quote
  accepted — order the parts*) and `PartsOnOrder` (*Parts ordered from supplier*), and one step, *Order placed with supplier* — the old
  `order-placed` says *Paid —*, which would be untrue there. **The Parts fitted change is the trap the brief named**: without it a
  quoted job closes never invoiced, and the judge refuses every list with that switch off (proved below).
- **The photo gates** ask `JobTypes.PhotosInRequired` / `PhotosOutRequired` of the ticket's copy: `CheckBookInAsync` (new optional
  `routeOff`; null asks the company now, which is what the new ticket copies), the workshop conversion in `ActAsync`, Edit's change to
  Workshop, `PhotosOutRequiredAsync` (so Machine collected, Out for delivery and Close), `CheckCloseAsync`, and the console's
  `PhotosRequired`/`PhotosOutRequired` (0 when off — every check that reads them passes). The story says *Machine collected.* with no
  photo count when none were taken.

### The judge

**`JobTypes.Problem(off)`** walks each category that is on (`ProblemFor`) from its first stage through every step `RouteSteps` leaves,
to where `TargetOf` sends it. A position is stage, category, the return stage, repairable, collected and **whether the money is settled**
(an amount invoiced or paid, not a quote's price; do not invoice; SLA; General's and a recurring task's Done). Abandoned and Back finish
nothing and are left out. It refuses a position that cannot reach Closed (walked backwards from Closed), and **reaching Closed unsettled**.
`StagesReached` gives the stages a route reaches — for stage B's line under each card, and for the harness. A test hook is a parameter
(`ProblemFor(..., target)`), never a flag in the product.

### How it is proved

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/jobtypecheck` (new, in memory) | **65 of 65.** (1) every combination of the switches each category can reach — General 32, Remote support 16, Recurring 4, Workshop 1,024, **Call out 16,384** (it can become a workshop job), Walk in 8,192: **25,652 walks in 7 s, none refused**; and `Problem` on 4,000 random sets of all of them. (2) for each category, no switch outside its list changes a stage it reaches — so (1) left nothing untried. (3) every switch, off alone, takes something away (a stage, a button, a rule, a category). (4) each does what the brief says. (5) **the judge catches a broken route**: payment before ordering off without the Parts fitted change (*closed without ever being invoiced*), a step sent in a circle, a stage that does not exist. (6) `Clean`. **59 of 65 with the Parts fitted change out** — every list with that switch off refused. |

Clint: *"Commit stage A, then build stage B, the Job types page in the portal."* Stage A is commit `a524f4b`. **Walked in the browser;
NOT on hardware.**

### The page

- **Portal → Job types, `/portal/jobtypes`** (`Pages/Portal/JobTypes.cshtml`). Every role may READ it — it sits under the folder's
  `PortalUser` policy, and is in the owner/supervisor and the office menus (not a technician's: theirs is their work, nothing about the
  company). **Only a supervisor or the owner sees boxes that work and a Save**; everybody else is told *Only a supervisor or the owner
  can change this* with every box disabled, and a post anyway is refused by `TenantService.SetJobTypesAsync` (nothing stored).
- **The cards are `JobTypes.Cards`** — one per category, then *Quotes* and *Every category* — each line a switch (with *With it off: …*
  from `JobSwitch.Off`) or a LOCKED step (🔒, greyed, with why). Remote support and General say *🔒 Always on* and why. A category's
  tick is *We use this*; unticked, its lines grey out and are disabled — **so they are not posted, and `Clean` leaves them out**: switched
  on again, the category comes back whole. `jobtypecheck` holds the cards to every switch on exactly one card, the card its group
  names, every lock with a reason.
- **Under each card, the way a job usually goes** — `JobTypes.Path(category, off, through)`: at each stage the FIRST step the route
  offers (`Workflow.Actions` is in that order on purpose), never Abandoned, waiting, a step that stays put or Back; a finished workshop
  machine is collected when nothing else is left; *through* forces a step (the Quotes card's line goes through *Quote needed*). Built from
  `RouteSteps` and `TargetOf` like everything else. Workshop, everything on: *Booked in → Inspected → Repairable → To be invoiced →
  Invoiced — awaiting payment → Awaiting collection → Closed*.
- **As boxes are ticked**, `?handler=Path&off=…` (read only, anybody who can read the page) answers every card's line AND
  `JobTypes.Problem` for the unsaved set; a refused set shows *This would not save: …* and disables Save. **The browser has no copy of the
  routes** — the line and the judge are the server's. No combination is refused today; the box exists for a switch added later.
- Save → *Saved. New tickets follow this from now on; tickets already open finish the way they started.* and *Last changed by … on …*.
- **Free and Basic companies never see it**: `FreePortal`'s allow-list does not name it, so it is refused like every page it does not
  name (`jobtypepage` checks: sent to `/portal/machines`).

### Shown once, to the owner

**`Portal/Index` sends an OWNER (`TenantRole.Owner`, not a supervisor) to `/portal/jobtypes?first=1` while `JobTypesChosenUtc` is
null** (full version only) — every company already running included, Anywhere I.T too. The page then says *Everything is switched on.
Untick what your company doesn't use…* and offers **Keep everything** (`OnPostKeep`: saves nothing off, which still sets the date) beside
Save. **The TRIP is what is remembered, not an answer (fixed 2026-10-28)**: as built it waited for Save or Keep everything, so Clint, clicking away, was sent back on every Dashboard click — *"When I click on the dashboard tab, it jumps to job types."* Now the redirect sets `Tenant.JobTypesShownUtc` by one conditional update (`TenantService.MarkJobTypesShownAsync`, migration `JobTypesShown`, both databases) and is never made again; the page still offers Keep everything until somebody answers. `jobtypepage` 34 (32 with the old rule). An owner already sent there before this goes once more, then never. **`first` is an `int`**: `?first=1` does not bind to a `bool`, and the line silently never
showed —
`jobtypepage` found it. **Four harnesses expected an owner's first page to be the dashboard** and were changed, not the product:
`invitecheck` and `admincheck` accept `/portal/jobtypes` as "in their portal"; `activitycheck` and `ticketeditcheck` save Job types for
their seeded company first, as any company already set up has. **A new harness that opens `/portal` as an owner must do the same.**

- **Still to come, stage C — the console**: `NewTicketDialog`'s own `PhotosRequired = 3` (it BLOCKS a workshop booking with fewer, so

## 169. Our site's chat bubble says The Remote Support Program; -RealSite opens signups — 2026-10-27

Clint, getting ready for 1 November: *"Make the chat bubble on theremotesupportprogram.com say The Remote Support Program, answered
by the Anywhere I.T people as now. And fix the deploy so -RealSite opens signups and switches the bubble on."*

### The fault in the deploy

`go-live.sh` wrote `RSP_Platform__SignupsEnabled=false` (and `"SignupsEnabled": false` in `appsettings.live.json`) on EVERY deploy,
and `-RealSite` changed only Caddy. So on 1 November the real site would have gone up with the signup page saying signups are
closed, and a signups switch made by hand would have been undone by the next deploy. `Platform:SiteChatSlug` was set nowhere.

**Now both follow the holding page** (step 3 of go-live.sh, from `HOLDING`, which step 2 decides): with the holding page in front
(the default) signups are closed and there is no bubble; with **`-RealSite`** signups are OPEN and `RSP_Platform__SiteChatSlug` is the
company given by **`Publish-Platform.ps1 -SiteChat`** (default `anywhereit`; `-SiteChat ""` for none) — `go-live.sh`'s third argument,
refused unless it is a short code. **Written on every deploy, so after 1 November EVERY deploy needs `-RealSite`**, or the holding page
comes back and signups close with it — the same as before for the page; now the two cannot disagree.

### The bubble wears our name on our site only

`Services/SiteChat.cs` is the one rule. The site's layout writes `<script src="/webchat/{slug}.js?site=1">`; `webchat-embed.js` reads
`site=1` off its OWN script address and passes it to `/api/webchat/{slug}` (the button's label and colour) and to the frame (the
window's heading and colour). **`SiteChat.Ours` honours it only when the slug IS `Platform:SiteChatSlug`** — any other company asking
gets its own name. On our site it says *The Remote Support Program* in `#6d28d9` (site.css `--fill`); in every other way it is Anywhere
IT's chat: the same people rung, the same hours, the same Website chat window, and a message out of hours becomes an Anywhere IT
ticket. **Anywhere IT's own website is unchanged** — its pasted line has no `site=1`. The emails a visitor may get afterwards (a
reply to a left message) are Anywhere IT's, as they are from its own site.

| | |
|---|---|
| `tools/webchatcheck` | **135 of 135** (127 + 8): the site's pages carry `?site=1`; on our site the state and the window say our name and colour; without it the company's own; **another company asking with `site=1` keeps its own name** (state and window); the script passes the ask on. **133 of 135 with the slug match taken out of `SiteChat.Ours`.** Its platform now runs with `SiteChatSlug`. |
| go-live.sh step 3, run against stand-in folders | holding page: `SignupsEnabled=false`, no slug, in both files; `-RealSite` + anywhereit: `true` and `SiteChatSlug=anywhereit`; `-RealSite` with none: `true`, no slug; a bad code refused. `bash -n` parses; `Publish-Platform.ps1` parses. |

## 170. Knowing when the site is down: a check from the office PC — 2026-10-27

Before 1 November (GO-LIVE.md's *"Monitoring — nothing tells us the service is down except a customer"*). Clint chose the office
PC — the one that already copies the backups (§120) — over an outside service. **`deploy/monitor/README.md` is the set-up**: one
command on that PC, `Install-SiteWatch.ps1`.

- **`deploy/monitor/Watch-Site.ps1`**, a scheduled task every 2 minutes (*Remote Support - watch the website*, runs with nobody
  signed in, `IgnoreNew` so two never overlap). It asks `/health` for `{"ok":true}` (20 s). **Two misses in a row** before the
  DOWN email — a deploy's restart is seconds (§165), and one miss alone is only logged. **One email down, one back up** with how
  long; nothing between. Once a day: the certificate under 14 days (Caddy renews at 30) and the backup copy's `LAST-OK.txt`
  older than 36 hours (§120 only ever wrote WARNING to a log nobody reads).
- **The office's own internet is asked first** (1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 on 443): with neither, the run is *office offline* and
  counts for nothing — no false alarm, and no mail could go anyway.
- **Mail goes through a theremotesupportprogram.com mailbox on xneelo's shared hosting**, port 587 STARTTLS — apart from the
  server it watches. The mailbox password is `Get-Credential | Export-Clixml` (`%USERPROFILE%\.rsp-watch\mail.xml`, DPAPI, that
  account on that PC). **A DOWN email that fails to send is not marked sent**, so the next check tries again.
- **The installer's test email goes through the check's own `-TestEmail`** — the very path an alert takes; it stops before
  scheduling anything if that fails. `-Remove` undoes it all.

## 172. Removing a client: a misspelling or a duplicate, its work moved to the right one — 2026-10-27

Clint: *"We do not seem to have the ability to remove clients. One of my staff created a client with the incorrect spelling and
the proper client already exists."* There was none — `Client.Archived` existed and nothing ever set it. **Removing is MOVING**:
the client page's new **Remove this client** card (bottom of `/portal/c/{n}`) asks *Move everything to* — the usual client picker
— says what will move (*"33 tickets, 2 machines, 4 people…"*), confirms, and lands on the right client's page saying so. A client
with nothing on it is simply removed (no picker). **Every rule is `Services/ClientService.Remove.cs`**:

- **Who**: `Permissions.CanRemoveClients` — the owner, a supervisor or an office administrator (the same people as Import clients;
  an assumption, since it cannot be undone). A technician does not see the card, and the service refuses them too.
- **Refused before anything moves**: anything on it and no client named; itself; another company's client; another company asking.
- **What moves**: tickets (each gets an AUTOMATIC story line *"Moved from X to Y — X was removed."*, so not in Latest activity, and
  `UpdatedUtc` is NOT touched — the list's order stays), machines (then `TenantHub.RefreshDeviceOwner` for each, which also
  re-tells its health check), people (archived too), knowledge base articles (deleted ones too) **and their saved versions** (or a
  restore would name a client that is gone), folders (a TOP folder whose name the right client already has, any case, becomes
  *"Network (from X)"* — the rule removing a folder uses), recurring tasks, website chats, health check reports.
- **The right client stands**: its details are kept, the wrong one only fills its BLANKS (the import's rule) and its notes are added
  (*"From X: …"*). **Its health check tick is the right client's** — the moved machines follow it; a spelling mistake must not
  install or remove anything on a customer's PCs by surprise.
- **One person on both** (same name, any case and spaces, or the same email) becomes ONE — the right client's, its blanks filled;
  their machines, tickets and chats are pointed at them. Anybody else moves as they are.
- **Then the row is DELETED**, not archived: nothing is left on it, and an archived row would be found again by
  `ClientService.ByNameAsync` the next time somebody typed the misspelling (it does not skip archived) — a new client silently
  reusing an invisible one. Typing the misspelt name again now makes a new, empty client. **The old `/portal/c/{n}` is a 404.**
- **One save**: all of it moves or none of it does.

Not done, on purpose: the console has no client page, so nothing there — its machine list follows through the hub; a client
picker in the console asks the server each time.

|---|---|
| `tools/clientremovecheck` (new) | **47 of 47 on both databases**, in-process against the real `ClientService`: a technician refused; an empty client removed and a second removal "not on file"; what is on it counted and said; the four refusals, with nothing moved after them; then Acme Ltdd into Acme Ltd — the phone kept, the address and notes filled, the health check tick the right one's, Sue on both one Sue (blanks filled), Jo by email one Jo, Bob and the archived leaver moved, no person left on a client that is gone, both machines moved and handed to the hub with Sue's PC still Sue's, a machine already right not told again, both tickets moved with Sue's naming the Sue kept, the automatic story line, `UpdatedUtc` untouched, no line on a ticket already right, articles (deleted too), versions, the clashing folder renamed, a folder inside keeping its place, the recurring task, the chat (and its contact), the health report, another company untouched, nothing anywhere naming the removed client, the misspelling typed again making a NEW empty client. **42 of 47 with the machines' contact and the versions/recurring moves taken out.** `--seed <folder>` leaves the same data for a platform to open. |
